The cloud lifted, and there it was shown, Miriam leprous, her skin like snow, alone.
Aaron turned, saw his sister's plight, "Forgive our sin, we've acted without sight!"
"Don't let her be like the dead," Aaron pled, Moses cried out, "Heal her, God," he said.
"If her father had spit, she'd hide seven days, Let her stay outside, then heal her ways."
Seven days passed, she was out of the camp, The people waited, till her return from the tramp.
Then they journeyed on, with lessons learned, From Hazeroth to Paran, they moved, discerned.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, here's what He said, "Send men to Canaan, see where you're led. Pick a prince from each tribe, a leader in rank, To spy out the land, from river to bank."
Moses obeyed, sent them out from Paran, Leaders of Israel, each a strong man. From Reuben, Shammua, son of Zaccur, Simeon's Shaphat, son of Hori, for sure.
Judah's Caleb, son of Jephunneh, bold, Issachar's Igal, son of Joseph, we're told. Ephraim's Hoshea, son of Nun, strong and keen, Benjamin's Palti, son of Raphu, on the scene.
Zebulun's Gaddiel, son of Sodi, stands, Manasseh's Gaddi, son of Susi, in the plans. Dan's Ammiel, son of Gemalli, in the zone, Asher's Sethur, Michael's son, not alone.
Naphtali's Nahbi, son of Vophsi, strides, Gad's Geuel, son of Machi, he abides. Moses called Hoshea, Joshua by name, Sent them to Canaan, fortune or fame.
"Head south," he said, "and climb high, Check out the land, strong or weak, tell me why. See the cities, camps or strongholds they keep, The soil, the wood, the secrets that sleep."
So up they went, from Zin's wild sand, To Rehob's gates, surveying the land. To Hebron they trekked, where Anak's sons stay, Grapes and figs from Eshcol, carried away.
Forty days later, they came back to report, To Moses and Aaron, told tales of the sort. "The land flows with honey, milk so sweet, But giants and walls, make us retreat."
Caleb rose up, stilled the crowd's fear, "Let's go and take it, the victory's near!" But the others said, "They're stronger than we, The land eats its own, it's not meant to be."
"The Nephilim are there, giants so tall, We felt like grasshoppers, ready to fall." Yet their tale spread fear, a shadow so wide, As the children of Israel, trembled and sighed.
The people cried out with a mournful sound, Their hearts heavy, they gathered around.
"Why did we leave Egypt's land, Just to die here, by Yahweh's hand?
Let's go back, find another way, Choose a leader, return today."
Moses and Aaron hit the ground, Before the crowd's angry, restless sound.
Joshua and Caleb, clothes torn, Spoke of the land they had sworn,
"The land's good, so rich and fine, Flowing with milk, honey, divine.
If Yahweh's pleased, He'll lead us in, Don't rebel, we'll surely win."
Yet the crowd, with stones in hand, Threatened them, made their stand.
Yahweh's glory then appeared, His voice to Moses, loud and clear:
"How long will they doubt my might? I'll make a nation strong, in their spite."
Moses pleaded, "What will they say? You led them here, show them the way.
Your name's known, your power's great, Forgive them now, don't seal their fate."
Yahweh replied, "I've heard your plea, But those who doubted won't see the land, not through me.
Caleb, with a spirit true, He'll enter in, his seed too."
Yahweh spoke, wrath in His tone, "In this wilderness you'll be alone.
Forty years, for forty days, You'll wander lost in the haze."
The spies who spread the false report, Paid the price in Yahweh's court.
But Joshua and Caleb stayed alive, From that land, they'd not be deprived.
The people mourned, they rose to fight, "We'll go, we've seen the light!"
Moses warned, "Don't disobey, Yahweh's not with you today."
But they climbed the mountain high, Ignoring Yahweh's clear reply.
The Amalekites came down swift, With strength and force, they gave no lift.
The people fell, defeated, torn, Their disobedience left them forlorn.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, clear and strong, "Tell Israel when they come along,
Into the land, I promised to give, Make offerings by fire, for me to receive.
Burnt offerings, vows, free will at your feasts, Pleasant aromas rise with the beasts.
Bring fine flour mixed with oil, it’s divine, And wine for the drink, measure it fine.
For each lamb, each ram, bring it right, A meal offering, a sacrifice, a pleasing sight.
Every bull gets its share, don’t you forget, Flour, oil, and wine, make the table set.
Native-born or foreign, all the same, One statute, one rule, in Yahweh’s name.
When you enter the land, and eat the bread, Offer your first dough as a wave, ahead.
If you err, forget these commands, Bring a bull for atonement, to Yahweh’s hands.
The priest will make atonement, your sins will clear, For errors done without knowledge, no need to fear.
If one sins unwittingly, a goat will do, The priest will atone, Yahweh forgives you.
But if with high hand, a soul defies, Cut off they'll be, no more lies.
In the wilderness, a man gathered sticks, On Sabbath he was caught, his fate was fixed.
Yahweh commanded stoning, no mercy to lend, Israel executed, as Yahweh did send.
Then Yahweh spoke, with wisdom and might, "Fringes on garments, a reminder in sight.
A cord of blue on the edge you'll place, Remember my commands, keep your faith.
I'm Yahweh your God, out of Egypt I brought, Be holy to me, remember what I taught."
Korah and his crew, they started to rise, Challengin' Moses, bringin' surprise. Two-fifty leaders, men of renown, Standin' tall, tryin' to take him down.
They said, “Moses, you take too much on your plate, We’re holy too, we all relate! Why you lift yourself above the rest?” Moses heard, fell down, distressed.
“In the morning,” said Moses, “God will choose, He’ll show who’s holy, who will lose. Korah, bring your censors, light the flame, Tomorrow we’ll see who’s callin’ His name.”
Moses spoke, “Levi, hear me right, God's brought you close, givin' you the sight. Yet you want the priesthood, grabbin' more, Against Yahweh, you wage this war.”
Dathan and Abiram, Moses did call, “We won't come up, we'll not fall. You brought us from milk and honey's land, Now we're in the wilderness, this ain't grand.”
Moses got angry, spoke to the Lord, “Don’t accept their offering, hear my word. I didn’t take nothin', no donkey in sight, I've done them no wrong, not a single slight.”
Moses to Korah, “Tomorrow's the day, Bring your censers, come and pray. Yahweh's glory will show what’s real, Fire and incense, His truth will reveal.”
Yahweh's glory shone bright, "Sinners, separate, before I smite." Moses down, face to the ground, “God, spare them, one man sinned around.”
“Get away from Korah,” Moses said, “Don’t touch their tents, or you’ll be dead.” The earth opened wide, swallowed them whole, Korah and crew, down they roll.
People ran, screaming, “We’ll be next,” Fire from Yahweh burned the rest. Censers taken, turned to bronze, A sign of what went wrong.
People complained, “You killed our kin!” Cloud covered the Tent where Yahweh's been. “Step away,” Yahweh warned again, Wrath unleashed, a plague did begin.
Moses commanded, “Aaron, make it stop, Incense now, before they drop.” Aaron ran, stood between life and death, Stopped the plague, gave them breath.
Fourteen thousand, seven hundred gone, The plague halted, Aaron won. Returned to Moses, their work done right, The plague was stopped, saved from blight.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, his voice clear and bold, "Gather rods from each tribe, let the story unfold. One for each house, twelve rods in line, Each name written clearly, each sign to define.
Aaron's name on Levi's, for that tribe's head, Place them in the Tent where my presence is spread. The rod that buds, it's the one I've chosen, Silence the murmurs, their complaints will be frozen."
Moses spoke, and each prince gave, Twelve rods in total, each tribe's stave. Aaron's rod there among the rest, In the Tent before Yahweh, the ultimate test.
Next day came, Moses entered the Tent, Behold Aaron's rod! Blossoms it sent. Sprouted, budded, bloomed, almonds ripe, A miracle shown, an end to the gripe.
Moses brought the rods, showed them all, Each man took his rod, saw Aaron's call. Yahweh said, "Put Aaron's rod back in its place, A sign against rebellion, to limit their space."
Moses did just as Yahweh had bade, To quell their complaints, the foundation laid. The people cried out, "We're doomed, we're lost! Approach the tabernacle, and we'll pay the cost!
Will we all perish, is this our end?" With fear in their hearts, on Yahweh they depend.
Aaron, Yahweh spoke, hear these words divine, "You and your sons, the priesthood's line. Bear the weight of the sanctuary's care, Levi’s tribe stands with you, to serve and share.
Keep commands, guard the Tent — that's your call, But don't touch the sacred, or you'll fall. Stay close, keep responsibility tight, A stranger comes near — they're out of sight.
Perform your duty, shield from wrath's rise, For Israel's peace, heed these ties. I've taken Levites, a gift, my decree, For the Tent’s service, they're dedicated to me.
Priesthood's yours, a sacred role to fulfill, Strangers come near, they face the chill. "Wave offerings, holy, are yours," I say, Your sons' forever, in the priesthood's sway.
Holy offerings, meal, sin, and more, Eat like it's sacred — it's yours to the core. Wave offerings too, for you and your kin, Clean in your house, let the feast begin.
Best oil, vintage, grain — first fruits are yours, Bring to Yahweh, open the stores. Firstborn of flesh, man or beast, Redeem the unclean — that's the least.
Cattle, sheep, and goats — they remain, Sprinkle blood, burn fat, in Yahweh's name. Meat of offerings, it's yours, understand, A covenant of salt, forever at hand.
No land inheritance, Yahweh’s your gain, Tithes for the Levites, a service chain. Israel keeps distance, sin to avoid, Levites serve, their task deployed.
Moses, my message to the Levites take, "From Israel's tithe, a wave offering make. Tithe of the tithe, to Yahweh present, To Aaron's hands, the offering's sent.
Give the best, holy in sight, As threshing floor and wine press might. Eat it anywhere, your service’s due, With no sin burden — this is what's true.
Profane not the holy, respect the name, So you won't perish, avoid the shame."
Yahweh spoke out to Moses and Aaron, no delay, "Here's the law, listen up, hear what I say.
Bring a red heifer, perfect, no defect or yoke, Hand her to Eleazar, in camp she'll be broke.
Eleazar takes her blood, with a finger, a sweep, Sprinkles it seven times, before the Tent, keep it neat.
Burn the heifer in sight, skin, meat, blood ignite, Add cedar, hyssop, scarlet, in the fire so bright.
Priest washes his clothes, bathes in water's embrace, Returns to the camp, unclean till night takes its place.
The one who burns her, too, wash and bathe, Unclean till the evening, in the water they're saved.
A clean one collects ashes, stores them outside, Use it for cleansing, a law to abide.
Touch a dead body, unclean seven days, Purify on third and seventh, or be cut away.
In a tent where a man dies, unclean all who enter, Every open vessel, unclean at the center.
Touch the slain in the field, a grave or a bone, You're unclean seven days, don't stand alone.
Take ashes, pour water, let it mix in the vessel, Hyssop and water, all impurities wrestle.
Third day, seventh day, sprinkling's done, Wash clothes, bathe, by evening, it's a clean run.
But fail to purify, and be cut from the crowd, Defiles Yahweh’s sanctuary, no impurities allowed.
Perpetual statute, wash after the sprinkle, Touch impurity, unclean till stars twinkle.
Whatever the unclean touch, it spreads their stain, Unclean till evening, till night's calm reign."
In Zin, the people stayed, where Miriam laid, Her life came to an end, in Kadesh she was laid.
No water in the land, the people were upset, Against Moses and Aaron, their complaints were set.
"Wish we’d died with kin, why lead us here to fall? This place is barren, no crops, no fruits at all!"
From the crowd they fled, to the Tent's gate, Fell on their faces, awaiting Yahweh’s fate.
"Take the rod," said Yahweh, "speak to the rock's face, Water it will flow, to quench the people's chase."
Moses took the rod, as Yahweh had decreed, Gathered all the people, their thirst he would heed.
"Hear me now, you rebels, shall water come from stone?" Struck it twice with the rod, the water made its own.
Waters rushed out, the people and beasts drank well, But Yahweh's voice rose, with a truth to tell.
"Because you lacked trust, my name you did not raise, You won't lead them into the promised place."
Meribah’s waters, a story of strife and test, Where Israel quarreled, and Yahweh was blessed.
Moses sent word, to Edom’s king with hope, "Let us pass through, we won’t stray or grope."
But Edom’s response was cold as stone, "You shall not pass, leave my land alone."
Israel begged once more, offering peace in their plea, But Edom stood firm, with a threat and decree.
So Israel turned, from Edom’s harsh command, Journeyed on to Hor, as Yahweh planned.
At Mount Hor, Yahweh’s voice did proclaim, "Aaron will be gathered, his time has come to claim."
Moses took Aaron, Eleazar by side, On top of Mount Hor, where Aaron would abide.
Striped of his garments, Eleazar was dressed, Aaron died there, in his eternal rest.
The whole congregation, saw Aaron’s end, Wept for thirty days, for their priest and friend.
In the South, King Arad had heard the news, Israel's coming, so he'd better choose. He went to war, took captives in the fight, Israel vowed to Yahweh, "Give us might."
"If you deliver, we'll destroy their town," God listened, brought the Canaanites down. Called it Hormah, where they did prevail, Onward toward Edom, their spirits frail.
Complaints rose up, "Why this desert trek? No bread, no water, food makes us wreck." God sent snakes, venom struck them all, Israel cried to Moses, "Pray, don't fall."
Moses did, and God replied clear, "Make a snake, lift it high, no fear. Look and live, that bronze serpent's key," Moses raised it up for all to see.
Israel journeyed, camped in the land, Through Oboth, Iyeabarim, by God’s hand. On to Zered and beyond the divide, Moab's border, where Arnon's waters glide.
Wars of Yahweh spoke of this turf, "Vaheb in Suphah," the valleys' worth. To Beer they traveled for God’s supply, "Gather 'round, I'll give water," was God’s reply.
"Singing to the well, spring up!" they cried, Princes dug deep, where life abides. From Mattanah to Nahaliel they roamed, Up to Pisgah, where they called home.
Israel sent word to Sihon, king strong, "Let us pass, we’ll do you no wrong." Sihon refused, brought his army's might, Israel fought, took the land that night.
From Arnon to Jabbok, they claimed the ground, In Heshbon's cities, victory was found. Proverbs spoke, "Heshbon's flame burns bright," Moab's defeat was clear in sight.
"Woe to you, Moab!" cries of despair, Children of Chemosh taken there. Israel dwelled where Amorites stood, Moshe's spies took Jazer, understood.
Then to Bashan, Og rose to fight, God said, "Fear not, you'll claim his might." Just as with Sihon, the land was won, Israel prevailed, no foe left to run.
Israel camped by Moab’s plain, Where Balak saw what they had gained.
Moab feared, their numbers vast, Said to Midian, "They won’t last."
"An ox licks grass, so they consume, Balak’s reign may find its doom."
Messengers sent to Balaam’s land, "Curse them, for they’re too grand."
"From Egypt, they came to be, Covering earth like a vast sea."
"Curse them, so I might win, Drive them out, take back my kin."
Moab’s elders, rewards in hand, To Balaam spoke Balak’s command.
"Lodge here, I’ll seek Yahweh’s voice, I’ll bring back His choice."
God asked Balaam, "Who are these men?" "Brought by Balak, to curse with pen."
"Don’t go, don’t curse, they’re blessed," Balaam to Moab, "Yahweh says no quest."
Princes returned, "He won’t engage," Balak sent more with greater wage.
"Come curse, gain great honor, I’ll do whatever you ponder."
Balaam said, "Even treasure, I can’t defy, Yahweh’s word is my guide."
"Stay, I'll seek Yahweh’s night reply," God said, "Go, but heed My word, don’t lie."
Balaam rose, saddled the donkey, God’s anger burned, angel stood ready.
Donkey saw angel, sword in hand, Turned from the path, out to the land.
Balaam struck, turned her back again, She saw the angel in the narrow lane.
Crushed his foot, he struck with might, Angel blocked left and right.
Donkey lay down, Balaam’s wrath grew, Struck her hard, but she knew.
Yahweh opened her mouth to speak, "What did I do, for this harsh streak?"
"You mocked me, if I had a sword, I’d have killed you, with this cord."
"Am I not your trusty steed? Have I ever been in need?"
"No," he admitted, then saw with fright, Yahweh’s angel in the light.
"Why strike her thrice?" the angel asked, "Your perverse way is my task."
"Donkey saved you, turned away thrice, Else you’d be gone, and she’d suffice."
"I have sinned," Balaam confessed, "If it's wrong, I’ll turn, if you suggest."
"Go, but speak what I say," So Balaam went on his way.
Balak met him at Moab’s gate, "Why delay? Honor awaits."
Balaam said, "I’m here to speak, What God says, I will repeat."
To Kiriath Huzoth they came, Balak sacrificed, in Yahweh’s name.
Next morn, to Baal’s high place, Balaam saw the people’s face.
Balaam said to Balak, "Seven altars, make them grand, Prepare seven bulls, seven rams in this land." Balak followed through, just as Balaam had planned, A bull and a ram on each altar did stand.
Balaam spoke to Balak, "Stay by your offering's flame, I'll seek Yahweh's word, see what He'll proclaim." To the heights he ascended, seeking divine acclaim, God met him there, and spoke to his name.
Balaam reported, "Seven altars I've built, A bull and a ram on each, the incense spilt." Yahweh put His word in Balaam's mouth, "Return to Balak, let the truth go south."
He came back to Balak, who stood by the fire, Princes of Moab with him, their eyes filled with desire. Balaam began his chant, from Aram he'd come, "Curse Jacob, defy Israel," Balak's beating drum.
"How can I curse whom God has blessed? This nation stands tall, unoppressed. From the rocky heights, their strength I can see, A people alone, bound to be free."
"Count their dust? Who can even endeavor? May I die as they, blessed forever." Balak cried out, "What have you done? I sought their curse, but blessings you've spun!"
Balaam replied, "I speak what Yahweh imparts, His words in my mouth, direct to your hearts." Balak pleaded, "Try another place, See just a part, let curses trace."
To Zophim's field, atop Pisgah they went, Seven altars again, their offerings sent. "Stand by your flames," Balaam said, taking leave, To meet with God, His word to receive.
Yahweh spoke again, placed words in his mouth, Balaam returned, the plan heading south. Balak asked, "What did Yahweh reveal?" Balaam spoke, "Listen, here's the deal:
God's no man, no lies, no mistaken vow, He blesses, who can reverse it now? In Jacob, no fault, no sin in His sight, Yahweh's with them, their king's delight."
"Out of Egypt God brought them strong, Like a wild ox, they cannot go wrong. No enchantment can hold them, no diviner's spell, 'What has God done?' the world will tell."
"A lioness rising, ready to strike, Till prey is devoured, their strength's a spike." Balak sighed, "Neither curse nor bless, Your words bring me no rest."
Balaam replied, "Didn't I say it true? Yahweh's words command what I must do." Balak, persistent, "Another place we'll find, Perhaps God will permit your curse this time."
On Peor's peak, looking into the sands, Balaam instructed, "Seven altars, our final stands." Balak complied, once more with the plan, A bull and a ram on each altar grand.
Balaam saw pleasing Yahweh was the game, No divination now, just the wilderness to claim.
Lifted his eyes, saw tribes in their places, Spirit of God came, filled him with graces.
"Words of God I hear, vision of the Almighty," "Falling down, eyes open, all truth in clarity."
"How good are your tents, Jacob, Israel's homes," "Like valleys, gardens, where clear water roams."
"Water flows from his buckets, seeds in the stream," "King higher than Agag, kingdom's esteem."
"God brings him strong out, like a wild ox might," "His foes' bones crushed, arrows take flight."
"He lies like a lion, who dares wake his rest?" "Blessed are those who bless, cursed spurned at best."
Balak’s anger flared, clapped his hands in wrath, "I called you to curse, but blessings you path."
"Flee to your place, no honors await," "Yahweh blocks your honor, seals your fate."
Balaam replied, "Didn't I say it clear?" "Can't stray from Yahweh, His words I revere."
"House filled with riches, silver, and gold," "Can't change the message Yahweh has told."
"I'll go to my people, but listen up now," "I'll tell of the future, hear this vow."
"Vision afar, a star from Jacob's side," "Scepter rises, Moab crushed with pride."
"Edom, Seir, shall fall to the hand," "While Israel valiantly takes command."
"Amalek's first but ends in demise," "Kenite's stronghold, still wasted, it lies."
"Kittim's ships will come, afflict the shore," "Destruction follows, the end of war."
Balaam stood, returned to his own space, Balak too left, with anger's trace.
In Shittim, Israel stayed, but trouble was ahead, They fell for Moab's daughters, into mischief they led.
Called to false gods' altars, they ate, kneeled, and bowed, Joined with Baal Peor, and Yahweh's wrath was loud.
God told Moses, "Hang the chiefs up high, Let my anger turn away, let justice touch the sky."
Moses said to the judges, "Deal with every man, Who followed Baal Peor, strike them where they stand."
Then came a man with a Midianite dame, Right before all eyes, no shame in their game.
Phinehas saw it, his heart in a flame, Grabbed his spear, to put an end to the shame.
He struck them both, stopped the plague's cruel course, Twenty-four thousand gone, oh the remorse.
God spoke to Moses, this is what He said, "Phinehas has turned my wrath, no more bloodshed.
For his zeal, my covenant of peace he receives, An everlasting priesthood, for all his family's leaves."
The man was Zimri, from Simeon's line, The woman, Cozbi, Midian's design.
God told Moses, "Fight the Midianite fight, For their deceit with Peor, set things right."
After the plague, God called to Moses, said with might, “Count my people, those ready to fight.” In Moab's plains, by Jordan's flow, Moses and Eleazar made sure they'd know.
Reuben's sons, the count began, Forty-three thousand, in a warrior clan. From Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi's line, Eliab's sons rebelled, crossed the divine.
When Korah’s crew faced their doom, The earth opened wide, swallowed up in gloom. Yet Korah's sons lived; they didn’t die, Their numbers stayed, while others said goodbye.
Simeon’s tally, twenty-two thousand strong, Counting Nemuel, Jamin, Zerah, where they belong. Gad's tribe next, with a roll call too, Forty thousand five hundred, the dream they pursue.
Judah's sons listed, Er and Onan gone, Seventy-six thousand with Perez marching on. Issachar’s group, sixty-four thousand plus, From Tola to Shimron, they made a fuss.

Zebulun's families counted, sixty thousand and more, From Sered, Elon, Jahleel, they marched forth to explore. Joseph's sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, With fifty-two thousand, their ranks were a grand hymn.
Benjamin's numbers, forty-five thousand six, With Ard and Naaman, they joined the mix. Dan and Asher, with families vast, Naphtali's forty-five thousand, marching fast.
“Grant the land by number,” God commanded, with a plan, “To the many, more land; to fewer, less span.” The Levites special, no land for their claim, But counted they were, in honor, not in name.
From Gershon to Kohath, Levi’s sons stand, Amram’s line through Moses, Aaron, a righteous band. With strange fire, Nadab and Abihu fell, Their tale a warning, a story to tell.
Moses and Eleazar counted anew, In Moab's plains, Israel's strength they knew. But none remained from Sinai's old count, Except Caleb and Joshua, whose faith did surmount.
Five daughters of Zelophehad stepped near, Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, Tirzah clear.
They stood before Moses, the priest, the crew, At the Tent of Meeting, they spoke what was true:
"Our father died in the wilderness, you see, Not with Korah's crowd, just his own decree.
He left no sons, just daughters here, Why should his name disappear?
Give us a share, let his name survive, Among his brothers, let it thrive."
Moses took their cause up high, Before Yahweh, the Most High.
Yahweh spoke, straight and right, "The daughters speak, they have the light.
Give them a share, rightful and real, Among their father's brothers, seal the deal.
Tell Israel, 'If a man leaves no son, His daughter takes the inheritance won.
No daughter, then it goes to the brothers, Still no brothers? To the father's others.
And if kin are nowhere to be found, Pass it on, keep it sound.'
This rule I declare, just and strong, A statute for Israel, where it belongs."
Then Yahweh said, "Moses, climb high, See the land for Israel, under the sky.
Once you've seen, you'll join the rest, Like Aaron, your brother, laid to rest.
For you defied my word in Zin, At Meribah's waters, you didn't begin."
Moses answered, with a plea, "Appoint a leader, God of all we see.
One to lead, in and out, So they're not like sheep, wandering about."
Yahweh chose Joshua, Spirit-driven, "Lay hands on him, the charge is given.
In front of Eleazar, make it known, Commission him, let it be shown.
Give him authority, let them obey, He'll guide by the Urim, lead their way."
Moses did as Yahweh spoke, Hands on Joshua, the Spirit woke.
He was set before the crowd, Commissioned strong, Moses proud.
Yahweh spoke to Moses, words clear to relay, “Tell my people, bring offerings, don't delay.
See my aroma's sweet in seasons set, Two male lambs, perfect, each day met.
One in the morn, one as the sun sets, Fine flour and oil, the recipe’s set.
From Sinai it came, a fire offering's scent, A drink poured out, in holiness, spent.
Evening comes, repeat the morning's due, For a pleasant aroma, offering anew.
On the Sabbath, two lambs without a flaw, Double flour and oil, the offering’s law.
New months call for bulls, rams, and seven lambs more, With fine flour and oil, pour as before.
Wine’s poured in fractions, each measure known, Monthly offerings, on altars shown.
One goat for sin, alongside the daily flame, Yahweh's commands, all offerings the same.
In the first month, Passover's here, Unleavened bread for a week is clear.
A holy gathering, work set aside, Burnt offerings pure, Yahweh's delight.
Two bulls, one ram, seven lambs without blame, Flour and oil blend, their offering’s fame.
Seven days straight, the scent rising high, Adding to the daily, reaching the sky.
The seventh day calls for sacred rest, No work, just gather, Yahweh’s blessed.
First fruits bring, a new feast in weeks, Holy convocation, no work, just peace.
Bulls and rams, seven lambs burn bright, Fine flour with oil, perfect in sight.
One goat for atonement, a sin’s release, With the regular offering, Yahweh’s feast.
Follow these commands, without defect, An aroma to Yahweh, in all respect.
Seventh month begins, hear the trumpet sound, A holy convocation, no work around. Burnt offerings rise, aroma sweet and grand, A bull, a ram, lambs without a blemish stand.

Israel journeyed, from Beeroth they moved, At Moserah, Aaron died, his life removed.
Eleazar stepped up, took the priestly place, From Gudgodah to Jotbathah, they resumed their pace.
Yahweh chose Levi, to bear His sacred ark, No land for Levi, but Yahweh left His mark.
Forty days on the mountain, like before, Yahweh listened, wouldn't destroy, He swore.
"Arise," He said, "Lead the people, take their stand, To possess the promised, father-sworn land."
Israel, what does Yahweh need you to see? Fear Him, love Him, walk faithfully.
Keep His commands, for your own good, He owns the heavens, that's understood.
He loved your fathers, chose their seed, Circumcise your heart, from stubbornness freed.
God of gods, Lord of lords, great and mighty, No respecter of persons, no bribes, He's rightly.
Justice for the fatherless, loves the alien, Feed and clothe them, show compassion.
Love the stranger, you were once foreigners too, Fear Yahweh, serve Him, be true.
He is your praise, your God above, Great things He's done, a labor of love.
Seventy went to Egypt in the past, Now like stars, your numbers are vast.
"Love Yahweh your God," that's the command, Keep His words, His laws, with a steady hand.
"Not to your children, this message I bring, But to you who've seen Yahweh do mighty things."
In Egypt's land, great signs were made, Pharaoh's army in the Red Sea laid.
He led you through desert's demanding test, To this very place, where you now rest.
Dathan and Abiram felt the earth's embrace, Swallowed whole, gone without a trace.
Your eyes have seen all these wonders and more, So keep the commandments, victory's at your door.
That you may be strong, take the land you see, A land of milk and honey, flowing free.
Not like Egypt, where seeds were sown, But hills and valleys where rains have grown.
Yahweh’s eyes upon it, all through the year, "Love Me, serve Me," His voice you'll hear.
"I'll send the rains, early and late, Grain, wine, and oil, on your plate."
Fields with grass, full stomachs you'll find, But stray from Him, and rain won't be kind.
"Bind my words, close to your heart, Teach them daily, never depart."
Write them down, on your home's door, That your days be multiplied evermore.
Keep these words, cling to His way, And you'll drive out nations, come what may.
From wilderness to sea, your feet shall roam, Every path, every place, yours to call home.
"Before you today, a choice to make, Blessing or curse, paths you take."
A blessing if you heed, His commands you hold, A curse if you stray, if other gods you behold.
When Yahweh brings you, to the land so wide, Set the blessing on Gerizim, curse on Ebal's side.
Cross the Jordan, take the land He gives, Observe His statutes, in His ways you live.
Listen up, here’s what you gotta know, In the land that Yahweh’s givin', let His commandments flow.
Smash their altars, break their stone, Burn down their idols, don’t leave a bone.
"Seek the place that I choose to honor My name, Bring your offerings there, don’t play no game."

Listen to what Yahweh commands, It’ll go well for you and your lands.

"Whatever I command, observe and do, Don’t add or subtract, keep My words true."

"Yahweh's testing your heart and soul," Keep Him first; make Him your goal.

From Egypt's bondage, He set you free, Cut off the one who talks deceitfully.

Hear His voice, His commands obey, Do what's right in Yahweh's way.

No poor among you, bless the land, If you heed God's command.
"Listen to My voice," Yahweh will say, Lend to nations, lead the way.

Poor will always be around, that's true, Open your hand, it's what you must do.

"Don't bring Yahweh a sheep with a flaw, A defect or evil—that's against the law.

When you enter the land Yahweh gives, And want a king like the neighbor lives,

So his kingdom endures, his days extend, He and his children, in Israel's land, their story won't end."

Yahweh chose them, out of all tribes, To minister forever, they keep the vibes.

"My words in his mouth, he'll speak them all, If they ignore, it's their own fall."

“The avenger may chase with anger in his heart, But he didn’t mean to, that's the crucial part.”

“Innocent blood mustn't stain your ground, In the land Yahweh gives, let peace be found.”

“You shall not pity, purging guilt from your view, Keep Israel pure, let justice be true.”

“If found false, their fate you’ll reverse, Remove the evil, end the curse.”

“Life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, Hand for hand, foot for foot, pursue the truth.”

The priest steps up, his voice loud and clear, "Hear, Israel, the battle is near. Let not your heart faint or be filled with dread, For Yahweh fights for you, ahead."

"Forgive, Yahweh, your people, redeemed, Keep innocent blood from being deemed."
Put away the guilt, do what's right, In Yahweh's eyes, bring justice to light.
Going to battle, foes delivered in hand, Captives taken, you see a woman stand.
She's beautiful, you want her as wife, Bring her home, let her mourn her life.

If the delight fades, let her go free, Don't sell her, no slave shall she be.
Two wives, one's loved, the other's scorned, Firstborn's rights, to the hated's son adorned.
Double portion, the firstborn's due, Acknowledge the strength, his rights are true.
A stubborn son, rebellious, won't hear, Parents bring him to the elders, voice their fear.

Sin worthy of death, a man on a tree, Bury him that day, don't let the curse be.
Don't defile the land, your inheritance pure, In God's given land, keep justice sure.

Don't wear clothes meant for another, God's word says "don't bother."
Find a nest with eggs or young, don’t take the hen, Let her go, so good may come again.
Build a house, make that rail strong, Prevent a fall, right a wrong.
Don't mix seeds in your vineyard, heed the warning, Keep your fields pure, no defiling in the morning.
Don't plow with ox and donkey combined, Keep clothes of wool and linen unaligned.
Fringes on your cloak, four corners they adorn, Remember the commandments, the ones you've sworn.
Man takes a wife, then spreads false shame, Parents present proof, clear her name.

Man lies with another's wife, both must die, Remove the evil, let justice fly.

In the field, her cries unheard, Only the man punished, as per God's word.
A virgin unpledged, caught in the act, He pays her father, marries her, that's the pact.
No man shall take his father's wife, Respect the bond, honor life.
Don't step into Yahweh's crew, if you've been crushed or cut, The forbidden union's kids, in the tenth gen, still shut,

Not just you, but those to come, Remember Egypt, where you were from.

No root of poison, no heart astray, Yahweh’s wrath for those who stray.
"The curse will fall," Yahweh declares, Blot out their name, no pardons, no dares.
Future folks will see the land, Sulfur, salt, no grass, barren sand.
"Why this wrath?" the nations will cry, "They broke Yahweh's bond, that's why."
Served other gods, left Yahweh behind, Anger burned, land undermined.
Secret things are Yahweh's own, But what’s revealed, is ours alone.
To keep the law, to do what's right, Yahweh's word, our guiding light.
When blessings and curses fill your mind, Recall them all, don't leave them behind.
Among the nations where you're driven, Turn back to Yahweh, your heart's been given.
With all your soul, obey His call, Yahweh will release you, break the wall.
From every land where you've been scattered, He'll gather you, your heart unshattered.
He'll bring you back to your fathers' land, You'll possess it, like a king you'll stand.
He'll do you good, your numbers grow, More than before, His mercy flow.
Yahweh will change your heart's direction, To love Him fully, feel His affection.
Enemies cursed, while you arise, Obey His word, make it your prize.
Prosperity in all your labor, Fruit of your body, Yahweh's favor.
His voice, His law, hold them tight, Turn to Him with all your might.
Commands not distant, they're near and clear, No need to ask, "Who's bringing it here?"
Not beyond seas, no distant quest, The word's in your heart, it knows you best.
Life and death, they stand before, Choose life today, and live much more.
Love Yahweh, follow His ways, In His land, prolong your days.
But if you turn and walk astray, Worship idols, lose your way.
Then perish you will, in this land, Across the Jordan, without His hand.
Heaven and earth bear witness true, Life and death set before you.
Choose life, you and your kin shall live, Love Yahweh, obey, and give.
For He's your life, your days to prolong, In the land He promised, where you belong.

Moses stepped up, words ready to flow, "Listen up, Israel, there's something you should know. I'm one-twenty today, can't come and go no more, Yahweh said, 'Moses, you ain't crossing this Jordan shore.'
But don't you worry, God Himself will lead, He'll wipe out nations, make 'em scatter like seed. Joshua's your man, he's gonna guide your way, Just like Yahweh promised on another day.
Remember Sihon and Og, those kings got beat, Yahweh crushed their lands, laid 'em down at your feet. Be strong, courageous, don't you dare feel small, Yahweh's got your back, He won't let you fall."
Moses called Joshua for all to see, "Be strong, be brave, lead 'em to victory. Yahweh's with you, He won't let you go, Don't be scared, don't let your courage get low."
Moses penned the law, gave it to the priests, "Every seven years, read it for the feasts. Gather everyone, men, women, and kids, Teach 'em to fear Yahweh, do all He bids."
Then Yahweh spoke, “Moses, time's running out, Bring Joshua to Me; let there be no doubt.” In the Tent of Meeting, a cloud did descend, Yahweh said, "Moses, your journey's at an end.
This people will stray, chase gods not their own, My anger will rise, they'll reap what they've sown. But teach them this song, let it ring in their ears, A witness for Me through all of their years.

When the land's theirs, flowing with milk and sweet honey, They'll get fat, turn away, forget who saved 'em from money. Troubles will come, but this song will stay true, A reminder of what they forgot to do."
Moses wrote the song, taught it that day, Commissioned Joshua, "Lead them the right way. Take the law, place it by the Ark's side, A witness against you, let it be your guide.
I know you're stubborn, even while I'm alive, After I'm gone, will your faith survive? Gather the elders, let them hear this word, Let heaven and earth be the witnesses stirred."
Moses sang the song, every word clear, To remind Israel of Yahweh, keep Him near.
Listen up, skies, hear me, earth, when I speak, My words like rain, gentle, so unique.
"Yahweh's name I’ll proclaim, so great, The Rock, his ways perfect, never late."
But the people turned, crooked and wrong, They forgot the God to whom they belong.
"Is this how you repay the Almighty's grace, The Father who saved you, set your place?"
Remember the past, the old days of yore, Ask your elders, they'll tell you more.
God set the nations, each with its own, Israel's his portion, his very own throne.
Found in the desert, waste howling and wild, He cared and protected, like a father to a child.
Like an eagle's wings, spread and wide, Yahweh led them, no others by his side.
He gave them riches from the land so sweet, Milk, honey, and grain, at their feet.
But Jeshurun grew fat, kicked and turned, Forgot the Rock from whom they’d learned.
Provoked by idols, anger was stirred, Sacrificed to demons, not his word.
"See now, I’ll hide my face, see their fate, A faithless generation, filled with hate."
Jealousy burned, with gods they adored, A fire consumed, from earth to the core.
"I’ll heap evils, spend arrows in strife, Hunger and beasts, they’ll know my knife."
Nations void of counsel, so blind, Enemies will rise, leave them behind.
"See your gods, where’s their aid? Can they save you, the choices you made?"
"I alone am He, no one can save, I wound, I heal, from cradle to grave."
"Vengeance is mine, when the time is near, Calamity rushes, instills them with fear."
Yahweh will judge, compassion he’ll give, For his people, in mercy, they’ll live.
"Rejoice, nations, Yahweh’s right, Avenge his own, lead to the light."
Moses spoke the words, the song of his heart, Joshua beside, ready to impart.
"Keep these words, they’re your life and way, Cross over Jordan, where you will stay."
God spoke to Moses, "Climb up, see the land, But not to enter, just understand."
Moses would see from afar, not near, For past missteps, the consequence clear.
"Look, but don’t touch, this is the decree, Israel will enter, but not you, nor me."
Moses stood and blessed the crowd, his words were strong, his voice loud. "Yahweh came from Sinai's peak, from Seir He rose, His glory did speak.
From Mount Paran He shone bright, ten thousand holy ones in His sight. At His right, a fiery law He gave, to His people, the ones He'd save.
He loves them all, they're in His hand, they sit at His feet, they understand. Moses gave the law to keep, an inheritance for Jacob deep.
Reuben's tribe, let them survive, never let their numbers dive. For Judah, he called on Yahweh’s might, to bring him home, to win each fight.
"Levi," he said, "has sacred stones, proven in trials, they've held their own. Teach the laws, the incense burn, bless their skills, for justice yearn."
Benjamin dwells under Yahweh's care, safe and sound in a love so rare. Joseph's land, blessed with earth’s best, mountains and fruits, he's truly blessed.
Zebulun and Issachar, rejoice and call, gather the people, offer it all. Gad's a lioness, he takes his claim, righteousness in Yahweh's name.
Dan, a cub, leaps fierce and free, Naphtali's favor, full as can be. Asher's strength like iron bars, blessed with children and under the stars.
No one like God who rides the skies, beneath His arms, His people rise. Israel safe, with grain and wine, Yahweh saves, His help divine.
Happy is Israel, saved by Yahweh's might, tread on high places, His shield is right."
Moses climbed up from Moab's plain, to Nebo's peak so high, He's opposite Jericho, with a view that touched the sky.
God showed him lands wide, from Gilead to Dan, Through Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh—what a plan!
All the land of Judah, stretching to the Western Sea, Jericho, the city of palms, down to Zoar's territory.
God spoke clear, "Here's the land I swore to Abraham's line, To Isaac and Jacob, their offspring's future sign.
I've let you see it with your eyes, but you won't cross that shore.” So in Moab's land, Moses lived no more.
He died as God said, buried deep where none can say, In Moab's valley, his grave unknown to this day.
At a hundred and twenty, his sight still strong, His strength not waned, though his days were long.
Israel wept thirty days, mourning in the Moab sand, Till tears dried and they moved by God's command.
Joshua stood ready, wisdom in his hand, For Moses touched him, making him grand.
No prophet like Moses has risen since that day, Face to face with God, leading in His way.
In Egypt's land, he performed every sign, Mighty deeds and wonders, his legacy divine.
Moses’ mighty hand, awesome deeds in sight, A leader unmatched, leading them to light.
Moses is gone, Joshua steps to the line, Yahweh speaks, "It's your time to shine.
"Moses is dead, now rise and lead, Cross the Jordan, fulfill the need.
"Every place your foot will tread, I've given you, just like I said.
"From Lebanon to Euphrates wide, To the Great Sea where the sun slides.
"None can stand, all your days, As with Moses, I'll guide your ways.
"Be strong, be brave, lead this crowd, To the land promised, loud and proud.
"Observe the law, don’t turn aside, In success and prosperity, you'll abide.
"Meditate on this day and night, Keep it close, do what’s right.
"I've commanded, don’t show fear, For Yahweh your God is always near."
Joshua commands, with a voice so clear, "Prepare yourselves, the time is near.
"In three days, the Jordan we’ll cross, Possess the land, gain not loss."
To Reuben, Gad, Manasseh he spoke, "Moses' words, no idle joke.
"Your families stay on this side, But you must cross, with brothers ride.
"Help them rest as you were blessed, Then your land will be possessed."
The people replied, ready to go, "Where you lead, we will follow.
"As we listened to Moses, so to you, May Yahweh be with you in all you do.
"Rebellion will face death's toll, Be strong, be brave, that’s our goal."
Joshua sent his spies from Shittim's place, "Check the land, Jericho, see every face." They slid into Rahab's house to rest, A secret spot, a hidden nest.
The king heard news, his heart in a bind, "Israelite spies? I need them to find!" He sent word to Rahab, "Hand them over, They came here to spy, uncover, discover."
But Rahab was smart, she hid them well, She spun a tale the king couldn't quell, "Men came by, yes, but where they went, I don't know, chase fast, be diligent."
Up on the roof, under flax they laid, While pursuers chased, the gates firmly stayed. She whispered to them under the night, "Yahweh's with you, a fearsome sight."
"We heard of the sea that split so wide, The Amorite kings you cast aside. Our hearts have melted, spirits fled, 'Cause your God rules above our heads."
"Swear to me by Yahweh's might, Show kindness back, protect our light, Save my family, keep us alive, When Jericho falls, let us survive."
"Our life for yours," the spies did vow, "When Yahweh gives us this town, We'll keep our promise, deal true with you, But keep this secret, speak only what's due."
Down by the cord, they slipped through the wall, "Hide in the mountains, 'til pursuers fall." The spies agreed, "Here's what to do, Tie the scarlet thread, make your mark true."
"When we come back, stay in your space, Anyone outside, they're not in a safe place. Keep silent, and we'll hold our word, Tell one soul, and the deal's disturbed."
"Let it be as you have said," she sighed, The scarlet thread in the window tied. Three days passed, hidden from the chase, Then they returned to Joshua's place.
"Yahweh's given us this land," they declared, "The people tremble, their spirits bared." The spies' report, a promise grand, The land was theirs, by God's hand.
Joshua rose at dawn, ready to lead the way, From Shittim to Jordan, where they'd camp and stay.
Three days passed, the officers took their stride, "In sight of God's ark, you'll follow and abide.
Keep your distance, a space you must hold true, This path is new, it's fresh, it's made for you."
Joshua to the crowd, "Sanctify tonight, Tomorrow Yahweh's wonders, a wondrous sight."
To priests, he called out, "Lift the ark, go ahead, Cross before the people, take the path we tread."
Yahweh spoke to Josh, "I'll lift you high, you'll see, With Israel watching, like Moses, you'll be.
Tell the priests at the brink, 'Stand in Jordan's flow,' Watch the waters stop, let the story grow."
Josh gathered Israel, "Hear what God has planned, He'll clear the way, drive enemies from the land.
The living God leads, the ark goes before, Twelve men from the tribes, for what's in store."
"When priestly feet touch Jordan's rolling tide, Waters will halt, the path will open wide."
Tents left behind, the people made their quest, Priests at the water's edge, stood the test.
Water rising high, like a wall so steep, Jordan parted wide, in one mighty heap.
The priests stood firm, dry ground 'neath their feet, Israel crossed over, their victory complete.
When the nation crossed the Jordan, standing tall, Yahweh spoke to Joshua, gave him a call:
"Take twelve men, one from each tribe, And have them lift stones from where the waters divide.
Place them where you camp tonight, A reminder of this powerful sight."
Joshua gathered the chosen twelve, Said, "Step into the river, where the priests dwell.
Each carry a stone on your strong shoulder, A tale to tell when your children get older.
When they ask, 'What’s the story behind these stones?' Tell them how the Jordan's waters turned to bone.
With Yahweh’s ark, the waters did part, And these stones will forever be close to our heart."
The people obeyed and brought stones to the shore, A testament to God's mighty roar.
Joshua placed stones in the river's flow, Where the priests with the ark stood, long ago.
The priests held their ground, their task was clear, Until all God commanded was brought near.
Forty thousand soldiers, armed and ready, Crossed the river, their hearts steady.
On that day, Joshua's name grew great, Feared like Moses, by Israel's state.
Yahweh spoke again, clear as day, "Tell the priests it's time to walk away."
Joshua echoed, "Priests, come forth from the tide," And as they did, the waters returned wide.
Camped in Gilgal, east of Jericho’s gate, The twelve stones stood, their story innate.
Joshua said, "When asked by your kin, 'What do these stones mean?' Let the story begin.
Yahweh dried up Jordan, just like the Red Sea, So the whole world knows, His might you will see.
Remember His power, remember His hand, Fear Yahweh your God, in this promised land."
The kings heard tales, their hearts did quail, No spirit left, their courage frail.
Water dried, the Jordan crossed, Fear filled their souls, a line was tossed.
Yahweh said, "Joshua, grab those knives, Circumcise again, renew their lives."
Joshua moved, with flint in hand, At foreskin hill, he took a stand.
Those who left Egypt, warriors brave, Died in the desert, none to save.
In the wild they roamed, forty years, long and wide, Till the old warriors faded, the promise denied.
Their children rose, a new generation’s birth, Joshua circumcised them, claimed their worth.
When all was done, healing came fast, The camp settled down, pain didn’t last.
Yahweh spoke, "Reproach of Egypt's gone away," Gilgal's the name, a new dawn in display.
In Gilgal’s embrace, they camped, they ate, Passover kept, aligned with fate.
Unleavened bread, grain from the ground, Manna ceased, new food they found.
Joshua near Jericho, eyes lifted high, A man with a sword, ready to try.
"Are you friend or foe?" Joshua asked bold, "Commander of Yahweh, truth's been told."
Joshua bowed low, face to earth, "What does my lord say, what's this worth?"
"Remove your sandals, this ground is holy," Joshua obeyed, approached it slowly.
Jericho's gates were locked up tight, no one's goin' in or out, Israel camped outside those walls, no doubt, God's got a plan, a route.
The Lord told Joshua, "Jericho's yours, with its king and might, March 'round the city for six days, warriors ready to fight."
"Seven priests with trumpets, rams' horns in hand, On the seventh day, seven laps, like planned."
"When you hear that trumpet blast, shout loud with all your soul, And those walls will crumble down, you'll take control."
Joshua called the priests, "Lift the ark, let's move, Seven trumpets lead the way, it's time to groove."
"Advance!" he said, "March 'round, armed and bold, Wait for my command to shout, let the story unfold."
Day by day, they circled once, silent and slow, Until the seventh day, they marched seven times, ready to blow.
When the horns blew long, Joshua yelled, "Shout out loud, For Yahweh's given us this town, let’s make Him proud!"
The city's devoted, all's for Yahweh, except Rahab's crew, She hid our spies, she'll survive, along with her family too.
"Silver and gold, the Lord's treasure they’ll be, But take nothing else, or cursed you will see."
The people roared, the trumpets blared, the walls fell flat, The army charged in, victory in their hat.
They destroyed it all, man and beast alike, Israel took Jericho with power and might.
Joshua sent spies to Rahab's place, as he swore, Saved her and her kin, brought them through the door.
They burned the city, left nothing standing tall, Gold and silver in Yahweh’s house, they took it all.
Rahab lived in Israel, her story's no bluff, For she protected those spies, proved courage enough.
Joshua spoke a curse, "Rebuild Jericho, you'll pay, Firstborn for the foundation, youngest for the gates that day."
So Yahweh was with Joshua, his fame spread wide, Israel knew their leader, with God by his side.
Israel stumbled, broke the rule, took what's devoted, not so cool, Achan grabbed, Yahweh's wrath, burned hot, that's the aftermath.
Joshua sent spies to Ai's gate, "Check it out, don't hesitate." They said, "Just a few thousand will do, no need for everyone to go too."
But three thousand men went, tried to fight, They fled, Ai chased, hearts melted, lost the light.
Joshua tore his clothes, fell to the ground, Dust on heads, elders all around.
He cried, "Lord, why bring us here just to lose, Amorites will hear, how will we choose?
Canaanites will mock, our name erased, What of Your name, what's to be faced?"
Yahweh spoke, "Get up, why on your face? Israel sinned, broken covenant, a disgrace.
Stolen goods hidden, can't stand and fight, Destroy what's taken, make it right.
Sanctify, prepare, tomorrow's the test, Tribes come near, find the one detest.”
Morning came, tribes gathered by, Judah chosen, no need to lie.
Family by family, down to the core, Achan stood guilty, couldn't ignore.
Joshua said, "Tell me, son, your act, Give glory to Yahweh, state the fact."
Achan confessed, "I took the gold, Robe so fine, silver in the fold.
Hidden it lies beneath my tent, Coveted treasures, now I repent."
Messengers ran, found it below, Brought to Joshua, for all to know.
Achan's fate, set in stone, Troubled Israel, now alone.
Stones flew, fire burned, Valley of Achor, lesson learned.
Heap of stones, marks the place, Yahweh's anger, turned from disgrace.
Yahweh said to Josh, "Don't be afraid, don't be dismayed, Take your warriors, rise up, and make Ai afraid.
I've given their king, their city, and land, Do what you did to Jericho, with my command.
Take the goods, the livestock, all for your crew, Set an ambush, that's what you'll do."
Joshua got up, warriors in the night, Thirty thousand men ready to fight.
He told them, "Lie in wait, be tight, When they come out, we'll make it right.
We'll act like we're beat, flee and run, They'll chase us, thinking they've already won.
Then you'll rise, take the city in your hand, Yahweh'll deliver it, as he planned.
Seize the city, set it on fire, Obey His word, fulfill His desire."
Joshua sent the men; they took their place, Between Bethel and Ai, in silence, no trace.
Joshua stayed with the crowd that night, Rose early, ready for the fight.
Encamped on Ai's north side they lay, Five thousand hidden, prepared for the fray.
City's king saw them, rose with pride, With all his men, rushed outside.
Joshua's crew pretended defeat, Fled to the wilderness in quick retreat.
All Ai's men chased, city left bare, No soul behind, none would dare.
Yahweh spoke, "Stretch your javelin high, For I give you Ai, victory's nigh."
Joshua raised his hand, the ambush ran, Into the city, like a well-laid plan.
They set the city ablaze, flames reached the sky, Ai's men turned, but nowhere to fly.
Smoke rose, Israel saw their chance, Turned back, with swords to advance.
Captured Ai's king, ended his reign, Struck down foes, left none to remain.
Joshua's hand stayed firm with might, Till Ai was destroyed, day turned to night.
Livestock, goods, they took as their own, As Yahweh had ordered, it was known.
Ai burned, a heap, a desolate scene, King hanged till sundown, a fate so mean.
Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal, Following Moses' law, he stood tall.
Offered peace, and burnt offerings high, Wrote Moses' law for every eye.
Israel stood, from all around, Before the ark, as blessings abound.
He read the law, blessings and curse, Every word heard, none would disperse.
In front of all, with women and young, Foreigners too, Yahweh's praises sung.
When the kings heard news, they gathered with spite, To fight Joshua, Israel, under one united might. But Gibeon's folk hatched a clever disguise, With old sacks and sandals, they aimed to surprise.
Old wine skins, garments worn and beat, Moldy bread they brought as the trick's deceit. They reached Joshua in Gilgal, with a plea sincere, "We're from a distant land, make a covenant here."
Israel’s men questioned, "Could you be near?" "Who are you? Where from? Make your story clear." "We're from far away, served by Yahweh's fame, He conquered Egypt, and kings in His name."

"Our elders sent us with dry, moldy bread, Our journey was long, shoes and clothes now threadbare," they said. The men of Israel tasted but didn’t ask God’s voice, Joshua made peace, with the covenant their choice.
Three days in, truth was found in disguise, Neighbors, living near, brought a new surprise. Israel reached Gibeon, their cities to see, But couldn’t strike, bound by oath and decree.
The people murmured, but princes stood firm, "We swore by Yahweh, so here’s what we’ll affirm: Let them live, make them wood cutters and drawers, For Yahweh’s house, our covenant's powers."

Joshua called them out, "Why deceive us with lies? You claimed distance, but lived under our skies. Now cursed, you’ll serve, cut wood, fetch water's flow, For my God’s house, this is the task you’ll know."
They confessed, "We feared Yahweh’s mighty decree, He gave Moses the land, to destroy us utterly. In your hands now, do what seems right, We sought just to live, not bring on a fight."
Joshua spared them from Israel’s wrath, Made them servants for Yahweh’s path. That day they became cutters and drawers of water, Bound by the covenant, a new role they sought after.
Yo, listen up, 'bout Adoni-Zedek's fear, Joshua took Ai, made it disappear. Just like he did to Jericho, no doubt, And Gibeon's peace deal made the kings shout.
Gibeon was big, like a royal scene, Greater than Ai, its men were mean. Adoni-Zedek called his crew, Five kings, plotting what they would do.
"Come help me strike Gibeon down, They made peace, don't let them wear the crown." So the kings of the Amorites gathered their might, Set their sights on Gibeon, ready to fight.
Gibeon's men, scared, sent word to Josh, "Don't leave us now, come help us squash, These five kings rising from the hills, Come quick with your mighty skills."
Joshua marched with his crew all night, Ready to fight, ready to fight. And Yahweh said, "Don't fear their band, I've delivered them into your hand."
Joshua struck fast, took them by surprise, Yahweh confused 'em, left 'em in cries. Hailstones rained, more died from the sky, Than by the sword, those Amorites would die.
Then Joshua spoke, "Sun, stand still, Moon, halt in Aijalon, until we kill." The sun paused, the moon delayed, A day like no other, Yahweh's aid displayed.
Five kings fled, hid in a cave, But Joshua found them, none he would save. "Roll stones, guard them tight," Joshua spoke, But first, strike your enemies, make 'em choke.
Joshua's crew finished the fight, Then returned to Makkedah, all was right. "Open the cave, bring out those kings, Put your feet on their necks, see what it brings."
Joshua said, "Don’t fear, be brave and bold, Yahweh fights for us, His power we hold." The kings were struck, hung on trees, Til sunset, then thrown in their stone-made freeze.
Joshua conquered, city by city, With Yahweh's hand, no room for pity. Libnah, Lachish, Eglon fell, Hebron, Debir, Joshua's story to tell.
From Kadesh Barnea to Gaza's gate, Joshua struck, sealing their fate. Yahweh fought, gave them the land, Joshua returned to Gilgal, God's plan was grand.
Jabin heard the news, and he called his crew, Jobab, Shimron, Achshaph's kings, too. North, south, east, west, he rallied the might, Canaanites, Amorites, set for the fight.
Armies like sand, horses, and chariots came, To Merom's waters, they marched without shame. Yahweh spoke to Joshua, "Don't you fear, Tomorrow's their end, I'll make it clear."
Joshua struck at Merom, a sudden attack, With Yahweh's hand, they chased them back. Sidon to Mizpah, they ran them down, No one left standing, took the crown.
Horses hamstrung, chariots aflame, Hazor fell, its king met the same. No soul was spared, no breath remained, Hazor burned, its rule was drained.
Cities captured, kings laid low, Joshua followed Yahweh's flow. Hazor alone felt the fire's embrace, Israel kept cities in their place.
Plunder taken, livestock claimed, Every foe with the sword was named. Joshua did just as Moses said, Left not a single word unread.
He took the land from hill to sea, Goshen, Arabah, and all that be. Kings were struck, put to their rest, With Yahweh's aid, they passed the test.
No city made peace, none dared to plea, Yahweh's plan, hearts hardened, you see. Anakim cut from Israel's soil, Gaza and Gath, their last coil.
Joshua took it all, as promised before, Divided the land, tribes galore. At last, the land had a moment's pause, Israel rested from the wars' harsh laws.
Yo, listen up, these are the kings they faced, Israel's children moved in, took their place.
Beyond the Jordan, where the sun does rise, From Arnon's valley up to Hermon's skies.
Sihon the Amorite, in Heshbon he stayed, Aroer to Jabbok, his border was laid.
Chinneroth eastward, to the Salt Sea's shore, Beth Jeshimoth and Pisgah, they claimed more.
Og of Bashan, a remnant strong and might, In Ashtaroth and Edrei, he'd hold his fight.

Moses, Yahweh’s servant, struck them down, Gave Reubenites, Gadites, half-Manasseh their crown.
Then Joshua led, west of the Jordan's flow, From Baal Gad to Mount Halak, on they'd go.
Hill and lowland, Arabah and south, Hittite, Amorite, they'd clear them out.
Canaanite, Perizzite met their fate, Hivite, Jebusite couldn't escape.
Jericho's king, Ai near Bethel's space, Each king they faced, none could keep their place.
Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth's fall, Lachish, Eglon, Gezer, they took all.

Adullam, Makkedah, Bethel's end, Tappuah, Hepher, the list extends.
Aphek, Lassharon, Madon, Hazor's done, Shimron Meron, Achshaph, one by one.
Taanach, Megiddo, Kedesh, Kings fell, Jokneam of Carmel's story to tell.
Dor and Goiim, Gilgal's power fled, Tirzah, thirty-one kings now lay dead.
Israel's tribes claimed what was theirs by right, United, they stood, in Yahweh's might.
Joshua was old, the years had passed, But land remained, vast and vast.
"You're old," God said, "Yet much remains, Philistine lands, in their domains.
From Shihor near Egypt, north to Ekron, The five Philistine lords upon the dawn.
Canaanite south to Sidonian turf, Amorite borders on this earth.

Sidonians there, in hill country dwell, But I'll drive them out; hear the bell.

Reubenites, Gadites, got their share, Beyond Jordan, eastward, they'd declare.
