A chest by the altar, a hole in the lid, Money flowed in, as the priests bid. The king's scribe and high priest counted it all, To workers' hands, the funds would fall.
Carpenters, builders, they set to restore, Masons, stone cutters, and timber galore. No silver cups or trumpets made, All went to repair, where damages laid.
Faithful they worked, no need for account, Trust in their honesty, a fine amount. Trespass and sin offerings, priests kept aside, Hazael of Syria, to Gath took stride.
Jehoash sent gold, treasures too, To keep Jerusalem safe, his fears did strew. The chronicles hold his story tight, But his end came in the night.
Servants conspired, struck him down, In Millo's house, his life unbound. With fathers he lay, buried with care, Amaziah, his son, the crown would wear.
In the twenty-third year, Joash on Judah's throne, Jehoahaz began his reign, not alone. Seventeen years in Samaria, he stayed, But Jeroboam's sins, he never strayed.
Evil in Yahweh's sight, he did all wrong, God's anger burned hot, it didn't take long. Into Hazael's hand, they fell deep, Syrians oppressed them, made them weep.
Jehoahaz prayed, begged for a plan, Yahweh listened, heard the cry of man. He sent a savior, Israel was free, Back to their tents, like it used to be.
Still, they clung to Jeroboam's sin, Asherah poles, they lingered within. Fifty horsemen left, chariots few, Like dust in threshing, the Syrians slew.
Written are the deeds of Jehoahaz's might, In chronicles of kings, they’re out of sight. He slept with fathers, buried in Samaria ground, Joash took the throne, a new king was crowned.
In Judah’s thirty-seventh year, Joash's son, Jehoash, appeared near. Sixteen years, walked in Jeroboam's sin, The evil ways, he was caught within.
Acts of Joash, battles and fights, Chronicles hold those, under history's lights. He slept with kings, buried in Samaria's land, Jeroboam took the throne, in Israel, he would stand.
Elisha fell sick, Joash by his side, Weeping for the chariots’ ride. Elisha spoke, "Take bow and arrows in hand," King obeyed, followed the command.
"Open the window, shoot east," was the cue, "Yahweh's victory will come through. Strike Syria, victory will shine, Consume them at Aphek, all in due time."
"Strike the ground," Elisha said plain, King struck thrice, but stopped again. "You should've struck more, five or six at least, Now only three times will Syria's power cease."
Elisha passed, buried and gone, Yet his power lived on and on. A dead man thrown, touched his bones, Revived, stood up, life once more his own.
Hazael oppressed, but Yahweh was kind, Covenant with forefathers kept in mind. Benhadad reigned when Hazael died, Jehoash struck cities, three times he tried.
Regained the cities, Israel's pride restored, A tale of kings and battles, in the Lord.
Amaziah steps up to take the reign, Twenty-five young, in Judah's domain.
He did right in Yahweh's sight, But not like David, his light wasn't as bright.
High places remained, incense burned high, Kingdom secure, but he wouldn't let that lie.
Servants who killed his father faced his wrath, But spared the children, followed Moses' path.
Ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, He took Sela, but his pride would halt.
Sent word to Jehoash, "Let's face each other, man," Jehoash replied with a wise man's plan.
"Thistle to cedar, don’t be hasty, stay wise, Enjoy your glory, don’t risk your demise."
Amaziah wouldn't heed, the battle was set, Beth Shemesh met, but Judah's defeat was met.
Jehoash broke walls, took gold and more, Yahweh’s house emptied, he evened the score.
Jehoash laid down, his battles complete, Jeroboam rose up, taking the king's seat.
Amaziah lived on, years passed by, But in Jerusalem, they plotted, he couldn’t fly.
Fled to Lachish, but found no reprieve, Caught and killed, his city left to grieve.
Azariah, young at sixteen, took the throne, Built up Elath, made Judah his own.
Jeroboam in Israel reigned forty-one, Evil deeds carried, from father to son.
Borders restored from Hamath's gate wide, Yahweh's word by Jonah's side.
Israel in pain, bitter and alone, Yahweh saved them, His mercy was shown.
Jeroboam's might in records laid, Passed on, Zechariah the next they made.
In Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year reign, Azariah of Judah took the king's domain. Just sixteen when he took the throne, Reigned fifty-two years, never alone.
In Yahweh's sight, he did what was right, But high places stayed, burning incense at night. Struck by Yahweh, a leper, he lived apart, Jotham his son took over the king's part.
Acts of Azariah, the chronicles tell, He slept with his fathers, his story to dwell. Zechariah in Israel, just six months to rule, Evil in Yahweh's sight, played the same old fool.
Shallum struck Zechariah, took the throne quick, Chronicles hold the story, if you want the pick. Yahweh's word to Jehu, "Fourth generation's reign," Shallum ruled a month, and Menahem brought pain.
Menahem struck Shallum, new king's claim, Acts of Shallum, in chronicles, stay the same. He attacked Tiphsah, left no stone unturned, Reigned ten years, and evil he learned.
Pul from Assyria came with might, Menahem's silver made his kingdom tight. He taxed the wealthy, paid the Assyrian king, And Pul turned away, didn't do a thing.
Menahem's deeds, in chronicles they lie, He slept with his fathers, his time went by. Pekahiah, his son, took the reigns for a time, Evil like Jeroboam, walked the same line.
Pekah conspired, with fifty men strong, Killed Pekahiah, reign didn't last long. Chronicles hold Pekahiah's tale, Pekah took over, his rule set sail.
Twenty years for Pekah, in Israel's land, Evil in Yahweh's eyes, sin at hand. Tiglath Pileser took cities away, Carried captives to Assyria, in a dark day.
Hoshea struck Pekah, took the throne's space, Jotham began his reign in Judah's place. He did what's right, like his father before, High places stayed, incense burned more.
Acts of Jotham, the chronicles display, Rezin and Pekah came Judah's way. Jotham slept with his fathers, his rule did cease, And Ahaz his son took the throne in peace.
In the seventeenth year of trouble and fame, Ahaz the young king of Judah came to reign.
Just twenty years old, sixteen years he'd rule, But in God's eyes, he played the fool.
Walked in Israel's kings' old ways, Made his son pass through the fires ablaze.
Sacrificed on hills, incense burned high, Under green trees reaching for the sky.
Rezin of Syria and Pekah from Israel, Besieged his city but couldn't make him fail.
Rezin took Elath, drove the Jews away, Syrians there lived to this very day.
Ahaz sent word to Assyria's land, "I'm your servant, need a helping hand."
Silver and gold from the temple he sent, To Tiglath Pileser, a desperate present.
The Assyrian king listened well, Took Damascus, Rezin fell.
Ahaz traveled, saw an altar grand, Sent plans to Urijah with a command.
Urijah built it, just like the design, For when the king returned, it was time.
The king approached, offerings ablaze, Burnt, meal, drink, in a ritual haze.
Bronze altar moved to the side, North of his altar, a prideful stride.
"Burn on the great altar," the king did say, All offerings, blood, all in one display.
Urijah obeyed, did what was planned, Ahaz's words, his direct command.
Bases cut, the basin removed, The sea on stone, his power proved.
Covered way and entry changed for gain, To please Assyria, Ahaz did reign.
His acts recorded in the chronicles' line, Then he slept with fathers, his time to resign.
Hezekiah his son, the throne did grace, Ahaz's reign, in history's embrace.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz's reign, Hoshea took the stage, Ruling Israel from Samaria, in a nine-year engage.
He did evil in God's sight, not as bad as before, Yet still, Shalmaneser came knocking at his door.
Hoshea bowed to Assyria, paying tribute as the norm, But when he conspired with Egypt, it brought on a storm.
The Assyrian king found out and threw Hoshea in chains, Marched through the land, to Samaria he came.
Three years of siege, till Samaria was taken, Israel led to Assyria, a new path forsaken.
Why? God had freed them from Pharaoh’s cruel hand, But they feared other gods, forgot His command.
Built high places in secret, from watchtower to town, Pillars and Asherah poles, defying God’s crown.
They burned incense, served idols, made God frown, Yahweh said, “You shall not do this,” but they did it anyhow.
Prophets warned them, “Turn back, keep the law,” But they hardened their necks, ignored what they saw.
Rejected His covenant, followed the crowd, Made idols, served Baal, ways of sin they allowed.
Sacrificed sons and daughters, provoked God’s wrath, So He removed Israel, left Judah on a narrow path.
Judah too strayed, didn’t heed God’s way, Yahweh afflicted them, cast them away.
Carried off by Assyria, new folks took their place, They didn’t know Yahweh, lions set the pace.
They called on a priest to teach God’s law, But each nation, their own gods they still saw.
They feared Yahweh, yet served idols in stride, Passed down from fathers, a divided pride.
God said, “Fear Me, remember the covenant made, Don’t bow to others, let My commands be obeyed.”
Yet they did as before, mixed worship and sin, Fear of Yahweh and idols, from father to kin.
In the third year of Hoshea, a new king's tale begins, Hezekiah of Judah, where righteousness wins. At twenty-five he rose, reigned in Jerusalem bold, For twenty-nine years, this story's told.
He did right in Yahweh's sight, like David before, Tearing down altars, idols, and more. Broke the serpent of bronze, turned it to dust, Called it Nehushtan, for in God he did trust.
He held fast to Yahweh, never turned aside, Among Judah's kings, none could match his stride. Yahweh was with him, success in his hand, He rebelled against Assyria, taking a stand.
Struck Philistines down, from tower to city walls, In his fourth year, Samaria falls. Assyria took Israel, scattered them wide, For they broke God's covenant, turned aside.
In Hezekiah's fourteenth year, the tension peak, Sennacherib of Assyria, Judah he seeks. Hezekiah reached out, said, "I’ll bear the load," Paid gold and silver, down a heavy road.
But Assyria sent Rabshakeh with words to declare, "Who do you trust, that you dare not despair? Don't lean on Egypt, a reed that will pierce, Or on Yahweh, whom Hezekiah has dismissed."
"Give pledges, I'll grant you horses to ride, Yet can you face even one captain with pride? Yahweh told me, 'Destroy this land,' so I came, To break you down, to make my name."
The people stayed silent, obeyed the king's call, Hezekiah's men returned, their clothes did fall. They told the king of Rabshakeh's loud boast, But Hezekiah trusted Yahweh, more than most.
Hezekiah heard the news, tore his robe, and cried, In sackcloth he went where Yahweh resides.
Sent Eliakim, Shebna, elders to Isaiah's dome, Covered in sackcloth, seeking a word from home.
"Hezekiah says, 'Trouble’s here, no strength to give birth, Maybe Yahweh heard the blasphemer's mirth.
Lift up your prayers for the remnant still here.'" So they went to Isaiah, with hearts full of fear.
Isaiah replied, "Tell your king this from Yahweh, 'Don't fear the Assyrian words that sway.
I'll put a spirit in him, news he'll hear, Back to his land, by the sword, he'll disappear.'"
Rabshakeh found the king at Libnah, in fight, He heard Ethiopia came with might.
Sent word to Hezekiah, "Don't be deceived, Jerusalem’s fall is what we’ve achieved.
The gods of the nations fell one by one, Will yours be different when we're done?"
Hezekiah read the letter, laid it before the Lord, Prayed for deliverance from the Assyrian horde.
"Yahweh, you're the God enthroned above, Creator of heaven and earth, show your love.
Hear Sennacherib's words, defying your name, Save us, so all know you're the same."
Yahweh spoke through Isaiah, a message so clear, "Sennacherib’s pride, I’ve heard, and his sneer.
Zion despises, shakes her head at you, You've defied the Holy One in all you do.
I’ll turn you back, put my hook in your nose, The way that you came, that’s how it goes."
A sign for Hezekiah, that year’s yield will grow, And Judah’s remnant will again flow.
Assyria won't breach, not a single arrow fly, "I’ll defend this city," Yahweh's reply.
That night, Yahweh's angel struck with might, 185,000 fell in a single night.
Sennacherib retreated, back to Nineveh he fled, In his own temple, by his sons, he bled.
Esarhaddon reigned, as the story shifts, In Yahweh’s power, Jerusalem lifts.
Hezekiah was sick, lying in bed, Isaiah came with words that filled with dread.
"Yahweh says, 'Get your house in line, Your time is up, end of the line.'"
Hezekiah turned, face to the wall, Prayed to Yahweh, in tears he'd fall.
"Remember how I've walked with you, In truth and heart, I've been true."
Bitter tears flowed as he spoke, But Yahweh's word to Isaiah broke.
"Tell Hezekiah, I've heard his plea, I've seen his tears, now listen to Me.
I'll heal, on the third day rise, Fifteen more years, a gift to your eyes.
Assyria's threat, I'll push away, For My sake and David's, this city's okay."
Isaiah then said, "Bring the figs here," On the boil they laid, recovery near.
Hezekiah asked, "What sign will be, That Yahweh will heal and I'll be free?"
Isaiah responded, "Shadow's the sign, Forward ten steps, or back in time?"
Hezekiah chose, "Backward it should sway, Let the shadow move the opposite way."
Isaiah called out, Yahweh did align, Shadow stepped back, a miracle in time.
Babylon’s king sent gifts and cheer, Hezekiah healed, they came to hear.
Hezekiah showed all his prized delight, Nothing in his palace stayed out of sight.
Isaiah asked, "What did they see?" Hezekiah said, "All, nothing hid from me."
Isaiah warned of days coming near, All taken to Babylon, nothing left here.
"Your sons will serve in Babylon's hall," Hezekiah accepted, seeing peace for all.
Acts of Hezekiah, written in the book, He slept with his fathers, Manasseh took.
Manasseh was twelve when he took the throne, Fifty-five years he reigned, but not alone. He did evil in Yahweh’s sight, Rebuilt high places, brought darkness, no light.
He raised Baal altars, Asherah the same, Worshiped the skies, all in Yahweh’s name. In Yahweh's house, altars he made, “Jerusalem's mine,” Yahweh had once said.
Through fire his son passed, sorcery he sought, Spoke with spirits, wizards he brought. Engraved image of Asherah he placed, In the house Yahweh chose, His name erased.
Yahweh warned, but they wouldn't heed, Manasseh's influence, evil's seed. Prophets spoke, Yahweh's voice clear, “For his abominations, judgment is near.
Evil so great, ears will ring, Jerusalem wiped clean, no king. Remnant cast off, enemies will seize, For provoking My wrath, won't find peace.”
Blood flowed innocent, streets ran red, Manasseh's sins piled high, dread. When he passed, his deeds were known, A book of kings, where they're shown.
Amon, his son, two years he'd reign, Like his father, evil again. Idols he served, Yahweh he spurned, In his own house, betrayed and burned.
People rose up, avenged their king, Josiah crowned, a new hope to bring. In the garden, Amon lay, Josiah reigned, a brighter day.
Josiah was just eight, when he took his seat, Reigned in Jerusalem, made his rule complete. His mother Jedidah, her name we relate, From Bozkath she came, Adaiah's fate.
Did right in Yahweh's sight, walked David's line, Left or right, he didn't stray, stayed in the right design. Eighteenth year, he sent Shaphan, wise and fast, "Go to Yahweh's house, set the task."
"Count up the money the keepers took, Deliver to workmen, to repair the book. Give to the carpenters, builders, and stone, Faithful they work, let no fault be shown."
Hilkiah the priest to Shaphan did say, "Found the law's book, in Yahweh's way." Shaphan to the king brought the word, About money handled, and the book he heard.
When the king heard, he tore his robe, Deep was his sorrow, his heart probe. He sent for Hilkiah, Ahikam, and more, "Seek Yahweh's word, what’s in store?"
Great is the wrath, it's kindled high, For our fathers' deafness to this cry. To Huldah the prophetess, they went to hear, In the second quarter, her home was near.
"Yahweh says, 'Tell the man who sent, Evil will come, anger won’t relent. They’ve forsaken me, incense to others burned, Wrath will not quench, it’s what they've earned.'"
"But to Judah's king, who sent for divine, Yahweh says, 'For your humble sign, Your heart was tender, tears and torn clothes, I’ve heard your cries, Yahweh knows.'"
"In peace you'll rest, no evil to see, Gathered to your fathers, in calm you'll be." Message delivered, the king heard it plain, Peace was promised, amidst the pain.
The king sent word, all elders came near, Judah and Jerusalem gathered to hear.
In Yahweh's house, the king took his stand, With priests and prophets and people at hand.
He read aloud the covenant's code, The words from Yahweh's house, in their abode.
By the pillar, the king took a vow, "To walk with Yahweh in heart and soul now."
The people agreed, the covenant sealed, A promise to keep what was revealed.
"Bring out the vessels made for Baal," The king commanded, removing them all.
Burned them outside in Kidron's field, To Bethel the ashes, forever sealed.
Idolatrous priests, he cast aside, Judah's high places, now denied.
He crushed the altars, beat them to dust, A cleansing act, deemed fair and just.
The Asherah poles, he broke them too, On common graves, the dust he threw.
From Geba to Beersheba's stretch, He tore down high places, those of wretch.
Topheth defiled, no child would face, The fire of Molech, erased with haste.
The sun’s horses he took away, Chariots of fire burned that day.
Altars of Ahaz, broken and gone, Manasseh's works to dust were drawn.
Solomon's places, where idols were praised, Smashed and scattered, no trace erased.
At Bethel's high place, his anger burned, Tombs were opened, bones overturned.
"What’s this monument I see?" he inquired, "Prophet's grave," the people replied, inspired.
"Let him rest," Josiah decreed, Bones untouched, his legacy freed.
Samaria's places, he did dethrone, Priests and altars, all overthrown.
"Keep the Passover," the king declared, A celebration, none compared.
No spirit or wizard, none would remain, Josiah purged them, cleansing the land's stain.
A king like no other, heart full and true, In God’s eyes, his deeds shone through.
Yet Yahweh’s wrath wouldn't relent, For Judah’s sins, his anger still sent.
"I’ll cast off Judah, my chosen site, Just as Israel, removed from my sight."
Josiah's acts, written in the scroll, A life recorded, in chronicles whole.
Pharaoh Necoh rose, Josiah opposed, At Megiddo's field, his life was closed.
Carried by servants, in a chariot of death, To Jerusalem, he took his last breath.
Jehoahaz reigned, but only three months’ span, Did evil in Yahweh’s sight, like his clan.
Bound by Necoh, a tribute laid bare, Silver and gold, a burden to bear.
Eliakim, renamed Jehoiakim's reign, In Judah he ruled, under Egypt's chain.
Like those before, evil he did, According to the deeds his fathers hid.
Nebuchadnezzar came, Babylon's might, Jehoiakim served three years, then took flight in the night.
Yahweh sent bands—Chaldeans, Syrians too, Moabites, Ammonites, came for Judah's undo.
It was Yahweh's command, Judah's time was done, Manasseh's sins, innocent blood—Judah's spirit overrun.
Jehoiakim passed, laid with his kin, Jehoiachin rose, a new reign to begin.
Egypt's king stayed put, Babylon owned the land, From Egypt's brook to Euphrates, all under his hand.
Jehoiachin at eighteen took the throne, Three months he reigned, but evil was sown.
Nebuchadnezzar's servants came, city under siege, The king himself arrived, fulfilling the league.
Jehoiachin went out, mother, servants, and all, Captured by Babylon, Judah's king did fall.
Treasures taken, Yahweh's house stripped bare, Solomon's gold vessels, gone without a care.
Jerusalem's elite, ten thousand captives bound, Craftsmen and smiths, none left to surround.
To Babylon they went, from Jerusalem's heart, Jehoiachin, his kin, from the land did depart.
Nebuchadnezzar set Mattaniah on the throne, Zedekiah his name, a king yet unknown.
Zedekiah at twenty-one, reigned eleven years long, But Yahweh's sight, evil remained strong.
Judah's fate, Yahweh's anger cast them out, Zedekiah's rebellion, Babylon's clout.
In the ninth year, tenth month, tenth day, Nebuchadnezzar and his army made their way, Jerusalem surrounded, forts all around, Until the eleventh year, the city was bound.
By the ninth day of month four, famine hit hard, No bread left, the situation was scarred. A breach in the city, warriors slipped through, By night, through the garden, the king went too.
But on Jericho's plains, the Chaldeans closed in, The king captured, his army lost in the wind. To Riblah, Zedekiah was brought, His sons slain, his sight lost, Babylon caught.
Fifth month, seventh day, Nebuzaradan came, Jerusalem burned, in fire and flame. Houses great and small, Yahweh's house too, Walls broken down by the Chaldean crew.
The people taken captive, the rest left behind, To work the fields, the poorest resigned. Bronze pillars shattered, vessels taken away, Gold and silver, carried without delay.
Seraiah, Zephaniah, chiefs in the fray, Taken to Riblah, where judgment held sway. Sixty men of the city, all brought near, In Hamath they died, Judah shed tears.
Gedaliah made governor, but fear stayed strong, Ishmael struck him down, it didn’t take long. To Egypt fled the people, great and small, Afraid of the Chaldeans, fearing the fall.
In the thirty-seventh year, Jehoiachin’s fate, Evilmerodach lifted him from prison’s gate. Spoke kindly, gave him a throne high, Changed his garments, bread supply.
Daily allowance, for the rest of his days, A king redeemed, in Babylon he stays. Judah's tale, of exile and pain, Of kings fallen, and the Babylonian reign.
Listen up, gather 'round, here's the family line, From Adam to Abraham, let's keep it in rhyme.
Adam had Seth, then came Enosh and Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, and Lamech in the plan.
Noah came next with sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Japheth's sons Gomer, Magog, and Tubal, no less.
Gomer had Ashkenaz, Diphath, Togarmah, Javan’s kids were Elishah, Kittim, and Rodanim’s drama.
Ham had Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan, Cush's son Nimrod became mighty in the land.
Mizraim begot Ludim and Anamim, Philistines from Casluhim, oh, what a scene!
Canaan fathered Sidon, Heth, and more, Jebusites, Amorites, they all came before.
Shem had Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram, Arpachshad's line led to Eber and Peleg, oh man!
Eber had Peleg, earth's division, that's key, Joktan his brother, with sons like Sheba, you see.
Shem's line goes on, leading to Abraham, Isaac and Ishmael, his sons in the clan.
Ishmael's sons: Nebaioth, Kedar, Mibsam, Adbeel, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, it ran.
Abraham’s concubine Keturah bore Zimran, Medan, Their line branched to Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah, understand?
Isaac fathered Esau and Israel, Esau had Eliphaz, Reuel, and a tale to tell.
Eliphaz’s sons: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Kenaz, Reuel begot Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, like jazz.
Kings of Edom reigned before Israel's day, Bela, Jobab, Husham, Hadad, they held sway.
Kings came and went, each in their place, Till Hadad reigned last, then Edom’s chiefs took space.
Chiefs Timna, Aliah, Jetheth, and more, Leading Edom’s tribes in the days of yore.
The family tree spans wide and deep, From Adam to nations, this history we keep.
Israel's sons, a legendary crew, Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah too.
Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, and Joe, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, in the flow.
Judah's boys, Er, Onan, Shelah three, Born of Shua's daughter, Canaan's decree.
Er was wicked, God took him down, Tamar bore Perez, Zerah, in Judah's town.
Perez had Hezron and Hamul in line, Zerah's five were Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara, all fine.
Carmi's son Achar, a trouble did make, Ethan's son Azariah, for righteousness' sake.
Hezron's sons Jerahmeel, Ram, Chelubai, Ram fathered Amminadab, prince in the sky.
Amminadab to Nahshon, Nahshon to Salma, Salma to Boaz, who knew Ruth like a drama.
Boaz to Obed, Obed to Jess, Jess to Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, no less.
Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem, and lastly Dave, Zeruiah and Abigail, sisters brave.
Zeruiah birthed Abishai, Joab, Asahel, Abigail bore Amasa, his tale they would tell.
Caleb's line through Azubah, Jesher, Shobab, Ardon, When Azubah passed, he married Ephrath, Hur was born.
Hur to Uri, then Bezalel came, Hezron's adventures, his age had no claim.
Machir's daughter bore Segub, a Gilead affair, Jair with his cities, land of Gilead, rare.
Caleb's territory in Ephrath, Hezron's rest, Abijah bore Ashhur, Tekoa's manifest.
Jerahmeel's sons, Ram and Bunah's flair, Oren, Ozem, Ahijah, a family rare.
Ram's sons Maaz, Jamin, Eker, line's run, Onam's Shammai and Jada, dynastic fun.
Shammai's line, Nadab, Abishur takes, Abishur's wife Abihail, Ahban and Molid make.
Nadab's Seled and Appaim, Seled bore none, Appaim to Ishi, Sheshan, Ahlai, the sun.
Jada's sons Jether, Jonathan live, Jether died childless, Jonathan had Peleth and Zaza to give.
Sheshan had no sons, gave a daughter to Jarha, Jarha to Attai, and the line would go far.
Attai to Nathan, Zabad then, From Zabad to Ephlal, Obed again.
Obed to Jehu, then Azariah, To Helez and Eleasah, Sismai in the choir.
Sismai to Shallum, Jekamiah then, Elishama's name completes the men.
Caleb's sons Mesha, Ziph the sire, Hebron's sons Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, Shema, take you higher.
Shema to Raham, Jorkeam where they're from, Rekem to Shammai, Maon and Beth Zur hum.
Caleb's concubines, Ephah bore Haran, Moza, Gazez, and Jahdai's clan.
Jahdai's Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, Shaaph, Maacah’s tale to set.
Maacah bore Sheber, Tirhanah's line, Shaaph of Madmannah, Sheva, Machbena, Gibea in time.
Caleb’s daughter Achsah, more tales unfold, Shobal, Kiriath Jearim, Salma, Beth Gader told.
Kiriath Jearim's sons were many, Haroeh, Menuhoth, not just any.
Families of the scribes at Jabez, Kenites from Hammath, Rechab's house impress.
David's sons were born in Hebron, a grand sight, Amnon first, then Daniel, their future was bright.
Absalom came third, Maacah's prideful heir, Adonijah fourth, Haggith's child with flair.
Shephatiah fifth, Abital's delight, Ithream sixth, by Eglah, shining light.
Six sons in Hebron, where David's throne lay, Seven years and six months, he ruled day by day.
In Jerusalem, his dynasty grew, Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon too.
Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet came next, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, the family complexed.
Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet again, Sons of David, the legacy they extend.
Tamar, their sister, in the royal line, While Solomon's seed would rise and shine.
Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa, in line, Jehoshaphat, Joram, their futures entwine.
Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah in place, Azariah, Jotham, each took their space.
Ahaz and Hezekiah, Manasseh's reign, Amon, then Josiah, continued the chain.
Josiah's sons, Johanan to start, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, Shallum took part.
Jehoiakim's children, Jeconiah, Zedekiah next, Jeconiah the captive, with history vexed.
Shealtiel his first, Malchiram, more came, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah by name.
Hoshama, Nedabiah, sons in their prime, Pedaiah fathered Zerubbabel, Shimei in time.
Zerubbabel's line, Meshullam, Hananiah the claim, Shelomith their sister, in their family's name.
Hashubah, Ohel, five sons, they grew, Berechiah, Hasadiah, Jushab Hesed too.
Hananiah's sons, Pelatiah, Jeshaiah's line, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, Shecaniah in kind.
Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah's feat, Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, Shaphat repeat.
Neariah's three, Elioenai, Hizkiah, Azrikam's plan, Elioenai's seven, Hodaviah, Eliashib in the clan.
Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan in the fold, Delaiah and Anani, their stories told.
Judah's line: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, Shobal, Shobal's boy Reaiah had sons, Jahath in the hall. Jahath begat Ahumai and Lahad, that's their fate, Families of the Zorathites, they relate.

In Etam, the sons were Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, you see, Their sister was Hazzelelponi, quite the family. Penuel fathered Gedor, Ezer fathered Hushah for more, Sons of Hur, Ephrathah's first, Bethlehem's core.

Ashhur of Tekoa, two wives, Helah and Naarah in life, Naarah bore Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari, no strife. Helah brought forth Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan, Hakkoz begat Anub, Zobebah, and Aharhel's clan.

Jabez outdid his brothers, his name came from pain, Called to God of Israel, blessings he'd gain: "Oh, bless me indeed, enlarge my border wide, Keep me from evil, in you I confide." God granted his prayer, his borders increased, His life was blessed, from worry released.
Chelub fathered Mehir, who fathered Eshton, Eshton begat Beth Rapha, Paseah, Tehinnah’s son. The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah, no doubt, Othniel's son was Hathath, their names we shout.

Caleb’s sons, Jephunneh's pride: Iru, Elah, Naam, Elah’s son, Kenaz, joined the family jam. Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, Asarel, While Ezrah’s sons were Jether, Mered, Epher, Jalon — they dwell.

Mered’s wife bore Jered, Heber, Jekuthiel in her day, The sons of Pharaoh’s daughter, Bithiah, along the way. Hodiah’s wife’s sons fathered Keilah Garmite, Eshtemoa Maacathite, Shimon’s sons, Ishi's too, their names in the light.
Shelah’s sons, Judah's posterity: Er of Lecah's name, Laadah of Mareshah, from linen workers came. Jokim, men of Cozeba, Joash, Saraph, once ruled, These records are ancient, their lineages schooled.

Simeon's sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul's kin, Shallum, Mibsam, Mishma, lineages within. Mishma's sons were Hammuel, then Zaccur and Shimei, Shimei’s offspring many, unlike his brothers’ way.

They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazarshual’s land, In Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad, their cities they planned. In Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag, they spread their fame, Till David’s reign, their cities bore their name.
Villages of Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, Ashan, five wide, To Baal, their settlements, genealogies as their guide. Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah of Amaziah’s line, Joel, Jehu of Joshibiah, lineage so fine.

Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, listed in show, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah, and Ziza to grow. Princes in their families, their father's house grew, To Gedor's entrance, east valley, their flocks pursued.

In Hezekiah's days, they struck, Meunim's land they took, Destroyed utterly, for the flock's sake, they shook. Simeon’s five hundred reached Mount Seir, in might, Led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, Uzziel’s sight.
They struck the Amalekites, remnants disappeared, In Seir, they settled, in history endeared.
Reuben's sons, Israel's firstborn line, Lost their birthright, Joseph's time to shine. Judah led, his brothers praised, But Joseph's place, the birthright stayed.
Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, Carmi there, Joel's sons, a lineage to declare. Shemaiah, Gog, Shimei, and more, Micah, Reaiah, Baal to explore.
Beerah, the prince, by Assyria taken, Reubenite chief, his lineage shaken. Jeiel and Zechariah, listed in the lore, Bela of Azaz, they roamed Gilead's shore.
To Bashan's land, Gad's sons came, Joel, Shapham, and others in name. Michael, Meshullam, Sheba in line, Seven sons, Abihail's family sign.
In pastures of Sharon, they spread wide, Listed in Jotham and Jeroboam's pride. Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh stand, Forty-four thousand, warriors of the land.
War with the Hagrites, Jetur and Nodab, Helped by God, their victory nabbed. Livestock taken, camels and sheep, God answered their cry, faith to keep.
Manasseh's sons, from Bashan they grew, Epher and Ishi, warriors true. Yet they turned from God, idols in hand, Trespassed and lost, by Assyria's command.
God stirred Pul, Assyria's might, Reubenites, Gadites, all in flight. Taken to Halah, Habor's flow, Their fate sealed, in exile they go.
Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari, Kohath's line: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel, a grand story.
Amram’s kids: Aaron, Moses, Miriam, they lead, Aaron's sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, Ithamar's seed.
Eleazar fathered Phinehas, who fathered Abishua, Then came Bukki, Uzzi, and Zerahiah, for sure.
Zerahiah begot Meraioth, who had Amariah to raise, Amariah fathered Ahitub, Zadok the priest in those days.
Zadok birthed Ahimaaz, who fathered Azariah, Azariah to Johanan, building the Messiah.
On and on, the line continues, priests in the holy place, Solomon's temple, where they served, each in their grace.
Aaron’s line offered sacrifices, smoke rose high, “Keep the holy fire burning,” God’s command they supply.
David set them over music, songs of praise they’d sing, In the house of Yahweh, their voices would ring.
Given cities with pasture lands, for the tribes to share, To Kohath, Gershom, Merari — fair and square.
The story of Levi’s sons, serving in their line, Faithful in their duties, holding priestly design.
In captivity, Jehozadak, carried by Babylon's hand, But still, the Levites’ legacy in Yahweh’s land would stand.
Issachar’s sons roll out, four strong as they soar, Tola, Puah, Jashub, Shimron, warriors galore. Tola's boys, mighty men in every generation, Twenty-two thousand six hundred, David's foundation.
Uzzi’s boy Izrahiah, five chiefs in line, Michael, Obadiah, Joel, Isshiah, they shine. With thirty-six thousand, ready for war, Brothers in valor, eighty-seven thousand, more.
Benjamin's sons—Bela, Becher, Jediael—three, Bela's sons, five leaders, valorous as can be. Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, Iri stand tall, Twenty-two thousand thirty-four, they heed the call.
Becher's sons count nine, heads of their clan, Zemirah to Alemeth, each a mighty man. Genealogy listed, twenty thousand strong, Ready for battle, where they belong.
Jediael's next, with sons to the brim, Bilhan's boys—Jeush, Benjamin, and kin. Seventeen thousand two hundred, fit for the fight, Shuppim, Huppim, Ir, Hushim, ready day and night.
Naphtali's sons—Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, Shallum's line, Through Bilhah they descend, warriors who shine. Manasseh's sons, Asriel leads the path, Machir’s kin, Gilead’s aftermath.
Machir wed into Huppim, family ties tight, Zelophehad's daughters, a unique sight. Peresh and Sheresh, born to Maacah’s side, Ulam and Rakem, the family's pride.
Ephraim’s clan, Shuthelah and heirs, But tragedy came, as the men of Gath dared. Ephraim mourned, comfort from his kin, Named his son Beriah, trouble within.
Sheerah, Ephraim's daughter, builder of lands, Beth Horon and Uzzen, built by her hands. Line after line, through generations they go, Joshua at the end, his legacy aglow.
Asher’s sons, Imnah, Ishvah, they lead, Followed by Ishvi and Beriah, they succeed. Twenty-six thousand strong, for service in war, Mighty men of valor, Asher's pride in store.
Benjamin's line, let’s start the scene, Bela the first, then Ashbel, Aharah in between. Nohah came fourth, Rapha was fifth, Bela's sons, this is the list.
Addar and Gera, Abihud too, Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah crew. Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram in sight, Ehud's sons, leading with might.
Captured in Geba, to Manahath they went, Naaman, Ahijah, Gera, on mission bent. Gera fathered Uzza and Ahihud, From Moab, Shaharaim understood.
Hushim and Baara, wives sent away, By Hodesh, more sons came to play. Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, Jeuz, Shachia, Mirmah’s calm.
By Hushim, Abitub and Elpaal shine, Elpaal's sons built Ono in line. Eber, Misham, Shemed, builders of towns, Beriah, Shema, in Aijalon they crowned.
Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth they rolled, Zebadiah, Arad, Eder, bold. Michael, Ishpah, Joha, sons of Beriah, Zebadiah, Meshullam, down to Heberia.
Ishmerai, Izliah, Jobab renowned, Elpaal's sons, their roots are profound. Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi, they claimed, Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel named.
Adaiah, Beraiah, Shimrath, from Shimei’s side, Ishpan, Eber, Eliel, in line they bide. Abdon, Zichri, Hanan, they knew, Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah too.
Iphdeiah, Penuel, from Shashak's line, Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah in time. Jaareshiah, Elijah, Zichri, Jeroham's sons, Chief men, in Jerusalem, their story runs.
Gibeon's father, Maacah his wife, In Gibeon they settled, living life. Abdon, Zur, Kish, and Baal, Nadab, Gedor, their story's a tale.
Ahio and Zecher, together they roamed, Mikloth fathered Shimeah, near home they homed. Ner fathered Kish, who fathered Saul, Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab stood tall.
Merib Baal, Jonathan's line, Micah's father, through time they shine. Pithon, Melech, Tarea, Ahaz, With Jehoaddah continuing the jazz.
Alemeth, Azmaveth, Zimri came next, Moza, Binea, in family text. Raphah, Eleasah, Azel his kin, Azel's six sons, where stories begin.
Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael’s might, Sheariah, Obadiah, Hanan's light. Ulam's sons, archers of renown, Mighty men of valor, Benjamin's crown.
Israel's tale, written down in the king's own books, Judah's captive to Babylon for disobedient looks.
First to settle back, in their own land they reside, Israel, priests, Levites, temple servants by their side.
In Jerusalem, children of Judah took their place, Benjamin, Ephraim, Manasseh joined the race.
Uthai, Asaiah, sons of Perez, they stood tall, Jeuel and brothers, six hundred ninety in all.
Benjamin's kin, Sallu and crew, they had the claim, Nine hundred fifty-six, heads of households they became.
Priests like Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin, bold, Azariah, Adaiah, in God's house they took hold.
Heads of houses, one thousand seven sixty they were, Able men serving in God's house without a slur.
Levites came forth, Shemaiah led the line, With Bakbakkar, Heresh, in service, they did shine.
Gatekeepers like Shallum, at the king's gate they'd stand, Over camp, keepers of entry, they had the command.
Zechariah, Phinehas, in times past they ruled, With Yahweh's presence, their leadership fueled.
Two hundred twelve, chosen to guard and to serve, Every seven days, their posts they wouldn't swerve.
Four chief gatekeepers, Levites with trust in hand, Over rooms, over treasuries, in God's house they'd stand.
In charge of vessels, by count they'd take and give, Some over furniture, spices, by faith they lived.
Mattithiah baked, Kohathites showed the bread, Singers of the Levites, in their rooms they spread.
Jeiel in Gibeon with his family close by, Saul's line through Kish, in that lineage lies.
Father of Jonathan, Saul's legacy strong, Micah and sons, in the family throng.
Generations recorded, Azel's six sons named, Their stories, their legacy, in history acclaimed.
The Philistines charged, Israel took flight, On Mount Gilboa, they fell in the night.
Chased after Saul, his sons in the fray, Jonathan, Abinadab, Malchishua lay.
The battle was fierce, the arrows flew, Saul felt the pain, he knew what to do.
"Draw your sword," was Saul's grave request, But fear stopped his bearer, couldn't protest.
With his own blade, Saul took his fall, His bearer followed, ended it all.
Saul and sons, all in one breath, Together they faced the shadow of death.
Israel saw, and they left their land, Philistines moved in, took command.
Next day they stripped the slain in pride, Saul and sons on the mountain side.
Armor to idols, head to Dagon’s place, Philistines spread news, a victorious case.
Jabesh Gilead heard of the shame, Valiant men rose to reclaim the name.
Took the bones, buried them deep, Under an oak, their memory to keep.
Saul fell for not heeding divine word, For seeking spirits when Yahweh he spurned.
So Yahweh judged, David was crowned, The son of Jesse, new king renowned.
Israel's gathered, speaking bold and clear, To David in Hebron, "We're your kin, we're near. Even with Saul, you led us, we recall, God said, 'You'll shepherd, be the prince of all.'"
Elders met David, a covenant they made, Anointed him king, with Yahweh's word conveyed. To Jerusalem, they marched with a plan, Jebusites defied, but David, he ran.
"Who strikes first?" David asked, to claim the fame, Joab answered swift, earned the captain's name. In Zion, David lived, the city bore his name, Built it up strong, Joab did the same.
David grew greater, for Yahweh was his guide, With mighty men and Israel by his side. Jashobeam, chief, with spear he did thrill, Three hundred men he courageously killed.
Eleazar stood with David, ground to defend, Philistines were beaten, victory in the end. Three mighty went down to the cave by night, Philistine army surrounded, ready to fight.

David longed for water from Bethlehem's well, Three broke through, but he wouldn't drink, you can tell. Poured it out to Yahweh, for their sacrifice, Said, "I can't drink blood, they've risked their lives."
Abishai's spear took three hundred down, Honored among the three, known in town. Benaiah, bold, in a pit with a lion, Killed an Egyptian, with courage he's flyin'.
More honorable than thirty, his name they did hail, David set him guard, his loyalty couldn't fail. List of mighty men goes long and wide, With names like Asahel and Elhanan with pride.
Joab's brother, Elhanan, and more, These were the warriors, ready for war. From Asahel to Jaasiel, mighty and bold, David's army fierce, the tales are told.
David's in Ziklag, on the run, on the mend, Hiding from Saul, but with strong men to defend.
They're brothers with bows, ambidextrous might, Flinging stones, shooting arrows, ready for a fight.
Ahiezer, Joash, from Gibeah's land, Jeziel, Pelet, fierce, with weapons in hand.
Ishmaiah the leader, thirty men strong, Jeremiah, Jahaziel, marching along.
From Gad came warriors, faces like lions, Swift as gazelles, on mountains they're flyin'.
Ezer the chief, Obadiah the next, Mighty men of valor, never perplexed.
Through swollen Jordan, they charged on through, Scattering foes, east and west they flew.
David asked those who came, "Are you friend or foe? If you're here for peace, then let us grow."
Amasai spoke, "We are yours, son of Jesse, Peace to you, your God helps plenty."
Manasseh joined in, with Philistines they came, But they turned Saul's way, risking their name.
Day by day, warriors gathered 'round, An army like God's, they stood their ground.
To Hebron they came, Judah's men in line, Turning Saul's kingdom, by Yahweh's design.
Judah, Simeon, Levi, standing tall, Benjamin, Ephraim, came at David's call.
Zebulun, Naphtali, ready for war's parade, Danites, Asher, their battle array displayed.
Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, with instruments of fight, Came to make David king with hearts aligned right.
Three days of feasting, they gathered 'round, Provisions abundant, joy in the land profound.
Bread, wine, cattle, gifts they bring, To celebrate David, Israel's king.

David huddled with the leaders, he sought their advice, "If it's good and God's will, let's make it precise. Send word to our brothers all over the lands, With priests and the Levites, get them in bands.
Let's bring back the ark, left in Saul's days, All agreed, they said, 'Yeah, this is the way.' From Egypt's brook to Hamath's gates wide, To bring home the ark, with all Israel's pride.
To Kiriath Jearim, the sacred place, The ark of God's Name, we would embrace. On a new cart, it rolled from Abinadab's door, Uzza and Ahio, guiding it forth.
David and Israel, with might they did sing, Harps, strings, tambourines, made the air ring. But when to Chidon’s threshing place they came, Uzza reached out, and Yahweh’s wrath flamed.
God struck him down, for touching the prize, David, displeased, saw the anger in his eyes. Called it Perez Uzza, marked with pain, "How to bring it home?" David exclaimed.
So the ark stayed at Obed-Edom's place, Three months of blessings, God's favor and grace. Yahweh poured blessings on all he had, For the ark's presence made the house glad.
Hiram sent a crew with cedar trees and skill, To build David's house, a king's home on a hill.
David knew God placed him high on the throne, For Israel's sake, not for his alone.
In Jerusalem, more wives he gained, Sons and daughters, his family name proclaimed.
Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet—like a song they run.
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia—each a treasure, Elishama, Beeliada, Eliphelet, beyond measure.
The Philistines heard and sought David out, Anointed king—his power, they had no doubt.
In Rephaim's valley, they made a bold raid, David heard and to God’s wisdom he prayed.
"Shall I face the Philistines? Will you deliver them to me?" "Go up," God said, "Victory’s yours, like the breaking sea."
To Baal Perazim, David took the fight, Enemies broken, like waters in flight.
Their idols left behind, David gave the decree, Burn them with fire, as a symbol of victory.
Another raid came, in the valley once more, David sought God, like he did before.
"Don't go up this time, turn around instead, Wait by the trees till you hear marching overhead."
"When you hear that sound, strike with force and fire, For God has gone before, as your fierce supplier."
David followed through, as commanded above, From Gibeon to Gezer, he fought with God's love.
Fame spread wide, fear fell on each land, For Yahweh brought victory by David's hand.
David built up houses in the city's heart, A place for God's ark, he made from the start. "No one but Levites should carry it, no doubt, Yahweh chose them, that's what it's all about."
He called all Israel to Jerusalem's gate, Prepared a place for the ark, didn’t hesitate. Gathered Aaron's sons, Levites in file, Each clan chief and brothers, marching in style.
Uriel led Kohath, with a hundred twenty, Asaiah with Merari, two twenty plenty. Gershom's sons with Joel, one thirty they bring, Shemaiah's two hundred, their voices to sing.
David summoned Zadok and Abiathar, Called Levites, spoke clear, he raised the bar. "Sanctify yourselves, you heads of the line, It's time to bring up the ark, make it shine."
"Before we failed, God’s anger did rise, We’ll do it right now, no more disguise.” Levites cleansed, purified for the task, To carry God's ark, as Moses did ask.
The ark on their shoulders, each pole in place, The word from Yahweh, they embraced. David spoke to Levites, "Music we'll employ, Bring out the instruments, lift up in joy."
Heman, Asaph, Ethan, leading the sound, Zechariah and crew, stringed instruments abound. Cymbals of bronze, the singers did shout, Harps and lyres, their melodies about.
Chenaniah led the song with his skill, Doorkeepers on guard, alert and still. Priests with trumpets, sounded the call, Bringing the ark, a celebration for all.
David and the elders, captains in line, With joy they marched, the ark divine. God helped the Levites, they offered sacrifice, Seven bulls, seven rams, a holy device.
David wore linen, robe shining bright, The Levites, singers, all in white. Israel shouted, trumpets and strings, As the ark entered, their voices did ring.
Michal watched David, dancing and free, But in her heart, disdain was her decree.
They brought God's ark, set it center stage, In David's tent, amidst holy sage. Burnt offerings flared, peace offerings too, David blessed the people, God's name shining through.
Bread, meat, and raisins to each man and wife, A feast for all, a moment of life. Levites were called, their roles they knew, To praise, to thank, for all God would do.
Asaph with cymbals, Zechariah nearby, Strings and harps played, the music soared high. Benaiah, Jahaziel, trumpets in hand, Sounding before the covenant's stand.
David commanded thanks on that day, "Give thanks to Yahweh," he'd say. "Sing praises, tell of His marvelous deeds, Seek His strength, fulfill your needs."
Remember His wonders, Israel's kin, His covenant spoken, time and again. Promised to Abraham, Isaac too, Jacob's inheritance, every word true.
"From few to many, I led you all, Protected by my hand, no harm would befall." "Touch not my anointed, my prophets are mine," Reproved the kings, a promise divine.
"Sing to Yahweh, all earth's expanse, Declare His glory, let nations dance. Great is Yahweh, above all gods revered, He made the heavens, His majesty cleared."
"Honor and strength, before Him stand, Bring offerings, worship, with open hand. Let earth and heaven rejoice and sing, For Yahweh reigns, let praises ring!"
"Save us, O God, gather us near, In Your name's triumph, quiet all fear." Blessed be Yahweh, eternal His name, "Save us," they cried, "forever the same."
The people cried "Amen," praise would not cease, Asaph and brothers, their duties in peace. Day by day, they ministered there, In Yahweh's presence, in constant prayer.
Morning and evening, offerings raised, In holy array, His name be praised. David returned, his house to bless, In Yahweh's love, they found their rest.
David sat at home, cozy in cedar's embrace, But the ark of Yahweh stayed in a tented space. He spoke to Nathan, prophet and friend, “I’m in a house, while God’s ark’s got no end.”
Nathan said, “Do what's in your heart's lane, For God’s with you, no need to restrain.” But that night, God’s word came to Nathan in sight, “Tell David, ‘It’s not you who'll build my house bright.'”
“I’ve roamed in tents since Israel’s birth, From tent to tent, I moved on this earth. Did I ask any judge, ‘Build me a house of cedar?’ Never did I demand such from any leader.”
“Tell David, ‘I took you from sheep’s pen, Raised you up high, above other men. With you, I defeated your foes in the land, Made your name great, with a strong, mighty hand.’”
“I’ll plant a place for Israel to stand, No more will wickedness trouble this land. I’ll subdue enemies, build you a house of might, Your son will rule, his kingdom in sight.”
“He’ll build me a house, his throne will not end, I’ll be his father, him I’ll defend. My love won’t depart, as it once did before, In my kingdom, his throne will endure evermore.”
Nathan shared these words with the king that night, David pondered, in Yahweh's sight. “Who am I, God, that you've brought me so far? You've lifted my house, like a bright shining star.”
“You’ve honored your servant, in ways so grand, Respected me, lifted me by your hand. Yahweh, none like you, no other god compares, You redeemed a people, showed them you care.”
“Israel’s your own, forever to keep, Yahweh, you became their God, a promise deep. Let your word be firm, as you have proclaimed, Let the house of David be forever famed.”
“Blessed is your servant, with courage, I pray, Your promises stand firm, never to sway. Yahweh, you’ve blessed, your will, let it be, For your blessing remains through eternity.”
David rose up, Philistines under his boot, Took Gath and towns, gave them the recruit. Moab fell, became servants, tribute they bring, David's victories echoed, like a lion he'd sing.
Hadadezer of Zobah, David came to defeat, By Euphrates he marched, made his enemies retreat. Chariots and horsemen, he took them all, Hamstrung their steeds, made their power fall.
Syrians of Damascus, they came to aid, But David struck down theirs in a fierce cascade. Garrisons placed, Syrians served under his hand, Yahweh gave him victory, across the land.
Gold shields from Hadadezer, to Jerusalem they went, Tibhath and Cun's bronze, to Solomon was sent. Tou of Hamath, heard David's might, Sent Hadoram with gifts, acknowledging the fight.
Gold, silver, bronze from every land, David dedicated to Yahweh, by divine command. Edomites in the Valley met Abishai's blade, Eighteen thousand struck, their resistance decayed.
Edomites served, David's reign spread wide, Justice and righteousness, his people's guide. Joab led the army, Jehoshaphat kept the score, Zadok and Abimelech, the priests they bore.
Shavsha the scribe, Benaiah stood tall, Cherethites and Pelethites, at David's call. His sons chief officials, the kingdom in peace, David's reign, a testament, to war's fierce release.
Nahash passed, and his son took the throne, David said, “Kindness, I won’t leave alone.” He sent messengers, their mission was clear, To comfort Hanun, for his father dear.
But Ammon's princes whispered deceit, “David’s not here just to comfort or greet. Spies in disguise, to search and to pry, To overthrow, to see where you lie.”
Hanun believed, distrust took the lead, Shaved David’s men, made them flee in need. Garments were cut, humiliation was vast, David was told; his anger was cast.
“Stay in Jericho,” David advised, “Till your beards grow back, regain your pride.” Ammon knew they were odious now, Sent silver for chariots, to make a vow.
Thirty-two thousand strong, from far and wide, Encamped at Medeba, ready to collide. David heard, and Joab led the charge, With mighty men, their army was large.
Ammon and allies prepared for the fight, Joab saw the battle, surrounded left and right. “Abishai, my brother, stand strong beside me, If they’re too strong, help each other, be free.
“Be brave for the cities and our land, Yahweh will guide us, by His hand.” Joab moved forward, Syrians fled, Ammon saw, and in fear they sped.
Joab returned to Jerusalem’s gate, Syria regrouped, but it was too late. David crossed Jordan, battle aligned, Syrians fought, but defeat was designed.
Seven thousand chariots fell to the ground, Forty thousand footmen, silence profound. Shophach was slain, Syria knew peace, David’s might, their wars would cease.
Peace was made, servitude began, Ammon stood alone, without Syrian's plan.
When time came for kings to march in line, Joab led the army, crossed the borderline.
He struck the land of Ammon, made it fall, But David stayed in Jerusalem's hall.
Joab took Rabbah, brought it to its knees, While David sat back, enjoying the breeze.
Off came the crown from the Ammonite king, A talent of gold, a heavy, fine thing.
With jewels that shimmered, it adorned his head, And riches from the city, he then spread.
He brought out the people, tools in hand, Axes, saws—he made a stand.
To every Ammonite city, he did just the same, Then back to Jerusalem, he made his fame.
War rose with Philistines at Gezer’s gate, Sibbecai, strong, sealed Sippai's fate.
Elhanan stood firm in battle’s roar, Took down Lahmi, Goliath’s kin once more.
At Gath, a giant with fingers and toes that amazed, Jonathan, David’s kin, left him dazed.
Those born to the giant fell by David’s crew, By his servants' hands, they got their due.
Satan rose up, had a plan in his hand, Moved David to count all the people in the land. David told Joab and princes, "Go far and wide, Count from Beersheba to Dan, all of Israel's pride."
Joab said, "May Yahweh's people grow great, But why count them, King? Don't cause guilt on their fate." Yet the king's word stood, Joab went on his quest, Across all the land, then back to his nest.
Joab returned, the census was done, One million one hundred thousand men who could run, In Judah, four seventy thousand strong, Levi and Benjamin, Joab left out, felt wrong.
God was displeased, struck Israel with fear, David cried, "I've sinned, my mistake is clear! Take the guilt from your servant, I plead, I've done foolishly, seen the error of my deed."
Yahweh spoke through Gad, "Go to David and say, 'Three choices I give, pick one for the day: Three years of famine, or months before foes, Or three days of pestilence — let your answer disclose.'"

David said, "It's distress I feel in my heart, Let me fall into Yahweh's hand, His mercy's a part. But never let me fall to man's wrathful plan." Yahweh sent a plague, seventy thousand lost in the land.
An angel at Jerusalem, ready to destroy, Yahweh relented, said, "Enough, my envoy." David saw the angel, sword drawn in the sky, He and the elders in sackcloth, they cried.
David pleaded, "It was I who sinned, let it be, Not these people, O Lord, turn your hand on me." The angel told Gad, "Go speak to the king, Build an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor ring."
David went up as Gad had declared, Ornan saw the angel, his sons were scared. David approached, Ornan bowed to the ground, "Sell me this place, stop the plague that's around."
Ornan said, "Take it all, oxen, wood, and wheat, My king, do what's right, your way is complete." But David replied, "No, I will pay, Won't offer Yahweh what costs me no way."
Six hundred shekels of gold weighed and paid, An altar was built, offerings made. Yahweh answered with fire from the sky, The angel sheathed his sword, no more tears to cry.
David saw Yahweh's answer at the site, Sacrifices made under Ornan's light. The tabernacle was in Gibeon, high place and grand, But David feared the angel's sword, stayed his hand.
"This is Yahweh's spot, the altar for Israel's flame," David spoke, setting up the masons for God's house to frame.
Gathered foreigners in the land, bricks they laid, Iron for nails, bronze unweighed.
Cedar trees aplenty, Tyre and Sidon did provide, For David's vision to be a house worldwide.
"Solomon's young, the house must amaze, I'll prepare it big before my final days."
Summoned his son, said, "Now it's your turn, Build Yahweh's house, let the holy fire burn.
I wished to build it, but God's words were clear, 'You've shed blood, too much war, you hear.
A son of peace will rise, your legacy, His name's Solomon, bringing quiet to the sea.
He'll erect my house, I'll call him my son, His throne in Israel will never be done.'"
"Yahweh be with you, build as He planned, May wisdom guide you as you lead this land.
Keep His laws close, and strength will thrive, Be strong, don't fear, keep courage alive.
See, I've gathered gold and silver galore, Bronze, iron without weight, timber, and more.
Workers surround you, skilled in each trade, Rise and build, let no moment fade."
David told the princes, "Help Solomon, don't delay, Hasn't Yahweh blessed us, shown us the way?
Subdue the land, Yahweh's name proclaim, Build His sanctuary, magnify His fame.
Arise and bring the Ark to Yahweh's place, His sacred vessels in the holy space."
David's old, full of days, passed the crown, Made Solomon king, brought the leaders around.
Priests and Levites, all gathered in place, Counted the Levites in this sacred space.
Thirty-eight thousand, from thirty years on, Twenty-four thousand for work that must be done.
"Six thousand judges, officers in line, Four thousand doorkeepers, guarding what's divine."
"Four thousand praised with instruments of praise, In divisions by Levi's sons, set in ways."
Gershon, Kohath, Merari, divided by name, Ladan and Shimei in Gershon's claim.
Jehiel, Zetham, Joel, Shimei's line, Shelomoth, Haziel, Haran, they all align.
Jahath was chief, Zizah was next, Jeush and Beriah, fewer sons perplexed.
Amram, Izhar, Hebron, Uzziel's lot, Aaron and Moses, in Amram's plot.
Aaron set apart, sanctified the most high, Burned incense, blessed, to Yahweh testified.
Moses' sons, Levi's tribe they embrace, Gershom and Eliezer, in their rightful place.
Rehabiah's many, Eliezer's line, Izhar's son Shelomith, with Hebron's four in line.
Micah, Isshiah, Uzziel's sons known, Mahli and Mushi, Merari's own.
Eleazar's daughters wed Kish's sons, Mahli, Eder, Jeremoth, Mushi’s ones.
Levi's clans counted, from twenty years on, For Yahweh’s service, with strength and brawn.
David declared, "Yahweh gives rest, In Jerusalem, His dwelling's blessed."
No more to bear the tabernacle’s weight, For Levi's sons, a different fate.
Serving Aaron’s sons, in holy place, Purifying all things, with steadfast grace.
Morning and evening, Yahweh they praise, On Sabbaths, new moons, in feast day displays.
Keeping the Tent, the holy duty they bear, In service to Yahweh, with reverent care.
Aaron's sons were four, Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, they had priestly work to do. Nadab and Abihu died, leaving no heirs, So Eleazar and Ithamar took over priestly cares.
David with Zadok and Ahimelech in line, Divided duties, made everything fine. More chiefs from Eleazar's son, Sixteen in total, their work had begun.
Ithamar's line had eight heads to show, All were chosen fair, by lots they'd go. Princes of the sanctuary and God's holy lot, Eleazar and Ithamar, their service sought.
Shemaiah the scribe, Levite with a pen, Recorded the divisions, again and again. Lots drawn in the presence of the king, Priests and Levites around, the order they'd bring.
Jehoiarib first, Jedaiah was next, Harim third, Seorim fourth in text. On through the list, each name to call, Twenty-four in all, to serve in the hall.
Into Yahweh's house, by Aaron's decree, As God of Israel had set them to be. Sons of Levi were ordered too, Amram's line, Shubael, Jehdeiah to pursue.
From Rehabiah, Isshiah's the chief, Izharites, Shelomoth, Jahath, no grief. Hebron's sons, Jeriah, Amariah too, Jahaziel, Jekameam, the work they do.
Uzziel had Micah, and Shamir, his lad, Micah's brother Isshiah, Zechariah he had. Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi, Jaaziah's were Beno, Shoham, their duty.
Mahli's Eleazar had no sons to bear, From Kish, Jerahmeel, their names in the air. Mushi's descendants, Mahli, Eder, Jerimoth, Levitical lines, all in their oath.
As Aaron's line drew lots for their call, David, Zadok watched over them all. Priests and Levites stood, both young and old, In service to God, as the stories were told.
David and his captains, they set the scene, Sons of Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, keen. Prophesying with harps, strings, and cymbals clear, Skillful sons, each ready, God's voice they’d hear.
Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, they came through, Asharelah under Asaph, prophesied true. Under Jeduthun, six sons praised Yahweh's name, With harps, thanks, and praise, their hearts aflame.
Heman’s sons, a long list, Bukkiah leads, Fourteen sons, three daughters, where prophecy seeds. All under Heman, Yahweh’s house filled with song, Cymbals, strings, harps, lifting the praises strong.
Two hundred eighty-eight, each skilled, they sang, Casting lots, each role in harmony rang. First lot to Asaph’s Joseph, the second Gedaliah, Twelve each, every group, each son, a desire.
Third to Zaccur, then Izri, the fourth’s call, Nethaniah fifth, Bukkiah sixth, in all. Seventh Jesharelah, eighth to Jeshaiah’s tunes, Ninth to Mattaniah, with Shimei’s boons.
Tenth was Shimei, Azarel’s eleventh strike, Hashabiah twelfth, Shubael’s thirteen alike. Mattithiah fourteenth, then Jeremoth’s way, Sixteenth to Hananiah, they play.
Seventeenth, Joshbekashah, Hanani’s next, Mallothi nineteenth, their spirits flexed. Twentieth to Eliathah, Hothir’s twenty-first, Giddalti, twenty-second, with music versed.
Twenty-third to Mahazioth, Romamti-Ezer closed, Each twelve strong, their voices composed. In Yahweh’s house, all skillful and aligned, Serving with music, their hearts intertwined.
The Korahites stood strong, keepers of the door, Meshelemiah and his sons, ready for more. Zechariah, Jediael, Zebadiah, they came, Jathniel, Elam, Jehohanan, Eliehoenai, each with a name.
Obed-Edom was blessed, sons he had eight, Shemaiah and the rest, they were great. Mighty men of valor, Shemaiah's kin, Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad, with courage within.
Sixty-two from Obed-Edom, strong for the call, Meshelemiah's eighteen, prepared to stand tall. Hosah of Merari had sons on his side, Shimri led them, though firstborn defied.
Casting lots for the gates, east, north, and south, Obed-Edom took the storehouse, wisdom from their mouth. To the west stood Shuppim and Hosah's crew, Watchmen on alert, always something to do.
Ahijah had watch over treasures so grand, For God's house, all the riches on hand. Sons of Ladan, Gershonites in line, Jehieli's house, treasures divine.
From Moses to Shebuel, treasures they tended, Dedicated by kings, battles had ended. David, the captains, the plunder they gave, To repair Yahweh's house, the offerings they'd save.
Chenaniah's sons for Israel's affairs, Judges and officers, resolving all cares. Hebronites with valor, beyond Jordan's west, Hashabiah and brothers, serving the best.
Jerijah chief among Hebron's might, In David's fortieth year, they shone bright. Two thousand seven hundred, leaders in their stride, Overseeing tribes, with God and king allied.
Israel's leaders, standing strong, month by month they marched along, Each division twenty-four thousand strong, in their ranks they belong.
First up, Jashobeam, son of Zabdiel, leading the first month with a tale to tell, From the children of Perez, this captain's swell, he leads with pride, and he leads them well.
Second month's Dodai, the Ahohite, with Mikloth his right-hand knight, Their twenty-four thousand ready to fight, standing tall, standing bright.
Third in line, Benaiah, a priestly son, mighty man, his fame begun, With Ammizabad, his son, Benaiah had twenty-four thousand, their work never done.
Fourth month brings Asahel, Joab's kin, Zebadiah steps in after him, Twenty-four thousand more, they begin, moving with courage, these soldiers win.
Shamhuth the Izrahite takes the fifth month stand, Leading his troop of twenty-four grand.
Ira the Tekoite, sixth in line, with his twenty-four thousand, they shine, His father's strength in every spine, they march on, keeping time.
Helez the Pelonite, Ephraim's pride, claims seventh month, with strength applied, Twenty-four thousand at his side, in battle, they will never hide.
Sibbecai the Hushathite for the eighth month reigns, Twenty-four thousand in his chains.
Ninth month's captain, Abiezer the Anathothite, From Benjamin's line, his men are tight.
Tenth month, Maharai the Netophathite, commands his crew, Twenty-four thousand ready, strong and true.
Benaiah the Pirathonite takes the eleventh role, Ephraim's strength, his heart and soul.
Twelfth month, Heldai the Netophathite, Othniel's kin, Twenty-four thousand, they begin.
Each tribe with leaders, names they boast, From Reuben to Dan, each holds their post.
David, wise, counts not the young, "Israel shall grow, like stars among."
Joab starts a count, but doesn't complete, Wrath falls, the task left incomplete.
Treasures kept by Azmaveth's hand, Fields and vineyards, Jonathan's land.
Shimei, Zabdi, Baal Hanan, too, Look after vineyards, olives, trees that grew.
Over herds and flocks, trusted men stand, The king's wealth spread across the land.
Jonathan, uncle to the king's heir, Counselor wise, his advice rare.
Ahithophel, Hushai, friends to the king, Joab leads the army, with might they bring.
David's kingdom, organized and vast, With trusted men, it stands steadfast.
David called the leaders, the mighty, the strong, Gathered in Jerusalem, they all belong. "Listen up, my brothers, hear what I say, In my heart was a house where God's ark could stay.
But God said, 'David, not for you to build, A warrior's hands with blood are filled.' Yet from my family, He chose me, the king, Judah's line, where praises sing.
Solomon, my son, has been chosen by Name, To build God's house, to bring it fame. 'He'll be My son, I'll be his dad,' God said to me, making my heart so glad.
So follow His rules, in God put your trust, Possess this land, be righteous and just. Solomon, my son, know God deep inside, Serve with a pure heart, don't run and hide.
If you seek Him, you'll find Him, it's true, But forsake Him, and He'll leave you blue. God chose you, hear the call— Be strong, build it all."
David gave to Solomon the plans divine, For the temple, the courts, the rooms, every line. Gold and silver, all weighed right, For lamps and bowls that shine so bright.
"All this," David said, "by Yahweh's hand, Every detail, I understand. Son, be strong, courageous, and stand, Yahweh’s with you, a mighty band.
Priests and Levites, ready for the task, Every skilled man, just ask. Captains and people, at your command, To build the house, as God has planned."
David stood up, addressed the throng, "Solomon's young, the work is long; Chosen by God, this task is grand, The palace built by Yahweh's hand.
Prepared with might, I've gathered gold, Silver and bronze, stories told, Iron, wood, gems of every hue, Marble stones, more than a few.
From my treasure, gifts I bring, Gold and silver for Yahweh’s King. Who will offer? Who will give? Let's consecrate, let's truly live."
Princes and captains came with zeal, Offered their treasures, the love was real. Gold, silver, bronze, iron too, Donations from many, freely they flew.
Precious stones to Jehiel they gave, Rejoicing hearts, the people brave; With pure hearts, they offered here, David danced, joy was near.
David blessed Yahweh, lifted voice, "Our God is great, in Him we rejoice! Yours is the power, the glory, the might, Riches and honor, day and night.
All we give is yours to own, From your hand, blessings flown. We're strangers here, shadows pass, Our days like whispers, fleeting, fast.
God examines hearts, loves the true, In uprightness, offerings accrue. Let the people keep this fire, Hearts prepared, never tire.
To Solomon, grant wisdom's grace, To keep your laws, build this place." David turned to the crowd and said, "Praise Yahweh," as they bowed their head.
Sacrifices offered, fires burned bright, They celebrated with joy that night. Solomon crowned once again, With Zadok priest, it marked the reign.
Solomon sat as king on the throne, He ruled the land, not alone; Princes and warriors bowed in awe, Yahweh's majesty, all saw.
David's days, forty years long, Seven in Hebron, where he belonged. Thirty-three in Jerusalem’s light, He died rich, full, in Yahweh's sight.
Recorded deeds, written well, Samuel, Nathan, Gad did tell. David's story, his reign, his might, Over Israel, kingdoms in sight.
Solomon's throne, yeah, it's firmly in place, God's with him, giving him that amazing grace.
He spoke to Israel, leaders all around, Captains, judges, princes, where they could be found.
To Gibeon they marched, a high place so grand, God's Tent of Meeting, built by Moses' own hand.
David brought the Ark to a tent he prepared, In Jerusalem, with reverence, it was aired.
Before the bronze altar, Bezalel's creation, Solomon sought wisdom, seeking God's elation.
He offered a thousand burnt offerings that night, And God appeared, His presence, pure light.
"Ask what you want," the Lord did say, Solomon replied in a humble way.
"You loved my father, and made me king, Let your promise stand, like a bird on the wing.
Grant me wisdom to lead this multitude, For who can judge them with gratitude?"
God replied, "You asked wise and true, Not for riches or revenge, but wisdom for you.
So wisdom and knowledge I now do grant, Plus riches and honor, beyond any past chant."
Solomon returned, back to his city, Reigned over Israel, strong and gritty.
Chariots and horsemen, he gathered with might, Silver like stones, cedars in sight.
Horses from Egypt and Kue were bought, Merchants dealing, in riches they sought.
Chariots and horses, to Hittites and Syrians sold, Solomon's wisdom and wealth, a story told.
Solomon rose, with a plan in his mind, A house for Yahweh’s name and kingdom combined. Seventy thousand strong to carry the load, Eighty thousand stone cutters, down the mountain road.
Three thousand six hundred to keep the plan tight, Solomon wrote to Huram, seeking his might. "As you helped my father with cedars so fine, Help me build a house, in God’s grand design.
For Yahweh, my God, incense will rise, Showbread and offerings, up to the skies. Morning and night, Sabbaths and feasts, An ordinance of Israel, never to cease.
This house is for Yahweh, majestic and grand, Yet who can contain Him, with heaven in hand? Send me a craftsman skilled in the arts, Gold, silver, and purple, to play their parts.
Cedar and cypress, Lebanon’s pride, My servants with yours, side by side. Timber in abundance, for a temple so great, And in return, wheat, barley, wine on each plate."
Huram replied, with words on a scroll, "Yahweh loves His people; He’s made you whole. Blessed be Yahweh, the God of the skies, Who gave David a son, so wise and wise.
I send a craftsman, skilled and true, In every craft, he’ll work for you. Son of Dan’s daughter, Tyre his home, With skills to engrave, in wood or stone.
Send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine, We’ll cut the wood, send it down the line. Rafts on the sea, from Lebanon to Joppa, Then it’s yours to carry, to Jerusalem proper."
Solomon counted, the foreigners vast, One fifty-three thousand six hundred amassed. Seventy thousand to bear, eighty thousand to cut, Three thousand six hundred overseers, the work to strut.
Solomon starts to build, on Mount Moriah high, Where Yahweh met David, the place set to the sky.
Second month, fourth year, he kicked off his reign, Measured out the foundation, plans were insane.
Sixty long, twenty wide, God's house takes shape, With a porch in front, gold within, no escape.
A ceiling of cypress, gold overlay bright, Palm trees and chains, a glorious sight.
He adorned with stones, precious, beauty untold, From Parvaim the gold, bold stories unfold.
Gold on beams, walls, doors, cherubim engraved, Most holy place sparkles, treasures not saved.
Twenty by twenty, fine gold laid thick, Six hundred talents, nails of fifty, slick.
Carved cherubim, golden they soar, Wingspan twenty cubits, touching the floor.
Each wing five cubits, to walls they reach, Fierce faces forward, sacred they teach.
Veil of blue, purple, crimson so pure, Cherubim adorned, majesty sure.
Pillars stand tall, thirty-five to the sky, Chains and pomegranates, a sight to apply.
Jachin on the right, Boaz on the left side, Solomon's temple, where God's glory abide.
He built an altar, bronze, so grand, Twenty cubits each way it did stand.
A molten sea, brim to brim, ten cubits wide, Round and high, thirty cubits to stride.
Underneath were oxen, encircling in rows, Two tiers cast, as the sea arose.
On twelve strong oxen, the sea took its place, Facing every direction, their hindquarters in space.
A handbreadth thick, like a lily it spanned, Held three thousand baths, by His command.
Ten basins he made, five left, five right, For washing offerings, pure in God's sight.
Golden lampstands, ten in line, Set in the temple, with a holy sign.
Ten tables, five left, five right, so bold, And a hundred basins, shimmering gold.
Courts for the priests, with doors of bronze, Set the sea to the south, as the sun dawns.
Huram made pots, shovels, and more, Finished his work for Solomon's store.
Pillars, bowls, and capitals high, Networks adorned with pomegranates nigh.
Bases and basins, as they were planned, One sea on oxen, in the Promised Land.
Bright bronze vessels, cast with care, In the Jordan's clay, laid bare.
Solomon's vessels in abundance, no weight known, For Yahweh's house, His glory shown.
Golden altars, tables with show bread placed, Lampstands with lamps, pure gold they embraced.
Flowers, lamps, and tongs, perfect gold displayed, Snuffers, basins, fire pans, in splendor arrayed.
The holy inner doors, gold through and through, In God's house, His promise shone true.
Solomon, the work's complete, the temple's done, He brought the treasures in, one by one.
Gold, silver, vessels, all that David saved, Placed in God's house, where they'd be engraved.
Called the elders, tribes, the leaders to the scene, To bring up Yahweh's ark, where it had been.
Men of Israel gathered, the seventh month feast, Elders arrived, Levites with the ark in the least.
Carried the ark, the Tent, holy vessels they did, Priests with them, nothing hidden, nothing hid.
Before the ark, Solomon and Israel stood, Sacrifices uncountable, as best as they could.
The ark placed in the holy, under cherubim's wings, Wings spread wide, covering holy things.
Poles so long, ends seen in the sacred space, But not outside, still in their place.
Inside the ark, the tablets alone, Moses' covenant, etched in stone.
Priests came out, sanctified, divisions gone, Levites singing, with music drawn.
Singers and priests, in fine linen dressed, Trumpets and voices, praising with zest.
"For He is good, His love forever," they sang out loud, The house filled with a cloud, Yahweh's presence proud.
So thick the cloud, priests couldn't stand, Yahweh's glory filled the land.
Solomon spoke with a powerful tone, "Yahweh dwells where the shadows are grown. But I've built a house for You to stay, A place for Your presence every day."
He turned to bless Israel's crowd, His voice was clear, his words were loud. "Bless Yahweh, the God of our land, Fulfilling His promise by His own hand."
He chose no city, no land before, Until He called Jerusalem, His name to store. David was chosen, his heart set on fire, To build for Yahweh, his deepest desire.
But Yahweh said, "David, your heart is true, But not you, your son will build it anew." Now Solomon stands, he's on the throne, Building Yahweh's house, stone by stone.
The Ark is placed, covenant kept tight, In this house of worship, shining bright. Solomon knelt, hands spread wide, Prayed to Yahweh, none beside.
"Yahweh, Israel's God," He cried, "In heaven and earth, none can hide. You've kept your word to my father, King, Fulfill Your promise, let blessings spring."
"Will God dwell in houses man-made? Heaven can't hold You, nor our humble shade. Yet hear our cries, our daily plea, Be with us, God, eternally."
"If we sin, or face our foe, Return to You, blessings flow. If skies are dry, famine strikes, Turn to You, hearts ignite."
"Foreigners too, from lands afar, Will pray to this house, under your star. Hear their call, show them your might, Let them know your name, shining bright."
"When battles rage, hear our prayer, Guide us, Yahweh, everywhere. If captive taken, hearts contrite, Bring them back, into Your light."
He closed with words, so deep and true, "Yahweh, rise, strength anew. Let priests be clothed, saints rejoice, Hear our prayers, in Your voice."
Remember David, servant dear, Yahweh, in Your love, keep him near. Solomon's prayer reached the skies, And blessings rained from on high.
Solomon prayed, and fire hit the ground, Burnt offering consumed, God's glory all around.
Priests couldn't enter, the house was ablaze, God's presence filled the place, a glorious haze.
Israel saw the fire, they hit the floor, Faces down, they worshiped, "Forevermore!"
King Solomon stepped up with his crew, Twenty-two thousand cattle, sheep too.
With music and trumpets, the Levites played, "Praise the Lord!" with instruments made.
The altar couldn't hold all the sacrifice heat, So he made the court holy, where offerings meet.
Seven days of feasting, all gathered 'round, From Hamath to Egypt, joy did abound.
Eighth day, solemn assembly, they stayed, Then rejoiced back home, goodness displayed.
Solomon finished, God's house complete, His heart fulfilled with every beat.
God came at night, spoke clear and bright, "I've chosen this place, it's precious in my sight."
"If drought hits, or locusts swarm your land, Turn to me, humble, and take your stand."
"Hear you I will, forgive, and heal, My eyes and ears open, your prayers I feel."
"Walk like David, keep my ways true, And I'll keep your throne, always for you."
"But turn away, and worship wrong, I'll uproot you and make your end long."
"High house will fall, a shocking sight, People will ask, 'Why this plight?'"
"Answer will come, they left God's hand, Chased other gods, lost their land."
After twenty long years, Solomon built with might, Yahweh's house and his palace shining bright.
He took the cities Huram gave, made them homes, For Israel's children, under the sky's domes.
To Hamath Zobah Solomon went, and he won, He built Tadmor in the wild under the sun.
Beth Horon, both high and low, he fortified strong, Walls, gates, and bars, where they belong.
Baalath and storage cities, chariots' pride, In Jerusalem, Lebanon, Solomon didn’t hide.
People left from Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites in sway, Became forced labor, working day by day.
But Israel's sons were warriors bold, Captains and rulers, their stories told.
Two hundred fifty officers in command, Chiefs of Solomon's mighty land.
Pharaoh's daughter brought to her new home, "Not in David's house," Solomon said, alone.
Burnt offerings to Yahweh, flames reaching high, Day by day, offerings never dry.
On Sabbaths, new moons, feasts in line, Unleavened bread, weeks, booths divine.
