He set priests and Levites, each in their role, Doorkeepers stationed, guarding the whole.
From David's commands they did not stray, Solomon's work finished, Yahweh's house to stay.
To Ezion Geber and Eloth he traveled wide, Huram sent ships, with wisdom as their guide.
Four hundred fifty talents of gold in hand, To Solomon's kingdom, wealth and riches stand.
Queen of Sheba heard Solomon's name, Came to test him, play the wisdom game.
Caravan so grand, spices and gold, Precious stones in hand, stories to be told.
Questions she had, from her heart they came, Solomon answered, his wisdom like a flame.
Saw his house, the food on his table, Servants all around, Solomon was able.
Witnessed his ascent to Yahweh's place, No spirit left in her, awed by his grace.
She said, "In my land, your fame had spread, But seeing it now, those words were underfed.
Your wisdom surpasses what I once heard, Your happy people, blessed by your word.
Praise to Yahweh, who set you high, To rule with justice, under God's sky."
Gifts she brought, gold, spices never seen, Solomon received like a king, serene.
Servants brought treasures from distant lands, Algum trees, precious stones, in their hands.
Terraces built, instruments made, In Judah's land, a spectacle displayed.
Solomon gave her all she desired, Off she went, her heart inspired.
Gold flowed in, more than ever before, Kings and traders brought wealth to his door.
Bucklers and shields crafted from gold, In the Forest of Lebanon, a sight to behold.
Ivory throne, gold overlay bright, Lions stood guard, a royal delight.
Drinking vessels, gold in every cup, Silver was common, gold filled them up.
Ships to Tarshish, treasures they bore, Gold, silver, peacocks, and more.
Riches and wisdom, unmatched on earth, Kings sought his presence, a testament to his worth.
Tributes brought, silver and gold, Every year a story told.
Four thousand stalls, horses in line, Chariots, horsemen, all design.
Ruled over kings, his domain was vast, Silver like stones, cedar trees amassed.
Horses from Egypt, lands far and wide, Solomon's reign, a majestic ride.
Forty years, Jerusalem's crown, In David's city, they laid him down.
Rehoboam his son took the throne, Solomon slept, his legacy known.
In Shechem, Rehoboam aimed to take the throne, All Israel gathered, his reign to be shown. Jeroboam in Egypt heard the news loud, Returned from his refuge, joined the crowd.
"Your father gave us burdens, made us sweat, Lighten it up, serve you, you bet." Rehoboam said, "Three days, then come back, I'll give you my answer, stay on track."
He asked the old men, wise in their ways, "What should I say in these trying days?" They said, "Be kind, with good words please, And they'll serve you well, at ease."
But he ditched their advice, turned to his crew, The young men he knew, seeking something new. "What should I say to lighten their load?" They replied with heat, in a harsher mode:

"Tell them your small finger's thicker than his waist, More burdens will come, and whips be replaced. Whips for scorpions, yokes doubled, feel the sting, Let them know the weight your rule will bring."
The third day came, the people arrived, Rehoboam's harsh words made his rule contrived. Ignored the elders' plea, followed the youth's advice, "My father whipped, but scorpions will suffice."
The people saw he wouldn't listen, so they cried, "No part in David, to tents we’ll abide." Israel left, their tents was their only home, Rehoboam reigned Judah, all alone.
Sent Hadoram, the labor's overseer, But stones rained down, his end was near. Rehoboam fled fast, back to his seat, Israel rebelled, David's house beat.
From that day, Israel went their own way, In Judah, Rehoboam's rule did stay.
Rehoboam rolled back to Jerusalem's gate, Judah and Benjamin's warriors, ready to debate. A hundred eighty thousand strong, swords raised to fight, To claim back the kingdom, to battle for the right.
But God spoke to Shemaiah, His voice clear and true, "Tell Rehoboam, tell the tribes, what they must do: 'Don't go up, don't fight your own kin today, Head back home, this is My way.'"
They listened to Yahweh, His command they heeded, Returned from the brink, no battle was needed. Rehoboam settled in the city, built cities strong, Fortified Judah, where the brave belong.
Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa rose high, Beth Zur and Soco touched the sky. Adullam, Gath, Mareshah, Ziph fortified, Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah fortified wide.
Shields and spears in every place, Judah and Benjamin stood with grace. The priests and Levites gathered 'round, Left their lands, Jerusalem bound.
Jeroboam's false priests cast them away, True seekers of Yahweh came to pray. Strengthened Judah, Rehoboam's reign, Three years like David's, Solomon's gain.
Took Mahalath, David’s kin as his wife, With sons Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham, new life. Maacah of Absalom then bore him more, Abijah, Attai, Ziza, Shelomith, they swore.
Maacah loved above all, in Rehoboam's eyes, Eighteen wives and concubines, his family ties. Twenty-eight sons, daughters sixty strong, Abijah named chief, where he belonged.
Dispersed his sons, in Judah they roamed, Food in abundance, seeking wives for home. Wise in his dealings, a kingdom well spread, Rehoboam’s legacy, a path well tread.
Rehoboam rose, his kingdom strong and wide, But turned from Yahweh's law, took Israel for a ride.
In year five, Shishak from Egypt marched bold, With chariots and horsemen, numbers untold.
Cities fortified fell to his might, Judah shook under that ominous night.
Shemaiah spoke to Rehoboam and the crew, “Yahweh says, ‘You've left me, now Shishak's on you.’”
Humbled, they cried, “Yahweh is just,” Bowed their heads low, laid down their trust.
Yahweh observed, saw their hearts bend, Said to Shemaiah, “Destruction I’ll suspend.
They'll taste some freedom, wrath not full blown, Still serve Shishak, lessons to be known.”
Shishak took treasures from the Lord’s place, From the king’s house, left it a disgrace.
Gold shields gone, Rehoboam made bronze, Gave them to the guards, for defense upon.
Each time he walked through Yahweh’s door, The guards brought them out, then back once more.
Humbled, Yahweh’s wrath turned away, Judah found good in that fateful day.
Rehoboam reigned strong in Jerusalem's might, The city Yahweh chose, in his sight.
He did evil, heart not set on the Lord, Writ in Shemaiah and Iddo’s accord.
Wars with Jeroboam marked his days, Rehoboam’s end came, in David's tomb he lays.
Abijah his son took up the crown, As Rehoboam’s tale was written down.
Year eighteen of Jeroboam's reign, Abijah took the throne, In Jerusalem, three years he reigned, not alone. His momma Micaiah, from Uriel's line, War ignited with Jeroboam, a battle divine.
Abijah gathered four hundred thousand strong, Jeroboam had double, mighty men, couldn't go wrong. Up on Mount Zemaraim, Abijah stood tall, "Hear me, Jeroboam, and Israel, heed my call:

Didn't Yahweh give David's line the kingdom to hold? Yet Jeroboam rebelled, his heart was bold. Trash gathered round him, when Rehoboam was weak, Now you challenge Yahweh's kingdom, your hearts you must seek.
You flaunt golden calves, your gods falsely made, Chased out Yahweh's priests, traditions betrayed. But we serve Yahweh, we hold firm and true, Our priests burn offerings, both morning and dew.
God is with us, priests sound trumpets loud, Don't fight Yahweh, your pride is your shroud." But Jeroboam had tricks, an ambush set behind, Judah turned and saw, fear gripped their mind.
They cried to Yahweh, trumpets blared, Judah shouted, and God struck, enemies snared. Israel fled, defeated, God delivered the win, Five hundred thousand fell, Judah's strength from within.
Judah prevailed, Yahweh was their guide, Abijah chased Jeroboam, took cities far and wide. Jeroboam never regained, struck down, he died, Abijah grew mighty, with family by his side.
Fourteen wives, children galore, Power and might, his legacy bore. His story's penned by the prophet's hand, Abijah's reign, a tale of a land.
Abijah passed, laid to rest, a chapter closed, Asa stepped up, and in peace, the land arose. Ten years of calm, no turmoil in sight, Asa did good, in Yahweh’s divine light.
He tore down altars, idols, and high places, Broke the poles, banished unholy traces. "Seek Yahweh," he told Judah, "obey His command," He cleared the cities, gave faith a strong stand.
The kingdom was quiet, no battles to face, Yahweh gave rest, a peaceful embrace. "Let's build," Asa said, "walls and towers high, We've sought Yahweh, and his peace draws nigh."
They built and prospered, walls standing tall, With Judah's three hundred thousand ready to brawl. Benjamite archers, shields held tight, All mighty men, prepared for the fight.
Zerah the Ethiopian, a million strong, Chariots of war, marching along. In the valley of Zephathah, battle took its place, Asa cried to Yahweh, seeking grace:
"Yahweh, stand with us, strong against the might, We rely on You, in Your name we fight. Don't let man prevail, show them Your hand," Yahweh struck them down, couldn't withstand.
Ethiopians fled, Asa pursued fast, At Gerar, they fell, couldn't outlast. Booty was taken, cities were struck with fear, Plundered them all, victory clear.
Livestock and camels, they took in might, Returned to Jerusalem, after the fight.
The Spirit of God hit Azariah bright, He went to Asa, spoke truth, shed light. "Hear me, Asa, Judah, Benjamin too, Yahweh's with you, as long as you're true.
Seek Him, find Him, but leave and He's gone, Once Israel was lost, the true God withdrawn. Without law and priest, they wandered in pain, But in their distress, they called His name again.
No peace in the land, nation in strife, Troubles spread wide, danger was rife. Be strong, don't slack, keep hands on the task, Your work shall be blessed, that's all I ask."
Asa heard these words, courage he gained, Cleared Judah and Benji, where idols reigned. He renewed God's altar, the sacred site, Gathered the tribes, to set things right.
From Ephraim, Manasseh, folks came in droves, Jerusalem gathered, as loyalty rose. Sacrificed cattle and sheep, a grand display, In the fifteenth year, of Asa's sway.
Into covenant they went, heart and soul in the game, Seek Yahweh or face death, equal was the claim. Swore aloud, trumpets, shouting in the air, All Judah rejoiced, for God answered prayer.
Asa dethroned his mom, for her idol's blight, Cut, ground, and burned it, by Kidron's light. Israel's high places yet stood, true, But Asa's heart was strong, his days through.
Brought silver and gold, to God's holy site, Peace reigned 'til his thirty-fifth year, no fight. They sought with desire, with all they possessed, And Yahweh gave them peace, in His rest.
In Asa's reign, year thirty-six, Baasha came quick, Built Ramah up strong, tried to seal the trick.
Asa pulled treasures, silver and gold, Sent to Ben Hadad, with a story told.
"Make a treaty, like our fathers once knew, I've sent you riches, now do what you do.
Break with Baasha, make him retreat, Set my people free, let Judah feel peace."
Ben Hadad heard, sent captains with might, They struck down cities, put Baasha to flight.
Baasha stopped building, his plans fell apart, Asa took Judah, gave them a new start.
With Ramah's stones and timber so fine, He built Geba and Mizpah, made them his line.
Then came Hanani, seer of the Lord, Spoke to Asa, delivered God's word:
"Trusted a king, not Yahweh's own hand, Now Syria's army escapes from your land.
Remember the Ethiopians, their chariots and might? Yahweh delivered when your heart was right.
Now wars will follow, cause you've been a fool, Yahweh's strength seeks hearts that are true."
Asa in anger, put the seer away, Oppressed his people, his heart led astray.
His tale’s recorded, in the kings' great book, The lessons of Asa, if you take a look.
In year thirty-nine, his feet fell ill, Ignored Yahweh’s power, sought physicians’ skill.
Forty-one years and Asa was gone, In his own tomb, with a great fire shone.
Laid with sweet odors, spices to burn, Judah's king, with lessons to learn.
Jehoshaphat stepped up, took the throne with might, Fortified his cities, prepped them for a fight. God was with him, he walked David's trail, Shunned the Baals, he wouldn't fail.
Sought his father's God, commandments on track, Didn't follow Israel, no turning back. Yahweh gave him strength, his kingdom stood tall, Judah brought tribute, riches flowed like a waterfall.
His heart soared high, in Yahweh's name, Tore down high places, ended false fame. In the third year, sent princes to teach, With Levites, priests, knowledge they'd preach.
Through Judah they roamed, law book in hand, Taught the people, Yahweh's command. Fear of God fell on lands around, No war with Jehoshaphat, peace profound.
Philistines brought gifts, silver paid the dues, Arabians with flocks, rams and goats in queues. Jehoshaphat grew great, built up his store, Fortresses, cities, men of war galore.
Counted his warriors, mighty men of pride, Adnah with three hundred thousand by his side. Jehohanan next, two hundred eighty strong, Amasiah followed, in Yahweh he belonged.
From Benjamin came Eliada, bow and shield in hand, Two hundred thousand ready, a fierce war band. Jehozabad next, one hundred eighty ready for strife, Waiting on the king, prepared for life.
In fortified cities, his forces spread wide, Jehoshaphat's rule, righteous and dignified. A kingdom established, by God led in peace, In Judah's borders, prosperity wouldn't cease.
Jehoshaphat got riches, honor piled high, Linked with Ahab, an alliance on the sly.
Years later, down to Samaria he went, Ahab’s sheep and cattle, a feast was well-spent.
Ahab asked, "With me to Ramoth Gilead, will you go?" Jehoshaphat replied, "Your people are mine, let's show."
But Jehoshaphat asked, "Seek Yahweh’s word first, Before we dive into battle, before things get worse."
Ahab gathered prophets, four hundred strong, "Shall we fight or hold back?" they sang the same song.
"Go up," they said, "God will give you the win." But Jehoshaphat questioned, "Is there no other within?"
Ahab sighed, "One man, Micaiah by name, But he speaks only evil, never fortune or fame."
"Don’t say that," Jehoshaphat urged, "Bring him here, Let’s hear what he says, whether it’s bad or clear."
Thrones were set, kings royal in robes, Prophets shouted their hopeful probes.
Zedekiah made iron horns, bold and grand, "Push the Syrians," he declared, "with Yahweh’s own hand."
Prophets echoed, "Gilead’s yours to claim, Yahweh’s deliverance is the name of the game."
The messenger to Micaiah said, "Speak like the rest, Make your words good, at the king’s request."
Micaiah responded, "Yahweh’s truth I’ll relay, Whatever my God says, that will I say."
Before the king, Micaiah did stand, "Shall we go to Gilead, take the land?"
He answered, "Prosper, victory's in sight," But the king pressed for truth, "Speak Yahweh’s light."
Micaiah revealed, "Like scattered sheep they’ll be, No shepherd in sight, let them return home free."
Ahab to Jehoshaphat, "See, he speaks ill, No good from him, just words meant to chill."
Micaiah continued, "Hear Yahweh’s decree, Yahweh on His throne, the host heavenly.
Who will entice Ahab, make him fall? A spirit came forward, offering his call.
'I’ll be a lying spirit in their voice,' Yahweh said, 'Go, you’ve made your choice.'"
"These prophets lie, Yahweh’s spoken your fate," Zedekiah struck him, "Where’s Yahweh in debate?"
Micaiah replied, "You’ll see on that day, When you hide in a room, Yahweh’s spirit you’ll weigh."
Ahab ordered, "Take him back, keep him confined, Bread and water of affliction, till peace I find."
"If peace returns," Micaiah declared bold, "Yahweh’s not spoken, heed my words told."
Together the kings went to Ramoth Gilead’s ground, Ahab in disguise, with robes Jehoshaphat was crowned.
Syrian chariot captains targeting the king, Jehoshaphat cried out, God’s help did bring.
Realizing their mistake, they turned back, A random arrow hit Ahab, attacked his track.
"Driver, turn, take me away, I’m struck so deep," In his chariot, he propped up, till evening sleep.
The battle raged on, Ahab held till the end, With sunset’s fall, his life did suspend.
Jehoshaphat returned home, peace in his stride, Came to Jerusalem, where he'd abide.
Jehu the seer came forth to speak, "Helping the wicked, why do you seek?
Wrath from Yahweh's on your trail, But good you did, you will prevail.
You tore down idols, set your heart right, Now seek God and walk in His light."
In Jerusalem, Jehoshaphat stayed, From Beersheba to Ephraim, he paved the way.
Bringing people back to the Lord, To the God their fathers adored.
Judges he placed in cities strong, "Judge not for man, but for Yahweh all along.
Feel His fear, let it be clear, For Yahweh shows no favor here.
No bribes, no tricks, just pure decree, In His name, deliver justly."
In Jerusalem, Levites he set, To judge and solve disputes that met.
"Do this in fear, with heart that's true, Any conflict, let righteousness ensue.
Warn them well, for Yahweh's sake, Avoid His wrath, the right path take.
Amariah's chief, in Yahweh's sphere, Zebadiah leads Judah's affairs here.
Levites assist, be strong and good, May Yahweh's presence be understood."
Enemies gathered, ready to fight, Jehoshaphat heard, and fear took flight.
"From beyond the sea, they come with might, In Hazazon Tamar, they plan their strike."
Alarmed, he sought Yahweh, called for fast, Judah united, prayers amassed.
In the sacred court, Jehoshaphat stood, “Yahweh in heaven, above all that’s good.
Didn't You clear this land for us, Your own? A home for Abraham's children, Your throne.
When evil strikes, we cry and You save, Now they come to steal what You gave.
Judge them, O God, they're vast and strong, We look to You, and we belong."
Judah stood still, families gathered tight, Yahweh's Spirit spoke, brought them light.
“Fear not this multitude, hear My plan, The battle's Mine, not for man's hand.
Tomorrow, set out, stand and see, Yahweh's salvation, victory free."
Jehoshaphat bowed, all Judah praised, Levites sang loud, voices raised.
Early next day, to Tekoa they marched, Jehoshaphat spoke, faith firmly parched.
"Believe in Yahweh, prophets proclaim, Establish your steps, prosper with His name."
Singers led with songs of grace, Praise rang out, filled the space.
As music soared, chaos ensued, Ambushers struck, foes were subdued.
Ammon and Moab turned on Seir, Destruction raged, none left to fear.
Judah arrived, the enemy lay still, Riches abandoned, treasures to fill.
For three days they gathered, so profound, In Beracah Valley, blessings resound.
Back to Jerusalem, joy in their hearts, Yahweh's victory, a new start.
Fear spread through lands, God's name renowned, Jehoshaphat reigned, peace all around.
He walked the way his father had paved, But high places remained, hearts unbraved.
His deeds recorded, written in lore, But joining with wicked, brought destruction's door.
Ships wrecked in the sea, plans fell apart, "Because of this alliance," Yahweh's word did impart.
Jehoshaphat laid down with his forebears in David's town, Jehoram took the throne, wore the crown, no frown.
Brothers on the side, sons of Jehoshaphat's line, Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, all in their prime.
Their father gave them gifts, silver and gold, Fortified cities in Judah, stories retold.
But Jehoram got the kingdom, firstborn's right claim, When he rose to power, he played a deadly game.
Strengthened his throne, but his heart was stone cold, Killed his brothers, the princes, for power to hold.
Jehoram at thirty-two, began his eight-year reign, Walked like Ahab's house, brought evil and pain.
Married Ahab’s daughter, led astray in God's sight, But Yahweh spared David's house, a promise of light.
Edom broke free, declared a king of their own, Jehoram struck by night, but his power wasn’t shown.
Edom and Libnah both turned away, For Jehoram had left Yahweh astray.
He built high places, made Judah fall, A letter from Elijah, God’s warning call:
"Yahweh says, ‘You walked the wrong track, Not like your fathers, now Yahweh strikes back."
A plague on your people, a sickness for you, Day by day, your bowels will fall through.
Philistines and Arabians, stirred up to invade, Took his sons, his wives, all Jehoram had made.
Yahweh struck Jehoram with pain so severe, Two years later, his death was near.
His bowels fell out, his sickness was grave, No burning for him, no kingly grave.
Thirty-two when he started, eight years he stayed, Departed without love, in a tomb unlaid.
In Jerusalem, the youngest son took the throne, Ahaziah was king; the oldest were gone, overthrown. Just forty-two when his reign began, One year in power, according to the plan.
His mom Athaliah, daughter of Omri's line, Counseled him in ways less than divine. He walked in Ahab's path, against God's sight, His father's death led him to wrong, not right.

Followed his counsel, went to battle with Joram, Against Hazael, king of Syria, they fought hard and long. Joram was wounded, needed healing in Jezreel, While Azariah came to visit, to see how he'd heal.
God planned Ahaziah's fall, a destined end, At Joram's side, with Jehu he did contend. Jehu, God's anointed, aimed to cut Ahab's tree, Judah's princes and Ahaziah's kin met their decree.

Ahaziah hid in Samaria, but Jehu found his place, Brought him out, killed him, but with respect to save face. “Son of Jehoshaphat, who sought God’s grace.” The kingdom slipped from his family's embrace.
Athaliah saw her son’s fate, Rose in fury to eliminate the state's heir's slate. But Jehoshabeath took Joash, hid him away, With a nurse in a bedroom, keeping death at bay.
For six years Joash was hidden in God's own space, While Athaliah ruled, unaware of his place. The tale ends with a boy protected from the foe, In the house of God, where true safety does grow.
In the seventh year, Jehoiada stood tall, Gathered captains, a covenant to call.
In Judah they roamed, Levites they found, Fathers of Israel, to Jerusalem they were bound.
In God’s house, a pact they did make, The king’s son must reign, Yahweh’s words at stake.
“Here’s the plan, a third of you on guard, Gatekeepers on Sabbath, be ready, stand hard.
A third at the king’s house, a third at the gate, Yahweh’s courts filled, let none be late.
Only priests and Levites inside may tread, Holy they are, by Yahweh’s words led.
The Levites surround the king with might, Weapons in hand, ready to fight.
Anyone intrudes, let them be slain, Stand by the king, through night and rain.”
Judah and Levites, obeyed every word, Jehoiada’s command they all heard.
Weapons of David to captains were passed, In God’s house, they stood firm and fast.
From right to left, they took their stand, Near altar and house, weapons in hand.
The king’s son crowned, covenant in place, Anointed with oil, cheers fill the space.
“Long live the king!” they shouted loud, Athaliah heard, mingled with the crowd.
She saw the king, by the pillar he stood, Trumpets blaring, joy in the neighborhood.
“Treason!” she cried, as she tore her clothes, But the captains moved in, as Jehoiada chose.
“Bring her out, but not in Yahweh’s hall, Who follows her dies, heed the call.”
At the horse gate, her life they did end, Jehoiada’s covenant they did defend.
To Baal’s house they went, tore it down, Destroyed altars, broke idols, took Baal’s crown.
Mattan the priest of Baal met his fate, Jehoiada’s order sealed the state.
Appointed officers in Yahweh’s halls, Singing and rejoicing echoed the walls.
Gatekeepers placed, the unclean denied, Yahweh’s house purified, sanctified.
With nobles and governors, they brought the king, To the throne of the kingdom where praises did ring.
Rejoicing echoed, the city at peace, Athaliah slain, her reign did cease.
Joash took the throne at just age seven, Forty years in Jerusalem, looking to heaven. His mama Zibiah, from Beersheba's lane, Joash did right, with Jehoiada's reign.
Jehoiada found him wives, two for his kin, With sons and daughters, his legacy did begin. Joash set his mind, God's house to restore, Called priests and Levites, for funds to explore.
"Go to Judah's towns, collect the dues, Repair God's house, no time to lose." But the Levites delayed, the king wasn't pleased, He asked Jehoiada, "Why was the task ceased?"
Athaliah's lot had done wicked deeds, Breaking God's house, serving their needs. The king ordered a chest outside the gate, Proclaimed through the land, "Bring Moses' rate."
Princes and people, joy in their heart, Filled up the chest, doing their part. Day by day, coin overflowed, Scribes and priests, the treasure bestowed.
Masons and carpenters, hired for the task, Iron and bronze, they rebuilt fast. God's house restored, standing tall and bright, A testament of faith, a glorious sight.
When it was finished, with funds still to spare, Vessels of gold and silver, they'd prepare. Offerings burned, God's praise and might, All through Jehoiada's days, a sacred light.
Jehoiada grew old, full of days he'd see, At one hundred thirty, he passed peacefully. Buried with kings, for the good he had done, His deeds for God, second to none.
But after his death, the story took a turn, Princes swayed Joash, God's house they did spurn. Asherah poles and idols they revered, Wrath fell on Judah, for they didn't hear.
Prophets came to call them back to faith, Yet they ignored, continuing their wraith. Zechariah stood, the Spirit in his say, "Why forsake God? He'll turn you away."
But they stoned him, on the king's decree, Joash forgot Jehoiada's loyalty. "May Yahweh see, and repay your way," Zechariah's words lingered that day.
Syrians arrived, with a tiny band, Judah's great army fell, by God's hand. Judgment on Joash, forsaking the Lord, His own servants struck, by the sword.
In his sickbed, Joash met his end, Buried in David's town, not with royal friends. Zabad and Jehozabad sealed his fate, Amaziah his son, the throne did await.
Amaziah took the throne at twenty-five, In Jerusalem, he ruled, kept the kingdom alive.
He did what was right, but his heart had a flaw, Yet he followed the path laid down by the law.
Avenging his father, he punished the crew, But spared all the children as the law said to do.
He gathered Judah, soldiers handpicked, Three hundred thousand with spears and shields, equipped.
Hired warriors from Israel, a hundred thousand strong, Paid them silver, but was it right or wrong?
A man of God came, spoke truth to the king, "Don't take Israel's army, they won't help you win.
God's got the power to help or take down, Trust in Him, and you’ll wear the crown."
Amaziah worried, "What about the silver I spent?" But God’s prophet said, "Much more can be sent."
So he sent Israel back, they left with a scowl, Their anger burned fierce, like a dog on the prowl.
Amaziah led Judah to the Valley of Salt, Struck ten thousand Seir, halted their assault.
Ten thousand alive were carried to rock, Thrown down, shattered, their bones did knock.
But the army sent home wasn't done, They raided Judah, plundered, won.
Amaziah returned with spoils of war, But bowed to false gods, Yahweh abhorred.
Yahweh sent a prophet with a burning word, "Why worship gods that didn't save their herd?"
Amaziah dismissed him, "Stop or be struck!" Prophet said, "God’s judgment, you'll self-destruct."
He challenged Joash, king of Israel's might, "Face me now, let's have a fight."
Joash replied, "You're a thistle, I'm the cedar, Stay home or fall, don't be so eager."
But Amaziah wouldn't heed, Pride drove him to mislead.
They met at Beth Shemesh, face to face, Judah defeated, lost the race.
Joash captured him, tore down the wall, Took treasure, made Jerusalem small.
Amaziah lived on, fifteen more years, The record of his reign, written through tears.
Once he turned from God, a plot was laid, In Lachish he died, his escape plan frayed.
Brought back on horses, laid him to rest, With his fathers, his story confessed.
In Judah, young Uzziah, just sixteen, Was crowned as king, stepping on the scene. He rebuilt Eloth, brought it back strong, After his father's reign, he came along.
For fifty-two years, he held the throne, With Jechiliah from Jerusalem, not alone. Did right by God, like his father taught, With Zechariah's guidance, wisdom he sought.
He waged war on Philistines, walls came down, Gath, Jabneh, Ashdod, he took that crown. Cities he built, lands he claimed, With God's help, his strength was famed.
Ammonites paid tribute, his name spread wide, From Judah to Egypt, power amplified. Towers in Jerusalem, strong and high, With cisterns and farms reaching to the sky.
His army vast, counted and arrayed, Three hundred thousand strong, ready and made. Weapons prepared, devices on the walls, His fame soared high, as strength recalls.
But pride came creeping when his power grew, Into the temple, incense he drew. Azariah and priests said, "No, you can't stay, It's for Aaron's sons to burn and pray."
Angry, he stood with censer in hand, Leprosy struck by God's command. Priests pushed him out, as his fate was sealed, A separate house, his end revealed.
Uzziah lived as a leper, cut off and alone, Jotham, his son, took on the throne. Isaiah wrote of his deeds, first and last, He was buried with kings, but his leprosy cast.
Though he was great, his fall was deep, In the field of kings, he now sleeps.
Jotham was young, just twenty-five when he took the throne, Sixteen years he reigned, Jerusalem was his zone.
His mom Jerushah, Zadok's daughter by name, Kept him steady on the path of righteous fame.
He did what's right in Yahweh's eyes, followed Uzziah's stride, But stayed out the temple; the people's corruption he couldn't hide.
Built the upper gate, Yahweh's house got some love, Fortified the wall, Ophel's heights soared above.
In Judah's hills, cities rose and spread, Fortresses and towers in the forests he led.
Fought Ammon's king, came out on top, Got silver, wheat, barley, their tribute wouldn't stop.
Mighty Jotham, for his ways were just, Before Yahweh, his faith was a must.
His wars, his ways, all written in the scroll, King of Israel and Judah, his story they told.
Reigned from twenty-five, sixteen years strong, Laid to rest in David's city, where he belongs.
Ahaz, his son, took the king's place, Jotham's legacy, a steady pace.
Ahaz was young, just twenty, when he took the throne, Reigned sixteen years, but his heart was cold as stone.
Didn't walk with Yahweh like his father, King David, Followed Israel's kings, with molten gods he played with.
Incense burned in Hinnom's valley, children in the fire, Mimicking nations Yahweh did expire.
Sacrificed on high places, hills, beneath green trees, Turned from Yahweh’s path, doing as he pleased.
So Yahweh handed him to Syria’s king, Struck him hard, captives they'd bring.
Pekah of Israel dealt a heavy blow, 120,000 valiant men, all fell low.
Zichri from Ephraim, a mighty foe, Killed the king’s son, the ruler, swift in woe.
Two hundred thousand taken, women, sons, and daughters, Plunder to Samaria, chaos in Judah falters.
Oded, a prophet, came to meet the host, “Yahweh’s anger on Judah, you've made a mighty boast.”
“Do you plan to enslave your kin as slaves? Remember your sins, let Yahweh’s wrath be waived.”
Ephraim's leaders stood, heads held high, “Don't bring captives here, or wrath will multiply.”
They clothed the naked, gave them food and drink, Anointed, carried, to the city of palms, they'd sink.
Ahaz cried to Assyria for aid, But Edomites and Philistines raided, unafraid.
Cities of Judah fell to the foe, Ahaz's missteps made Judah's strength go.
He stripped Yahweh's house, gave gifts to Assyria's king, But it brought no help, no strengthening.
In distress, Ahaz strayed further still, Sacrificed to Damascus gods, hoping they'd fulfill.
Ruined by false gods, Israel’s king, Ahaz closed Yahweh's temple, a dangerous thing.
Altars in every corner, incense to idols burned, Provoked Yahweh’s anger, but lessons weren’t learned.
All his acts, written down, from start to end, Ahaz slept with fathers, his reign at an end.
Hezekiah his son took the throne's embrace, Judah’s hope renewed, in a different place.
Hezekiah took the throne at twenty-five, In Jerusalem, he ruled, kept the faith alive.
First year, first month, he swung Yahweh's doors wide, With priests and Levites, he stood by their side.
"Listen up, Levites, sanctify your space, Cleanse Yahweh's house, no time to waste.
Our fathers failed, turned their backs in shame, Shut the doors, let out the flame.
Because of them, wrath came to our land, Now rise, be ministers, by His command."
Levites stood up, Mahath and Joel too, Along with their brothers, they knew what to do.
Sanctified themselves, followed the king's decree, To cleanse Yahweh's house, set His temple free.
Priests went deep, found filth to expel, Levites carried it out, to the Kidron well.
They started the month, worked eight days straight, By the sixteenth day, Yahweh's house was great.
"Yahweh's house is clean," to the king they said, "Every vessel restored, once left for dead."
Hezekiah rose early, gathered the crew, Bulls, rams, lambs, and goats, offerings made new.
Killed the bulls, sprinkled blood on the stone, Rams and lambs followed, altar's call was known.
Goats for sin, the priests laid their hands, Blood spilled on the altar, for all the land.
Levites took their place, cymbals in hand, With harps and trumpets, by the king's command.
Burnt offering began, Yahweh's song on high, Worship soared, lifted to the sky.
When offerings were done, they bowed low, Hezekiah commanded praises to flow.
"Now come near," said the king with zeal, "Bring sacrifices, thank offerings real."
Seventy bulls, a hundred rams they gave, Two hundred lambs, for Yahweh, brave.
Cattle, sheep, more than they could handle, Levites stepped up, lit the worship candle.
Priests few, Levites showed their heart, Burnt offerings in abundance, they played their part.
The service set, all in Yahweh's plan, Hezekiah rejoiced, for what God began.
The people cheered, for what swiftly came, Hezekiah's reign, glorifying Yahweh's name.
Hezekiah sent out the call to the land, To Judah and Israel, with letters in hand. “Come to Yahweh's house and keep the feast, Join us in Jerusalem, to say the least.”
Counsel was taken, the king had a plan, Passover in the second month for every clan. Priests not ready, people not there, But the king and assembly thought it fair.
From Beersheba to Dan, the word went wide, "Come to Yahweh, do not hide. Too long we've strayed from the ancient way, Now in great numbers, come and pray."
The couriers traveled with their decree, "Turn to Yahweh, and be free." "Don't be like your fathers, lost and stiff, Yield to Yahweh, let your spirits lift."
"Turn back to Yahweh, He's gracious and kind, Return to His mercy, peace you will find." Though some mocked and laughed with disdain, From Asher and Manasseh, some came again.
God's hand moved Judah, one heart, one mind, To follow the king's word, no one left behind. A great assembly for the unleavened bread, All altars cleared, Kidron swallowed their dread.
Passover was killed on the fourteenth day, Levites and priests in their ordered array. Though many unclean, Levites took their part, Hezekiah's prayer showed his heart.
"May Yahweh pardon those who seek His face, Even if unclean, grant them grace." Yahweh heard Hezekiah, healing ensued, Feast of gladness, hearts renewed.
Seven days of singing and praise, Levites and priests in joyful phase. Peace offerings made, confession done, Seven more days, the feast went on.
Hezekiah gave bulls and sheep, The people’s joy was true and deep. In Judah and Israel, voices raised, In Jerusalem, Yahweh was praised.
Since Solomon's days, no joy like this, Levitical priests blessed with heavenly bliss. Their prayers reached up to the throne, In God's holy place, they were known.
All Israel gathered, the scene was set, They broke down the pillars, no idol was left. Asherah poles and high places they tore, In Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and more.

Hezekiah stood tall, made the priests their divide, For offerings and praise, in Yahweh's courts they'd abide. The king's portion given, burnt offerings laid, Morning and evening, on Sabbaths displayed.
Jerusalem's folks were commanded to share, Gifts for the priests, so Yahweh's law they'd bear. With first fruits in plenty, the people complied, Grain, wine, and oil, their fields magnified.
Cattle and sheep, tithes were piled high, In the third month they started, by the seventh they'd fly. Hezekiah saw the heaps, blessed Yahweh's name, Asked the priests about the abundance that came.
Azariah spoke, “Yahweh's blessings overflow, We’ve more than enough, from His hand it does show.” Rooms in Yahweh’s house, Hezekiah had made, Offerings and tithes, in faith were laid.
Conaniah led, with Shimei his kin, Overseers named, keeping watch within. Kore at the gate, handled the free will, Eden and friends, their roles did fulfill.
For those in the house, from age three and above, Priests and Levites served, with duty and love. With all generations, they sanctified their way, With trust in their office, in holiness they'd stay.
Sons of Aaron, in pasture lands wide, Gave portions to priests, in every divide. Hezekiah's deeds, righteous before Yahweh, With heart full of zeal, he prospered each day.
Sennacherib marched, Judah in his sight, Hezekiah saw the threat, preparing for the fight. Princes and warriors, gathered for a plan, Stop the waters, leave the enemy in a jam.
"Why should Assyria find water to drink?" Hezekiah built the walls, made the city a strong link. Weapons crafted, shields in store, Captains appointed, warriors ready for war.
"Be strong, be bold, don’t fear his might, For Yahweh’s with us, in this fight. He's got flesh, but we’ve got the divine, Yahweh fights our battles, we'll be fine."
Sennacherib sent words, mockery and scorn, "Trust in your God, to be left forlorn? Hezekiah deceives, I’ll starve you all, No god has stopped me, watch your kingdom fall."
Taunts and letters, aimed to sow fear, But Hezekiah and Isaiah, in prayer sincere. Yahweh sent an angel, struck down the foe, Sennacherib fled, with shame in tow.
Back in his land, in his god's own place, His sons rose up, ended his disgrace. Yahweh saved Judah, gifts flowed in, Hezekiah praised, from lands he'd win.
Though he prospered, pride caused wrath to rise, Hezekiah humbled, in time grew wise. Riches and honor, in abundance shown, Yet Babylon’s questions left him alone.
Hezekiah passed, honored in death, Manasseh his son, took his final breath. Acts of a king, in the books they remain, A life of trust, through triumph and pain.

Manasseh was just a kid, twelve years old and green, When he took the throne, reigned like a king who'd never seen. Fifty-five long years in Jerusalem he stayed, But did evil in God's sight, in darkness he played.

He rebuilt the high places, Hezekiah had torn down, Raised Baals, made Asheroth, served the skies without a frown. Altars in God's house stood, despite His word— "My name shall rest in Jerusalem," His voice was heard.

But Manasseh turned from Yahweh’s eternal decree, Built altars for the skies, in God's courts they'd be. He even burned his children in Hinnom's fiery vale, Practiced dark arts and sorcery, like ships with evil sails.
He set an idol in the house where God said clear, "In this place forever, my name draws near. I'll keep Israel steady if they heed my command, The laws of Moses, observe and understand."
Judah was seduced, more wicked than before, More than nations Yahweh drove, they closed the righteous door. Yahweh spoke, but they turned a deaf ear, So Assyria's king came, bound Manasseh in fear.
Chained, distressed, in Babylon he cried, Begged Yahweh, humbled, God heard his side. Brought back to his kingdom, Manasseh knew, That Yahweh was God, steadfast and true.
He built a wall around David’s town's edge, Fortified Jerusalem, made a solemn pledge. Removed foreign gods, idols thrown away, Rebuilt Yahweh’s altar, peace offerings they'd lay.
Judah was told, "Serve Yahweh, the God of our land," But high places remained, despite the command. Manasseh’s story, his prayer and his fall, Written by the seers, a record of it all.
He slept with his fathers, his reign put to rest, Amon, his son, took the throne, not blessed. Amon followed the path of idols and stone, Did not humble like Manasseh, his heart was his own.
Servants conspired, took Amon's life away, But the people rose up, vengeance they did repay. Josiah, his son, was made king in his stead, A new chapter began, as the old was put to bed.
Josiah, just eight, took the throne with might, Reigned thirty-one years, doing what was right. Walked David's path, didn't stray left or right, In his eighth year, sought God with all his might.

At twelve, he purged altars, idols, and poles, Smashed them to dust, scattered on graves, took souls. Burned priests' bones, cleansed Judah through and through, Cities felt the change, as Josiah's vision grew.
In year eighteen, fixing God's house was the plan, Sent Shaphan and crew, to repair what they can. Gathered funds from Judah and Israel's hands, Paid workers and builders to restore God's lands.
Faithful men worked, Levites oversaw, Musicians, scribes, and guards, all in awe. Hilkiah found the law, Moses had penned, Passed to Shaphan, to the king it would send.
Shaphan read aloud, king tore his robe in grief, "Go seek Yahweh," he said, "find relief. Our fathers strayed, God's wrath is near, We must act now, make intentions clear."
To Huldah the prophetess, they ran quick, "Yahweh says, curses will stick. Forsaken, provoked, his anger won't dim, Wrath on this place, a fate so grim."
"But Josiah, tender heart, you will find peace, Gathered to your fathers, your days will cease. Your eyes spared from the evil I'll bring, Words returned to the king, a hopeful ring."
King gathered elders, all of Judah's lot, At Yahweh's house, the covenant he sought. Read to the people, great and small, Renewed their pledge to God's law, stood tall.
Cleared abominations, served Yahweh alone, In Josiah's days, God's love was known. Never departed from the path he laid, All his days, Yahweh's word was obeyed.
Josiah set the scene, Passover in full swing, Fourteenth day of the month, praises they would sing.
He placed the priests in their rightful place, Encouraged them to serve with steadfast grace.
To the Levites he spoke, in words so clear, "Put the ark in Solomon's house, have no fear.
No longer a burden on your shoulders to bear, Now serve Yahweh, His word declare."
"Prepare by your houses, your divisions stand tall, As David and Solomon wrote, heed their call.
Stand in the holy place, each tribe in line, For the Levites to serve, everything's fine."
"Kill the Passover, sanctify, prepare, For Yahweh's word through Moses we share."
Josiah gave lambs, young goats, thirty thousand strong, Three thousand bulls, to the people they belong.
Princes offered freely, to priests, Levites too, With livestock and cattle, their offerings they grew.
With Conaniah and brothers, Levites were fed, Five thousand small livestock, five hundred head.
The service was ready, priests took their spot, And Levites divided in lines that never forgot.
They killed the Passover, sprinkled blood with care, Levites skinned, prepared, and offerings they’d share.
Roasted the Passover, boiled pots of holy meat, Quickly served to the people, everything complete.
Priests worked, offerings burned, into the night, Levites prepared more, keeping it right.
Singers of Asaph sang in their place, Gatekeepers stood firm, never left their space.
All for Yahweh was done in a day, Offering burnt offerings, in their own way.
Children of Israel kept the feast of seven days, None like this Passover, Josiah's ways.
No king kept Passover with such a grand show, In the eighteenth year, Josiah let it flow.
Then Egypt’s king Neco rose for a fight, Josiah went out, ready to face the night.
Neco sent word, "This fight’s not with you, God’s commanded me, heed and be true."
Josiah ignored, went in disguise, In Megiddo’s valley, arrows did fly.
"Take me away," the wounded king cried, In his chariot, to Jerusalem he died.
Mourned by all Judah, they lamented in song, Jeremiah wept, their lamentations were long.
Josiah's deeds, from start to end, Written in books, remembered by friend.
They took Jehoahaz, Josiah's own kin, Made him king in Jerusalem, let the reign begin. But just three months, then Egypt came, Removed him, fined them, changed the game.
Eliakim, his brother, took the throne, Named Jehoiakim, but not his own. He reigned eleven years, did what was wrong, In God's sight, where he didn't belong.
Nebuchadnezzar came, put him in chains, Took him to Babylon with Yahweh's remains. The vessels of God’s house, they were taken too, Placed in Babylon's temple, where no light shone through.
Jehoiakim's story, written in the book, Jehoiachin, his son, a new king took. Eight years old, he reigned for a short while, Did evil in God's sight, a wayward style.
Nebuchadnezzar returned, took him away, With treasures from God’s house, no time to sway. Zedekiah, his brother, took the crown, Reigned eleven years, but brought God frown.
Rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar, broke his vow, Hardened his heart, wouldn’t bow. The priests and people polluted God's space, Mocked his messengers, turned from grace.
God's wrath rose, no remedy found, The king of Chaldeans brought them down. He killed the young, in the house so grand, Compassion lost, they fell to his hand.
God’s house burned, Jerusalem's wall fell, Palaces aflame, a story to tell. Those who escaped, taken to serve, In Babylon, they got what they deserve.
Seventy years, the land lay still, Sabbaths kept, by God’s will. Cyrus of Persia, his heart stirred right, Proclaimed aloud, put his words to light:
“Yahweh, the God of heaven, gave me the lands, To build him a house, with my own hands. Whoever is among you, rise and go, To Jerusalem, let your faith show.”
In Persia's land, Cyrus took the throne, God stirred his heart, he wasn't alone.
"Yahweh's word through Jeremiah's call, Now fulfilled, let the nations hear it all."
Cyrus declared, "The God of heaven's decree, Build Him a house in Jerusalem, let it be free."
"Who among you belongs to His clan, Rise up, and build, do all that you can."
"Those who remain, lend a hand, With silver, with gold, all at His command."
Judah and Benjamin's leaders rose, Priests and Levites, in spirit they chose.
Neighbors gave gifts, strengthened their way, Silver and gold, for the new day.
Cyrus brought out what Nebuchadnezzar stole, Yahweh’s vessels, once hidden in the fold.
Mithredath counted, to Sheshbazzar's hand, Gold and silver to rebuild the land.
Thirty gold platters, a thousand silver more, Twenty-nine knives, and bowls by the score.
Five thousand four hundred vessels in all, Sheshbazzar carried them back, heeded the call.
Captives from Babylon to Jerusalem went, To rebuild God's house—their hearts content.
They rose from captivity, a journey to start, From Babylon's grip, they were set apart. Led by Zerubbabel, they walked the line, Returning to the cities, a sign of the divine.
Children of Parosh, two thousand plus, Shephatiah's clan, three hundred a must. Arah’s seven hundred, nearly eight, Pahathmoab's thousands, carrying fate.
Elam, Zattu, Zaccai, they come, Bani, Bebai, marching like a drum. Azgad, Adonikam, numerals in the mix, Bigvai, Adin, Ater, in fixed.
Bethlehem’s children, a hundred strong, Netophah’s men, not left for long. Anathoth's group, counted right, Azmaveth’s few, they take flight.
Jericho, Lod, Hadid, Ono, Gathering their numbers, ready to go. A mighty assembly, rising like dawn, One by one, they journey on.
Priests and Levites, singers in tune, Gatekeepers stand, 'neath the moon. Temple servants, Solomon's line, Working together, a purpose divine.
"Don't eat," said the gov'nor, "until the time, The priest stands with Urim and Thummim, in their prime." Forty-two thousand, their numbers complete, With servants and singers, the sound was sweet.
Horses, mules, camels, donkeys in stride, A community together, a unified tide. Heads of households offered their wealth, For the house of God, they gave with stealth.
Gold and silver to the treasury pour, Priests and Levites, now restored. In their cities, they found a home, All Israel together, no longer to roam.
When the seventh month arrived, they gathered in the land, As one in Jerusalem, united they stand.
Jeshua and his crew, with Zerubbabel in line, Built an altar for offerings, a task divine.
Despite the fear from neighbors all around, They set the altar firm, on holy ground.
Morning and evening, the offerings rise, Obeying Moses’ law, under the skies.
Feast of booths they kept, as the scripture required, With daily offerings, they never tired.
The new moons and set feasts, offerings flowed, From the first of the month, the devotion showed.
But the temple's foundation remained untouched, While masons and carpenters were richly clutched.
To Sidon and Tyre, for cedar they paid, Following King Cyrus’ grant, the plans were laid.
In year two, month two, the work began to bloom, Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the Levites made room.
Oversight given to those twenty and above, Working on God's house, guided by love.
Jeshua and crew, with sons by their side, Directed the craftsmen with unified pride.
When the temple's foundation was finally placed, The priests and Levites sang and embraced.
With trumpets and cymbals, they praised Yahweh, "For His loving kindness endures," they'd say.
The people shouted, with a joy that was grand, As the temple's foundation, firm did stand.
Yet old men wept, for the first house they had known, Joy mixed with tears, in the cries that were shown.
Shouts of joy and weeping intertwined, The sound carried far, in Israel's mind.
The adversaries heard the temple was on the rise, Judah and Benjamin building, aiming for the skies.
They came to Zerubbabel, heads of the kin, Saying, "Let us join, we've worshipped where you've been."
But Zerubbabel and Jeshua, they stood their ground, "Your help we don't need, by the king's command, we're bound."
So the locals, they schemed, tried to weaken the hand, Hiring counselors, frustrating the plan.
Through Cyrus to Darius, they caused delay, Penning accusations in a crafty play.
In Ahasuerus' reign, they wrote with no shame, Saying, "Jerusalem’s rise will tarnish the king's name."
To Artaxerxes, they sent words in a Syrian script, Claimed, "This city builds bad, a power they'll equip."
"These Jews from you, they're rebellious and bold, They finish the walls, their defiance will unfold."
"We eat the palace salt, can't watch the king's disgrace, Search the records, see the rebels' past erase."
"If they finish, you'll lose beyond the river's span, Your grip on this land, will slip from your hand."
Artaxerxes heard, and with a decree, Ordered the work to stop, until further from me.
"Make sure the damage doesn't grow, Let no city rise until I say so."
The letter read, they rushed with force, To stop the building, they took their course.
God's house paused, the work ceased, Until Darius, the king released.
Prophets Haggai and Zechariah, they spoke real bold, To the Jews in Judah, God's story retold.
Zerubbabel and Jeshua, they rose to the call, Building God's house, with the prophets standing tall.
Then Tattenai came, asking, "Who gave you the right, To build up this house and finish it tight?"
They wanted names, the builders to find, But God's watchful eye, left them in a bind.
The elders didn't stop, they knew their cause, Till King Darius would give his applause.
A letter was sent, to the king in command, "To Darius, peace, from the river's land.
We saw the great work, stones laid with care, The house of God rising, in Judah's fair air.
We asked the elders, 'Who gave you this decree?' They replied, 'Servants of God, that's who we be.
The house once built by a king so grand, Destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar's hand.
Cyrus then decreed, in his first year's reign, To build it anew, in God's holy name.
The vessels of gold taken away, Cyrus returned them, for God's display.
Sheshbazzar came, foundations to lay, The work continues, still on the way.
Now, dear king, let it be known, Search your records and let truth be shown.
See if Cyrus decreed this plan, And send us your word as only you can."
Darius the king made a decree, search the Babylon vault, Found a scroll in Achmetha's palace, held in Media's halt.
Cyrus once decreed, "Build God's house, make it tall, Sixty cubits high and wide, its foundations won't fall.
Three layers of stone, new timber in the mix, From the king's own treasury, let's fix up these bricks.
Return the gold and silver Nebuchadnezzar stole, Back to Jerusalem's temple, place each in its role.
Tattenai and crew, stay away, let the Jews build, Let the elders and the governor see this prophecy fulfilled.
From the king's goods, let expenses flow, For bulls, rams, and lambs, as offerings to show.
Wheat, salt, wine, and oil, give it day by day, So the priests can pray for the king, keep obstacles away.
If you alter this decree, your house becomes a heap, Pulled beams for a gallows, punishment runs deep.
Let no king nor people touch this divine place, Darius' word stands strong, steady in its pace."
Tattenai obeyed, with diligence they moved, The elders of Jews built, by the prophets approved.
Finished on Adar's third day, in Darius' sixth year, Israel's children rejoiced, their dedication clear.
One hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs they brought, Twelve goats as a sin offering, by Moses' law were taught.
Priests and Levites in order, serving God's plan, Captivity's children kept Passover, as only they can.
Purified, they slaughtered for their brothers and kin, Those who sought Yahweh joined in, leaving filth and sin.
Seven days of unleavened bread, joy filled the air, God turned Assyria's heart, to aid them with care.
In the days of Artaxerxes, king's reign was wide, Ezra, son of Seraiah, had the law as his guide.
From Aaron's line, a priestly crew, Ezra rose, his mission true.
From Babylon he made his start, A scribe with wisdom, set apart.
The king said, "Ezra, go, take your crew, To Jerusalem, and do what you do."
With priests and Levites by his side, They journeyed forth, their faith as their guide.
"Take silver and gold, offerings bold, To honor the God whose stories are told."
Artaxerxes' decree was clear and grand, "Support Ezra, God's scribe, across the land."
"Need supplies? The king will provide, For God's house, let nothing be denied."
"No taxes for priests, the singers, the gate, Their service to God, we celebrate."
Ezra taught, with wisdom in hand, Judges to guide, in Yahweh's command.
"Whoever disobeys, let justice be swift, In law and in truth, let no one drift."
Praise to Yahweh, who moved the king's heart, To beautify His house, set apart.
Ezra felt strength, by God's hand was led, Gathered Israel's leaders as ahead they tread.
Gather 'round, let me tell you a tale, Of folks who left Babylon, set to sail.
In Artaxerxes’ reign, they left the land, Led by the heads, a strong, mighty band.
From Phinehas, Gershom took his place, Daniel from Ithamar joined the race.
David's line, it was Hattush who came, Shecaniah and Parosh, in the genealogy game.
Zechariah rolled with a hundred fifty men, Pahathmoab’s crew, two hundred, again.
Shecaniah's son brought three hundred strong, Adin's line came with fifty along.
Elam's group, seventy, marching tall, Shephatiah's eighty ready for the call.
From Joab, two eighteen in the pack, Shelomith's one sixty had their back.
Bebai’s Zechariah brought twenty-eight, Azgad's Johanan had a hundred ten in state.
Adonikam’s crew, last on the list, With Eliphelet, Jeuel, and Shemaiah, none missed.
Bigvai’s boys, seventy more to go, Gathered by the river Ahava’s flow.
For three days, encamped, we did wait, No Levites found, so we changed our fate.
Called for Eliezer, Ariel, Elnathan, too, A team of chiefs, teachers, knew what to do.
Sent them to Iddo, at Casiphia, to say, “We need ministers, for God's house, come our way.”
God's good hand brought us what we sought, Sherebiah and brothers, Levites they brought.
With Hashabiah, Jeshaiah, from Merari’s line, Two hundred twenty temple servants, all fine.
Called for a fast, by the river’s side, To seek God’s way, in Him to abide.
Ashamed to ask the king for soldiers strong, Told the king, “God’s hand guides us along.”
We fasted, we prayed, our God did bless, Twelve priests chosen, to manage the rest.
Silver, gold, vessels, weighed and pure, For God’s house, offerings to endure.
“Holy to Yahweh,” I told them straight, “Guard these gifts, till in Jerusalem’s gate.”
Priests and Levites took the precious load, To Jerusalem, along the winding road.
Departed from Ahava, God’s hand was sure, Delivered us safe, from bandits secure.
Arrived in Jerusalem, three days rest, On the fourth, counted treasures, all were blessed.
Burnt offerings given to God of Israel, Bulls, rams, lambs, goats, as the numbers tell.
Delivered king’s commissions, far and wide, Support for the people, with God’s house allied.
Princes came near, they had something to say, “Israel's folks have gone astray.
Priests and Levites, they're mixed with the rest, Canaanites and Hittites, they've failed the test.
Taking daughters, giving sons, that's the story, Princes themselves have led in this folly.”
When I heard, I tore my robe, pulled my hair with dread, Sat down motionless, feeling dead.
Those who feared God gathered 'round, In silence, we sat, no sound.
At the evening offering, I rose from my shame, Torn clothes and spirit, calling God's name.
Said, "My God, ashamed, I can barely lift my face, Our guilt's like a flood, filling every space.
From our fathers' days, we've been guilty and weak, Kings and priests, all laid low, can't even speak.
Yet a little grace, a remnant you gave, In our bondage, you reached out to save.
Though we're bondservants, you showed us love, Persian kings see us blessed from above.
You revived us, repaired your house, Built walls in Judah and Jerusalem, no more doubts.
Now what can we say, God, what can we do? We've forsaken commands, forgotten you.
The land's unclean, filled with wrong, Don't mix with them, stay strong.
In spite of our sins, you punished less, Yet we stray, breaking commandments, making a mess.
Would your anger consume, leave no trace? Stand before you, guilty, seeking grace.
God of Israel, righteous and true, We stand in guilt, but our remnant's from you."

Ezra wept before God's place, a sorrowful sight, Men, women, kids gathered, tears flowing all night. Shecaniah spoke up, "We've made a wrong move, Married foreign women, against God's groove. Yet hope remains, for Israel's not done, Let's make a deal with God, get the wrongs undone."

"Put away the wives, the children they bore, Follow the law, hear God's mighty roar. Stand up, be brave, this task is yours, We'll follow you, Ezra, for the cause." Ezra rose, made them all swear true, Priests, Levites, Israel, they all knew.

Ezra left God's house, no food or drink, Mourning the sins, he sat to think. A call went out through all the land, "Gather in three days, or lose what you hand. From Judah and Benjamin, they came with haste, In front of God's house, in the rain, they faced."

Ezra stood tall, "You've trespassed, it's clear, Separate from foreign wives, do not fear. Confess to Yahweh, make his pleasure your goal, Leave behind the wrong, cleanse your soul." The assembly cried, "We'll do as you said, But this takes time, the rain we dread."

"Let the leaders appoint, in cities they stay, Until God's fierce wrath is turned away." Yet Jonathan and Jahzeiah stood opposed, With Meshullam and Shabbethai, their case they closed. The children of captivity took it to heart, With Ezra's lead, they all played their part.

Month by month, they examined each case, Sons of priests found guilty, they embraced grace. They offered a ram, their guilt to atone, Step by step, they returned to their own. Names were listed, from tribes far and wide, Commitment to change, they did not hide.

All who married foreign, names were read, They put away their wives, on their knees they pled. Foreign wives, children, their ties were cut, To reconcile with God, the door was shut. In the end, they faced their wrongs, Israel's hope in repentance, forever strong.
Nehemiah speaks, son of Hacaliah's line, In Chislev's month, twentieth year, Susa's palace shine. Hanani, my brother, from Judah did arrive, I asked of the Jews, those who managed to survive.

"The remnant's in trouble," they said with a sigh, Jerusalem's walls, broken, gates burned, oh my! I heard it, I wept, couldn't hold back the tears, Fastened my heart to God, prayed through the years.
"God of heaven," I cried, "great and awesome you are, Keeping love and promise, never straying far. Hear my plea, open eyes, as I pray night and day, Confessing all sins that led us astray.
We broke your commands, corrupt through and through, Forgot the laws Moses taught us to pursue. Remember your promise, scattered if we stray, But if we return, you'll gather us one day."
"By your power, great and strong, you redeemed your own, These are your people, let your mercy be shown. Listen, Lord, to your servant's humble plea, Grant mercy now, as cupbearer I be."
In Nisan's month, in Artaxerxes’ reign, I served the wine, hiding my pain.
The king looked up, "Why so down? You’re not sick, yet you wear a frown."
Fear gripped my heart, but I spoke, "Long live the king!" My courage awoke.
"Why should I smile when my city’s in flame, Where my fathers lie, it’s not the same."
The king leaned in, "What do you seek?" So I prayed to God, my voice didn't squeak.
"If it pleases you, let me go, To rebuild my city, restore its glow."
The queen by his side, the king replied, “How long will you be on this ride?”
I set the time, and the king agreed, His favor was with me, indeed.
I asked for letters, to cross the streams, And timber for gates and temple beams.
Granted, his hand was kind to me, I thanked God for this decree.
To governors, I gave the letters in hand, With captains and horsemen, a strong band.
Sanballat and Tobiah, they frowned in spite, But for Jerusalem, I rode through the night.
Three days in Jerusalem, I kept it tight, With a few men, I moved in the night.
Through gates and walls, broken and charred, I inspected the city, though the journey was hard.
The rulers knew not where I went or why, I kept it secret, under the night sky.
Then I spoke to them, laying the plan, "See the ruins, let's build, if we can."
I shared God's hand and the king's decree, They said, "Let’s build, strong and free."
Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem heard, They mocked us, with spiteful word.
I stood firm, "God will aid our climb, You have no claim, not this time."
Eliashib, high priest, rose with his crew, Built the sheep gate, sanctified it too. Set up its doors, from Hammeah to Hananel's tower, With sacred might, they wielded holy power.
Next to him, Jericho's men took their place, Zaccur came with hammer, adding to the race. Hassenaah's sons built the fish gate, beams laid, Doors, bolts, and bars—every part displayed.
Meremoth, son of Uriah, took his turn, Meshullam, Berechiah's son, made it firm. Zadok, Baana's boy, fixed what he found, Tekoites repaired, their nobles stood down.
Joiada and Meshullam, old gate restored, Beams, doors, bolts, and bars—strength they poured. Melatiah from Gibeah, Jadon from Mizpah, Fixed the governor's place, working near and far.
Uzziel, the goldsmith, built beside the wall, Hananiah, the perfumer, answered the call. Rephaiah of Jerusalem's half did not fail, Jedaiah fixed up by his own house's trail.
Malchijah and Hasshub repaired more space, Tower of furnaces renewed in their pace. Shallum and daughters worked side by side, Building Jerusalem, their hearts open wide.
Hanun from Zanoah mended the valley gate, Next, Malchijah at the dung gate sealed fate. Shallun at the spring gate, pool of Shelah's shore, Repairing steps to David's city, they swore.
Nehemiah, Azbuk's son, fixed tombs of old, Levites joined in, their work bold and bold. Brothers of Keilah, repairing in their lands, Ezer of Mizpah, built with skilled hands.
Baruch, Zabbai's son, worked with a will, From Eliashib's door, the gap to fill. Priests from the plains took up their tools, Benjamin, Hasshub, keeping repair rules.
Azariah by his house, Binnui went on, Building walls strong, from dawn to dawn. Palal, standing firm by the king's court wall, Pedaiah, Parosh’s son, heard the call.
Temple servants in Ophel, eastward to the gate, Tekoites built more, they did not wait. Above the horse gate, priests did their job, Each one working, no time to sob.
Zadok, Immer's boy, at his house repaired, Shemaiah at the east gate, his duty declared. Hananiah, Hanun, and then Meshullam too, Repaired near their rooms, each work crew.
Malchijah, a goldsmith, merchants at the line, Between corners and sheep gate, they shone, divine. From goldsmith to merchant, the city was restored, Walls standing strong—a testament to the Lord.
Sanballat heard we were up on the wall, Got angry, indignant, mocked us all.
He sneered to his crew with a laugh and a jeer, "What can these weak Jews do here?
Will they build it up, can they sacrifice? Revive burnt stones from trash, ain't gonna suffice."
Tobiah chimed in, adding more to the plot, "Fox on their wall? It'll crumble on the spot."
We called out to God, "Hear us, we're despised, Turn their own shame on them, let it be realized.
Don't hide their sins, keep it clear in view, They insulted the builders, oh Lord, it's true."
But still we built, wall rising in height, With hearts full of purpose, our minds set right.
Enemies heard, they were seething with rage, Conspired to fight, make confusion their stage.
But we prayed to our God, set a watch day and night, Judah warned us, "Strength fades, rubble in sight."
Enemies whispered, "They won't see us creep, We'll stop their work, their dreams we'll sweep."
Neighbors warned us, "Beware, they're near, Wherever you turn, attacks will appear."
I posted guards low, in the open space, Families armed, ready to embrace.
I rose up and spoke, "Don't be afraid, Remember the Lord, let courage invade.
Fight for your kin, for your homes and your land, The Lord is mighty, take your stand."
Enemies found out, their plans fell apart, Back to the wall, with courage in our heart.
Half worked hard, while the others stood guard, Spears and shields ready, the task wasn't hard.
Builders worked with swords at their side, Trumpet bearer close, in us he relied.
I warned the people, "The wall is vast, When you hear the trumpet, gather fast.
God fights for us, don't lose sight, Work till stars appear, through the night."
No rest for us, our clothes stayed on, With our weapons ready from dusk till dawn.
The people cried out, voices loud in the night, "Too many mouths, not enough grain in sight."
Fields and vineyards, mortgaged away, Houses for bread, in famine's sway.
Borrowed money for the king's demand, Fields and vineyards slipped from our hand.
Flesh of our flesh, brothers the same, Children in bondage—oh, what a shame!
I burned with anger, heard their plea, Faced the nobles, confronted the greed.
"You take from your kin, charging them debt," Called a great meeting, their silence met.
"The act is wrong, should you not fear? Nations observe, their reproach is near."
"I lend them too, but without this weight, Let's end the usury, before it's too late."
"Restore their lands, their vineyards, give back, The hundredth part, remove the lack."
"We'll do as you say," they vowed and swore, I called the priests, they promised more.
Shook out my lap, a warning made clear, "God shake you out if you don't adhere."
"Amen," they cried, praised Yahweh's name, Kept their promise, upheld their claim.
As governor in Judah, twelve years spent, No bread of the governor, our labor lent.
Others took from the people's hand, But I feared God, worked the land.
At my table, the rulers sat, One hundred fifty, no land we spat.
Oxen, sheep, and wine were shared, For the people's burden, their welfare cared.
"Remember me, God, for the good I've done, For helping these people, every last one."
Enemies heard, the wall was done, no breaches left, not a single one. Sanballat and Geshem tried to sway, "Come to Ono, let's meet today."
They meant me harm, I saw the game, "Great work here, I can't be tamed." Four times they called, four times I said, "Why should the work stop? I'm ahead."
Fifth time's a letter, open wide, "Rebellion's brewing," they all lied. "King in Judah," they accuse, "Come, let's talk, you can't refuse."
I shot back fast, "You're making it up, None of these lies are gonna disrupt." They tried to scare us, weaken our hands, "God, make us strong, help us withstand."
Shemaiah spoke, a trap laid bare, "Hide in the temple, danger's there." "Should I flee?" I said, strong and bold, "I'll stay my ground, not be controlled."
God didn't send him, I saw the ploy, Tobiah and Sanballat's hired decoy. They wanted fear, wanted me to sin, "God, remember their evil spin."
And then we finished, the wall was high, in fifty-two days beneath the sky. Enemies trembled, nations shook, "God's work, His hand," they overlooked.
Judah's nobles wrote to Tobiah, his letters flew like a secret fire. Tied by marriage, they spoke him well, while he tried threats, their stories fell.
The wall was built, the doors set tight, Gatekeepers, singers, Levites in sight.
I put my brother Hanani and Hananiah there, In charge of Jerusalem, with faithful care.
To them I said, "Don't open the gates till it's hot, Bar the doors while guards watch the spot."
The city was wide, but not many stayed, Few homes were built, foundations had laid.
God whispered in my heart, a task He gave, Gather the nobles, write the names of the brave.
Found the book of those who came before, Out of Babylon, to their cities they swore.
Zerubbabel led, with Jeshua and more, Nehemiah, Azariah, and noble men galore.
Children of Parosh, two thousand strong, Shephatiah's crew, three seventy-two along.
Arah's lot, six-fifty-two in their stride, Pahathmoab's tribe, led by Jeshua, with pride.
Elam's sons, twelve hundred fifty-four, Zattu's kin, eight hundred forty-five more.
Counted them all, their numbers we knew, Israel's children, the faithful and true.
Priests, Levites, singers, and gates' crew, Temple servants and the rest came too.
Together they stood, forty-two thousand proud, Plus their servants, singing voices loud.
They had horses, mules, camels in line, Donkeys aplenty, all in time.
The heads of houses gave to the cause, Gold and silver, without pause.
Darics and minas, gifts they did bring, Priests' garments, a holy offering.
So priests and Levites in cities took place, In the seventh month, God's people, His grace.
In front of the water gate, they gathered tight, Ezra with the law, ready to recite.
Men, women, all who could understand, Listening closely, as he took the stand.
From morning light till midday sun, Ezra read the law, and the crowd was one.
On a wooden pulpit, he raised the book high, The people stood up, as if touching the sky.
"Bless Yahweh, the great God," Ezra exclaimed, “Amen, Amen,” the people proclaimed.
Heads bowed low, faces to the ground, In worship and awe, no sound but profound.
Jeshua and the Levites made the meaning clear, Each word of the law, they helped the people hear.
Nehemiah and Ezra, with the Levites beside, Told the people, “Don’t weep, don’t cry.”
“This day is holy, let joy be your might, Eat, drink, and share, in Yahweh’s light.”
The Levites calmed them, “Hold your peace, For this day’s sacred, let your worry cease.”
So they feasted and shared, joy in their hand, Understanding the words, they now could stand.
Next day, to Ezra, heads of families came, Studying the law, from which wisdom they’d claim.
Found in the law, a command they’d missed, “Live in booths during the festival twist.”
“Go gather branches, olive and palm, Build your shelters, stay calm.”
The people went out, they gathered the wood, Made shelters everywhere, as they understood.
From roofs to courts, the shelters stood tall, Since Jeshua’s days, they hadn’t done this at all.
Great was the gladness, from the old to the youth, Seven days of feast, in the joy of the truth.
Day by day, Ezra read from the law, On the eighth, they assembled, without a flaw.

On the twenty-fourth day of the month, they gathered in a scene, Fasting, wearing sackcloth, with dirt, they leaned. Israel stood apart, from foreigners they estranged, Confessed their sins, their fathers' wrongs, unchanged.
They stood up in place, reading the law's decree, A fourth of the day in worship, confessing earnestly. Jeshua, Bani, on the stairs they stepped, Cried to Yahweh, as their voices leapt.
"Stand up and bless Yahweh, our God forever praised, His glorious name, above all blessing raised! He's Yahweh alone, made heaven's high dome, Earth and its fullness, sea's endless foam."
He chose Abram, and called him Abraham, Found a faithful heart, made a covenant grand. The land promised, from Canaanite to Jebusite, Given to his seed, in God's righteous sight.
Saw their pain in Egypt, by the sea they cried, Signs and wonders against Pharaoh, in pride. Split the sea apart, on dry land they crossed, Their enemies drowned, in the waters tossed.
Pillar of cloud by day, fire by night, Guided them steady, in Yahweh's light. He came down at Sinai, gave right rules, Statutes and commands, through Moses' tools.
Bread from the sky, water from the stone, Promised land to take, as their own. But they turned proud, necks hardened and stiff, Ignored commandments, God's gifts they missed.
Made a calf of gold, "This is your God!" they cried, But Yahweh's mercy, stayed by their side. Pillar of cloud stayed, by night fire's glow, His Spirit instructed, manna did flow.
Forty years sustained, clothes and feet intact, Kingdoms and peoples, were their lands backed. Children multiplied, stars in the sky, Entered the land, promises not a lie.
Took cities and lands, filled with good things, Yet disobedient, they rebelled against the King. Prophets killed, laws cast aside, Delivered to foes, their cries amplified.
When they cried, God heard their plea, Sent saviors to set them free. But after rest, evil returned, Enemies ruled, lessons unlearned.
Yet God's mercy, never did cease, Though they turned away, He offered peace. Kings and priests, fathers too, Ignored commandments, hearts untrue.
"Behold, we're servants in this fruitful land, Kings hold power, as sin expands. In distress we stand, yet make a vow, A covenant sealed, before God now."
Sealed by Nehemiah, the governor, in the lead, Then Zedekiah, Seraiah, followed the creed.
Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur took their stand, With Amariah, Malchijah, a righteous band.
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, on the scroll, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, played their role.
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch stood tall, With Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, they call.
Maaziah, Bilgai, Shemaiah, the priests in line, Levites like Jeshua, strong, divine.
Binnui of Henadad, Kadmiel, the crew, Shebaniah, Hodiah, in faith they grew.
Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan add to the list, Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah, they persist.
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah again, Hodiah, Bani, Beninu, these were the men.
Chiefs of people: Parosh, Pahathmoab, stand, Elam, Zattu, Bani, strong in the land.
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai, names in the set, Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin, don’t forget.
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur, in their might, Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai, in the light.
Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai, in their place, Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir, in grace.
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua, they came, Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah, known by name.
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub, in line, Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek, divine.
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah, stand tall, Ahiah, Hanan, Anan, gave their all.
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah, closed the crew, The people, priests, Levites, all in view.
Separated from the lands, in God’s law they found, Moses' commandments, in unity, they’re bound.
“Don’t give our daughters to the land’s folk,” they swore, “Nor take theirs for our sons,” they vowed once more.
No buying goods on Sabbath, rest is the key, Every seventh year, debts forgiven, be free.
Yearly ordinances, a third of a shekel, For the house of God, where righteousness dwells.
Show bread, meal offerings, burnt offerings too, For Sabbaths, new moons, holy feasts, they knew.
Casting lots for the wood, by father’s decree, “Burn on Yahweh’s altar,” year by year, faithfully.
First fruits of ground, first fruits of trees, To Yahweh's house, as grateful as can be.
Firstborn sons, livestock, herds and flocks, To the priests who minister, all as the Law instructs.
First fruits of dough, wave offerings pure, New wine, oil, tithes, Levites ensure.
Priests and Levites, tithe upon tithe they bring, To the house of our God, where the praises ring.
Offerings of grain, new wine, and oil, In the sanctuary, their faith won’t spoil.
"We won’t forsake the house of our God," they say, In unity and strength, they’ll walk His way.
Princes in Jerusalem, that's where they stay, The rest cast lots, to see who'd make their way.
One in ten moved to the holy ground, While others in different cities were found.
Blessings on those who chose to dwell, In Jerusalem, where stories they’d tell.
Chiefs of the province, they took their stand, In city or country, they claimed their land.
Judah’s sons, like Athaiah, Uzziah’s seed, In Jerusalem, they lived, with courage and creed.
Maaseiah, from the line of Baruch he came, Sons of Perez, valiant, known by name.
Benjamin’s boys, led by Sallu with pride, Nine hundred twenty-eight, they reside.
Joel was overseer, Judah second in command, Together they ruled this sacred land.
Priests like Jedaiah, Seraiah, they served, God's house their realm, never unnerved.
Brothers worked, eight hundred twenty-two, Adaiah's clan, chiefs, stood strong and true.
Amashsai’s kin, mighty men indeed, One hundred twenty-eight, they lead.
Levites like Shemaiah, kept things intact, Shabbethai, Jozabad, with oversight exact.
Mattaniah began the thanks and prayer, Levites in the city, they were always there.
Gatekeepers like Akkub stood at the gate, One hundred seventy-two, they watched and wait.
In cities of Judah, others took their claim, Temple servants at Ophel, known by name.
Uzzi the overseer, making sure it’s right, Singers had provisions, every day and night.
Pethahiah by the king’s side, handling affairs, Children of Judah lived in towns with their cares.
From Kiriath Arba to Beth Pelet wide, Through Ziklag to En Rimmon, they reside.
Benjamin from Geba to Bethel’s ground, All these towns, their roots were found.
In fields and valleys, craftsmen laid their stake, From Levite divisions, new homes they’d make.
Zerubbabel's crew, they rose up with a shout, Priests and Levites, they were stepping out.
Leading the charge were Seraiah and Jeremiah, Ezra, Amariah, Malluch, Hattush, on fire.
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth, in line, Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah, shining fine.
Mijamin, Maadiah, and Bilgah in the game, Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah, carrying the flame.
Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, Jedaiah too, Heads of priests in Jeshua's days, they knew what to do.
Levites came next: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, With Judah, Mattaniah, they rang the thanksgiving bell.
Bakbukiah and Unno, their brothers close, In their appointed roles, they did the most.
Jeshua fathered Joiakim, who fathered Eliashib, Eliashib to Joiada, passing on the crib.
Joiada to Jonathan, his line did flow, Jonathan to Jaddua, steady as they go.
Priests in Joiakim's day, heads of homes, you see, Seraiah's house had Meraiah, Jeremiah had Hananiah, free.
