Ezra had Meshullam, Amariah had Jehohanan, Malluchi had Jonathan, Shebaniah had Joseph's clan.
Harim had Adna, Meraioth had Helkai's name, Iddo had Zechariah, Ginnethon had Meshullam's fame.
Abijah's son was Zichri, Miniamin and Moadiah's Piltai, Bilgah's line was Shammua, Shemaiah had Jehonathan nearby.
Joiarib's Mattenai, Jedaiah's Uzzi, Sallai's Kallai, Amok's Eber, flying high.
Hilkiah's Hashabiah, Jedaiah's Nethanel, Levites were recorded, like a story to tell.
Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, In praise and thanks, they did excel.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam strong, Gatekeepers guarding, where they belong.
In Joiakim's days, with Nehemiah, the boss, Ezra the scribe, no matter the loss.
Dedication day at Jerusalem's wall, Levites gathered, with glad thanksgivings all.
Singers from regions, villages they came, To praise with harps, and lift up God's name.
Priests and Levites purified all, People, gates, and wall — they stood tall.
Princes of Judah up on the wall, Two great companies, giving it their all.
One group to the right, toward the dung gate stride, Hoshaiah and half the princes walked with pride.
Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam in their lane, Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah, no shame.
Priests with trumpets, Zechariah leading the pack, Brothers with instruments, never looking back.
Ezra the scribe, leading the parade, To the water gate, east they'd invade.
The other company met them there, Half the people followed, climbing the stair.
Above Ephraim’s gate, the old gate they passed, Fish gate to sheep gate, standing steadfast.
Two companies gave thanks in God's own abode, Priests and singers, lifting the load.
Great sacrifices offered, joy so profound, Women, children, with joy they resound.
Rooms for treasures, offerings stored, Priests and Levites, their duty restored.
Singers, gatekeepers, according to command, David and Solomon, singing hand in hand.
In days of old, they praised God’s might, Zerubbabel, Nehemiah, kept it tight.
Portions to singers, gatekeepers they gave, Levites and Aaron’s sons, for whom they saved.
Opened the book, the words were read, The law was heard, here's what it said:
"Ammonites, Moabites, can't join this game, 'Cause bread and water they never came."
They hired Balaam to curse and fight, But God turned curses into blessings bright.
Heard the law, they took a stand, Separated the mixed from Israel's land.
Priest Eliashib, with Tobiah's hand, Gave him a room, in God's house it would stand.
But I wasn't there, I was with the king, Returned to see what this mess would bring.
Saw Eliashib's deed, Tobiah's domain, Threw out his stuff, to cleanse again.
Put God's vessels back in their place, Restored the offerings, to show His grace.
Levites' portions were gone, not paid, Left their work, to the fields they strayed.
I asked the rulers, "Why's God's house forsaken?" Brought them back, got the gears awaken'.
Tithes of grain, new wine, oil too, Stored in treasuries, where they were due.
Set the faithful to manage that stash, "Remember me, God, for my deeds, not trash."
Saw work on the Sabbath, carts rolling in, Testified against them, calling out sin.
"Why do this wrong, and profane the day?" I shut those gates, kept burdens away.
Warned those merchants camping round, "Stay away, or I'll bring you down."
Levites purified, guarding the gates, "Remember me, God, my kindness is great."
Saw Jews with wives from lands afar, Children’s tongues mixed, setting the bar.
Contended hard, plucked hair, and swore, "Don't mix daughters and sons anymore."
Solomon's tale, a lesson learned, Foreign wives his heart had turned.
Chased out the priest with foreign kin, "Remember them, God, the faults within."
Cleansed them from outsiders' sway, Set priests and Levites to work and pray.
Kept the offerings, first fruits, all good, "Remember me, God, I've done what I could."
Ahasuerus showed his kingdom’s riches, splendor on display / He feasted princes, officials for one hundred eighty days
Seven days all Susa feasted, royal wine aplenty / No guest was bound to drink; each cup could stay empty
On the seventh day, wine-merry, the king made his call / Seven eunuchs, bring Vashti with crown; show her beauty to all
Vashti refused the call; she would not comply / The king grew very angry, his anger rising high
The king asked wise men what the law required him to do / “Vashti disobeyed my order; what judgment is due?”
Memucan warned Persian princesses would repeat her tale / The wives would scorn their husbands; contempt would then prevail
Vashti must no more appear before the king’s face / Her royal estate goes to someone better in her place
Publish the decree: wives honor husbands, great and small / The king and princes approved Memucan’s call
His letters reached each province, carrying the decree / Each man should rule his household, speak as his people speak
When Ahasuerus’ wrath cooled, Vashti came to mind / He recalled her deed and the decree that cast her aside
His servants said, “Seek beautiful young women for the throne” / He approved; one would be queen, and Vashti’s place her own
In Susa, Jew Mordecai took his orphaned niece in / His uncle’s daughter Esther, whom he raised as kin
Young women were gathered; Esther was taken there / She was taken to the king’s house, in Hegai’s care
Hegai gave her food and maids, and moved her to the best / She hid her kin and people, as Mordecai had stressed
Mordecai walked daily, to learn how Esther fared / After twelve months’ preparation, her turn was declared
She took only what Hegai had advised / All who looked on her favored her, in their eyes
Ahasuerus loved her more than all the rest / He set the crown upon her head, and made her queen instead
The king held Esther’s feast, proclaimed a holiday / He then gave gifts by his bounty, in his royal way
Bigthan and Teresh plotted; Mordecai told Esther their aim / She told the king in his name; proved true, both hanged, as chronicles claim
King Ahasuerus raised Haman above princes in the land / The king’s gate servants bowed, as they were obeying the king’s demand
The king’s gate servants asked why he defied the decree / Mordecai told them he was a Jew; he would not bend the knee
Haman burned with wrath when Mordecai would not bow / He would not strike him alone; all Jews he’d overthrow
In Nisan, year twelve, before Haman the lots were cast / Adar, the twelfth month, it was chosen at last
He said their laws differed; they would not the king obey / He asked they be killed; silver to the treasury he’d pay
The king gave Haman his signet ring, and left the choice in his hand / “The silver and the people—do as you see fit,” was his command
Order written, sealed: all Jews would die that day / Young and old, children and women; goods stripped away
Couriers rushed; all peoples were told to be ready, says the text / The king and Haman sat down and drank; Susa was perplexed
When Mordecai heard the decree, he tore off his clothes / Jews throughout the provinces mourned, fasted, and wept for their woes
Esther heard Mordecai’s distress, sent clothes to change his gown / He would not take the clothes; he kept his sackcloth on
Esther sent Hathach to learn what had happened and why / He went to Mordecai in the square before the king’s gate nearby
He told Hathach of Haman’s promised sum for the king / He gave him Susa’s decree, urged Esther to plead for her kin
She said, “Uncalled, I may die unless golden scepter’s raised; / I have not been called by the king in these thirty days.”
Don’t think you’ll escape; silent, you and your father’s house won’t remain / Relief will come from elsewhere; perhaps this time you came to reign.
Susa’s Jews heard: “Fast for me three days, no food or drink, day or night / My maidens and I will fast; I’ll go against law, though I may die”
Mordecai went and did as Esther told him to do / He’d wailed loud in sackcloth and ashes, bitter too
On the third day, Queen Esther wore her royal array / She stood in the inner court; the king sat on his throne
The king held out the golden scepter, asked what she would want / She touched the tip; up to half his kingdom he would grant
She asked the king to bring Haman to the feast she’d made / He summoned Haman quickly; both arrived, as she bade
At wine, the king asked what petition she would declare / She asked them both to dine tomorrow at a feast she’d prepare
Haman left joyful; Mordecai sat at the gate / He would not rise or move for him; Haman’s wrath grew great
He called friends and wife; praised wealth, children, king-raised rank / Above princes, servants; twice sole guest, yet the Jew made it vain
They said, “Build fifty cubits high; tomorrow, tell the king / To hang Mordecai; then merrily go feast with him”
Their counsel pleased Haman; he approved their plan / Fifty cubits high, the gallows rose at his command
The king could not sleep that night; his rest had fled / He had the book of chronicles brought and read
Mordecai exposed the two gatekeepers’ plan / No honor had been done for him, the record made plain
Haman came to ask the king to hang Mordecai, his aim / The king asked what to do for the man he wished to acclaim
He thought the king meant him; proposed royal clothes to wear / Ride him through town on the king’s horse, proclaim his honor there
The king ordered Haman: take the horse and garments too / Go do all that you said for Mordecai the Jew
He dressed Mordecai, had him ride through the city square / He cried, “Thus shall be done to him whom the king delights to honor!”
Mordecai came back to gate; Haman mourned, head covered that day / Wife, wise men said: if Jewish, you'll fail; before him you'll fall, they say
While they were still talking, the king’s eunuchs appeared / They hurried Haman to the feast Esther had prepared
The king and Haman joined the queen’s banquet to dine / Again, up to half my kingdom, your wish I’ll assign.
She asked, “Spare my life, my people; let us remain / We’re sold to be destroyed, to perish, and be slain.”
The king demanded, “Who is he, and where does he reside?” / “Who dared presume this in his heart?” the monarch cried.
She named wicked Haman, adversary and foe / Before the king and queen, his fear began to show.
The king left for the palace garden in his wrath / Haman begged Esther for life, seeing the king’s wrath.
The king returned; Haman fell on the couch beside the queen / “Would he assault her here before me?” His face was screened.
At Haman’s home, fifty-cubit gallows for Mordecai stand / The king then said, “Hang him on it!”—that was his command.
They hanged Haman on the gallows he had made / The king’s wrath was pacified, its fury allayed.
The king gave Haman’s house to Esther; it was placed in her care / Mordecai got Haman’s ring; she put him over its affairs
With tears, she begged to stop Haman’s plot against her kin / He held the golden scepter out; she stood before him
Esther asked to reverse Haman’s letters, undo the plan / He said sealed decree can’t be reversed; write as you command
The Jews could gather, defend themselves with all of their might / Kill those who assail them, their women and children outright
The king’s name marked the decree; his ring sealed it for all / And it was sent through every province; all heard the king’s call
Couriers hurried with the decree, their royal horses sped / In Susa’s citadel, the decree was published and spread
Mordecai left in royal blue and white, a gold crown / Fine linen, purple robe; Susa shouted, glad through town
Across each province, the Jews did have feasts and days of cheer / Many among the peoples became Jews, since Jews were feared
As foes hoped to conquer, Jews gathered to withstand / The king’s officials helped; fear of Mordecai gripped the land
Five hundred men and Haman’s ten sons in Susa were slain / They left all plunder untouched; no spoils did they claim
The king heard Susa’s death toll, asked Esther what she sought / He vowed to grant whatever further wish she brought
She asked one more day for the Jews in Susa to fight / And Haman’s ten sons be hanged, their bodies raised high
The king consented; Haman’s sons were hanged at his command / Three hundred more in Susa fell; no plunder touched their hand
In other provinces, Jews fought, their lives at stake / Seventy-five thousand foes fell; no spoils they’d take
On Adar’s fourteenth, provincial Jews saw fighting cease / They rested, feasted, glad, and made the day a feast
In Susa, on the fifteenth, they laid their fighting down / They feasted in gladness, with joy and delight
From Mordecai, letters set the yearly date / Adar’s fourteenth and fifteenth: keep them to celebrate
They sent food to each other, gave gifts to those in need / Their sorrow turned to gladness, as Mordecai decreed
They kept the custom: Haman’s scheme had aimed to slay / He cast Pur, the lot, to choose the fatal day
They named those days Purim, from Pur, the lot they cast / Their descendants kept them through each generation that passed
Esther and Mordecai confirmed the custom they undertook / Her command concerning Purim was written in the book
King Ahasuerus laid tribute on the land / And on the islands of the sea, along each strand
The king’s power and might, Mordecai’s rise, are writ in rolls / The chronicles of Media and Persia’s kings record it all
Next to the king, great among Jews, his brothers’ acceptance was known / He sought his people’s good, spoke peace to descendants of his own
In Uz, Job was blameless, upright in his way / He feared God, turned from evil, kept it at bay
Seven sons, three daughters, vast herds and household great / No one in the East surpassed his vast estate
After feasts, Job sanctified them each in turn / He offered burnt gifts, lest his sons their God might spurn
Yahweh said Job stood blameless, upright, unmatched in worth / Satan came from walking back and forth across the earth
Does Job fear You for nothing? You hedge his house around / You bless his hands; his wealth and household both abound
“Touch all he owns; he’ll renounce You to Your face,” Satan declared / Yahweh put his goods in Satan’s power; Job himself was spared
Sabeans took oxen, donkeys; God’s fire burned sheep, servants slain / Chaldeans took the camels; each lone survivor came to explain
A great wind struck the four corners of the house and made it fall / His children ate and drank; the wreckage killed them all
Job tore his robe, shaved his head, then fell down / He worshiped there, his body on the ground
“Naked I came, naked I return; Yahweh gave and took away” / He blessed Yahweh’s name, sinned not; on God no blame did he lay
Satan said, “I walked the breadth of the land” / Among God’s sons before Yahweh, he came to stand
“None like Job: blameless, upright, fears God, turns from evil—no flaw” / Though you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause
“Skin for skin,” Satan says; all a man has he will give / “Touch bone and flesh; he’ll renounce you to your face just to live”
Yahweh said, “He’s in your hand; only his life you must spare” / Satan struck sores head to foot; Job sat in ashes, scraped with shard there
His wife asked, “Does your integrity still remain?” / She said, “Renounce God and die”; she made her meaning plain
Job said, “You speak like foolish women; should good be all we’ve got? / Should we not receive evil from God?” His lips sinned not
His friends came to comfort, but from afar could not recognize / They wept, tore their robes, tossed dust on their heads to the skies
They sat with Job on the ground seven days, seven nights / They spoke no word, for his grief was very great in their sight
Job cursed the day that saw him first brought to birth / And cursed the night that spoke of life conceived on earth
Let day become darkness, its light kept away / Let God from above not seek it, nor send a ray
Let death’s shadow and cloud claim that day as their own / Let blackness terrify it, its darkness made known
Let thick darkness seize night, bar it from the year / No joyful voice within; count it not in months here
Its twilight stars go dark; no morning can rise / It looks for the light, but no light meets its eyes
That dark night did not shut his mother’s womb’s door / Nor did it hide the trouble from his own eyes
Why didn’t I die from the womb, give up my breath? / Why did knees receive me, then nurse at the breast?
I would have lain down, been quiet, slept, and been at rest / With kings and counselors who built waste places for themselves
Or a hidden, untimely birth, unseen from the light / Where wicked cease their troubling; the weary rest outright
There prisoners find ease, beyond taskmasters’ command / The servant is free from his master’s demand
Why give light to the bitter, who long for death in vain? / They dig as for hidden treasure, rejoice when graves attained
Why is light for him whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in? / My fear comes; groans pour like water; no ease, no rest within.
If one ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved there? / Who can withhold himself from speaking? Who can forbear?
You instructed many, made weak hands firm and right, / Your words upheld the falling; feeble knees stood upright.
Now it has come to you; you faint beneath the strain, / It touches you; you’re troubled, shaken by the pain.
Is piety your confidence, a trust you hold secure? / Is integrity of your ways your hope that will endure?
Do guiltless perish, are the upright swept away? / Those plowing wrong and sowing trouble reap their pay.
By God’s breath they perish; his anger’s blast makes them die, / The fierce lion’s roar, young teeth break; old ones starve, cubs scatter wide.
My ear received a secret whisper in the night, / Night visions, deep sleep; fear shook bones; spirit passed my sight.
“Can mortal be more just than God, or purer than Maker? / He trusts not servants; charges angels with error.”
Crushed before the moth, in the dust-founded houses of clay, / Dawn to dusk destroyed, forever unregarded, they pass away.
Call now: is there anyone who’ll answer your cry? / Which holy one will you turn to for reply?
Resentment kills fools, brings their lives to an end; / Jealousy will kill the simple, leave them dead.
I saw a fool take root, then cursed his dwelling there; / His children crushed at the gate; the hungry stripped their share.
Affliction doesn’t spring from dust, nor trouble arise; / Man is born to trouble, as sparks fly upward through the skies.
As for me, I’d seek God, whose works none fathom or count; / I’d commit my cause to Him who sends rain on the ground.
He lifts the low, makes mourners safe, thwarts crafty plans outright; / He traps the wise in their craft; at noon they grope in the night.
He saves the needy from the sword their mouths can wield; / The poor have hope; injustice’s mouth is sealed.
Happy is the one God corrects, though He may wound; / He injures, binds; His hands make wounded ones sound.
Six troubles He’ll deliver; in seven, no evil draws near; / In famine, sword, tongue, ruin—you will not ever fear.
You’ll live at peace with fieldstones and the beasts that roam; / Your tent and fold stay safe, with nothing lacking at home.
Your offspring will be great, like grass across the plain; / You’ll come to your grave full of years, like sheaves of grain.
We searched these matters through and found them to be true; / Hear it, and know it for your good, as we say to you.
Oh, weigh all my anguish; lay calamity there / It outweighs sea-sands; my words were rash, I declare
His arrows are within; my spirit drinks poison inside / God’s terrors stand arrayed against me on every side
The wild donkey does not bray when grass is at its feet / The ox does not low over fodder set to eat
Can flavorless food be eaten unsalted? Is egg white bland? / My soul, it won’t touch them; loathsome food I cannot stand
I long for God to crush me, let His hand go free / Then cut me off, and let my life cease to be
My consolation: exult in pain that does not spare / I have not denied the words of the Holy One, I declare
What is my strength to wait? What end to patience be? / Am I stone, or bronze? No help; wisdom’s driven from me
To one ready to faint, a friend should be kind / Even to one who has left God's fear behind
My brothers deceive like brooks, black with ice; snow hides below / In the heat they vanish, leaving no water to flow
Caravans turn from the streams, then perish in the waste / Tema looks; Sheba’s companies wait in that place
Confident, they came distressed, then were confounded / You are nothing now; you see terror, are afraid
I never asked for gifts from you, nor begged your aid / Nor did I ask rescue from my foes or oppressors’ blade
Teach me, and I’ll hold my peace; make my error clear / What does your reproof reprove? Desperate words are air
You’d even cast lots for orphans, make your friend merchandise / Now look at me; return; my cause is right, no lies
A man is forced to labor upon the land / Are all his days like those of a hired hand?
Like a hireling longing for shade and his pay / Months of misery; nights weary me each day
I toss and turn all night until the dawn breaks through / My flesh wears worms and clods of dust; skin seals, then breaks anew
My days fly like a weaver’s shuttle, swiftly spun / Without any hope, they are spent; their course is run
My eye will see no good; my life’s a breath of air / Like clouds, the dead rise no more; you’ll look, but I’m not there
I will not stay silent; anguish makes me complain / Am I the sea or monster you must restrain?
My bed should comfort me; night dreams bring me strife / My soul chooses strangling, death rather than life
I loathe my life; don’t want forever; turn away / Why magnify me, visit each dawn, test all day?
Watcher of men, why do you mark me, a burden to me? / Why not pardon my sin? I’ll lie in dust; seek me, I won’t be.
Bildad asks, “How long will you keep speaking this way?” / “Are words from your mouth a mighty wind?” he says.
God does not twist justice; righteousness isn’t bent / If your children sinned against him, he gave them to their sin.
Seek God diligently; make your supplication / Ask past generations; learn their fathers’ instruction.
If you were pure and upright, God would wake for you / He’d make your righteous dwelling prosper anew.
Though your beginning was small, your latter end would grow / Shall they not teach you, tell you words their hearts bestow?
We are but of yesterday, know nothing; our days are a shadow / Their words come from the heart; shall they not teach you what they know?
Papyrus needs the mire; rushes need water to thrive / Those who forget God lose hope; their godless hopes won’t survive.
His confidence will break apart, a spider’s web / He leans upon his house; it will not stand, nor endure.
Green shoots spread through his garden; roots clasp the rock and stone / If destroyed, place denies him; others spring from earth alone.
God will not cast the blameless off, nor uphold the evildoers / He fills your mouth with laughter, your lips with shouts and cheers.
Those who hate you will be clothed with shame, put to disgrace / The tent of the wicked will be no more, erased.
Job knows it’s true, yet asks how man can stand in God’s sight, / How can a human be made just, and counted right?
If God contends, Job can’t reply one time in a thousand tries, / God’s wise in heart and mighty; who resists him and still thrives?
In anger, God removes the mountains from their base, / Before they know, he overturns them in their place.
He shakes the earth out of place; its pillars tremble below, / He seals the stars, commands the sun, and it will not rise or show.
He stretches out the heavens, treads the sea below, / He forms the constellations, works wonders none can know.
He goes past me unseen; I don’t perceive him passing through, / He snatches away; who can hinder him, or ask, “What do you do?”
His anger turns not back; Rahab’s helpers bend their knees, / How could Job argue? Even just, he has but pleas.
If Job called and God answered, he still would not believe, / That God had listened to his voice, though he heard reply.
God breaks him with a storm; no cause is there for all his pain, / He adds his wounds, denies him breath; bitterness remains.
If strength, he’s mighty; if justice, who’ll summon him to court? / Though blameless, Job’s own mouth would cut his defense short.
Job claims he’s blameless; he despises his own life, / He says, “I don’t respect myself”—that’s his reply.
It’s all the same: God destroys blameless and wicked alike, / If sudden scourge kills, he mocks the innocent’s trial outright.
The earth lies in the wicked’s hand; its judges hide their face, / If God is not the one, who’s responsible in this place?
Job’s days outrun a runner, swift ships cross the sea, / Like eagles swooping on their prey; no good they see.
If I forget my complaint, put off my sad face, cheer, / I fear all my sorrows; you won’t hold me innocent, I fear.
Though I wash myself with the snow and cleanse my hands with lye, / You’ll plunge me in the ditch; my own clothes abhor me thereby.
He’s not a man like Job; no umpire stands between them here, / If he withdraws his rod and dread, Job could speak without fear.
My soul is weary of life; complaint I give free rein / I speak in bitterness of soul, and voice my pain
Do not condemn me; show me why You contend / Why oppress Your handiwork, wicked counsel commend?
Do You have eyes of flesh, or see as mortals do? / Are Your days and years like ours, and search my sins too?
You know I am not wicked; You understand / No one can deliver me out of Your hand
Your hands have fashioned me, yet You tear me down / Remember clay You shaped; will You return me to ground?
Poured like milk, curdled like cheese, You clothed my flesh in skin / You knit bone and sinew, gave life, love and kindness, kept breath within
You hid these things within Your heart; if I sin, You mark my blame / You will not acquit me; if wicked, woe; if righteous, shame
When I lift my head, You hunt me like a lion’s prey / You renew witnesses, bring wrath; change and war fill my days
Why bring me from the womb? I wish I’d passed away / I’d been as though I had not, womb to grave that day
My days are few; leave me alone; grant comfort for a time / Before I go where none return, to darkness without light
Zophar asks if all your words should meet reply / Can boasting hush them when your mockery flies?
You say, “My doctrine is pure,” and make that claim / You say, “I am clean in your eyes,” you maintain
Would God show wisdom’s secrets, its two sides to you / He exacts less than your iniquity is due
His secrets are high as heaven; what can you know? / Deeper than Sheol, longer than earth, broader than seas below
If he passes, confines, or convenes court, who can oppose? / For he knows the false men, sees their wrong, though no heed he shows
Could an empty-headed man ever become wise? / When a wild donkey’s colt is born human, wisdom can rise
Set your heart aright; stretch out your hands his way / Put sin far from your hand and tents; send wrong away
You’ll forget your misery; recall it like waters swept away / Life clearer than noonday; darkness will be like morning’s ray
The wicked’s eyes will fail; no route remains to flee / Their hope is that the spirit will cease to be
You alone are the people, the only ones wise, / As though all wisdom itself with your passing dies.
I know as much as you; I’m not inferior, it’s clear, / I called on God; He answered; I, blameless, was jeered.
Those at ease scorn misfortune; it waits when their foot slips, / Robbers prosper; God-provokers feel safe, their god in their grips.
Ask beasts, birds, earth, and fish; they tell you the same, / Yahweh’s hand has done this; all creatures make it plain.
Each creature’s life and all mankind’s breath are in His hand, / The ear tests words; the palate tastes what nourishes man.
The aged have wisdom; their years teach what is true, / With God are wisdom, might, counsel, and understanding too.
God breaks what none can rebuild, keeps captives ever bound, / He holds back waters, or sends them to overturn the ground.
Both the deceived and deceiver are His; kings’ bonds unbound, / He belts kings, strips priests and counselors, fools judges, casts strong down.
Trusted speech He removes; elders’ insight He takes back, / The princes do face contempt; the belt of the strong hangs slack.
He uncovers deep things concealed beyond our sight, / Brings the shadow of death from darkness into light.
He enlarges nations, destroys them, leads captives away, / Their chiefs roam wilderness, grope in dark, stagger drunk, lose their way.
I've seen and heard it all; I understand it too / I know what you know; I am not inferior to you
I'd speak to the Almighty; my wish is plain and clear / I desire to reason with God; let him hear
You forge lies; physicians of no value, that's clear / Be wholly silent; then wisdom would appear
Will you lie for God, show partiality, take his side? / He'll surely reprove you for the bias you hide
His awesome majesty should make you stand afraid / Your sayings turn to ash; your defenses are clay
Be silent! Leave me alone; I have words to say / Let come on me what will; let it come my way
Why take my flesh in my teeth, as if to take a bite? / Why put my life in my hand, risking it outright?
He'll kill me; I have no hope, my prospects gone / Yet before him I'll maintain the ways I've known
This too is my salvation: that no godless man will come near / Listen carefully; let my declaration be in your ears
My case is set in order; I know that I am right / Who will contend with me? I'd hold my peace and die outright
Withdraw your hand; don't let your terror make me fear / Then call; I'll answer, or let me speak; you answer here
How many sins? Make known my guilt; why hide your face from view? / Why treat me as your enemy, chase leaves and stubble too?
You write bitter charges; my youth's old sins I bear / You set my feet in stocks, mark paths; I rot and wear away
Born of a woman, few days, full of trouble each day / He grows like a flower, cut down; a shadow fades away
Why fix your eyes on me, and bring me to your court? / No clean thing from unclean; not one can be brought forth
You fixed my days and bounds; their measure is set / Look away; let me rest till the hireling’s day is met
A cut-down tree can sprout again, though old roots lie below / The trunk dies in the ground; water-scent makes new boughs grow
A person dies and does not rise, like waters gone dry / He will not wake till heavens vanish from the sky
Hide me in Sheol till wrath is past; set time, remember me / I’d wait through all my warfare till release; you’d call, I’d answer thee
You count each step that I take; my sins stay in view / My disobedience is sealed in a bag by you
Mountains fall, rocks shift; streams wear stones down to ground / Torrents wash dust from the earth; you bring man’s hope down
His sons come to honor, are brought low; he won’t know / You prevail against him, change his face, then make him go
His flesh on him has pain; his body aches and groans / His soul within him mourns; its grief comes out in moans
He calls your words vain knowledge, an east wind’s roar, / He asks what good your speeches do, what are they for?
You do away with fear; devotion before God you impair; / Do you claim wisdom all your own, and no one else can compare?
Your iniquity teaches your mouth the crafty words you choose; / Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips accuse.
Were you the first man born before the hills arose? / Did you hear God’s secret counsel, all that wisdom knows?
Gray-haired men are older than your father by years; / Are God’s consolations too small for your ears?
Why does your heart carry you off, why do your eyes flare? / You turn your spirit against God, let your words declare.
No mortal ever born of woman is righteous or clean; / Even heavens fail God’s sight; the corrupt drink sin like a stream.
I’ll declare what I have seen, as wise men taught before; / Their fathers never hid it; they passed down this lore.
The wicked man writhes in pain throughout his days; / Even amid prosperity, terror sounds and stays.
He does not believe he’ll return from darkness; the sword waits near; / He wanders, asking, “Where is bread?”; the day of darkness waits there.
Distress and anguish make him afraid; they prevail, / Like a king prepared for battle, poised to assail.
He stretches out his hand against God, proud in his might; / He charges stiff-necked, with his thick shields held upright.
His face is covered with fat; he dwells in towns run down; / Lives in empty houses, soon reduced to heaps on the ground.
His wealth won’t last; he will not leave the dark’s sway; / Flame dries his branches; God’s breath blows him away.
Let him not trust in emptiness; self-deceived, its void he reaps; / His branch won’t turn green; unripe grapes drop, olive blooms from trees.
Godless company is barren; fire consumes bribery’s tents; / Conceive mischief, produce iniquity; deceit their heart invents.
You all are miserable comforters, I've heard / What makes you answer? Shall vain words have an end?
In your place, I could join words against you in speech / But I’d strengthen you with words; my lips would bring relief
Though I speak, my grief won’t subside; it stays with me / Though I forbear, no easing comes; I find no release
God wears me out; my company lies scattered, laid to waste / My leanness rises up as witness, testifies to my face
He tears me in wrath, pursues; teeth gnash, his eyes glare / They gape, strike my cheek in scorn, then gather there
He gives me to the wicked, breaks my ease, and wrecks my frame / He dashes me by my neck; ringed archers take their aim
I wear sewn sackcloth; press my horn down in the dust / My face red with weeping, dark lids; hands clean, prayer pure and just
Earth, don’t cover my blood; let my cry find no rest below / My witness is in heaven; he vouches for me on high
My friends scoff; my eyes pour tears to God, asking a favor / That he maintain man’s right with God and with his neighbor
In a few more years, my time to leave draws near / I’ll go the way from which none ever reappear
My spirit’s consumed; my days have dwindled to none / The grave is ready for me when my days are done
Mockers with me; my eye dwells on all their taunts / My gaze dwells on provocations that they flaunt
Give pledge; be collateral for me with yourself / Who is there who will strike hands with me? Who else?
You hid their hearts from understanding; you won’t exalt them at all / He who denounces friends for plunder: his children’s eyes fail
He made me a byword of the people; they spit in my face / Sorrow dims my eye; my body fades to shadow’s trace
Upright men stand amazed; the innocent resist the wrong / The righteous will hold their way; clean hands will keep growing strong
You all, come back; no wise man among you is in sight / My days are past; plans, heart-thoughts break; they call night day: “Light’s nigh”
If Sheol’s my house, couch in dark; rot father, worm mother, sister to me / Where is my hope? Who sees it descend to Sheol’s gates or dust with me?
Bildad asks, “How long will you hunt for words? Consider; then we’ll speak.” / “Should earth be forsaken for you, or rock moved from its seat?”
The wicked’s light is put out; no spark will glow / His lamp above him goes out; his tent lies dark below
His strength steps are shortened; his own counsel brings him low / His feet cast him in the mesh, where he wanders to and fro
A snare catches his heel; traps wait along the road ahead / From every side the terrors chase and drive him on in dread
His strength goes hungry; calamity waits at his side / Death’s firstborn devours his members from inside
He’s uprooted from his secure tent, to the king of terrors led / Sulfur is scattered over the home where he dwelled
His roots are dried up beneath him, withering away / His branch is cut off above him, left to decay
His memory perishes from earth; his name fades out of sight / He’s driven from light into darkness, banished outright
No son or grandson remains, nor any where he lived before / Those after are astonished; those before were frightened more
How long will you with words torment and crush me? / Ten times you've reproached me, unashamed to attack me
If truly I have erred, the fault is mine, you see / You magnify yourselves, plead my reproach against me
God has overthrown me, laid me low upon the ground / He has surrounded me with his net, bound tightly round
I cry of wrong, unheard; for help, no justice comes at all / He walled my way so I can't pass; darkness is the wall
He stripped me of my glory, took my crown and brought me down / He plucked my hope up like a tree, roots torn out of the ground
His wrath is kindled; he counts me as his foe / His troops build siege ramps round my tent and camp below
My friends whom I loved abhor me, have turned away / Those in my house and my maids see a stranger where I stay
My breath offends my wife; my servant gives no reply / My mother's children loathe me; young children scorn me when I rise
My bones cling to my skin and to my flesh beneath / And I have escaped by the skin of my teeth
Have pity, my friends; God's hand has touched me—hear my plea / Why persecute me as God, not satisfied with my flesh?
Oh, that my words were written, inscribed in a book for all time / With iron pen and lead, engraved in rock, each line
I know my Redeemer lives; at last on earth he'll stand / After my skin is destroyed, I'll see God in my flesh, firsthand
My heart is consumed; if you say, “We’ll persecute him,” beware / Fear the sword: wrath brings sword's punishments; know judgment is there
Haste and reproof that shame me stir my thoughts to reply / My spirit of understanding answers me inside
Since man was placed on earth, this truth has held its sway / The wicked triumph briefly; godless joy fades away
His head may touch the clouds; like dung, forever he perishes / Those who have seen him will say, “Where is he?”—he vanishes
He flies away like dreams, chased off like visions at night / The eye sees him no more; his place is lost from sight
His children will seek the favor of the poor / His hands return the wealth that they held before
Wickedness tastes sweet, concealed beneath his tongue / It turns to cobra venom; his bowels are stung
He swallows riches, then he vomits out his store / God casts them from his belly; they are his no more
They won't look at rivers of honey and butter that flow / They will give back what they have labored for, with no joy to show
He oppressed and forsook the poor, seized a house by force / He will not build it up again, and that is his course
He knew no quiet; devoured all, his wealth could not stay / In fullness, distress will come; those in misery come his way
As he fills his belly, God’s wrath rains while he eats / He flees the iron; bronze pierces through; its point from his liver comes into view
Darkness waits for his treasures; fire consumes his tent / Heaven reveals his guilt; earth rises in dissent
His house’s increase departs; they rush away / The wicked’s lot God sets, his heritage that day
The wicked’s portion is the heritage God willed / His heritage is the portion God willed
Listen closely to my speech; let this console you / Allow me first to speak; then mock when I am through
Why shouldn't I be impatient? Is my complaint to man? / Look at me and be astonished; on your mouth lay your hand
When I remember, I am troubled, full of distress / Horror takes a firm hold over all of my flesh
Why do the wicked live so long and grow in might? / Their children stand secure, established in their sight
Their houses safe from fear; God's rod is not on them / Their bulls breed without fail; cows calve, they don't miscarry
They send their little ones like flocks; their children dance / They sing with harp and tambourine, rejoice at pipe’s sound
They spend their days in prosperity and ease / In an instant they go down to Sheol beneath
They tell God, “Depart from us; we reject your ways” / “Who is the Almighty? Why serve? What profit if we pray?”
Their prosperity is not within their own hand / The wicked’s counsel stays far from where I stand
How often their lamp goes out; God sends sorrows in wrath? / How often are they stubble, like chaff swept away?
You say God stores his guilt for children; let him know it / He repays it to himself; sees ruin, drinks wrath’s hard blow
Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges those who are high? / In his full strength, being at ease and wholly quiet, one dies
His pails brim full of milk; his marrow is moist / Another dies bitter, tastes no good; worms cover both in dust
I know your thoughts, the plans with which you'd wrong me / You ask where prince's house and wicked tent might be
He’s borne to the grave; men watch; valley clods lie sweet / How can your nonsense comfort me? Your answers are deceit
Can human righteousness benefit God in any way? / The wise benefit themselves, Eliphaz says.
Your piety is not why God calls you to account; / Your wickedness is great, your sins beyond all count.
You took your brothers’ pledges though no debt was owed; / You stripped the naked, left them bare and exposed.
You gave no water to the weary, left them dry; / You kept bread from the hungry and passed them by.
You sent the widows away empty, with nothing to share; / You broke the fatherless arms, their strength impaired.
Snares surround you; sudden fear comes from all sides; / And darkness, so you cannot see, as floods cover your eyes.
You say, “What does God know? Can he judge through the night? / Thick clouds conceal him; he walks the sky from sight.”
Don’t follow wicked men, swept off in their prime; / Their foundation was poured out like a stream.
They said, “Depart from us; what can the Almighty do?” / Their houses filled with good; their counsel I eschew.
The righteous see and are glad; the innocent mock their foes; / They say the fire consumed their remnant, laid them low.
Be at peace with him; receive the words he imparts; / Take instruction from his mouth and lay it in your heart.
Return to the Almighty; let unrighteousness go; / Lay Ophir’s gold in dust among the stones where brooks flow.
The Almighty will be your treasure and hear your prayer; / He’ll establish your decrees and make your way clear.
When they cast down, you say, “Be lifted up,” and command; / He saves the humble; the guilty are freed through your clean hands.
My complaint stays rebellious, though I am groaning / His hand stays heavy still despite all of my groans
I’d set my cause in order, my arguments prepared / I’d know the words he’d answer, understand what he declared
Would he contend by force? No, but he would listen to me / The upright could reason; from my judge I’d be free eternally
East or west, I search; I cannot find him there / North or south, I look; no glimpse of him anywhere
God knows the path I take, each turn along the road / Through testing I will come out shining like the gold
My foot held fast his steps; I never turned away / His words I treasured more than food I need each day
He stands alone; who can oppose him? What he desires, he does / He performs what’s set for me; many such things are with him too
God made my heart grow faint; his presence fills me with fright / I wasn’t cut off before dark; thick darkness stayed in sight
Why has the Almighty not set times, made things clear? / Why don’t those who know him see his days appear?
They move the landmarks, then seize flocks beyond the hedge; / They take the orphan’s donkey, widow’s ox as pledge.
They drive the needy aside till the poor go and hide; / Like wild donkeys they range; the wild keeps their young supplied.
They glean the wicked man’s vineyard, sleep naked in the cold; / They cling to rocks for shelter, arms around the stone they hold.
They carry sheaves, hungry, stripped bare beneath the sky; / They tread the winepress, thirsty, their mouths gone dry.
In crowded streets, men groan; the wounded cry aloud; / But God does not regard their folly, though cries resound.
They rebel against the light; the murderer rises with light; / He kills the poor and needy by day; by night he’s thief-like.
At twilight adulterers wait, disguising their face; / Others break into houses at night, by day hide in place.
Their morning’s thick darkness; like foam on water, they fade; / The womb forgets; worms feed them; widows get no aid.
God keeps the mighty by his power; the unsure are raised; / He grants them safety, keeps his eyes upon their ways.
They stand exalted, soon brought low, cut off like grain; / Who proves me a liar, makes all my speech seem vain?
Dominion and fear are with him; he makes peace / In his high places
Can his armies be counted? / On whom does his light not arise?
How then can man be just with God? / How can one born of a woman be clean?
Even in his sight the moon has no brightness / And the stars are not at all pure in his sight
How much less, then, is the man who is a worm / The son of man, who is the one who is a worm!
How have you counseled the witless, declared sound knowledge true? / To whom have you uttered your words? Whose spirit came from you?
Sheol is naked before God, and it is laid bare / Abaddon has no covering anywhere
He stretches out the north across the empty space / He hangs the earth on nothing, with no support in place
He binds the waters in his thick clouds, held in air / The cloud is not burst beneath them, hanging there
Heaven's pillars tremble, astonished at his rebuke / He stirs up the sea and he pierces Rahab through
These are the outskirts of his ways, a whisper small / His thunderous power—who can comprehend it all?
As God lives, He took my right, made my soul feel pain / My life and God's own spirit still within me remain
I will not speak unrighteousness, nor deceit, nor justify you / Till the day I die, I'll hold my righteousness, steady and true
Let my enemy be as the wicked, through and through / Let him who rises against me be unrighteous too
What hope has godless man when God takes life away? / Will God hear his cry when trouble comes his way?
I'll teach you God's hand; conceal nothing that is shown / You've seen it all; why has your vanity grown?
The wicked's grim portion comes from God, the Most High / Their children face the sword; their widows make no cry
Though he heaps silver like dust, prepares clothes to wear / The just put them on; the innocent divide his share
His moth-like house is like a booth that is a shelter slight / He lies down rich, won't do so again; opens his eyes, gone from sight
Terrors like waters overtake; a storm steals him in the night / A storm steals him; the east winds do bear him off in flight
Men clap their hands at him, palms beating the air / They hiss him from his place, driving him elsewhere
Silver is mined; gold is refined until it glows / Iron and copper are drawn from the earth below
He drives through the dark to its farthest edge out of sight / He seeks hidden stones thick darkness keeps from the light
He sinks a deep shaft where the settled folk fade away / Forgotten miners hang far from people and sway
Earth yields its bread above; below, it burns like fire / Its rocks yield sapphires; gold dust rests there entire
No falcon sees the hidden path, though keen its eye / No proud beast, nor fierce lion, ever passes by
He breaks flint, uproots mountains, sees each treasure in stone / He cuts channels, binds streams; hidden things are brought to light
Where will wisdom be found, where does it abide? / Where is understanding’s place, where does it reside?
Man does not know its worth; the living cannot tell / The deep says, “Not in me”; the sea says, “Not here as well”
Gold, silver, Ophir’s wealth can’t buy wisdom’s worth / No jewel equals its price; above rubies on earth
Wisdom is hidden from the eyes of all who live / Even the birds in the sky cannot perceive
Destruction and Death say, “We’ve heard a report” / Of wisdom, a rumor they heard with their ears
God knows wisdom’s way and its place, and searches it out / Sees earth’s ends, sets wind’s force, measures water, rain, lightning’s route
He tells man, “Fear of the Lord is wisdom; this truth is known” / “To depart from evil is understanding shown”
I long for the old days, when God watched over me / His lamp lit my head; its light led me through dark to see
God’s friendship filled my tent; the Almighty stayed near / My children gathered round; oil streamed from the rock for me
At the city gate, young men hid; the aged stood tall / I took my seat; princes fell silent, saying nothing at all
I rescued the poor and fatherless when they cried / I helped the widow; her heart sang, her joy revived
Righteousness clothed me like a robe, wrapped all around / My justice was as a robe, a diadem on my crown
I was eyes to the blind, and I was feet to the lame / A father to the needy; I pursued the stranger’s claim
I broke the jaws of the unrighteous, and freed their prey / I plucked the prey from their teeth and took it away
I said I’d die in my own house, count days like grains of sand / Roots spread by waters, dew on my branch, bow renewed in hand
Men waited in silence for my counsel, every word / My speech fell on them; their mouths drank rain, as they heard
I smiled on them when they had no confidence that day / They did not reject my face’s light, nor turn away
I chose the way for them and sat as their chief / A king among the troops, I comforted those who grieve
Young men whose fathers I deemed unfit beside my sheep dogs / Now mock me, sing me as their byword, heap scorn
Gaunt, hungry outcasts gnaw dry ground, eat salt herbs, then roots of broom / They hide in frightful valleys, rock holes, in waste and gloom
I am their song, their byword, held in disgrace / They shun me, stand aloof, and spit into my face
He loosed his cord, afflicted me; they cast restraint away / At my right hand, the rabble rise and thrust my feet askew
They burst through the breach; terrors chase my honor in flight / My welfare passes like a cloud, then fades away
My soul pours out; days of affliction seize my frame / At night my bones are pierced; gnawing pains won’t wane
My garment’s warped by force, and binds me like a collar / He casts me into mire; like dust and ashes I fall
I cry to you; you do not answer my plea / I do stand up, and you do gaze upon me
You turned cruel to me; with your mighty hand you persecute me / You lift me to the wind; the storm dissolves me completely
I know that you will bring me to death, as all must go / To the house appointed for all the living below
Who wouldn’t reach a hand, or cry for help in distress? / I wept for the troubled; for needy, I grieved no less
I looked for good; I waited for light, but evil came / My troubled heart has no respite; darkness came
I mourn without the sun; in assembly I cry for help / Jackals are my brothers; ostrich companion am I
My skin grows black and peels; my bones burn in the heat / My harp is mourning; my pipe voices those who weep
I made a covenant with my eyes: no lustful sight / How then look lustfully at a young woman with delight?
Is calamity the wicked’s portion, disaster for them all? / God sees my ways, and counts every step, both great and small
If I have walked in falsehood, hurried toward deceit / Let God weigh me in even scales, know my integrity
If my heart chased my eyes, defilement clung to my hands / Then let another eat; uproot the crop from my lands
If enticed, I waited at my neighbor’s door / Let others sleep with my wife; let fire consume my store
If I despised my servants’ cause, what answer when God stands? / He made us both within the womb, shaped by his hands
If I withheld from poor and widow, ate my meal alone / The fatherless grew up with me, as with a father of his own
If I saw the needy unclothed, no covering to keep / If his heart blessed me not, nor warmed by my sheep
If raised my hand to the fatherless, let shoulder and arm break / God’s calamity brings terror; before his majesty I quake
If gold was my hope, and fine gold was my confidence / If wealth made me rejoice, my hand had gained abundance
If sun or moon enticed me, hand cast kisses toward the sky / The judges would punish this: I’d deny the God on high
When evil found my hater, I did not rise in pride / Nor curse him, ask his life; I kept that wish aside
My tent folk asked, “Who has not been filled with my meat?” / I opened doors to travelers, not leaving them in the street
If like Adam I hid my wrong, fearing the crowd’s blame / Kept silent, terrified by families’ contempt and shame
I long for someone to hear; my signature is here / Almighty, answer; accuser, write my indictment clear
I’d carry it upon my shoulder, as I have said / And I would bind it like a crown around my head
I’d declare each step to him, the number as I stride / As a prince I’d draw near to him, and be standing at his side
If I took fruit unpaid, or its owners lost their lives / Let briers replace the wheat, stinkweed grow where barley thrives
Job justified himself rather than God; Elihu’s wrath burned / His friends gave him no answer, yet condemned him in turn
He held back, for they were older; gave them their say / He said that days should speak, and years teach wisdom’s way
Within man is a spirit; the Almighty gives insight / Greatness isn’t wisdom; age may not discern what is right
Listen to me; I too will tell you what I know / I’ll offer my own view, and let my judgment show
I gave you full attention as you searched for words to say / Yet none convinced Job or answered him, not they
Don’t claim, “We’ve found wisdom”; God may refute, not men / He spoke no words against me; I won’t answer him with them
They stand amazed, answer no more; no word is heard / Should I keep waiting while you stand and say no word?
The spirit within me presses; words fill my chest / I must speak now; its force will not be suppressed
My breast, whose words are pent, is wine with no vent / Like new wineskins, ready to burst, with pressure pent
I’ll speak and be refreshed; I won’t let rank hold sway / I know not how to flatter; else Maker takes me away
Elihu asks Job to hear the words he says / His upright heart speaks sincerely in each phrase
The Spirit of God made me; by breath I live / I open my mouth; my tongue has words to give
Job, answer; I too was formed from the clay / Set your words in order; now stand up and say
I won’t bring terror; no weight on you I’ll lay / My pressure won’t be heavy; you need not be afraid
You say, “I’m clean, no disobedience, innocent; no wrong in me / He finds cause against me, counts me foe; stocks feet, marks all paths, you see”
Elihu says your claim is wrong; you’re not right / For God is greater than all mankind in might
Why strive with God? He gives no account of His ways / He speaks once, yes twice, though people heed not what He says
In dreams and night visions, when deep sleep comes to men / He opens their ears, seals instruction in them
He withdraws man from purpose, hides pride from his sight / He keeps back his soul from the pit, his life from sword’s bite
Pain racks him there on his bed; his flesh grows thin / His bones jut out; his soul nears the pit within
If one angel in a thousand shows what is fit / God grants him grace: “I found ransom; release him from the pit”
His flesh grows fresh again, like a child made new / He sees God’s face with joy; his righteousness renewed
He sings, “I sinned, strayed from what was right; it brought no gain / He redeemed my soul from the pit; my life sees light again”
God does these things twice, yes three times, to restore / A soul from the pit, to the light of the living once more
Job, answer if you can; I wish to justify your case / If not, hold your peace; I will teach you wisdom’s ways
Wise men with knowledge, hear; weigh each word you've heard / The ear tests words as the palate tastes what’s served
Choose what is right; let us make that our sure guide / Know what is good; discern it on every side
Job says, “I’m righteous; God has taken away my right” / “My wound won’t heal; though blameless, I’m called a liar outright”
Who drinks scorn like water? Elihu says of Job / He walks with workers of wrong, with wicked men in tow
He says delight in God brings no profit at all / That is Job’s own claim, as Elihu recalls
God surely does no wickedness; that is not His way / The Almighty will not pervert justice; that is plain
He repays each person according to the work they do / He calls a king “Vile!” and nobles “Wicked!” too
No one appointed God to rule the earth below / If He gathers breath and spirit, all flesh to dust will go
Should one who hates justice be fit to lead? / Can anyone condemn the righteous, mighty God indeed?
All are His handiwork; no prince or rich outranks the poor / At midnight, the mighty are taken without hands; they are no more
His eyes watch every road that human feet have trod / No darkness hides the wicked from the seeing God
He breaks the mighty, puts new rulers where they stood / At night He overturns them, destroys them for good
They turned from Him, ignored His ways, and would not heed / He has heard the poor and the afflicted in their need
When He gives quiet, who can condemn? Who can withstand? / When He hides His face, who sees? He rules nation and man
Has anyone told God, “I’m guilty; no more will I offend”? / “Teach me what I don’t see; if I have done wrong, not again”?
The wise say Job speaks without knowledge, his words unwise / Elihu wants him tried to the end for wicked replies
He adds rebellion to his sin, claps hands among our men / Against God he multiplies his words again and again
Elihu asks if Job says his righteousness exceeds God’s own; / What profit would you gain compared with sin alone?
Look to the skies; behold, they rise beyond your height; / I’ll answer you and your companions outright.
Your sin or right gives God no gain, nor gift from your own hand; / Your wickedness may hurt a man; your right may help mankind.
By many oppressions, under the mighty arm, they cry; / No one says, “Where is God my Maker?” as their cries arise.
The Maker gives them songs at night, and teaches them to be wise; / He makes them wiser than the beasts and birds beneath the skies.
Because of evil men’s pride, their cries receive no reply; / Surely the Almighty will not hear an empty cry.
Your cause is before God though you say he’s not in view; / Yet you wait for him, as Elihu says you do.
God has not come in anger, nor greatly regards your proud display; / Job speaks empty talk, multiplies words without knowledge, they say.
Bear with me a little; I’ll show you what I know / I still have words on God’s behalf; there’s more to show
From far away I draw my knowledge, this I share / My Maker’s righteousness is what I declare
God is mighty, despises none, strong in understanding’s might / He won’t preserve the wicked; the afflicted get their right
His eyes stay on the righteous, keeping watch each day / He sets kings on their thrones forever, lifts them high
When fetters bind them, cords of pain hold them in thrall / He shows their work and sins, their pride laid bare to all
He opens ears to instruction; calls them to return / From their iniquity, and heed the lesson learned
If they listen, serve, their days prosper, years bring delight / Those who won’t listen die by the sword, without insight
The godless in heart store anger, held within / When bound, they do not cry for help, nor make a din
They die in youth; among the unclean, their lives disappear / He saves the afflicted through their pain, opens ears to hear
He’d draw you from distress to a wide place, unbound / Your table full of fatness, with plenty around
Your wicked judgment grips you; let no riches stir your wrath / Nor bribes turn you aside; can wealth or strength sustain in distress?
Don’t desire the night when people are cut off where they stay / You chose iniquity, not affliction, your way
God’s power is exalted; who can teach him? None can / His works are sung, seen from afar; his years no man can scan
He draws up drops of water, then the vapors pour rain / The skies rain down in plenty; who can clouds and thunder explain?
He spreads his light around; covers the sea’s floor / He judges people, gives abundant food and more
He covers his hands with lightning; commands it to strike its mark / Its noise tells of him; the livestock warn of storms that start
At this my heart trembles, moved out of place by his voice / Hear the sound that pours from his mouth, a thundering noise
God's voice rolls beneath the whole sky, resounding wide / His lightning reaches earth's far ends, from side to side
God's voice thunders marvelously, majestic in its roll / Great things exceed all human thought; no mind can grasp the whole
He orders snow and rain; seals hands to show all men / The animals take cover, remain within their dens
The storm comes from its chamber; north winds bring the chill / God's breath gives ice; the waters' width lies frozen still
He loads thick clouds with moisture; lightning turns at his will / For correction, his land, or kindness, his commands fulfill
Job, listen; stand still; consider what God has done / His works are wondrous; his knowledge perfect, second to none
Can you tell how God does steer the clouds and the lightning in flight? / Your clothes warm when south winds still earth; can you spread sky, mirror-bright?
Darkness has barred our case; we cannot make our plea / Tell him I would speak—or should a man wish swallowed to be?
Men don't see the bright sky-light till the wind clears / From the north comes golden splendor, then it appears
We cannot reach the Almighty, exalted in power afar / He won't oppress; men revere him; the wise of heart he won't regard
From the whirlwind Yahweh answers Job, rebuking words unwise; / “Who darkens counsel, speaking without knowledge?” he replies.
Brace yourself like a man; prepare for what I ask. / I will question you; then answer me—your task.
Where were you when I laid earth’s foundations in their place? / Who set its measures, stretched the line across its face?
What holds earth’s foundations? Who laid its cornerstone? / The morning stars sang; God’s sons shouted joy as one.
He shut the sea behind doors as it burst from the womb. / He clothed it in clouds, wrapped it in thick darkness and gloom.
He marked its bounds, set bars and doors, restrained its proud roar. / “You may come here, but no further”; its waves stop at the shore.
Have you commanded morning, made dawn shine its light? / To seize the far ends of earth, shake wicked from sight?
Have you entered sea’s springs, walked the deep below? / Seen death’s gates, grasped earth’s width—do you know?
Do you know where light dwells, where the darkness stays? / Surely you know—you were born then, your days are great.
I keep snow and hail in treasuries, reserved for war; / For days of trouble, days of battle, held in store.
Who directs lightning, scatters east winds as they blow? / Who cuts flood channels, paths where thunderstorm waters flow?
I send rain where no man lives, where wastelands lie; / To satisfy the waste and make tender grass rise.
Does rain have a father, who fathers drops of dew? / Whose womb brought ice and gray frost, while the deep froze through?
Can you ever bind the Pleiades, or loosen Orion’s tie? / Lead stars in season; guide Bear and her cubs through the sky?
Do you know heaven’s laws, their rule over the land? / Can you establish their dominion by command?
Can you call clouds, that abundant waters may cover you? / Can lightning say, “Here?” Who gives minds wisdom, understanding too?
Who counts the clouds, pours out the sky’s containers in a mass? / As the dust runs into a mass, the clods of earth stick fast.
Who provides prey for lioness and young lions in their lair? / Who feeds the raven’s young, who cry to God and wander without fare?
Does Job know when mountain goats give birth in the wild? / Can he watch the doe bear fawns as they come to life?
Can Job count the months they fulfill, know when they’re born? / They go out from the field and never come back home.
Who loosed the wild donkey’s bonds, who set it free to run? / Wilderness and salt land are its home beneath the sun.
It scorns the city’s clamor, ignores the driver’s cry. / It searches mountain ranges for green things growing high.
The wild ox will not serve at Job’s trough on demand. / Nor till the valley furrows at the urging of his hand.
Can Job trust the ox to bring home his seed to his door? / Will it gather the grain from the threshing floor?
The ostrich waves its wings with pride beneath the sky. / She leaves her eggs on earth, warms them in the dust where they lie.
She forgets that feet may crush the eggs upon the ground. / Wild animals may trample them wherever they are found.
She deals harshly with her young, as though they were not hers. / Though her labor is in vain, she has no fears.
God denied her wisdom, withheld understanding too. / When she rises, she scorns the horse and rider in view.
Did Job give the horse its might and quivering mane? / Does it leap like locust, rejoice in strength, unrestrained?
It goes out to meet armed men, the sword cannot dismay. / It mocks at fear, unshaken; it will not turn away.
Quiver, spear, and trumpet fail to make it veer. / It snorts, scents battle afar, hears captains’ thunder clear.
Can Job command the hawk to fly south, or make the eagle rise? / From cliffs it spies prey afar; its young drink blood as prey dies?
Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? Speak / He who argues with God, let him answer; let him speak
I am of small account; my hand seals my mouth / I spoke once, then twice; now no more words come out
From the whirlwind, Yahweh says, brace yourself like a man / I will question you; you will answer me then
Can you annul my judgment, condemn me, claim you’re right? / Can you wield God’s arm, thunder with a voice of might?
Deck yourself with honor, majesty; bring the proud ones low / Crush the wicked in their place; hide them in dust below
Then I’ll admit your own right hand can save you / Behold Behemoth; as well as you, I made
He eats grass like an ox; his strength is in his thighs / His force is in his belly muscles, where it lies
His tail moves like a cedar; his thigh sinews knit together / His bones are like tubes of bronze; his limbs are bars of iron
He is the chief of the ways of God; his Maker gives his sword / The one who made him gives him that sword, as the text has told
Mountains feed him; in reeds and marsh beneath lotuses he lies / Lotuses shade him; brook willows surround him on all sides
Though Jordan swells to his mouth, he does not tremble or fear / Can anyone seize him on watch, pierce his nose with a snare?
Can you hook Leviathan, press his tongue down with a cord? / Rope his nose, pierce his jaw—will he plead or speak soft words?
Will he make a covenant with you, be your servant forever? / Would you play with him as a bird, bind him for your girls ever?
Will traders barter for him, divide him among merchants? / Can barbed irons fill his skin, his head with fish spears?
Lay hand on him, remember the battle, do so no more; / Behold, his hope is vain; who won’t fall at the sight?
None is so fierce he dares stir him up, or challenge him to fight; / Who then can stand before Me, when none can match My might?
Who has first given to Me, that I should repay? / Everything under the heavens is Mine, I say.
I won’t keep silent on his limbs, his strength, his frame; / Who strips his outer garment, enters his jaws all the same?
Who can open the doors of his face? Terror rings his teeth; / Strong scales are his pride, shut close and sealed beneath.
One lies so near another, no air can pass between; / They stick together, can’t be pulled apart, firm and clean.
His sneeze flashes light; his eyes are morning’s start; / From his mouth, torches and sparks leap out in a bright burst.
From his nostrils smoke rises like a pot over reeds; / His breath kindles coals; flame from his mouth proceeds.
His neck is strong; before him terror starts to dance; / His flesh is joined and firm, unmoved by advance.
His heart is as firm as a stone, as firm as a millstone; / When he rises, mighty men retreat before his thrashing alone.
No sword or spear or dart, nor pointed shaft can win; / He counts iron as straw, bronze as rotten wood again.
Arrows can’t make him flee; sling stones are chaff; / Clubs are stubble; he laughs at javelins rushing past.
His underside is sharp potsherds, mud-trail like a threshing sledge; / He boils the deep, the sea like ointment; his shining path leaves a trace.
On earth there is no equal, made without fear; / He sees all that is high; pride’s sons have their king here.
You can do all things; no power can block your way / No purpose of yours can be restrained or swayed
You asked, “Who hides counsel with no knowledge to show?” / I spoke of wonders too great for me; I didn’t know
My ears had heard of you; now my eye sees you clear / I abhor myself, repent; in dust and ashes, laid bare
Your wrath at Eliphaz and his friends burned, you said / They spoke not rightly of you; Job spoke right instead
Take seven bulls and seven rams; burnt offerings bring to me / Let Job pray for you; I will accept him and his plea
Yahweh gave Job twice what he had when he prayed for them / His kin and old friends shared bread, comforted him
God doubled Job’s former wealth; ten children filled his home / His daughters got inheritance alongside brothers of their own
Job lived hundred forty years; four generations he'd behold / He died old, full of days; his life complete, his story told
He walks not in the wicked's counsel, blessed is the man / Nor stands on sinners' path, nor sits where scoffers stand
He delights in Yahweh’s law, and ponders it by daylight / He meditates upon that law throughout the night
Like a tree planted by streams, its fruit in season grows / Its leaf does not wither; all he does prospers as it goes
The wicked are not so, unlike the righteous tree / The wind blows all their chaff away upon the breeze
The wicked cannot stand when judgment they must face / Nor sinners join the righteous in their gathering place
Yahweh knows the righteous way; its path is known to him / The wicked way will perish; its course will end for them
Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain? / Kings, rulers stand against Yahweh, his Anointed they align
“Let’s break their bonds apart,” the rulers all cry / “And cast their cords from us,” they say in reply
The One enthroned in heaven laughs, then speaks in anger / His anger terrifies them; his words bring danger
Yahweh has set his King on Zion, as decreed / I will tell of the words that Yahweh spoke to me
Yahweh declares, “You are my Son,” to me / “Today I have become your Father,” says he
Ask me, and nations, earth’s farthest ends are yours to own / With iron rod, dash them to pieces, like potter’s vessels thrown
Be wise, you kings; earth’s judges, be instructed, take heed / Serve Yahweh with fear; rejoice with trembling indeed
Wrath soon kindled; give the Son homage, lest you perish on your way / Blessed are all who take refuge in him, safe there to stay
O Yahweh, foes increase and rise against me / Many say, “No help for him in God,” they believe
You shield me all around, my glory, my pride / You are the one who lifts my head up so high
I cry aloud to Yahweh, my voice raised high / From his holy hill, he answers when I cry
I laid myself down and slept; I awoke from sleep / Yahweh still sustains me, and my life he keeps
Ten thousand stand against me on every side / I will not fear them, though they stand on every side
Yahweh, arise, save me, my God; you struck all foes on the cheek / You broke the teeth of the wicked; all their teeth
Salvation belongs to Yahweh; salvation is his / May your blessing rest on your people, Yahweh
God of my righteousness, answer me when I call / Give me relief from distress; show mercy, hear my plea
Sons of men, how long turn my glory into shame? / Will you love vanity, seek falsehood just the same?
Yahweh has set the godly apart for himself / Yahweh will hear me when I call out to him
Stand in awe, and do not sin in what you do / Search your own heart on your bed; be still there too
Offer righteous sacrifices; do what is right / Put your trust in Yahweh; rely on his might
Many cry, “Who will show us any kind of good?” / Yahweh, let your face’s light shine on us, as it should
You have put great gladness deep within my heart / More than their grain and their new wine can impart
I lie down and sleep in peace, feeling secure / For Yahweh alone will keep me safe and sure
My King and my God, hear my cry as I pray / Give ear to my words; consider what I say
At dawn I lay all my requests before you / I watch expectantly to see what you will do
You take no pleasure in evil; it has no place / The arrogant cannot stand before your face
Your abundant loving kindness brings me through the door / Toward your holy temple, I bow and adore
Because of my enemies, lead me in what is right / Make your road straight before me, plain to my sight
Their throats are open tombs; their hearts are bent to sin / They flatter with their tongues; no faithfulness within
Hold them guilty; let their own counsels be their downfall / They rebel against you; thrust them out, one and all
All who take refuge in you find joy that abounds / You shield the righteous with favor all around
Yahweh, don’t rebuke me in your anger’s reign / Nor discipline me within your wrath’s domain
Have mercy, Yahweh; I am so faint and sore / Heal me; my bones are troubled to the core
My soul is also in great anguish, Yahweh / But you, Yahweh—how long shall it be, how long?
Return, Yahweh; deliver my soul, set it free / Save me for your loving kindness; hear my plea
For in death there is no memory of you, Yahweh / In Sheol, who will thank you? Who can give reply?
Weary with groaning, each night I flood my bed / I drench my couch with the tears that I have shed
My eye wastes away because of grief; it grows / It grows old because of all my adversaries, foes
Yahweh, he has heard my weeping and accepts my prayer; depart / Evildoers; foes turn back, suddenly shamed, dismayed, disgraced
Yahweh, my God, I take refuge; save and deliver me / From all who pursue, lest they tear my soul like a lion, none to rescue
If guilt is in my hands, if I repaid my friend unjust / Let my foe pursue, overtake; tread life and glory into dust
Arise, Yahweh, in anger; face my foes; awake; judgment decreed / The gathered peoples circle you; rule them on high
You judge the peoples; judge my cause by what is right / Assess my integrity; weigh it in your sight
Let wickedness of wicked end; establish those upright / The righteous God searches their hearts and minds outright
My shield is God; the upright in heart he will save / God is a righteous Judge, indignant every day
The unrepentant sharpens sword, bends and strings his bow / He prepares death’s tools and readies flaming arrows to go
He labors with iniquity, conceives mischief, brings falsehood forth / He digs a pit and falls in; his trouble strikes his head, violence crowns
His trouble turns back on him; he falls in the pit he made / His violence comes down upon the crown of his own head
According to Yahweh’s righteousness, my thanks I raise / I sing praise to Yahweh Most High, his name I praise
Yahweh, our Lord, your name is majestic through the land / Your glory set above the heavens by your hand
From infants’ lips, you establish strength; your foes go still / The enemy and avenger silenced by your will
The moon and stars, your fingers’ work, are set in space / When I consider your heavens, I behold their place
What is humankind, that you keep us in your mind? / What is the son of man, that you care for him?
You make him a little lower than angels in rank / And you have crowned him with the glory and the honor
You make him ruler over the works of your hand / All things you put beneath his feet, there they are laid
All sheep and cattle, field beasts and birds of the sky / Fish of the sea and all that pass its paths by
With all my heart I thank Yahweh, tell all his wonders with joy / Most High, I’m glad and rejoice in you; sing praise with my voice
My foes turn back, then stumble, perish in Yahweh’s sight / He upholds my just cause and judges all things upright
Yahweh rebukes the nations; the wicked are overthrown / He blots their names; their cities’ histories are unknown
Yahweh reigns forever, seated on the judgment throne / He judges the world and peoples right, his uprightness shown
Yahweh’s high tower for oppressed in trouble, standing true / Those knowing your name trust you; you forsake not those who seek you
Sing praise to Yahweh in Zion; declare his deeds to all / Avenges blood, remembers them; forgets not afflicted’s call
Have mercy, Yahweh; see foes afflict me, lift me from death’s gates / At daughter Zion’s gates I’ll praise; your salvation I celebrate
Yahweh, why stand far off when trouble draws near? / Why hide yourself when times of trouble are here?
The wicked hunt the weak, their arrogance on show / Their schemes catch them, the plans they themselves sow
He prospers all the time; God has no place inside / Your laws are far from sight; he sneers at foes with pride
His mouth pours curses, deceit, oppression; mischief fills his tongue / He lies like a lion in ambush, nets the helpless one
The helpless collapse, crushed beneath his strength; they fall / He says, “God’s forgotten; he hides, sees nothing at all.”
Arise, Yahweh, God, lift up your hand today / Don’t forget the helpless, and don’t turn away
You see their grief and trouble; take it in your hand / Help victim and the fatherless; break the wicked’s arm
King Yahweh reigns forever; nations perish from his land / Hears, prepares humble hearts; judges orphans, oppressed; no terror stands
In Yahweh I take refuge; why flee like a bird in flight? / You counsel me to flee up to the mountain’s height.
The wicked bend their bows, set arrows on the string, / In darkness shoot the upright; their arrows take wing.
If foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do? / Yahweh in his holy temple, enthroned in heaven too.
His eyes do observe all the children of men; / His eyes do examine all the children of men.
Yahweh examines righteous; wicked he detests; / He does hate the one who loves violence, no less.
Blazing coals, fire, sulfur rain on the wicked there; / Scorching wind is their portion, the cup they share.
Yahweh is righteous; righteousness he loves; / The upright shall see his face when the time comes.
Help, Yahweh; the godly vanish from the land / The faithful fail from among the sons of man
Each one lies to his neighbor, his words are untrue / They speak with flattering lips, hearts divided in two
May Yahweh cut off all the flattering lips outright / And every tongue that boasts, be cut off from sight
They claim, “With our tongue we will prevail; our lips are our own” / They ask, “Who is lord over us?”—their words are a boast
Yahweh says, “The weak are oppressed; I will arise” / “The needy groan; I’ll shield the maligned from those who despise”
Yahweh’s words are flawless, like silver refined / In a clay furnace, seven times purified
You will keep them, Yahweh; you’ll keep them secure / Preserve them from this generation evermore
On every side the wicked walk among mankind / When what is vile among men is prized and enshrined
How long, Yahweh, will You forget me for all time? / How long will You hide Your face from my own sight?
I take counsel in my soul, with sorrow every day, / How long shall my enemy still triumph and hold sway?
Behold, answer me, Yahweh, my God, hear my plea, / Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep and cease to be.
