His relatives all shun him, turning him away / He pleads with friends and chases them; they don’t stay
A false witness will not escape the penalty due / The one who pours out his lies shall perish too
The person who gets wisdom loves his own soul / Keep on understanding; find good as your goal
Discretion makes a person slow to anger, restrained / To overlook an offense is glory he has gained
The king’s wrath, it is like the lion’s roaring blast / His favor is like the dew that rests on grass
The fear of Yahweh leads to life; contentment will remain / He rests, untouched by trouble’s reach, free from its strain
Whoever pities the poor, he lends to Yahweh / Yahweh will surely pay him his just reward
The sluggard buries his hand down in his meal / He will not bring his hand back to his mouth for his fill
Many plans are held within a person’s heart / But Yahweh’s counsel prevails and stands apart
Wine mocks; beer brawls, and they lead people astray / Whoever they lead is surely not wise that way
A king’s terror roars like a lion in its might / He who provokes him forfeits his life outright
It is an honor to keep yourself clear of strife / Every fool will be quarreling, picking a fight
The sluggard will not plow when winter chills the land / At harvest he begs, but has nothing in hand
Counsel in the heart is like deep water, held in store / The understanding draws it out from its core
Many men claim unfailing love, their words they share / But who can find a faithful man anywhere?
A righteous man walks in integrity, upright and true / His children who come after him, they are blessed too
From his judgment throne, the king looks over all / His eyes scatter all evil, making it fall
Who can say, “I have made my heart pure and clean?” / “I am clean and without sin”—who can make that claim?
Yahweh detests false weights; he knows they're not right / Differing measures, detestable in his sight
A child is known by deeds; their work comes to view / If it is pure, if it is right, it shines through
Yahweh’s lamp is the human spirit, burning bright / It searches every innermost part outright
Gold and rubies are plentiful, beyond compare / But lips that speak knowledge are a jewel rare
Don't you say, “I will pay back evil”; take heed / Wait for Yahweh, and he will save you indeed
Yahweh holds the king’s heart like channels through the land / He turns it where he wills, its course at his command
Each person sees their way as right within their sight / But Yahweh weighs each heart, though each deems their way right
To do what’s right and just is pleasing to Yahweh / More than the sacrifices people bring his way
The wicked lift a high look; their proud heart lights a lamp / That lamp is sin, the mark of wickedness’s stamp
Diligent plans lead to profit, carefully made / But haste rushes to poverty, its gains all fade
A lying tongue gains treasure, fleeting as the air / For those who seek their death, that vapor is their share
The guilty walk along a devious, winding track / The innocent walk upright, never turning back
A desert home is better than a house of strife / Than sharing life with fretful, contentious woman as wife
Who shuts their ears when poor ones plead and will not hear their cry / Will call aloud in their own need, but none will reply
A secret gift can pacify the anger in the heart / A bribe concealed inside a cloak still quiets wrath at its start
The righteous take their delight when justice has its day / For workers of iniquity, destruction comes their way
Who follows righteousness and kindness shall attain / Life, righteousness, and honor are his great gain
Who guards the mouth and tongue keeps speech in close control / And keeps their own soul away from trouble’s hold
No wisdom, understanding, or counsel can block Yahweh’s way / The horse is set for battle; victory is with Yahweh
A good name is worth more than riches you hold / Loving favor is better than silver and gold
Rich and poor alike share one Maker of all / Yahweh made them both, the great ones and the small
The prudent see danger and slip out of sight / The simple press on and then suffer their plight
Humility and fear of Yahweh bring wealth in their wake / Honor and life are the rewards that they do make
Thorns and snares line the wicked person’s pathway / Guard your soul, and from them keep yourself away
Train up a child in the way that helps them grow / When old, they won’t depart from the way they know
The rich rule the poor, their power holds sway / The borrower serves the lender and must obey
Whoever sows wickedness gathers up trouble / The rod of his fury is smashed into rubble
The generous share food with the poor and are blessed / Yahweh pleads the poor person’s case when oppressed
Drive out the mocker; let all quarrels now end / A pure heart and graceful speech make you the king’s friend
Yahweh, he watches over the knowledge with his eyes / He frustrates the words the unfaithful devise
The sluggard says that a lion will kill him in the street / The adulteress’s mouth’s a deep pit; the wrath-bound fall in it
Listen now to wise words; let your heart heed what they say / Their reliable words teach truth; so trust Yahweh
At the ruler’s table, consider what lies on your plate / Put a knife to your throat; don’t crave his deceitful bait
Don’t wear yourself out to be rich; keep your eyes / From what sprouts wings like an eagle and flies through the skies
Stingy-eyed, he counts the cost, says “Eat, drink,” but his heart’s not with you / The morsel that you ate comes back; you lose your good words too
Don’t speak in the ears of a fool; he despises wise words too / Don’t shift old bounds or orphans' fields; strong Defender pleads against you
Apply your heart to instruction; let knowledge reach your ear / Correct your child with the rod; he won’t die; save his soul from Sheol’s snare
Your wise heart makes your father take delight / He rejoices when your lips speak what is right
Don’t envy sinners; fear Yahweh throughout the day / There’s future hope; it will not be cut away
Listen, my son, and be wise, and keep your heart on the right path / Don’t drink too much or gorge on meat; drowsiness clothes them in rags
Hear your father; don’t despise your mother grown old / Buy truth, wisdom, discipline, understanding; don’t let go
The righteous father has great joy; a wise child delights him / Let father and mother be glad; let her who bore you rejoice
My son, now give me your heart; of my ways be aware / Prostitute, deep pit; wayward wife, narrow well to ensnare
Who has woe, sorrow, strife, complaints, bruises, bloodshot eyes? / Those who stay long at wine and seek mixed wine likewise
Don’t gaze at red wine sparkling inside the cup / It goes down so smoothly with each easy sup
It bites like a snake and poisons like a viper in the end / She waits like a robber; the unfaithful increase among men
Your eyes see strange things; confusion fills your head / Like one laid mid-sea, or on the rigging overhead
“They hit me; I was not hurt; they beat me; I don’t feel a thing. / When will I wake? I’ll do it again; I’ll find another.”
Don’t envy evil men, nor wish to join their way, / Their hearts plot the violence; their lips speak foul play.
By wisdom, build the house; let insight make it stay, / Then knowledge fills its rooms with rare treasures on display.
The wise man gains great power; knowledge makes his strength take flight, / Wise counsel guides your war; many advisers win outright.
Wisdom’s too high for fools; they don’t speak at the gate, / Evil plotters are schemers; folly’s sin, mockers men hate.
If you falter when trouble comes, your strength is small, / Rescue those led to death; hold back those near slaughter’s call.
If you say, “We didn’t know,” won’t the heart-weigher know? / The Keeper knows your soul; won’t he repay each deed you show?
Honey from the comb is sweet; wisdom feeds the soul, / Find wisdom; then its reward comes, and hope stays whole.
Don’t plot against the righteous home; don’t wreck his place, / The righteous rise seven times; the wicked are laid waste.
Don’t rejoice when your enemy falls down today, / Yahweh may see, be displeased, and turn wrath away.
Don’t fret over the wicked; no reward is due, / Their lamp will be snuffed out, extinguished from view.
Fear Yahweh and the king, and do not join the rebel band, / Their ruin rises suddenly; what both bring none can understand.
Show no partiality in judgment; don’t call the wicked right, / Peoples curse, nations abhor; convict the guilty, blessings alight.
An honest answer is a kiss laid on the lips, / Don’t falsely charge your neighbor; let no deceit slip.
Prepare your work outside; get your fields arrayed, / Afterwards build your house; the groundwork’s now laid.
Don’t repay; the sluggard’s field bore thorns and nettles round, / His wall fell down; little sleep brings want, like armed men around.
God’s glory is to conceal a matter; kings search it through / Their hearts, like earth’s depth and heaven’s height, stay beyond view
Take dross from silver; material comes to the refiner’s hand / Remove the wicked from the king; his righteous throne will stand
Don’t exalt yourself before king; among great men don’t claim your place / Better hear, “Come up here,” than be sent down before the prince’s face
Don’t hurry to court; debate your neighbor, your case with care / Guard another’s trust, lest shame and bad repute remain there
Gold apples in silver settings: a fitting word shines bright / A wise reprover’s gold adorns an ear that heeds aright
Faithful messengers refresh their masters, like harvest snow / Good news from far is like cold water’s welcome flow
Clouds and wind without rain: the gift-boaster’s hollow lie / Better a housetop corner than contentious home nearby
Patience persuades rulers; speak in measured tone / A soft-spoken tongue can break even a bone
Found honey? Eat what’s sufficient; too much, and you’ll vomit indeed / Seeking your own honor is not honorable; take heed
False testimony against your neighbor is club, sword, arrow’s flight / Confidence in the unfaithful in trouble: bad tooth, lame foot’s plight
Songs to a heavy heart are like a coat stripped in the cold / Like vinegar on soda, a jarring thing to behold
If your foe is hungry, feed him; give drink if thirst is true / Heap coals upon his head; Yahweh will reward you
Righteous man who yields before the wicked is a polluted well / A spirit without restraint is like a city with walls that fell
Snow in summer, rain at harvest—fool’s honor out of place / Like lame legs hanging loose, a parable in fools’ mouths misplaced
An undeserved curse flutters like a sparrow through the air / Like darting swallows, it won’t come to rest anywhere
A whip for the horse, a bridle for donkey to guide / A rod for the backs of the fools is prescribed
Don’t mirror foolish ways, lest you wear the fool’s disguise / Answer by his folly, lest he seem wise in his own eyes
To send a fool-borne message cuts off your feet / Then drink violence with it, and that’s the fate you meet
A fool’s parable pricks a drunkard’s hand with its sting / To honor a fool is to bind a stone in a sling
Hire a fool, like an archer who wounds all in his aim / A dog returns to its vomit; the fool repeats the same
There’s more hope for a fool than for one convinced he’s wise / The sluggard deems his wit above seven prudent men’s advice
“There’s a lion in the road!” he cries, won’t venture out / Like a hinged door he turns; dish-hand won’t reach his mouth
A passerby meddling in a quarrel grabs the dog’s ears tight / Deceiver: “Am I not joking?”—torches, arrows, death take flight
When the gossip is gone, the quarrel dies, its flame burns low / Folk who contend pile on fuel; whispered words sink below
Evil-hearted lips are silver dross on earthenware / Sweet speech hides seven horrors; the assembly lays them bare
Dig a pit, fall in; the rolling stone comes back around / A lying tongue hates its victims; flattery brings ruin down
Don’t boast about tomorrow, for no one knows what’s in store, / Grind a fool with grain; his folly won’t be removed anymore.
Let another man praise you; don’t claim your own fame, / A stranger, not your own lips, should praise you with acclaim.
A fool’s provocation does outweigh the stone and the sand, / Wrath is cruel, anger overwhelms; who before jealousy can stand?
Open rebuke is better than love kept inside, / A friend’s wounds are faithful; foes’ kisses come wide.
A full soul loathes the honeycomb, won’t take a bite, / The hungry find bitter things sweet to the appetite.
A man who wanders from his home is like a bird in flight, / A loud blessing at dawn may be heard as a curse outright.
Perfume and incense gladden hearts; a friend’s counsel brings cheer, / A neighbor near is better than a brother far from here.
The prudent see danger and take refuge from harm, / The simple pass on, then suffer the alarm.
The rain drips without cease; a contentious wife brings the same strain, / Restrain her like wind, or grasp oil in your right hand in vain.
Iron sharpens iron, and so a man sharpens his friend, / Fig-tenders eat fruit; a master’s keeper’s honored in the end.
The crucible tests silver; the furnace tests gold, / A man is refined by praise, as the proverb has told.
Know well the state of your flocks; riches and crowns will go, / Lambs clothe; goats buy a field; their milk feeds those at home.
With none pursuing, the wicked will flee in fright / The righteous stand like lions, fearless in their might
A needy man who oppresses the poor is like driving rain / That driving rain leaves fields without a crop or grain
Those who forsake the law give wicked men acclaim / Those keeping law contend with them, challenge their claim
A poor man walks in integrity, his path stays clean / Far better than the rich whose crooked ways are seen
He turns his ear from law, refuses what it says / His prayer is an abomination when he prays
He misleads the upright, then falls into his own snare / The blameless inherit good and claim their share
The rich man thinks he’s wise, deceived by his own eyes / The poor man understands, and sees through his disguise
Who hides their sins won’t prosper, no gains they achieve / Who confesses and renounces them, mercy they receive
He rules the helpless, roaring like a lion in its lair / He is a charging bear to helpless people there
The man who sheds blood flees as fugitive till the end / No one will support him, left alone to fend
Who works his land has plenty, his harvests grow / The one who chases fantasies will poverty know
Trusting yourself alone is foolish; you’ll fall / Who walks in wisdom stays secure through it all
When the righteous triumph, great glory lights the day / When wicked men arise, the people hide away
Often rebuked, stiff-necked, sudden ruin seals his fate / No remedy remains to pull him from that state
When righteous people thrive, the whole town joins in cheer / When wicked rulers hold the reins, their groans ring clear
The one who loves wisdom brings his father joy / A companion of prostitutes spends wealth till destroyed
A just king makes the land stand firm and sound / The one who takes bribes tears it down to the ground
By flattery, a man sets his neighbor a snare / A net for the feet of his neighbor is laid there
An evil man is snared by his sin, held tight / The righteous, they can sing and are glad outright
The righteous care that justice serves the poor / The wicked don’t care for knowledge, that’s for sure
Mockers stir the city and provoke its ire / The wise turn anger away; they don’t feed the fire
A fool lets all his anger run unrestrained / A wise man checks himself and keeps his anger chained
The rod of correction gives wisdom to youth / A child left to himself brings his mother shame too
Without revelation, people's restraint goes missing / The one who keeps the law receives a blessing
The fear of man proves a snare that leads astray / Whoever trusts in Yahweh is kept from harm's way
Agur tells Ithiel and Ucal, “I lack all human insight” / No wisdom have I learned, nor know the Holy One aright
Who rose and came down, wind in fists, waters bound in clothes? / Who set earth’s ends—and what his name, his son’s name, who knows?
God’s every word is flawless; He shields those who on Him rely / Add nothing to His words, lest He reprove you; you be found to lie
Remove falsehood and lies; keep them far away / Give neither wealth nor poverty, but food each day
Lest I be full, deny You: “Who is Yahweh?” I say / And poverty may lead to theft, bringing God’s name to shame
Don’t slander a servant to his master when you speak / He may curse you, and guilt will be yours to reap
One curses father, won’t bless mother, pure in their own sight / Yet filthy, proud-eyed, sword-teeth, knife-jaws devour poor outright
The leech’s two daughters cry, “Give, give”; their endless desire / Sheol, the barren womb, the dry earth, and the fire
The eye mocks its father, scorns its mother, won’t obey / Ravens pluck it out; young eagles eat it as prey
The eagle’s way through air, the serpent’s on rock, the ship at sea / A man’s way with a maiden—these are unknown to me
The adulterous woman eats and wipes her mouth clean / “I have done nothing wrong,” she says, her guilt unseen
Earth trembles: a servant king, fool filled with food bears weight / Unloved woman wed, servant heir to mistress’s estate
Small ants store food in summer; weak hyraxes hide in stone / Kingless locusts march in ranks; lizards creep where sits the throne
With stately stride, the lion fears none; greyhound and he-goat stand / The king no one can rise against completes the stately band
If lifted in folly or thinking evil, hand over your mouth / Milk churns to butter, noses bleed; forced wrath brings strife about
Lemuel, heed your mother’s words; attend her speech / My son, born of my womb and vows, hear what I teach
Don’t give your strength to women; turn your heart away / Nor follow what brings kings to ruin and decay
Kings, seek no wine or strong drink, lest law be denied / Or twist the justice due the poor, set truth aside
Give strong drink to the dying, wine for the bitter soul / Let them drink, forget their poverty and woe
Open your mouth for the mute, the desolate in need / Judge righteously; serve the poor and needy with just deeds
Who can find a worthy woman, whose worth is treasure? / Her price is far above rubies, beyond measure
Her husband trusts her fully; no lack of gain / She does him good, not harm, while her days remain
Like merchant ships, she brings her bread from distant lands / She rises while it’s night, portions food with her hands
She considers a field, then buys it with care / With fruit of her hands, she plants a vineyard there
Her lamp does not go out throughout the long night / Her hands work the spindle by its steady light
She opens her arms to the poor, extends her hands in aid / She fears no snow; her household in scarlet is arrayed
Strength and dignity clothe her; she laughs at what’s ahead / She speaks with wisdom, kind instruction her words spread
Charm is deceitful; beauty is vain in all its ways / The woman who fears Yahweh shall be praised
Her children rise, call her blessed; her husband gives praise / Her works shall praise her in the gates through her days
The Preacher says, “Vanity of vanities”; all is vain / What gain has man from all his labor beneath the sun’s domain?
One generation goes, another comes; earth stays / The sun rises, sets, then hurries back to its place each day
The wind turns south, then north, returning on its track / Rivers run into the sea; still unfilled, they flow back
All things are full of weariness beyond what words can say / The eye’s never satisfied; the ear’s unfilled, come what may
What’s called new existed in the ages long before / Former things, and things to come, won’t be recalled by those after
In Jerusalem, the Preacher-king’s search began / God gave a heavy burden to the sons of men
I saw all works as vanity, chasing wind in flight / The crooked can’t be made straight; what’s lacking can’t be tallied right
I sought wisdom, madness, folly; wind was all I caught / More wisdom brings more grief; more knowledge sorrow’s wrought
I tested mirth and wine, with wisdom as my guide / I found that pleasure, too, was vanity when tried
I built my houses, vineyards, gardens, parks, and fruit trees grew / I made pools to water forest trees, their waters set to flow
I gathered servants, herds and flocks, amassed wealth of my own / I got singers, instruments, delights of every tone
In Jerusalem, none before me could compare / I held no joy back; my labor was my share
I saw my works were vanity, a chase of wind / Beneath the sun, no profit could I ever find
Wisdom excels folly, as light excels the night / The wise man's eyes are in his head; the fool walks without light
The wise man, like the fool, must die; no memory can stay / In days to come, both will be forgotten, swept away
I hated life; beneath the sun, all labor caused me pain / All vanity, a chasing wind; no profit could remain
I leave my labor to the one who follows me / Who knows if wise or fool? Of all my works, ruler he'll be
His days are sorrow; all his work is grief and pain / His heart at night finds no rest; its grief remains
I find it good to eat and drink; my work brings me cheer / From God's own hand; who enjoys more? None can come near
God grants the pleasing one joy, wisdom, knowledge as his gain / The sinner gathers, heaps it up for him; all chasing wind is vain
Birth and death beneath heaven each arrive in their time / Plant, uproot, weep, laugh; war and peace fall in line
What profit has the worker from the toil he must bear? / God gives humanity its burden, a weight to wear
God makes each thing beautiful within its appointed span / He sets eternity in hearts; his work no mind can scan
Rejoice, do good, eat, drink; enjoy the work you do / Good in all labor is God’s gift, bestowed on you
Whatever God does lasts forever, beyond all years / Nothing added or taken away; God acts so they fear
What has been and what will come have long been here before / God seeks again what passed away, once more
Where justice and righteousness stand, wickedness is found / I said in my heart: God will judge both when time comes round
God tests each of them so that they may come to know / They themselves are like beasts that dwell here below
Both humans and the beasts die; one breath is theirs to share / All go to one place, dust; man has no advantage there
Who knows if man's spirit rises, beast's descends below? / Joy in his work is his portion; what follows, none can show
The oppressed wept beneath the sun; no one to hear their cry / Their oppressors held the power, and they held all sway
I praised the long-dead above those still alive / The unborn above both, who never saw evil thrive
Envy of neighbors drove their labor and their gain / All vanity; they chased the wind, their toil in vain
One quiet handful beats two, with labor chasing air / The fool folds his hands, and his ruin is laid bare
No son nor brother; his eyes crave wealth, toil won’t cease / “For whom do I labor, denying my soul its ease?”
Two earn good reward; when one falls, the other gives aid / Alone brings woe; they share warmth, withstand; threefold cord won’t quickly fray
Poor, wise youth outdoes the old fool-king, who won’t heed / From prison came the youth to reign, born poor indeed
The living were with the youth, successor to the throne / Those after him won’t rejoice; this too is vanity shown
At God’s house, draw near and listen; better than fools’ rite / They sacrifice, not knowing that their deeds aren’t right
God is in heaven, you’re on earth; let your words be few / As dreams bring many cares, fools speak with many words too
Pay the vow you made; don’t delay what is due / Don’t tell him, “Mistake!”; God may destroy your work too
Many dreams and words are vanity, all in vain / But you must still fear God; let that fear remain
Don’t marvel: poor oppressed, their justice stripped away / Higher officials watch below; the king gains from fields today
The lover of silver never feels complete / Goods bring more mouths; their owner watches them eat
The laborer sleeps sweet, eats little or much at night / A rich man’s abundance keeps sleep out of sight
Hoarded wealth harms its owner; misfortune brings loss / He leaves naked, with nothing in hand, bears the cost
Enjoy food, drink, and labor; this portion is your part / God gives wealth and power; joy fills the heart
God grants him riches, wealth, and honor, all he desires / Yet he has no power to eat; alien eats—vanity, evil disease
A hundred children, many years, may mark his span / Yet good does not fill him; no burial for that man
The stillborn comes and leaves in dark, no sun has shone / It has its rest, unlike the man whose years go on
Though twice a thousand years, he fails to taste the good / Don’t all go to one place, as all who live here do?
All labor feeds the mouth, but hunger lingers still / What gains the wise o’er fools, or poor man’s walking skill?
Better the sight of eyes than desire’s roaming flight / This too is vanity, a chase of wind from sight
All that has been was named; man’s nature has long been known / He can’t contend with the mighty; vain words bring no gain of their own
Who knows what good man has in life, his days a passing shade? / Who tells what comes after him, when he has passed away?
A good name is better than fine perfume on earth / The day of death is better than the day of birth
The house of mourning beats the feast; all men meet their end / The living take this to heart; sorrow makes hearts mend
The wise heart’s in the house of mourning, not where fools play / The fool’s heart rests in the house of mirth all day
Better hear the wise rebuke, not fools’ songs that entertain / Like thorns crackling under pots, fools’ laughter is vain
Extortion makes the wise man foolish, sends his thoughts astray / A bribe destroys understanding, takes good judgment away
The end is better than the start; patience outlasts pride / Anger rests in fools’ own bosoms, where it will abide
Don’t you ask why former days were better than today / Wisdom gives the wise more strength than ten rulers can display
Wisdom, good as inheritance, excels for those who see sun / Wisdom defends like money; knowledge keeps its holder living on
Consider the work of God: who can straighten what He made? / Good times, hard times side by side; rejoice, reflect; next undisplayed
The righteous may perish while still doing what is right / The wicked live long in evil, extending through the night
Don’t be over-righteous or wise; why bring yourself to fall? / Don’t be too wicked or foolish; fear God, come through them all
No righteous one on earth does good and never sins / Don’t heed words, lest your servant curse you; you’ve cursed others again
The Preacher sought wisdom’s depths; the woman, more bitter than death / Who pleases God escapes; sinners ensnared; one man, no woman found
Wisdom makes a man's face shine, a clear and steady glow / The hardness of his face is changed, its setness lets go
I say, “Keep the king’s command,” as the oath to God requires / His word reigns supreme; who can say, “What are you doing?”—no one dares
Who keeps commandment comes to no harm; wise hearts know when and how / Though the misery weighs heavy, none knows what is coming now
No one commands the spirit or the day death will arrive / No discharge in war; wickedness can’t keep its doers alive
I saw the wicked buried, forgotten in their town / Since judgment was delayed, men's hearts to evil were bound
The righteous get the wicked’s fate; the wicked, righteous fate / I call this vanity, this wholly reversed state
Eat, drink, and be joyful in the labor God provides / No better thing beneath the sun; with labor joy abides
Men seek God’s work beneath the sun, but cannot come to know / The wise may think they grasp it; still, they cannot make it show
The righteous and the wicked share one fate when life is done / After life, they go among the dead, every one
A living dog is better than a lion that is dead / The living know they’ll die; the dead know nothing, memory’s fled
God has accepted your works; wear garments always white / Eat bread with joy, drink wine; with wife you love, take delight
Do all your hand finds with your might, whatever you do / No work or wisdom waits in Sheol when life is through
The swift may lose the race; the strong may lose the fight / Time and chance come to all; fish and birds caught tight
A poor wise man's wisdom saved the town when the king bore down / His wisdom was despised; none remembered him in town
Quiet words of the wise can surpass the ruler’s cry / Wisdom beats strength and arms; one sinner can make much good die
Dead flies make the perfumer’s oil stink, a foul smell / A little folly outweighs wisdom and honor as well
A wise man’s heart is at his right; a fool’s is on the left side / His sense fails; he tells everyone, “I’m a fool,” far and wide
When a ruler’s anger rises, stay firmly in your place / For gentleness lays great offenses to rest with grace
Folly holds a high rank; the rich are brought down / Servants ride horses; princes walk on the ground
A pit-digger may fall into the pit they make / Whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake
A blunt ax will take much more strength; the skill can prevail / If the snake bites before it is charmed, the charmer’s words will fail
The wise man’s words are gracious; a fool’s own lips swallow what he said / He multiplies words, starts in folly, ends mad; none knows what’s ahead
Don’t curse the king in thought, nor rich men in your room; words may stray / A bird across the sky may carry your voice away
Cast your bread on the waters; send it away / After many days, what you sent finds its way
Give portions to seven, even eight, and share / You know not what evil on earth may appear
Full clouds pour rain on the earth, wetting the ground / A fallen tree stays in the place it came down
Wind-watchers won’t sow; cloud-watchers won’t reap; God’s work you don’t know / You don’t know the way of the wind, nor how bones in womb grow
Sow in the morning; at dusk, don’t hold back your hand / Which prospers—or both equally good—you don’t understand
Light is sweet, and the sun is a joy to behold / If years are many, rejoice in them all as they unfold
Remember days of darkness; many lie in view / They will be many; all that comes is vanity too
Young man, rejoice in your youth; heart cheer; walk as your heart and eyes lead / God judges; cast sorrow, flesh-evil; youth and life’s dawn recede
Remember your Creator in youth, before years draw near, / Before evil days come, when you say, “No pleasure here.”
Before the sun, moon, and stars darken from sight, / Clouds return again after rain, dimming the light.
The house’s keepers tremble; strong men bend and bow, / Grinders cease; few remain; almond blooms, desire lets go.
Silver cord snaps, golden bowl breaks; man goes to everlasting home, / Spirit returns to God; dust to earth; mourners through streets roam.
“Vanity of vanities,” the Preacher declares, / He taught the people knowledge, ordered proverbs with care.
He sought acceptable words of truth, blamelessly penned, / Wise words are like goads, and firm nails, by one shepherd sent.
My son, be warned: of making books there is no end, / Much study wears the flesh till weary strength is spent.
Fear God and keep his commands; this is man’s whole due, / God judges each work and each hidden thing, good or evil too.
Solomon's song, a tale of love's delight, "Your kiss is sweeter than wine," she recites.
Your oils, your scent, finer than gold, Your name's like perfume, a story retold.
"Take me away, let's run with haste, Into the king's rooms, where joy's embraced."
Dark but lovely, she stands with pride, "Like Kedar's tents, no need to hide."
"Don't gaze at my skin, sun-kissed and warm, My brothers' wrath became my norm."
"Where's your flock at noon?" she calls, "Why should I veiled wander these walls?"
He speaks, "Oh beauty, follow the way, By shepherds' tents, let your young goats play."
"You're a steed in Pharaoh's chariot ride, Cheeks adorned, jewels on your side."
"Gold earrings we'll craft, silver inlay, While the king dines, my perfume's display."
"My beloved's myrrh, so close, so near, Henna blossoms from En Gedi appear."
"Behold, you're beautiful, dove-like eyes, And our verdant couch, where love lies."
"See our home's beams, cedar strong, Firs are our rafters, where we belong."
Rose of Sharon, lily's grace, In the valleys, love finds its place.
Among thorns, my love shines bright, Apple tree stands, a pure delight.
In his shadow, I find rest, His fruit's sweetness, I am blessed.
Banquet hall, love's banner flies, "Strengthen me," my heart cries.
Left hand cradles, right hand holds, Love's embrace, as time unfolds.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, hear my plea, Don't stir love 'til it’s ready to be."
Oh, hear his voice, my love's approach, Leaping mountains, hills encroach.
Like a young deer, swift and near, At the window, he appears.
"Rise up, my love, come with me, Winter's gone, set us free.
Flowers bloom, songs abound, Turtledove's voice, sweet sound.
Figs ripen, vines in bloom, Fragrance fills every room."
"Dove in rock, come out, be seen, Your sweet voice, face serene.
Catch the foxes, the vineyard’s foe, For our blossoms, let love grow."
My beloved's mine, and I am his, Among the lilies, love is bliss.
'Til day cools and shadows part, Turn, my love, follow your heart.
In the night I lay, seeking the one my soul adores, Looked and searched, but found closed doors.
Jumped from bed, hit the streets wide, Seeking my love in the city's stride.
Watchmen found me, they saw me roam, "Seen my love?" I asked as I wandered alone.
Barely passed them, my heart took flight, Found my love, held him tight.
Brought him home, wouldn't let go, To my mother's room, where love would grow.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, hear me clear," "Don't wake love before it draws near."
Who's this rising from the wild, Pillars of smoke, smellin' sweet and mild?
Look, it's Solomon's ride in style, Sixty warriors strong, marching in file.
Swords at the ready, experts in fight, Guardians against the fears of night.
Solomon's chariot, crafted with care, Wood of Lebanon, silver flare.
Gold base, purple seat, love inlaid, Jerusalem's daughters, their craft displayed.
Step out, daughters of Zion, see him crowned, On his wedding day, pure joy abound.

You're stunning, my love, pure delight I proclaim, Your eyes like doves, framed by your veil, a gentle flame. Hair cascading like goats on Gilead's grand slopes, Teeth like fresh-shorn flocks, no missing hopes.
Lips of scarlet thread, your mouth speaks grace, Temples like pomegranate, behind the veil, in place. Your neck, a tower of David, shields hang and sway, Strength of mighty men, in every way.

Breasts like twin fawns, grazing lilies so fair, 'Til shadows flee, myrrh and frankincense in the air. You're flawless, my love, perfect in every view, "Come from Lebanon, my bride, I'll be with you."
Ravished my heart with a glance and a chain, Your love, oh my bride, like sweet wine, never plain. Lips drip honeycomb, sweetness flows deep, Garments smell of Lebanon, in them I steep.
Locked garden, sealed fountain, pure and bright, Orchards of pomegranates, in the soft moonlight. Spikenard, saffron, cinnamon's embrace, With myrrh and aloes, spices fill the space.

Fountain of gardens, living waters flow, From Lebanon's streams, where the best spices grow. "Awake north wind, south breeze, make my garden known, Let my beloved taste, where precious fruits have grown."
I stepped into my garden, with my bride by my side, Gathered my myrrh, spices, honey to abide. Drank my wine and milk, feeling satisfied, "Eat, friends! Drink deeply, be unified."
While I slept, my heart stayed awake, Heard my beloved, a soft knock to make. “Open, my love, my dove, in this night’s mist, For my head’s soaked from the dew’s gentle kiss.”
I’d shed my robe, should I wear it again? Washed my feet, should I soil them in vain? He reached through the latch, my heart gave chase, I rose to him, my hands with myrrh did grace.
Opened the door, found him gone away, My heart sank deep, heard his voice sway. I searched, no sight, my calls met air, The city’s watchmen found me in despair.
They struck me down, bruised my plea, Took my cloak, left me empty. Daughters of Jerusalem, hear my call, Tell him I’m faint with love, that’s all.
“What makes your beloved greater than the rest, Fairest of women, say why he’s the best?” He stands out in ten thousand, pure gold his head, Hair dark like a raven, where dreams are fed.
Eyes like doves, by waters they gleam, Cheeks spice-laden, perfumed in a dream. Lips like lilies, dripping myrrh, Hands are golden, beryl they stir.
Body ivory, sapphire inlay, Legs of marble, gold in display. He’s like Lebanon, cedars tall, Mouth sweet as honey, he’s my all.
This is my beloved, my friend, my song, Daughters of Jerusalem, to him I belong.
Where's your beloved gone, fair woman, where's he turned? We'll seek him with you, find him where he yearned.
He's down in the garden, beds of spice, Pasturing flocks, gathering lilies, oh so nice.
"I'm my beloved's, and he is mine," He browses among lilies, where they intertwine.
You're beautiful, my love, like Tirzah's grace, Lovely as Jerusalem, with an awesome face.
"Turn your eyes away, they've overcome my soul," Your hair's like Gilead's goats, on the gentle roll.
Your teeth are like ewes, fresh from the stream, Every one's got twins, perfect as they gleam.
Your temples, a piece of pomegranate's hue, Behind your veil, they shine through.
Sixty queens, eighty concubines in line, Virgins without number, yet you're divine.
"My dove, my perfect one, you're unique," Your mother's only, her favorite chic.
Daughters call you blessed, queens praise you high, Who is she, like morning, moon, sun in the sky?
I went to the nut grove, green valley's expanse, Watching vines bud, pomegranates dance.
Without knowing, desire drove my heart, With royal chariots, ready to depart.
Return, return, oh Shulammite, so rare, Why gaze at you, like Mahanaim's dance, fair?
Your feet in sandals, oh so neat, A prince's daughter can't be beat.
Thighs rounded, jewels so grand, Crafted by a skillful hand.
Your body's like a goblet round, No mixed wine lacking, profound.
Waist like wheat, lilies surround, Beauty in every pound.
Breasts like fawns, twin roe in grace, In this garden, you find your place.
Your neck's an ivory tower high, Eyes like pools where waters lie.
Nose like Lebanon's tower strong, Watching Damascus all day long.
Head like Carmel standing tall, Hair in purple, where kings fall.
How beautiful, how pleasant, love, Delights from earth and above.
Stature like a palm tree wide, Breasts like fruit on every side.
"I'll climb the palm, hold its fruit tight, Breasts like clusters, for my delight."
Breath's like apples, mouth like wine, For my beloved, smooth and fine.
"I'm my beloved's, his desire is mine," In this love, our hearts align.
"Come, my love, let's fieldward stray, In the villages, we'll stay."
To vineyards early, let's retreat, See the buds, the blossoms sweet.
Pomegranates in flower bloom, "I'll give you love, dispel the gloom."
Mandrakes fragrant, fruits galore, New and old, at every door.
Stored up treasures, love devout, For you, my beloved, no doubt.
Oh, that you were like my brother, my kin, I'd kiss you outside, no shame, no sin.
Lead you home, where my mother imparts, Pour you spiced wine, juice from my heart.
His left hand supports under my head, Right arm embracing, love's comfort spread.
"Daughters of Jerusalem, heed my plea, Don't wake love till it desires to be free."
Who emerges from the wild, leaning close, Under apple trees, where love first grows?
"Set me as a seal on your heart, so tight, For love’s strong as death, a fierce, burning light."
Many waters can't quench a love so grand, Floods can't drown it; it will withstand.
A sister, not grown, what shall we do? Build her a silver tower, strong and true.
"I am a wall, my form towers high, In his eyes, peace, where love does lie."
Solomon's vineyard leased at great worth, Shekels for fruit, a measure of earth.
"My vineyard's mine, yet for you a share, Silver for keepers, fruit they bear."
"You who dwell in gardens, friends near and clear, Let your voice echo, sweet in my ear."
"Come away, my love, like a gazelle's race, Bound on spice mountains, swift in grace."
Hear, O heavens and earth; attend to what I decree / I fed and raised my children; they rebelled against me
The ox knows its owner; the donkey knows its master's trough / But Israel doesn't know; my people don't consider at all
A sinful nation, packed with guilt, evildoers' brood astray / Forsook Yahweh, despised Israel’s Holy One, turned away
The whole head is sick; the heart faint, diseased to the core / From sole to head, open wounds, unbandaged and sore
Strangers devour the land; its cities burned and left bare / Zion’s like a hut in melon fields, exposed to open air
A remnant kept Judah from Sodom’s doomed state / Without it, Gomorrah’s ruin would have been their fate
He calls the rulers Sodom, rejects their rites outright / They trample through his courts; their offerings bring no delight
He hates their feasts, hides his eyes when they pray / Their hands are full of blood; he won’t hear what they say
Cease doing evil; seek justice; relieve those in need / Defend the fatherless; for the widow, plead
Your scarlet sins shall be as white as snow, Yahweh said / Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool instead
The willing and obedient will eat the land’s yield / Refuse and rebel; by the sword you will be killed
Faithful city turned harlot; silver dross, wine watered thin / Her rulers join the thieves; they welcome bribes within
Yahweh purges the city’s dross, restores judges again / Zion is redeemed through justice; righteousness shall reign
Forsakers are consumed; oak leaves fade, gardens dry / The strong like tinder; their work a spark; both burn; none puts out the fire
In latter days, Yahweh’s house-mountain rises high / All nations flow toward it from every side
Peoples call one another: “Come, to Zion let’s go” / He’ll teach us his ways; we will walk the paths he’s shown
Yahweh judges nations; each sword becomes a plowshare / Spears turn to pruning hooks; all nations cease warfare
House of Jacob, come; walk in Yahweh’s light, I say / You have forsaken your people, turned away
Eastern diviners and foreign ties spread around / Their silver, gold, horses, chariots all abound
Idols they worship, their own fingers have wrought / Humanity is humbled; forgive them not
Yahweh’s terror brings the proud and lofty low / Enter the rock; hide in dust when his majesty shows
Lebanon’s cedars, Bashan’s oaks are standing tall / Mountains, hills, towers, walls, Tarshish’s ships all fall
All their gold and silver idols to moles and bats they throw / Yahweh alone exalted; they flee to caves, earth shakes below
Stop trusting in man, whose nostrils hold his breath / Of what account is he? What worth can he possess?
Yahweh strips away their bread, water, and aid / From Judah and Jerusalem, supplies are denied
Boys sit as princes, the young rule the old / Each neighbor oppresses, while children grow bold
He grips his brother: “You have clothes; rule, take ruin in hand” / “I will not heal; no bread or clothes; don’t make me command”
Jerusalem lies ruined; Judah too fell / Their words and their deeds against Yahweh rebel
Their faces testify; their sins are on display / Like Sodom they flaunt them; disaster’s their pay
Tell the righteous, “Good!” They eat fruit they have earned / The wicked face disaster; their deeds are returned
Children oppress as the women now hold sway / Their leaders are turning Yahweh’s people astray
Yahweh stands to contend, calls elders before / They ate up his vineyard, kept the poor’s goods in store
The Lord Yahweh of Armies now speaks to the chiefs / “Why do you crush my people, grind poor men’s cheeks?”
Zion’s daughters walk, necks outstretched, eyes giving a glance / They trip as they go, their anklets jingling as they prance
Sweet spices rot; belts turn to ropes; fine hair falls bare / Beauty is branded; robes turn to sackcloth they wear
Men fall by the sword; the mighty fall, struck down / Her gates mourn; she sits desolate upon the ground
Seven women take hold of one man that day: “Call us by your name; / We’ll eat our own bread, and we’ll wear our own clothes; remove our shame.”
Yahweh’s branch in that day is beautiful, glorious in the land; / The land’s fruit is Israel’s survivors’ beauty and glory, grand.
Those left in Zion and Jerusalem are holy, all; / All written among living in Jerusalem, holy they’re called.
The Lord by justice’s spirit washes Zion’s daughters’ filth away; / Jerusalem’s blood is purged by spirit of burning that day.
Yahweh creates cloud and smoke above Zion’s assemblies by day, / A shining flame by night; over all glory, a canopy laid.
A pavilion gives shade by day from the heat; / A refuge and shelter from storm and rain, a retreat.
He cleared its stones, set choicest vines on the hillside / He built its tower and cut a winepress inside
He looked for grapes; wild grapes were all it bore / Jerusalem and Judah, judge: what could I do more?
Hedge removed; its wall breaks; vines trampled remain / Briers choke the rows; clouds are commanded: no rain
Yahweh’s vineyard is Israel; Judah his own / He sought justice, found oppression; distress was shown
They join house to house and field to field, till no room is there / You dwell alone; ten acres yield one bath; great homes empty, spare
At the dawn they chase the strong drink, and revel late at night / Harps, lyres, tambourines and flutes play; Yahweh’s work they slight
For their lack of knowledge, captive, they are bound / Sheol swallows pomp; the thirsty multitudes go down
People are humbled; Yahweh’s justice stands high / Lambs graze; the strangers now eat where rich ruins lie
They bind iniquity with cords of falsehood held tight / “Hurry his work; let his counsel draw near—we’ll see it outright!”
They call evil good, good evil; call bitter sweet / Call sweet bitter, dark light, light dark, wise in their own conceit
Mighty at drinking wine, strong drink they mix with their might / They clear guilty for bribes; deny the innocent right
They spurn Yahweh’s law; roots rot, blossoms rise as dust from the ground / His anger strikes; hills quake, dead bodies strewn around
He raises a banner; distant nations come fast / They roar, seize prey; none can deliver; darkness is cast
When Uzziah died, I saw the Lord enthroned on high / His train filled the temple before my very eyes
Six-winged seraphs called, “Holy, holy, holy!” / “Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth’s full of his glory!”
The caller’s voice shook thresholds; foundations quaked / The house was filled with smoke, filling its space
I cried, “Woe, I am undone; my lips, my people’s, unclean” / Yahweh of Armies, the King whom my eyes have seen
A seraph’s live coal touched my lips; my iniquity cleared / He said my sin was forgiven, my guilt disappeared
The Lord asked, “Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?” / I said, “Here I am; send me!”—I answered thus
He said, “Go tell this people: hear, don’t understand; see, don’t perceive” / “Make hearts fat, ears heavy, shut eyes, lest they turn and be healed”
I asked, “How long?” Till cities waste, homes empty, land laid bare / A tenth too consumed; stump remains, holy seed is there
They heard Syria joined Ephraim; their hearts turned pale / Like trees in the forest trembling hard against the gale
Yahweh sent Isaiah and his son to Ahaz by the pool / “Keep calm; fear not the two smoking torch tails, and just stay cool”
They plot to tear Judah apart, divide it as planned / Set Tabeel’s son as king; Yahweh says it won’t stand
Within sixty-five years, Ephraim’s people cease to be / If you will not believe, established you will not be
Yahweh said, “Ask for a sign, in depths or heights on high” / Ahaz said, “I won’t ask; I won’t tempt Yahweh,” his reply
The Lord himself gives sign: a virgin shall conceive / She’ll bear a son called Immanuel, as he decrees
He’ll eat butter and honey when he knows to refuse wrong, choose right / Before then, the land of two kings you hate is forsaken outright
Yahweh brings unseen days on Ahaz, his people, father’s house / He whistles for Egypt’s fly, and Assyria’s bee to rouse
They rest in desolate valleys, rock clefts of stone / On thorn hedges and pastures, they make their home
Assyria’s king, the hired razor, shears the head’s hair / He shaves hair from the feet and beard, stripping them bare
One man, he shall keep a young cow and two sheep alive / Rich milk; all eat butter, honey; thorns where oxen and sheep thrive
“Maher Shalal Hash Baz”—write it on a large tablet, Yahweh says / Uriah the priest and Zechariah witness what Yahweh says
Name him Maher Shalal Hash Baz; before “father” and “mother” / Assyria takes Damascus’ wealth, Samaria’s spoils away
They spurn Shiloah’s gentle flow; in Rezin’s son rejoice / Assyria, River, king and glory, floods with mighty force
It reaches Judah’s neck; its wings spread wide across the land / Immanuel, your land is filled across its span
Roar, peoples, be shattered; far nations, arm, then fall / Take counsel, speak the word; God with us, your plans won’t stand at all
Do not fear their threats or cry “Conspiracy!”; instead / Regard Yahweh as holy; fear him, he is the one to dread
Yahweh is sanctuary; to both houses, stumbling stone and snare / For Jerusalem, a trap; many fall, broken, captured there
I wait and look for Yahweh; his face from Jacob’s house he hides / Children Yahweh gave me and I are signs; in Zion he resides
Should the living ask the dead? Should they seek God, not spirits’ way / Turn to law and covenant; if they speak not this word, no day
Distressed and hungry, they fret, curse king and God, faces rise / They look to earth: distress, gloom, anguish, darkness fills their eyes
Zebulun, Naphtali, once scorned; Galilee shines bright / In latter days, the anguished land shines; gloom takes flight
They walked in darkness, where death’s shadow lay low / A great light shines upon them, its radiance aglow
You multiply the nation’s joy; the harvesters rejoice / Like those dividing plunder, they lift a joyful voice
As in Midian, you break the yoke and end oppression’s sway / Battle armor, bloodied clothes are burned away
A child is born, a Son is given; Wonderful Counselor reigns / Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace is his name
His rule and peace on David’s throne will evermore remain / Yahweh’s zeal upholds it; justice, righteousness will reign
His word falls on Israel; they boast, “Bricks fell—we’ll build in cut stone” / “Sycamores felled; we’ll put cedars in their place,” they intone
Syrians in front, Philistines behind, Israel they devour / They seek not Yahweh; his anger stays, hand stretched out once more
False leaders lead them astray; wickedness spreads and burns / Israel devours Israel; Yahweh’s anger never turns
They write oppressive decrees, leave the needy oppressed / They rob the poor; widows and orphans are dispossessed
When desolation comes from afar, where leave wealth, whom turn to? / Beneath the prisoners they bow, fall slain; God’s wrath still burns
God sends Assyria, his anger’s rod, to trample profane land / Yet many nations’ ruin is what his heart has planned
He says the kingdoms he has conquered all are alike / He asks if Jerusalem will face that same strike
When Yahweh’s work on Zion and Jerusalem is through / He’ll punish Assyria’s proud heart, its arrogant view
“My strength and wisdom moved their borders, seized their wealth; / I brought their rulers down, and did it all myself.”
“I gathered all the earth like eggs from an abandoned nest; / No wing stirred, no mouth opened, no chirp disturbed their rest.”
An ax can’t boast above the one who wields its blade / A saw can’t exalt itself above the hand that made
The Lord sends leanness on Assyria’s fat ones, thins their frame / Israel’s Light, the Holy One, becomes a consuming flame
His forest’s glory, fruitful fields, burn down to naught / So few trees remain, a child can count the lot
The remnant leans no more on him who struck them before / They truly lean on Yahweh; Jacob returns once more
Though Israel’s people are like sand beside the sea / Only a remnant returns; righteous destruction’s decreed
Zion, don’t fear Assyria’s rod, though he strikes as Egypt did / Soon wrath will turn on him; his destruction comes due
Yahweh will scourge Assyria as Midian was brought low / His rod is raised above the sea; the yoke breaks, burdens go
Townsfolk flee and quake; he shakes his hand at Zion’s height / The Lord cuts down the lofty boughs; Lebanon falls by His might
Jesse’s stock sends up a shoot; from his roots, fruit appears / Yahweh’s Spirit rests: wisdom, insight, counsel, might, knowledge, fear
He delights in Yahweh’s fear; eyes and ears don’t decide / He gives the poor just judgment, humble ones their right
His breath kills wicked ones; his mouth strikes earth outright / Righteousness and faithfulness bind his waist up tight
The wolf lies down beside the lamb; a child leads them at play / No hurt nor harm on Yahweh’s holy mountain shall stay
Yahweh’s knowledge fills the earth, as waters cover wide / The nursing child plays by cobra; weaned hand at viper’s side
The nations seek Jesse’s root, raised like a banner high / His resting place will be glorious, its glory high
The Lord again regathers remnant; old divisions cease / Ephraim won’t envy Judah; Judah won’t persecute—peace
Yahweh splits the sea and river, cuts a highway through / From Assyria, the remnant walks as once from Egypt too
Though angry with me, Your anger turned away / I thank You, Yahweh; You comfort me today
I trust and am not afraid; God is my salvation / Yah, Yahweh is my strength and song; He became my salvation
With joy you will draw water from salvation’s wells / In that day, you will say these words yourselves
Give thanks to Yahweh, and call on His name, proclaim / His deeds among peoples; declare His exalted name
Sing to Yahweh for the excellent things He’s done / Let this be known through all the earth, to everyone
Cry aloud and shout, you who dwell in Zion too / The Holy One of Israel is great among you
Isaiah saw Babylon’s burden; raise the banner high / On bare mountain, summon them to nobles’ gates; cry
Yahweh of Armies calls consecrated warriors to fight / Kingdoms’ uproar rolls through mountains; multitudes unite
From farthest country Yahweh comes, wrath-weapons in hand / His indignation brings destruction to the whole wide land
Wail, Yahweh’s day is at hand; destruction will appear / Hands grow feeble, hearts melt; labor pains seize them in fear
His cruel day makes the whole land desolate and bare / Stars and constellations give no light; sun and moon lose their glare
God punishes evil and pride; the proud are brought low / People grow rarer than Ophir’s purest gold
In Yahweh’s fierce anger, the heavens tremble and sway / The earth is shaken from its place, wrenched away
Like hunted gazelles, like sheep none gathers, they scatter abroad / Each flees home; found ones are thrust through, captives fall to the sword
Medes rise against Babylon; their bows shatter young men / They spare not the children; their eyes show no pity for them
Babylon’s glory falls like Sodom; none will dwell there / Wild beasts and jackals fill its houses as its end draws near
Yahweh shows Jacob compassion; Israel He’ll choose anew / He’ll set them in their land; the foreigner joins them too
Israel takes its captors captive, rules oppressors in chains / They will rest from their sorrow, trouble, hard service and its strains
The oppressor has ceased; the golden city’s reign is done / Yahweh broke the wicked rulers’ staff; their stroke is gone
The earth at rest breaks into song, released and free / The cypress and cedars rejoice; no ax comes for their tree
Sheol rises up to greet you, king, beneath the ground / The dead kings ask, “Are you as weak as us, cast down?”
Your pomp and music sink to Sheol, down in the deep / Maggots spread beneath; the worms around you creep
Shining one, son of dawn, you fell from heaven below / Cut down to earth, you who laid the nations low
You boasted, “I’ll climb above the stars and clouds into the sky” / “I’ll sit on assembly’s mountain, made like the Most High”
You’re brought down to the pit; they will stare at what they see / They ask, “Is this the man who kept captives from going free?”
The kings of nations sleep in glory, each within his home / You’re barred from burial; you killed your folk, wrecked land you own
Yahweh cuts Babylon’s name and remnant, leaves it bare / No offspring will be named; porcupines and pools lie there
Yahweh breaks Assyria on His mountains; its yoke slips from their backs / His hand spans all the nations; none of them can turn that hand back
Philistia, don’t rejoice: fiery serpent springs from the root / Your root and remnant starve; north smoke comes, no straggler in his troop
The firstborn poor will eat; the needy lie secure / Yahweh founded Zion; the afflicted shelter there
In a single night, Ar of Moab is laid to waste / For in one night, Kir of Moab is laid to waste
To Bayith and Dibon’s high places they climb, weeping there / Moab wails o’er Nebo and Medeba; heads shaved, beards shorn bare
In the streets they wear sackcloth and wail aloud / On rooftops, everyone weeps; wailing resounds
Jahaz hears Heshbon and Elealeh both wail / Moab’s armed men cry aloud; their souls all quail
My heart cries for Moab as its nobles all flee / They go up weeping, cry destruction as they leave
Nimrim’s waters lie desolate; grass withers and dies / Tender grass fails; no green thing remains alive
They carry their stored-up wealth across the willow brook’s far side / Their wails reach Eglaim, Beer Elim, and circle far and wide
Dimon’s waters are blood; more comes on Dimon / Those who escape and the land’s remnant face a lion
Lambs for the ruler of the land from Selah, toward Zion’s height / Through the wilderness to Zion’s mountain, where they alight
Like wandering birds, Moab’s daughters are scattered at Arnon’s fords in flight / Give counsel, do justice; shade noon like night, hide them, betray none outright
Let my outcasts dwell with you; be his shelter from the destroyer’s face / Extortionist brought to naught; destruction ends, oppressors erased
A throne in kindness stands; in David’s tent one sits true / The ruler judges, seeks what’s just, swift righteousness to pursue
We’ve heard Moab’s pride, arrogance, and wrath; its boasts are all in vain / Moab will wail for Moab; all mourn Kir Hareseth’s raisin cakes, stricken with pain
Heshbon’s fields and Sibmah’s vine languish; choice branches broken down / I weep with Jazer; tears water Heshbon, Elealeh; war shouts strike harvest ground
Gladness and joy are gone; vineyard songs cease; no feet tread the press / I stopped the shout; my heart sounds harp-like for Moab, inward parts for Kir Heres
Moab prays at its sanctuary, but cannot prevail / Three years, contract workers count; Moab’s glory shamed, remnant small, frail
Damascus is no city now; a ruinous heap lies there / Aroer’s forsaken towns: flocks lie down, none make them afraid
Ephraim’s fortress and Damascus’ kingdom cease to stand / Syria’s remnant is like Israel’s glory in the land
Jacob’s glory grows thin; his flesh grows lean like reaped grain / Two or three topmost; four or five outer boughs remain
In that day, they look to Maker, honor Israel’s Holy One / They turn from hand-made altars, Asherah and incense they shun
Strong cities become desolate, like woods and peaks alone / You forgot the God who saves, the Rock your strength had known
You plant fine plants, foreign seedlings, hedge them in that day / At morning seed blooms; grief comes, harvest flees away
The nations roar like seas, mighty waters rushing by / He rebukes them; like chaff before the wind, they fly
At evening, terror; before morning, gone from view / This is plunderers’ portion, the lot of robbers too
Far past Cush’s rivers, wings rustle in the air, / Envoys sail papyrus boats through waters there.
Swift messengers go to tall, smooth folk, formidable from birth, / Whose rivers divide their land; they measure and tread the earth.
All earth, look when the mountain banner lifts in view, / And listen when the trumpet sounds; its call rings through.
Yahweh says, “I’ll be still, and see within my dwelling place,” / Like clear heat in sunshine, dew-cloud in harvest’s blaze.
Before harvest, bloom ends; each flower ripens to grape, / He cuts sprigs, cuts spreading branches down, takes them away.
Together left for ravenous mountain birds and beasts on ground, / Birds eat them in summer; beasts eat them when winter comes round.
At that time, that people’s gift comes to the site, / To Yahweh of Armies upon Mount Zion’s height.
Yahweh rides a swift cloud; Egypt’s idols shake with fear / Egypt’s heart melts within it as his presence draws near
Egypt turns against itself; its spirit fails in the fight / They seek idols, charmers, familiar spirits, wizards outright
Yahweh gives Egypt to a cruel lord’s hand / Its waters fail; the river dries across the land
Nile reeds and fields wither; the sown crops are gone / Fishermen and workers mourn the trades they relied on
Zoan’s princes are fools; Memphis’s princes, deceived, lead astray / Egypt staggers like a drunk in its vomit, starts to sway
No work remains in Egypt; all its tasks lie still / They tremble at Yahweh’s hand, and Judah’s name sends a chill
Five Egyptian cities speak Canaan; to Yahweh they swear / One is called the City of Destruction, they declare
An altar in Egypt, border pillar: Yahweh’s witness stands / He sends a savior to free the oppressed from oppressors’ hands
Egyptians know Yahweh; they worship, give offerings, and vow / They keep those vows; he strikes, they turn, he hears and heals them now
Egypt and Assyria are linked by one road / Their people pass between, worshipping as one
Egypt, Assyria, Israel bless the earth they share / Egypt my people, Assyria my work, Israel my heir
Assyria’s king sent Tartan to Ashdod to fight / He fought against Ashdod and took it outright
Yahweh said, “Loose sackcloth from your waist; remove sandals from feet” / He did so, walked naked, barefoot, the command complete
Isaiah walked three years naked, barefoot, to foretell / A sign and wonder concerning both of the lands as well
Egypt’s captives, Ethiopia’s exiles, led naked to shame / Young and old, barefoot, with buttocks uncovered the same
Egypt was their glory; Ethiopia, their stay / Now dismayed and confounded, their hopes fall away
“Behold, this is our expectation, where we fled for aid” / “And we, how will we be able to escape?” they say
Grievous vision: south whirlwinds sweep; traitors destroy the land / Elam, attack! I stopped all Media’s sighing at command
My thighs convulse with labor pains; I cannot hear or see / My heart flutters; horror frightens; dusk I desired shakes me
They set the table, post the watch, then eat and drink / “Rise up, you princes; oil the shield!”—the words ring
The Lord says, “Set a watchman; let him report what he sees” / Paired horsemen, donkeys, camels—he listens carefully
From tower, day and night, the watchman cries with lion’s sound / “Fallen, fallen Babylon; her gods’ images smashed to ground”
“You are my threshing, grain of my floor!”—Yahweh’s words I say / What Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s God said, I now relay
Seir asks, “Watchman, what of the night?”—and asks again / He answers, “Morning comes, and night; inquire; return then.”
Dedan’s caravans lodge in Arabia’s forest land / Tema brings bread to fugitives, water to thirsty band
Within one year, Kedar’s glory will be through / Yahweh, Israel’s God, spoke: mighty archers will be few
The joyous, shouting city crowds its rooftops, loud / Its slain were not by sword or battle brought down
Rulers fled together; archers bound those caught in flight / Look away; don't comfort me; I'll weep for my people's plight
Yahweh’s day brings confusion; walls begin to break / Cries rise to mountains; foe chariots mass at the gate
Judah looks to arms; David’s breaches spread wide / They gather water, break homes, fortify the side
They fail to look to their Maker or honor His design / They feast: “Let’s eat and drink, for tomorrow we will die”
Shebna carves a high tomb in the rock by hand / Yahweh hurls him like a ball to die in a distant land
Yahweh pulls Shebna from his post; Eliakim succeeds / Yahweh clothes him in robe and belt; rule he receives
He fathers Judah, Jerusalem; David’s key opens the door / What he opens none will shut; what he shuts, none opens anymore
Yahweh fastens him like a nail, set firm in the wall / His father’s house hangs glory on him, vessels great and small
The nail will give way that day, be cut down, and fall / Its burden is cut off; Yahweh has made the call
Ships from Tarshish howl: Tyre’s stronghold is razed / No house remains, no entry; from Kittim it’s relayed
The Nile’s rich harvest sailed over waters wide / She was the market where nations’ wares were supplied
Sea’s stronghold: no labor, birth; no young men nursed, nor virgins raised / And her childlessness has been shown, Sidon; be ashamed
Is this your joyous ancient city, whose feet traveled far away? / Who planned against Tyre, crown-giver, whose princely traders held sway?
Yahweh planned to stain all glory’s pride and fame / To bring all earth’s honorable to contempt and shame
His hand stretched over sea; kingdoms shook; Canaan’s forts must fall down / “Rejoice no more, Sidon’s daughter; go to Kittim, rest’s not found.”
Tyre is forgotten for seventy years; her name disappears / Take up the harp, prostitute; sing till remembrance appears
Yahweh will visit; she’ll play prostitute with all kingdoms once more / Her goods, wages, holy, not stored, feed and clothe those at his door
Yahweh makes earth empty, waste, turns upside down / He scatters its inhabitants all around
Priest and people, servant, master share the level plane / Buyer and seller stand as equals, no ranks remain
Earth fouled: laws, statutes, everlasting covenant defied / The curse has devoured; those dwelling there are burned, few survive
Wine, music, mirth are stilled; all joyful songs are gone / Each house is shut; the gate is struck, its joy withdrawn
Among the peoples, like olives shaken from the tree / Like vintage gleanings left when gathering is through
From the sea and earth’s farthest reach, they sing the righteous praise / “I pine away, I pine away! Woe is me; they betray, betray”
Fear, pit, and snare await the people of the land / The high windows open; earth’s foundations shake where they stand
The earth reels like a drunk; its disobedience weighs it down / It falls and never rises from the broken ground
Yahweh punishes the host on high, and earth’s kings shut away / Gathered in pit, shut in prison, visited after many days
The moon is confounded, the sun is ashamed / Yahweh reigns on Mount Zion; glory before elders displayed
My God, I exalt you; praise your name for wonders done / Planned long ago, in complete faithfulness and truth, each one
You made city a heap, fortress ruins; strangers’ palace won’t reappear / And strong peoples will glorify; awesome nations stand in fear
For poor and needy in distress, you’re their stronghold, their retreat / You are a refuge from the storm, and a shade from the heat
As heat in dry lands, you bring strangers’ loud noise down / As heat by the shade of a cloud, dreaded songs are brought down
On this mountain, for all peoples, you prepare / Choice meat and choice wine—a feast they all will share
You tear the nations’ veil; death is swallowed forevermore / You wipe tears from all faces; reproach from earth is no more
They say, “Behold, our God! We waited; he will save us,” they say / “Yahweh! We waited; glad, we rejoice in his salvation that day”
Moab, like straw in dung-water, is trodden down / He spreads hands as one swims; pride, craft, high walls brought to ground
The city stands strong; God appoints salvation for its walls / Open the gates; the righteous, faithful nation enters all
You keep the steadfast mind that trusts you in perfect peace / Trust Yahweh forever, the Rock whose years don’t cease
Yahweh brings the lofty city crashing to the ground / The poor and needy tread its dust and press it down
You make the righteous path level; for your judgments we wait / Your name and renown our souls desire; we seek you till late
Though shown favor, the wicked do wrong; your majesty they don’t see / They miss your lifted hand; see zeal, dismayed; foes burn in fire’s heat
Yahweh ordains our peace; your work for us is done / Though other lords ruled, we acknowledge your name alone
Yahweh, you increased the nation; your glory and borders grew / In trouble they prayed; we birthed wind, no deliverance came through
The dead won’t rise; you crushed them, their memory fades away / Your dead shall live; awake and sing, rise from the dust one day
Hide in your rooms, shut doors awhile till wrath has passed / Earth will reveal the blood of its slain, no longer masked
Yahweh’s hard, great, strong sword strikes Leviathan in flight / He punishes twisted serpent, kills dragon in sea outright
Yahweh keeps the pleasant vineyard, waters it every moment / Keeps it night and day, lest anyone damage it any moment
“Wrath is not in me; but thorns I’ll battle, burn outright” / “I’ll march on them; or let him grasp my strength and make peace right”
In days to come, Jacob will take root; Israel blooms, buds unfurled / Their fruit, it will fill the whole surface of all the world
Did He strike them as their strikers were struck, kill them the same? / In measure you send them away; His rough east wind blows them away
Jacob’s guilt forgiven; fruit: sin gone, altar stones smashed to pieces / Asherah poles, incense altars rise no more; their use ceases
Fortified city deserted, like wilderness; calf will feed there / Women burn withered boughs; their Maker shows the witless no care
Yahweh threshes from Euphrates to Egypt’s border / He gathers Israel’s children one by one in order
Trumpet sounds: Assyria’s perishing, Egypt’s outcasts appear / They worship Yahweh on Jerusalem’s holy mountain here
Woe to Ephraim’s drunkards, proud crown o’er the fertile vale, / Their glorious beauty fades, its flower turning pale.
The Lord casts them to earth; hail and flood scour the ground, / Like first-ripe figs, picked and eaten as soon as found.
For the remnant, Yahweh is a crown of glory bright, / Spirit of justice to those who judge, strength to turn back the fight.
Priests and prophets reel with wine, their visions are blurred, / They stumble in judgment; their tables are vomit-smeared.
They ask, “Whom will he teach? To whom explain the word?” / “Precept on precept, line on line”—the words they heard.
They would not hear his offered rest; strange tongues resound, / They go, fall back, are broken, snared and taken down.
Jerusalem’s rulers boast, “With Death our pact is sealed; / With Sheol we agree; no scourge will come; lies keep us concealed.”
Yahweh lays in Zion a tested, precious cornerstone, sure; / Believers won’t act hastily; justice measures, right stands pure.
Hail and flood sweep lies; their pact with Death cannot stand, / Morning and night, they’re trampled; terror close at hand.
Their bed is far too short for them to stretch within, / Their blanket’s far too narrow to wrap around their skin.
Yahweh will do his strange work; destruction draws near, / Scoffers, do not scoff, or tighter bonds will bind you here.
The farmer won’t plow forever; dill and cumin he sows, / God teaches judgment; wheat and barley, spelt in rows.
Each crop receives its proper threshing, as each one requires; / Yahweh’s counsel is wonderful; in wisdom he excels.
Woe, Ariel, where David camped; Yahweh hems her round / She’ll be an altar hearth, brought low; her words whisper from the ground
Her foes like dust and chaff are swept off in a haze / Yahweh visits: thunder, quake, storm, devouring blaze
All nations dream they eat, wake hungry; hunger stays / They dream they drink, wake faint; their thirst won’t go away
Yahweh pours a deep sleep; not wine-drunk, they reel / Vision’s a sealed book; its words will stay concealed
With lips they honor Yahweh, but their hearts are far away / His marvelous work makes wisdom of the wise decay
Woe to those who hide their counsel from Yahweh / They say, “Who sees us?” their deeds they won’t display
They turn things upside down: the made thing denies the potter’s hand / The formed thing says, “Its maker cannot understand”
Lebanon becomes a fruitful field, regarded as a wood / The deaf will hear the words, and the blind will see what they never could
The humble and poor rejoice in Yahweh; their joy will increase / The ruthless, the scoffers, all who twist justice will cease
Yahweh, who redeemed Abraham, says Jacob won’t bear shame / His children, God’s own handiwork, will sanctify His name
Jacob’s Holy One they sanctify; Israel’s God revere / The erring understand; grumblers instruction hear
Rebellious children make their plans, with Yahweh left behind / They make pacts without his Spirit, with sin on sin entwined
They seek through Pharaoh strength and Egypt’s shadow for shade / But Egypt brings them shame and confusion, not aid
On donkeys, camels, wealth crosses the South’s harsh ground / For Egypt, Rahab sits still; no help or gain is found
They cast Yahweh’s law aside; to seers they say, “Don’t see!” / To prophets: “Speak no right; tell pleasant lies”—that’s their decree
Trust oppression; their wrong swells like a wall set to fall / Yahweh smashes it like pottery, sparing no shard at all
Return and rest will save you; quiet trust makes you strong / They say, “We’ll flee on horses”; swift pursuers press along
One threat sends a thousand fleeing; five threats drive them to flight / Till left like beacon on peak, like banner on height
Yahweh waits to show them grace, his justice is fair / Blessed are all who wait for him; his mercy meets them there
In Zion, tears will end; Yahweh answers every cry / He gives them hardship’s bread and affliction’s water supply
Their teachers will be seen; the voice behind gives insight / “This is the way; walk in it,” when they turn left or right
They cast their silver and gold idols away as unclean / They tell them, “Go away!”—cast out, no longer seen
Rain feeds the seed; rich bread from the ground abounds / Livestock feed in the broad pastures all around
High mountain brooks run even as the towers fall / Moon shines like sun, sun sevenfold, as Yahweh heals them all
His voice and arm send storm and hail against Assyria’s might / His people sing as at a feast, to Israel’s Rock by night
Each stroke of Yahweh’s rod on him rings with tambourine sound / He fights them in the battle, weapons brandished all around
The king’s deep, spacious pyre was readied long ago / Much wood and fire; Yahweh’s sulfur breath sets it aglow
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, not Yahweh / They trust horses, chariots, horsemen strong, but don’t seek Yahweh
Yahweh is wise; disaster comes; his words won’t be unsaid / He rises against evildoers and iniquity’s aid
Egyptians are men, not God; their horses flesh, not spirit at all / When Yahweh stretches his hand, consumed, helper and helped fall
A lion and young lion growl over prey, unmoved by shepherds’ roar / So Yahweh descends to fight on Mount Zion and its heights in war
Like hovering birds, Yahweh shields Jerusalem from harm / He protects and delivers, passes over, preserves her
Children of Israel, return to him you deeply defied / Your hands made silver and gold idols; cast them aside
The Assyrian falls by a sword no man wields in his hand / He flees that sword; his young men are forced to labor on command
Assyria’s rock passes in terror; princes fear the banner’s sight / Yahweh’s fire is in Zion; his furnace is in Jerusalem
A king reigns in righteousness; just princes rule the land / A man is refuge from wind and storm, rock shade and streams at hand
The eyes that see will not grow dim; the ears that hear will heed / The rash hearts will understand; stammering tongues speak clear indeed
Fools profane Yahweh; hungry souls emptied, thirsty drinks run dry / Rogues lie to crush the humble, though needy speak aright
Women at ease, hear, tremble: vintage fails; no harvest will arrive / Strip yourselves, wear sackcloth, beat your breasts for fields and fruitful vine
Thorns and briars cover my people’s land; joy’s houses stand bare / Palace and city lie deserted; hill, tower are wild dens there
The waste lasts till Spirit is poured from on high / Wildlands grow fruitful; fields become forests in time
Justice will dwell in the wilderness, righteousness in fields / Righteousness brings peace, quiet, confidence that never yields
My people dwell in peace, safe homes; quiet rest they share / Though hail flattens the forest and levels the city bare
Blessed are those who sow beside all waters that flow / They send the ox and donkey forth, their feet set to go
Woe, you destroy and betray, though none has done so to you / When your work is complete, you’ll be destroyed and betrayed too
Yahweh, be gracious; we have waited for you each day / Be our strength each morning, salvation when trouble holds sway
The peoples flee at the thunder; nations scatter away / As caterpillars gather plunder, men leap like locusts for prey
Yahweh exalted on high; Zion’s justice and right fill its core / Steadiness, salvation, wisdom, knowledge; fear of Yahweh, your store
Peace’s envoys weep bitterly; highways lie empty and bare / Broken covenant, cities despised; land mourns, withers, stripped bare
“Now I will arise,” says Yahweh; you conceive chaff, stubble is born / Your breath is fire that will devour you; peoples burn like cut thorns
Yahweh calls far and near: hear his deeds, acknowledge his power / Zion’s sinners tremble: who lives where burning lasts forever?
The just shun oppression and evil; their rock stands secure / Their bread is supplied; their waters will surely endure
They see the king in beauty; a distant land is shown / They ponder terror: fierce people gone, their speech unknown
Zion now rests in stillness; its tent, stakes, and cords will remain / Yahweh with us in majesty, our judge, lawgiver, saves; he’ll reign
Rigging untied; mast-foot unbraced; they cannot spread sail / Forgiven, none says, “I am sick”; the lame take their share
Come near, you nations; peoples, now lend your ear / Earth, the world, and all that they contain, must hear
Yahweh enraged at all nations and armies, gives them to slaughter / The slain are cast out; their stench rises; mountains melt in their blood
The sky’s host dissolves; its armies start to fade / The heavens roll up like a scroll; fig leaves fall away
Yahweh’s sword comes down on Edom; judgment on the land / Bozrah’s sacrifice, Edom’s slaughter; vengeance for Zion’s cause
Edom’s streams turn to pitch, its dust to sulfur, its land afire / Night, day, unquenched; its smoke forever climbs up higher
Desert birds and creatures possess the wasteland’s plain / Confusion and emptiness measured across the terrain
Its nobles are gone; thorns overtake palace halls / Jackals and wild creatures dwell within its walls
Search Yahweh’s book: none missing, none lack a mate; they remain / His mouth commands; his Spirit gathers, allots their domain
