"To every kingdom, they'll be tossed around, A curse, a taunt, wherever they're found.
I'll send sword, famine, pestilence in my wrath, Till they're wiped from the land, down to the last."
That's the vision, clear and bold, The fate of Judah, plainly told.
Jeremiah got the word, Judah was in his sight, Fourth year of Jehoiakim, Babylon's first flight. For twenty-three years, I've spoken day by day, But y'all ain't listening, just turn away.
Prophets sent early, God's voice in their stride, “Turn from your evil, in the land abide. Don't chase other gods, don't provoke my wrath, Then I'll keep you safe, stay on my path.”
But you ignored, turned your ear away, Provoking anger, bringing judgment your way. Yahweh speaks, "You heard not my cries, So Babylon's comin', it's time to rise."
Nebuchadnezzar, my servant, will come, Turn your land to shock, make you feel numb. No joy or laughter, bride's voice will cease, Mirth turned to mourning, no light, no peace.
Seventy years, Babylon holds sway, Then I'll bring judgment, they'll repay. Desolation to the land, Chaldeans fall, Great kings rise, and Babylon crawls.
"Take this cup, wrath’s bitter drink, Nations will stagger, they'll fall, they'll sink. Sword in hand, make them reel, Jerusalem, Judah, all will feel."
Kings and lands, from Egypt to Uz, Philistines, Ammon, each has a buzz. The north, the south, all will drink, God’s wrath poured out, no time to think.
"Drink deep, feel the sword's might, Fall and rise no more, in the night. Yahweh calls, no nation unscathed, Sword on earth, His judgment engraved."
Proclaim His roar, His mighty shout, Judgment's here, no doubt about. From end to end, His controversy flows, Wicked to sword, His justice shows.
Evil storm, nation to nation, Yahweh's fury, no hesitation. Slain on earth, no one cries, On the ground, life's demise.
Shepherds wail, leaders weep, No escape, judgment's deep. Yahweh roars from His place, Land astonished, His fierce face.
In Jehoiakim’s reign, Yahweh’s word came, To Judah's cities, loud and clear, no shame.
“Stand in my house, deliver my decree, Speak every word, don’t omit, hear Me.
Maybe they’ll listen, turn from their wrong ways, I might hold back the wrath that for years it weighs.”
“Tell them,” Yahweh declared, “listen up, Walk in my law, don’t interrupt.
Heed my prophets, I send them to you, Rise early, sending, but you refuse.
If not, this house becomes Shiloh’s fate, This city a curse, destruction’s gate.”
Jeremiah spoke, the priests heard it all, They seized him quick, in Yahweh’s hall.
“You’ll die,” they cried, “for your prophecy, Calling this house Shiloh, city's desolate sea.”
Princes from the king’s house heard the scene, Sat by the gate, where the crowd had been.
Priests and prophets shouted, “He should die, He’s spoken against us, why, oh why?”
Jeremiah rose, his voice was strong, “Yahweh sent me to right this wrong.
Change your ways, listen to Yahweh’s call, He’ll relent from evil, no downfall.”
“Do as you will, I’m in your hand, But shed my blood, you’ll curse this land.”
Princes and people, they took a pause, “This man speaks truth, he breaks no laws.”
Elders stood up, their words rang through, “Micah spoke too, and Hezekiah knew.
Zion’s fields plowed, Jerusalem in heaps, Yet they didn’t kill him, Yahweh keeps.”
Another prophet, Uriah by name, Spoke like Jeremiah, met the same game.
Jehoiakim sought his life, Uriah fled, But from Egypt taken, soon he was dead.
Jeremiah spared by Ahikam’s hand, Protected from death, in Yahweh’s land.
In Jehoiakim's reign, a word came through, Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, here's what to do: "Make bonds, make bars, put them on your neck, Send them to the kings — show them respect.
To Edom and Moab, Ammon, and Tyre, Sidon too, with messengers — don't tire. Tell their masters this command from above, Yahweh of Armies, the God they should love.
'I made the earth, men, animals with power, Gave it as I saw fit, in the right hour. Now Nebuchadnezzar, Babylon's mighty king, Holds these lands — to him the nations bring.
All will serve him, son, and grandson, Till his time's up and his own land's gone. But if a nation won't bow under his yoke, They'll face sword, famine, pestilence — no joke.
Don't heed your prophets, dreamers, or those, Who say "Don't serve Babylon" — they're false, God knows. They're lying, pulling you from your land, I drive you out — it's Yahweh's hand.
But nations serving Babylon, that's the key, They'll stay on their land, live peacefully. Zedekiah, listen to these words I bring, Serve Babylon's king, find life in this thing.
Why die by sword, famine, pestilence, When Yahweh’s words show the consequence? Don't buy the lies of prophets that deceive, I didn't send them, don't be naive.
I spoke to priests and the people too, Yahweh says, "Don't let false words fool you. The vessels won't be back from Babylon fast, Their prophets lie — that tale won't last.
Serve Babylon, live — don't let the city fall, If they speak truth, let them to Yahweh call. The vessels in His house will stay away, Till Yahweh visits them one fine day.
Nebuchadnezzar didn't take 'em all, When Jeconiah and nobles heard the call. Yahweh of Armies says, vessels will go, To Babylon, till His visit — this you should know.
Then they'll return, restored to this place, Yahweh will bring them back, in His grace."
In the reign of Zedekiah, the scene was set, Hananiah spoke with a claim you won't forget. “In Yahweh’s house,” he said to the crowd, “‘I’ll break the yoke of Babylon!’” he vowed.
“In two years’ time, vessels will return, From Nebuchadnezzar’s grasp, watch them burn. Jeconiah and captives will come back too, The yoke of Babylon, I’ll break through.”
Jeremiah stood, his voice rang clear, “Amen, may Yahweh make it happen here. But listen now, to the word I proclaim, A prophet’s truth is known by the peace he can claim.”
Hananiah took the bar from Jeremiah’s neck, “Yahweh will break Babylon’s yoke,” he said in check. Jeremiah left, the moment intense, But Yahweh’s voice came, making perfect sense.
“Hananiah, your work is flawed, You break wooden bars, but here's the rod. Iron yokes on nations, Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, The animals too, under his domain.”
Jeremiah warned, his words did fly, “Hananiah, false prophet, you lead with a lie. Yahweh declares, your time is done, In this very year, your life's undone.”
In the seventh month, Hananiah fell, A prophet's life ended, with truth to tell.
Jeremiah writes from the city's core, To exiles far, behind Babylon's door.
He sends the word, to captives bound tight, Saying, "Live your lives, don't fight the night.
Build your homes and gardens, plant seeds in the ground, Grow your families, let your joy resound.
Seek the city's peace, and pray for its good, In its welfare, find your own livelihood.
Don't trust the false dreams, or prophets who lie, I didn't send them," says Yahweh, "they defy.
After seventy years, I'll bring you back home, With peace and hope, no more to roam.
Call on me, I'll hear, I'll be found by you, With all your heart, seek, find a future true.
I'll end your captivity, gather from the lands, Bring you back to where your freedom stands."
But for those who remain in the city alone, Yahweh's wrath comes, through sword and stone.
Rotten figs they'll be, scattered and lost, For ignoring my prophets, this is their cost.
Ahab and Zedekiah, liars in my name, To Babylon's fire, they'll be put to shame.
Shemaiah's words, false letters he sends, Punishment awaits, for him and his friends.
The captivity's lengthy, but do not despair, In the ground of your trial, sprout hope everywhere.
For Yahweh's plans are good, though long may it seem, In the end, you'll awaken from this distant dream.
Listen up, Jeremiah, hear what Yahweh’s sayin’, "Write it all down, every word I'm relayin'.
"The days will come when I’ll flip the scene, Bring back my people to where they’ve been.
Fear and trembling, voices of dread, But in the end, they'll rise from the dead.
Why do I see men holding their waist? Faces pale, like they've been chased.
A day unlike any, Jacob's in trouble, But he’ll be saved, make that hope double.
"On that day, I’ll break your chains, No more strangers with their reigns.
Serve Yahweh, and David will rise, Don't fear, Jacob, no more cries.
I'll save you from afar, your kids too, Bring you back home, safe and true.
I'm with you, says Yahweh, your guide, Nations fall, but you'll abide.
Your hurt's deep, wounds severe, Nobody to help, no cure near.
Lovers forgot you, left you alone, Your sins piled up, like a heavy stone.
Why weep over pain that won't go? For your wrongs, the punishment flows.
Those who devour will be devoured, Adversaries captured, no more empowered.
Health I’ll restore, heal those wounds, Zion the outcast, now renewed.
"I’ll bring back Jacob's tents, show compassion, City rebuilt, in glorious fashion.
Thankful songs from voices raised, Multiply them, be amazed.
Kids like before, strong congregation, Oppressors punished, no hesitation.
A prince from them, a ruler so bold, Draws near to me, hearts of gold.
"You’ll be my people, I’ll be your God, Watch Yahweh’s storm, striking hard.
His wrath won’t rest till it’s done, Understand it all when it's begun."
"At that time," Yahweh spoke with might, "I'll be Israel's God, in their hearts, alight." Survivors in the wild, they found my grace, Even when they wandered in a restless place.
"I loved you long, with love that won't fade, With kindness I drew you, though you've strayed." "I'll build you again, with tambourines in hand, Dance with joy across this promised land."
"Vineyards on Samaria's hills you'll plant anew, Watchmen call, ‘To Zion, let's go, me and you!’" "Sing for Jacob, shout for nations to hear, 'Save your people, Yahweh, bring them near.'"
From the north and farthest land, they'll form a throng, The blind, the lame, together they belong. With tears they'll come, led by rivers' gentle flow, "For I am their Father, I will make it so."
"Declare my word to distant shores, 'He scattered, He'll gather, like a shepherd restores.'" Ransomed from the stronger hand, now redeemed, To Zion they sing, to Yahweh's goodness streamed.
Like a watered garden, their souls will thrive, Young and old dance, mourning can't survive. "I'll turn their sorrow to joy," Yahweh decrees, "Satisfy the priests, my goodness will please."

But Rachel weeps, her children are no more, "Hold your tears," Yahweh whispers, "I'll restore." "They'll return from the enemy's grasp," He declares, "There's hope in the end, renewal in their lairs."
Ephraim's grief, like an untrained calf's cry, "Turn me, Yahweh, for I have gone awry." Confounded by shame, yet remembered dear, "My heart yearns for mercy, I'll draw him near."
"Set up signs, guide your heart back home, Turn again, Israel, no longer roam." "A new thing's created, a woman will surround, Judah's speech will bless, as they are unbound."
The weary, replenished, find rest at last, Yahweh's watch over them, unbroken, steadfast. "The days approach," Yahweh says with grace, "To sow Israel and Judah in this sacred space."

Their sour grapes no longer the children's fate, Each bears their iniquity, their own weight. "A new covenant I'll write on their hearts within, They'll know me, from least to greatest, cleansed of sin."
The sun and moon obey Yahweh's command, "If these depart, Israel won't stand," Yet Yahweh's promise holds the nation tight, "Forever they remain in my sight."
"The city's built, from Hananel's tower to the gate, Holy to Yahweh, in peace they'll wait." The land, once marred by death and decay, Is Yahweh's forever, unthrown and to stay."
In the tenth year of King Zedekiah's reign, Jeremiah locked up, prophecy brought him pain.
Babylon’s army was at Jerusalem’s door, Zedekiah asked, "Why spread these tales of war?"
"Yahweh speaks," Jeremiah did proclaim, "This city's Babylon's prize, it's not to remain.
Zedekiah won't escape, Babylon's king he'll meet, Face to face, his eyes he'll greet.
"They'll take the king to Babylon until I visit," declares Yahweh, "Fight all you want, but victory won't stay."
Jeremiah recounted, "Yahweh's word to me came, Hanamel's field in Anathoth, 'twas part of the game.
'Buy the field,' he said, ‘it's redemption time.’ When Hanamel approached, I knew it was divine.
Seventeen shekels weighed, the deal sealed and signed, Witnesses gathered, the legal deed aligned.
Baruch held the deed, in an earthen vessel stored, Houses and fields will rise again, declared the Lord."
Jeremiah prayed, "Ah Lord Yahweh, great is your might, You made the heavens and earth, nothing's beyond your sight.
Loving and kind, to thousands you show, Repaying the fathers for deeds long ago.
Signs in Egypt, your name's renowned, You delivered your people with miracles profound.
You gave them a land, milk and honey it flows, Yet they disobeyed, calamity now shows.
Siege ramps rise, Chaldeans take the city by sword, Yet you say, ‘Buy the field,’ oh Lord."
Then Yahweh spoke once more, "Is anything too hard, I'm the God of all, for sure.
The city to Chaldeans and Nebuchadnezzar will fall, They'll burn it down, despite cries and calls.
From youth, evil in my sight they've done, Provoked my anger, now they're on the run.
But I'll gather them back from lands far and wide, They'll dwell safely, with me they'll abide.
My people they'll be, I'll be their God, One heart, one way, they'll fear, they'll laud.
An everlasting covenant, I’ll not turn away, With joy I'll plant them, they’ll forever stay.
Fields will be bought, deeds signed anew, For I will reverse their captivity," declares Yahweh—the truth.
Locked up tight, but Yahweh spoke again, To Jeremiah in the guard's domain.
"Yahweh's my name, I form and I make, Call to me, great things I'll awake.
The city houses, broken down with might, Men fight the Chaldeans, fallen in the night.
But behold, health and cure I'll bring, Peace and truth, like a mighty spring.
Judah and Israel, I'll restore their place, Cleanse their sins, and grant them grace.
The city's name, a joy to behold, Nations will tremble at the story told.
Voices of joy, bride and groom they'll say, Thanks to Yahweh, His love will stay.
Flocks will roam once more in peace, In Judah's cities, new life will increase.
Behold the days, a Branch will rise, Justice and righteousness in David's eyes.
Judah saved, Jerusalem safe and sound, Yahweh our righteousness, all around.
David's throne will never stand bare, Priests will offer, a continual prayer.
If day and night can break apart, Then my covenant too will depart.
David's line, countless like the sand, Priests my ministers, they'll expand.
Don't say Yahweh's cast off chosen kin, For their captivity I'll turn, mercy will begin."
Yo, Jeremiah's got a word from Yahweh, it's dire, The king of Babylon's here, gonna set the city on fire.
"Zedekiah, listen up," Yahweh’s message is clear, "You can't escape Babylon, your fate’s drawing near."
"You’ll see the king face to face, eye to eye, But you'll go to Babylon, you won’t die by the sword, you'll die with a sigh."
"They'll mourn you like kings who’ve passed before, Burning incense, they’ll cry out, 'Ah Lord!' evermore."
Jeremiah spoke it, while battles raged on, Babylon’s army strong, and the cities nearly gone.
Then a covenant made, freedom proclaimed, Servants set free, but the people felt chained.
They turned and took back what they had let go, Yahweh's anger flared, his words began to flow:
"I freed your fathers from Egypt's land, Said every seventh year, release them, that was my command."
"You did right for a moment, then profaned my name, Brought back your servants, played this wicked game."
"Now hear me out, you’ve ignored my decree, So I’ll proclaim a freedom — to sword, plague, and misery."
"Enemies closing in, bodies left for the birds, Zedekiah and his princes, captured, you heard."
"I’ll bring Babylon back, make this city a blaze, Judah’s cities desolate, no one left to praise."
Word to Jeremiah, came straight from Yahweh, "Go to Rechabites, bring them, hear what they say.
Invite them in, offer wine in Yahweh’s house, Test their resolve, see if they stick to their vows."
So I gathered Jaazaniah, the whole Rechab crew, Led them to the room, where the sons of Hanan grew.
Bowls full of wine, I set before their eyes, Said, "Drink up, enjoy, don’t be shy."
But they replied, "No wine will touch our lips, Jonadab, our father, gave us these tips:
'No wine, no fields, no homes will we claim, In tents we dwell, nomads in name.'"
Obeyed Jonadab, their father’s command, No wine, no homes, just tents on this land.
But Babylon’s king brought fear to the land, They said, "To Jerusalem, take a stand."
Yahweh spoke again, His words to share, "Judah, listen up, do you even care?
Jonadab’s words, his sons they obey, But you ignore Me, day after day.
Prophets I sent, calling you back, Turn from your ways, but you’ve kept off track.
Jonadab’s sons, they honor and heed, Yet you, My people, won’t listen, won’t lead."
"So watch out, Judah, hear the alarm, Evil comes your way, see the harm.
Rechabites stand firm, obey and stay true, And for this loyalty, here’s what I’ll do:
Their line will remain, forever they’ll stand, Before Me, Yahweh, their legacy planned."
In Jehoiakim's fourth year, a word came clear, "Jeremiah, write my words for all to hear.
On a scroll, inscribe what I’ve said in the past, 'Bout Israel, Judah, nations, warnings vast.
Maybe Judah will heed, turn from sin's dark thread, If they change their ways, I’ll forgive them,’ God said.
Jeremiah called Baruch, his scribe with skill, Baruch penned God’s words, Jeremiah's voice to fill.
Jeremiah instructed, "I’m bound, can't enter there, So you read Yahweh’s words, let the people be aware.
On the fast day, read aloud in Yahweh's holy space, Maybe they’ll seek mercy, return to God’s grace."
Baruch followed through, did just as he was told, In Yahweh's house, the words of wrath were bold.
In the fifth year, ninth month, a fast was declared, Judah’s people gathered, God’s message shared.
Baruch stood and read in the house up high, Gemariah's room, beneath the clear blue sky.
Micaiah heard the words, urgency in his stride, To the king’s house he went, the news couldn’t hide.
Princes gathered round, scribes and noble men, Micaiah shared the words, told them what and when.
They called for Baruch, "Bring the scroll you read, Let us hear these words that make hearts dread."
In their presence, Baruch read each line, Fear sparked in their eyes, a message so divine.
"We’ll tell the king," they vowed, trembling with fright, "Baruch, how did you write?" they asked that night.
"Jeremiah spoke, I wrote it down," Baruch replied, With ink upon the scroll, he couldn't hide.
"Go, hide yourselves," the princes then implored, "Stay out of sight, don’t be ignored."
They took the scroll to the king’s winter den, But kept it aside, told the king again.
The king sent Jehudi, "Bring the scroll, let’s see," He read before the king, beside the blazing heat.
As Jehudi read, the king with knife in hand, Cut the scroll, fed it to the fire as planned.
No fear in their hearts, no garments torn, Despite the warnings, contempt was born.
Elnathan pleaded, "Please, don't burn this scroll," The king wouldn’t listen, stubborn his soul.
He ordered arrests, Jeremiah and Baruch, But Yahweh hid them, their capture forsook.
Then God spoke again, once the scroll burned away, "Write once more, Jeremiah, what I have to say.
Tell of Jehoiakim’s fate, for burning My word, No son on his throne, his end shall be heard.
Punishment will come, for servants and kin, The evil declared, for ignoring their sin."
Jeremiah took another scroll, Baruch wrote anew, The same words of warning, and more God did imbue.
Zedekiah ruled, but not by his own hand, Nebuchadnezzar's choice for Judah's land.
Yet he and his servants shut their ears tight, Ignoring Yahweh's words, no prophet in sight.
Zedekiah sent his men to Jeremiah, to say, "Pray to Yahweh for us, guide our way."
Jeremiah walked free, mingling with the crowd, Not yet in chains, still speaking aloud.
Pharaoh’s troops advanced, breaking the siege wide, Chaldeans backed off, dispersed to the side.
Then Yahweh spoke clear, through Jeremiah's voice, "Tell Judah's king, there's no other choice.
Pharaoh's aid is fleeting; they'll retreat back in haste, Chaldeans will return, laying the city to waste.
Don't fool yourselves, thinking they've gone, They'll rise again, and the city's forlorn.
Even if wounded, their strength shall inspire, They'll come back and burn this city with fire."
With Chaldeans gone, Jeremiah tried to leave, Heading to Benjamin, his portion to retrieve.
At Benjamin's gate, a guard called him out, "You’re defecting," he claimed, with a shout.
Jeremiah declared, "It's a lie, I'm true!" But they dragged him to the princes, who beat him black and blue.
Locked up deep, in the scribe's prison kept, Jeremiah waited, while the city slept.
Zedekiah called him, secret words exchanged, "What's Yahweh's word?" Jeremiah's voice ranged.
"There is a word," he said, without a quiver, "You’ll be delivered to Babylon's river."
Jeremiah then questioned, "Why am I here? What have I done to earn this fear?
Your prophets lied, where are they now? They said Babylon would never come, with a bow.
Please, my king, don't send me back there, To the scribe's house, where death's in the air."
Zedekiah heard, and moved him with a nod, To the court of the guard, with daily bread from God.
So Jeremiah stayed, held but fed, Awaiting the fate that lay ahead.
Shephatiah and the crew, they heard the news, Jeremiah spoke truth, and it shook their views. "Yahweh says, stay here and face your doom, But head to the Chaldeans, and escape the gloom."
"This city's handed over," Yahweh declared, To Babylon's army, the king prepared. The princes said, "Let's put this man down, He's causing fear, spreading panic in town."
King Zedekiah sighed, "He's in your hand, I can't fight you, I can't command." Into the dungeon, they let Jeremiah fall, No water, just mire, he sank with it all.
Ebedmelech the Ethiopian heard the plight, Went to the king, said, "This isn't right. Jeremiah's cast in, with famine and dread, Without rescue, soon he'll be dead."
The king ordered, "Take thirty men, go quick, Lift him from the dungeon, don't let him stick." With rags and cords, they pulled him high, Jeremiah's safe, no longer to die.
Zedekiah called for Jeremiah's word, "Tell me the truth, let it be heard." But Jeremiah feared, "Will you take my life? You won't listen, just cause more strife."
Yet Zedekiah swore, "As Yahweh lives, Your life, I won't give." Jeremiah spoke, "The Lord's decree: Go to Babylon's prince, your life will be free."
"But if not, this city will burn, Chaldeans win, and you'll have no turn." Zedekiah feared the defectors' scorn, But Jeremiah urged him, "Obey, be reborn."
"Refuse, and ruin's what Yahweh showed, Your house will crumble, down that road." Zedekiah pleaded, "Let no one know, If they ask, tell them where you wish to go."
The princes came, asked their things, Jeremiah spoke as advised by the king. He stayed in the guard, his patience vast, Until Jerusalem's fall came at last.
In Zedekiah's ninth year, Babylon marched with might, Nebuchadnezzar's army came, set Jerusalem in their sight.
By the eleventh year, the city wall was breached, The Babylonian princes entered, the city's heart they reached.
Zedekiah saw them come, he and his soldiers fled, Through the garden's gate by night, to Arabah they sped.
Chaldeans gave chase, caught him in Jericho's field, To Nebuchadnezzar they brought him, his fate was sealed.
Sons of Zedekiah fell before his eyes, Nobles of Judah, too, faced their demise.
His eyes were put out, bound in chains so tight, To Babylon they led him, out of Judah's sight.
Chaldeans burned houses, Jerusalem's walls came down, Nebuzaradan took captives, led them to Babylon's town.
Yet some poor folk stayed, vineyards and fields they gained, A new life in the land, though much had changed.
Nebuchadnezzar spoke of Jeremiah, a command he gave, "Protect him, do no harm, as he wishes, behave."
Jeremiah was freed, Gedaliah took him in, Among the people now, a new chapter would begin.
Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, words to Ebedmelech brought, “Destruction's coming, but you, fear not.”
“I'll save you that day," Yahweh's promise clear, "You'll escape with your life, for in Me you hold dear."
Jeremiah, chains released in the land, Nebuzaradan set him free, gave him a stand. "Yahweh spoke this doom, here it's done, 'Cause you sinned, now the deed’s begun.
Today you're free, the chains are gone, Choose your path, where you belong. Come to Babylon, I'll care for you, Or stay here, where you feel it’s true."
While he lingered, he heard the call, "Go back to Gedaliah, stand tall. Live among those left behind, Or choose the path you want to find."
Food and a gift, the captain gave, Jeremiah, now no longer a slave. He went to Mizpah, with Gedaliah stayed, Where Judah’s remnant had obeyed.
The captains heard, from the fields they came, Gedaliah's rule, now his name. Men, women, children, left in the land, Not taken captive, under Babylon’s hand.
Gedaliah swore, "Don’t fear the Chaldeans, Serve them well, live with reason. I'll be at Mizpah, for the Chaldean sight, Gather your fruits, in vessels tight."
Jews from Moab, Ammon, and Edom’s shores, Heard Judah had a remnant once more. Back they came, with wine in hand, To Gedaliah in Judah's land.
But Johanan warned, "Baalis sends strife, Ishmael's coming to take your life." Gedaliah, calm, didn't believe the threat, "False words, Ishmael's not a threat yet."
In secret, Johanan tried again, "Let me stop Ishmael, save us men. Why risk your life, let us live, Prevent the chaos that he might give."
But Gedaliah shook his head, said, "You speak falsely, let it be dead." The tension rose, but he stood unmoved, In Mizpah, where the remnant proved.
Seventh month rolls in, Ishmael's on the scene, Royal blood, ten men, a deadly team. They met in Mizpah, broke bread with Gedaliah, Then Ishmael rose up, dealt death with fire.
With swords they struck, Gedaliah fell, Governor no more, by Babylon's spell. Jews and Chaldeans, they met their fate, Ishmael's wrath, they couldn't escape.
Two days passed, no news had spread, Eighty men came, mourning the dead. From Shechem, Shiloh, with offerings in hand, Ishmael met them, tears in the sand.
He lured them in, "Come see Gedaliah," he said, But into the pit, those men were led. Yet ten men pleaded, "Spare us, we pray, We've hidden treasures, just let us stay."
He spared their lives, but the pit was filled, With bodies of those whom Ishmael killed. He took captives, the king's daughters bound, Off to Ammon, they were outward bound.
But Johanan heard, and gathered his band, To fight Ishmael, to take a stand. At Gibeon's waters, the clash was near, People rejoiced when Johanan appeared.
Captives turned back, glad to be free, Yet Ishmael escaped, with a menacing spree. Johanan gathered the remnants, moved on, To dwell near Bethlehem, before the dawn.
Fear of Chaldeans drove them to flee, To Egypt they aimed, seeking to be free. For Ishmael had killed, and the land was torn, Babylon's governor, now forlorn.
Captains and people, from least to the great, Came to Jeremiah, with worries so weight. "Pray to Yahweh for this remnant, so few, Show us the path, the things we should do."
Jeremiah replied, "I hear your plea, I'll pray to Yahweh, wait and see. Whatever He speaks, I'll tell you straight, Not a word will I keep, no delay, no wait."
They swore to obey, come good or bad, Yahweh’s witness, in this they were glad. "Whether it’s tough, or makes us feel free, We'll follow Yahweh, so well it will be."
Ten days passed, Yahweh spoke at last, Jeremiah called them, no time to contrast. "Yahweh says, stay in this land, I'll build, Not tear you down, your hopes fulfilled."
"Don’t fear Babylon, I’ll save you, I'll grant mercy, help you through. Return to your land, don't break the plan, Stay in this place, where you began."
"But if you say, 'To Egypt we go,' No war, no sound of trumpet, no woe. Hear Yahweh's word, Judah’s remnant, In Egypt, death awaits, your fears sent."
"Sword and famine will chase you down, In Egypt's land, you’ll wear a frown. For Yahweh’s wrath will outpour, As Jerusalem saw, you'll see it more."
"Don’t go to Egypt," Yahweh declared, "You’ve been warned, you should have cared. Deceit against your souls you’ve shown, Prayed for a word, yet truth's unknown."
"I’ve told you today, but you've not heard, Yahweh's commands, not a single word. You'll die by sword, famine, pestilence near, In the place you desire, where you steer."
Jeremiah spoke God's truth, every word he said, Azariah and Johanan shook their heads, "It's all in your head.
Jeremiah, you're lying, God didn't send you here, Saying 'Don't go to Egypt'—that's not what we hear.
Baruch's turned you against us, to hand us to Chaldeans, To take us captive, that's his dark scheming.
But they ignored the voice of Yahweh, their God, Johanan and his men on a path that was flawed.
They gathered Judah's remnant, men and women in tow, All the people left in Judah, they had to go.
With Jeremiah and Baruch, they made their way, To Egypt's land—they didn't obey.
Down to Tahpanhes, they arrived with haste, Ignoring God's word, they sealed their fate.
Then Yahweh spoke to Jeremiah, clear and loud, "Take these stones, hide them in the crowd.
In Pharaoh's brickwork, where all can see, Say, 'Here Nebuchadnezzar's throne will be.'
The king of Babylon, my servant, he'll reign, His throne on these stones, it's all preordained.
Egypt will shatter, death and captivity, To the sword, the fire—it's their destiny.
He'll burn their gods' houses, take them away, Arrayed like a shepherd, he'll leave in the day.
Beth Shemesh's pillars, they'll break and burn, Egypt's gods' houses, to ashes they'll turn."
Jeremiah got the word, to Egypt's land he came, Speaking to the Jews, hear this message, feel the flame.
"Yahweh of Armies speaks, you've seen the ruin, Jerusalem's left empty, cities of Judah in ruin.
All 'cause of wicked deeds, incense to gods unknown, Provoking anger, my wrath has overthrown.
I sent prophets early, saying 'Don’t dare do this thing,' Yet you turned deaf ears, worshiping false gods like a king.
So my wrath poured out, in Judah's streets they fell, Wasted and desolate, in a sorrowful, silent shell.
Now Yahweh speaks again, why harm your own soul? Cutting off your kin, leaving not one whole.
Burning incense in Egypt, provoking with your hands, To become a curse, be scattered across lands.
Have you forgotten the sins of your fathers and kings? They walked not in my laws, disregarding all things.
So now I face you, cutting off all of Judah's might, Those who sought Egypt to live, consumed in the night.
By sword, famine, pestilence, they'll fall, A horror, curse, reproach — they won't stand tall.
No remnant will return, except the ones who flee, Yet all will see whose word will truly be.
The people answered Jeremiah, they wouldn’t heed the call, "We’ll do what we want, burning incense, offerings tall.
Back then life was sweet, food plenty, all was well, Now without our worship, sword and famine fell."
Jeremiah replied, "You think Yahweh forgot your actions? He remembers your incense, saw your transactions.
That's why desolation and curses now reign, You didn’t listen to His voice, hence the pain."
Jeremiah said further, "Hear Yahweh’s strong decree, You've declared your vows, now fulfill them, let it be.
Yet hear Yahweh’s word, your fate is clear, His name will no longer be spoken here.
Watched for evil, not good, by sword and famine consumed, Few will escape, back to Judah, where doom loomed.
This is your sign; Yahweh’s words will take their place, Pharaoh Hophra’s fate sealed, given to enemies who chase."
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign, Jeremiah spoke words that Baruch did gain.
"Yahweh, God of Israel, has this to say, To you, Baruch, listen, don't stray.
You cried out, 'Woe, for sorrow adds to my pain, I'm weary, groaning, seeking rest in vain.'
Tell him this, Yahweh's message is clear, 'What I've built, I'll break, what I've planted, I shear.
Do you seek greatness, things for yourself? Don't chase them, for I'll bring trouble to all else.'
Says Yahweh, 'But here's the deal, Your life I'll protect, it's the real seal.'"
The word came down to Jeremiah's ear, About nations far and nations near.
"Prepare your shield, get ready to fight, Mount the horses, stand up with might.
Polish those spears, put on the mail, Why do I see them dismayed and pale?
Mighty ones beaten, fleeing in fear, Terror's around, nothing is clear."
"Don't let the swift escape the fray, By Euphrates' river, they fall today.
Who rises like the Nile, high and wide? Egypt's waters surge like a pride.
'I’ll cover the earth,' Egypt boasts of power, 'I'll destroy cities, this is my hour.'
Charge, you horses! Chariots, rage! Mighty men, with strength engage.
For Yahweh's day, a vengeance to claim, The sword drinks blood, ends their game.
Go to Gilead, take balm for the pain, But healing escapes, all efforts in vain.
Nations hear cries, shame spreads wide, Mighty men stumble, side by side."
Yahweh spoke, a word to declare, "Babylon strikes, Egypt beware.
Shout in Egypt, Migdol, Memphis, hear, ‘Prepare for the sword, it's drawing near.’
Strong ones fall, they don't stand tall, Yahweh's push makes them all crawl.
‘Rise, return to our birthland,’ they say, Pharaoh's just noise, wasted the day.
'As I live,' Yahweh declares with might, Tabor and Carmel, he comes to fight.
Egypt, beautiful heifer, now desolate, From the north rides your fate.
Hired men like calves, fled away, On calamity's day, they can't stay.
Sound of a serpent, armies march on, Axes like woodcutters, Egypt's gone.
Yahweh says, 'I punish all in sight, Amon, Pharaoh, all in my might.
Into Babylon's hand, I’ll give them all, Yet Egypt will rise, as old days call.
But Jacob, don’t fear, my servant true, I’ll save you from lands, make you new.
Quiet and calm, Jacob returns free, No fear to be, for I am with thee.
I’ll end all nations, where you’ve roamed, But not you, Jacob, you’ll come home."
Yo, listen up, here's a tale from the land, Before Pharaoh's strike, Jeremiah takes a stand.
"Behold, waters rise, coming down from the north, Overflowing the land, pouring forth with great wrath.
Men will cry out, wails will fill the air, At the sound of hoofbeats, bringing despair.
Rushing chariots, wheels rumbling loud, Fathers too weak, not turning around.
The day is coming to end the Philistine's fight, Cutting off Tyre, leaving Sidon's helpers in fright.
Yahweh declares the Philistine's fate, From Caphtor's isle, there's no escape.
Gaza's gone bald, Ashkelon's no more, How long will your mourning cut to the core?
"Yahweh's sword, when will you cease? Return to the scabbard, find your peace."
But how can it rest, when Yahweh's command, Points against Ashkelon, the seashore's sand?
The sword is appointed, its path is set, No quiet will come till the goal is met.
"Woe to Nebo!" Yahweh's shout rings loud, Kiriathaim's taken, Misgab's lost its proud.
Moab's glory's vanished, Heshbon plots its fall, "Let's cut her off," they scheme, heed Madmen's call.
A cry from Horonaim, destruction's near, Moab's kids weep, their wails fill the air.
Up Luhith they climb, tears never cease, Down Horonaim's path, cries of no peace.
"Flee for your lives, like junipers wild," Trust in your works, but treasures defiled.
Chemosh's bound, his priests led away, The destroyer comes, no city will stay.
Give wings to Moab, let her fly fast, Desolation claims her, none there to last.
"Cursed is he," Yahweh warns with wrath, Who shirks his duty, who holds back his path.
Moab's been easy, settled since youth, But change is coming, this is the truth.
"Days will come," Yahweh sends pourers to Moab, Breaking and emptying, no pride to grab.
Moab shamed like Israel once felt, Valiant talk's cheap, when faced with what's dealt.
"The calamity's close," Yahweh's decree, Mourn for Moab, broken staff, bent knee.
Dibon's glory falls, sit in despair, The destroyer comes, your strength laid bare.
Aroer's watcher asks those who flee, "What happened here? What did they see?"
Moab's broken, wail by the Arnon's stream, Judgment hits plain country, no city's dream.
Moab's horn cut, his arm's now weak, Yahweh declares his pride's at its peak.
Moab's pride known, "I know his boast," Yahweh laments, Moab's place is toast.
Cry for Moab, Kir Heres too, Sibmah’s vine, your joy is through.
No joy, no wine, presses stand still, Moab's lamentation echoes the hill.
Pipes mourn Moab, from head to beard, Sackcloth worn, Moab's fate is feared.
Yahweh breaks Moab, like a vessel smashed, Moab's shame's a tale all will have hashed.
"Eagle flies," declares Yahweh bold, Moab's strongholds fall, hearts grow cold.
Moab destroyed, pride led to this, Terror, pit, snare—none can miss.
"Who flees terror finds the pit," Yahweh warns, Snare awaits all, in this year of scorns.
Fire from Heshbon, Sihon's flame, Moab devoured, head bowed in shame.
"Woe, Moab, Chemosh's folk are undone," Sons and daughters in chains, nowhere to run.
But Yahweh promises, "Days will change," Moab's future's written, though now's strange.
"Has Israel no sons, no heir?" God does declare, "Why’s Gad in Malcam’s care, cities laid bare?"
"Days will come," Yahweh’s voice thunders high, "Rabbah’s alarm will sound, flames touch the sky."
"Wail, Heshbon, Ai's ruins tell the tale, Rabbah's daughters in sackcloth, run and wail."
Malcam's downfall, priests and princes caught, Why boast in valleys? Your treasures are naught.
"From all around, terror I’ll bring," says the Lord, Driven out with no refuge, no accord.
"But one day, Ammon's fate will turn," God’s decree, Captivity ends, a future set free.
For Edom, Yahweh questions Teman’s wise, "Has wisdom vanished, counsel in disguise?"
"Dwell deep, Dedan, flee calamity’s reach, Esau’s judgment comes, lessons to teach."
Gleaners leave grapes, thieves take their fill, But Esau’s secrets laid bare, silent and still.
"Your children I’ll preserve," Yahweh does say, "Trust Me, widows, on this fateful day."
"Drink from the cup, punishment’s a must, Bozrah’s desolation, all cities to dust."
A call to nations, "Gather, rise to fight, Edom’s pride deceived by the mountain’s height."
"Edom shall astonish, just like before, No man shall dwell there, rooted to the core."
"Up like a lion from Jordan’s pride, I’ll make them flee, My power won’t hide."
"Who’s like Me?" Yahweh asks with might, "Who can challenge, in day or night?"
Yahweh’s counsel speaks, Teman’s desolate call, Little ones dragged away, earth trembles with their fall.
Eagles fly against Bozrah, mighty hearts will shake, Edom’s warriors feel the pangs they cannot fake.
Damascus hears news, fears melt and flow, City of praise now trembling below.
Men fall silent, war's sound fades away, Yahweh’s fire devours, judgment’s sway.
"Kedar and Hazor, rise up and destroy, Nebuchadnezzar’s plan, without joy."
Tents and flocks taken, terror on all sides, Flee and wander, travelers in the tides.
Hazor becomes a jackal's home, desolate, No man will dwell, sealed by fate.
To Elam, Yahweh’s word came down, "I’ll break your might, scatter you around."
Four winds scatter, outcasts spread wide, Enemies pursue, Elam cannot hide.
"My throne in Elam, kings and princes fall," But hope remains, I’ll restore them all.
Yo, listen up, this is a tale of Babylon’s fall, Jeremiah's words, Yahweh's call.
"Shout it out to the nations, don’t keep it inside, Babylon's been taken, her idols can’t hide.
From the north comes a force, making her land desolate, Man and beast flee, leave her to fate."
"In that time," says Yahweh, "Israel returns, Weeping, seeking, their hearts will yearn.
They’ll come together, a covenant they'll find, Never forgotten, forever aligned.
My people like lost sheep, stray and roam, But now they remember where they belong, their home."
"Flee from Babylon, get out now, ‘Cause nations are coming to bring her down.
Arrows fly like mighty men, Chaldea a prey, won’t rise again."
"You laughed and plundered, danced in the sun, But now your downfall has begun.
Desolate and dry, a wilderness so, Wrath of Yahweh, none will dwell, none will grow."
"Surround her now, archers take aim, Spare no arrows, for she bears shame.
Her walls crumble, vengeance is due, As Babylon did, do to her too."
"Israel, once hunted, now the lions are gone, Assyria's devoured, Babylon’s bones undone.
But Yahweh says: 'I’ll bring you back, To pastures green, no more attack.'"
In those days, no sin found, Remnant forgiven, grace abounds.
"Merathaim, Pekod, destruction’s tune, Battle cries echo, Babylon’s doom."
Hammer of the earth, broken apart, Caught in a snare, unaware from the start.
Yahweh opened his armory, weapons in sight, Against Chaldea, it's a brewing fight.
"Archers gather, surround with might, Babylon’s pride meets darkest night.
Her warriors fall, silence in the street, No one to lift the proud from defeat."
Yahweh of Armies, Israel’s strong, To give them rest, right every wrong.
"Sword on Chaldeans, princes in dread, Boasters turned fools, their strength fled.
Drought on waters, idols can’t save, Desert creatures in a city made grave."
"Like Sodom and Gomorrah, nothing will stand, No man will dwell, barren the land."
From the north, mighty nations rise, No mercy in their hearts, only battle cries.
King of Babylon hears, his strength fades away, Fear grips him, like labor pains sway.
"Enemy like a lion, from Jordan they roam, Stronghold to dust, making it their home.
Hear Yahweh’s counsel, against Babylon’s land, Desolation awaits, by Yahweh’s hand."
At Babylon’s fall, the earth shakes wide, A cry rises up, heard worldwide.
"Look around," Yahweh declares, "Babylon's got a storm ahead, Raising winds, strangers come, leaving her land empty, dead.
Bend your bows, archers, aim, destroy her young and strong, Every street sees the fall, Chaldeans' spirits gone.
Israel's not forgotten, no, nor Judah left all alone, Though they stumble in guilt, Yahweh still calls them His own.
"Escape now, flee fast, save your life from Babylon's sin, Yahweh’s vengeance falls, her payback will begin.
Once a golden cup, now nations drunk and mad, Suddenly she’s fallen, heal her if you can, feel sad.
"We tried to save her, but her wounds are too deep, Judgment rises to the skies, leave her, don’t weep.
"Sharpen arrows, hold your shields, the Medes stand tall, Yahweh's purpose is vengeance, Babylon's great fall.
"Set up a standard, guard the walls tight, Watchmen alert, ambush ready, Babylon’s long night.
Your waters rich, treasures vast, end now you must face, Yahweh swore to fill you with cries, in each desolate place.
"He made the earth with power, heavens stretched wide, Roaring skies, lightning, wind from His side.
"Fools in the land worship images of stone, They hold no breath, their hopes are alone.
"Jacob's portion, Yahweh’s name, breaks nations in hand, Battle axe of justice, laying waste to every land.
"With you I'll shatter kingdoms, chariots too, Older and younger, all will break with you.
"Babylon, your mountains burn, desolate you’ll be, No stone, no foundation, only Yahweh’s decree.
"Sound the trumpet, nations prepare, Ararat, Minni, join Ashkenaz there.
The land shakes, Yahweh's plans hold fast, Mighty men fail, their strength doesn't last.
Fire in her dwellings, runners bear the news, Babylon seized, her warriors confused.
"Zion cries out, Babylon devoured, Nebuchadnezzar's wreckage, hope turned sour.
Vengeance is Yahweh's, drying seas, fountains dry, Jackals dwell in heaps, under Yahweh’s watchful eye.
"Lions roar, then fall to sleep, Their feast made drunk, eternal rest they keep.
Babylon’s waves engulf, her cities dry and bare, Judgment falls on Bel, nations no longer care.
"Go from her midst, my people, flee, Fear not the news, trust in me.
"Her towers high, but destroyers rise, Babylon cries as Yahweh's judgment flies.
Princes, wise men, and mighty fall, Drunken sleep consumes them all.
"Wide walls of Babylon crash, gates burn down, Nations toil for vanity, Yahweh's the only crown.
Jeremiah wrote the woes, to Babylon they’d come, A stone to the book, in the Euphrates it’s done.
"Babylon sinks, never to rise again, Evil brought upon her, weary till the end."
Zedekiah's reign began at twenty-one, but his deeds were wrong, Did evil in Yahweh’s sight, like Jehoiakim's song.
God’s anger flared, Jerusalem faced His decree, Zedekiah rebelled against Babylon, seeking to be free.
Ninth year, tenth month, tenth day, Babylon came to play, Nebuchadnezzar’s army encamped, made Jerusalem their prey.
The city besieged, held tight until year eleven, Famine hit hard, bread less than a raven.
A breach in the walls, men of war took flight, Through the garden gate they slipped, vanishing into night.
The Chaldeans pursued, caught Zedekiah in Jericho's plain, His troops scattered, only fear and pain.
Captured and brought before Babylon’s king, Judgment pronounced, what suffering did bring.
Zedekiah's sons slain before his very eyes, Princes of Judah met their demise.
His eyes put out, bound and led away, To Babylon’s prison, there he’d stay.
Fifth month, tenth day, Nebuzaradan arrived, Jerusalem’s houses burned, none survived.
Yahweh’s house in flames, kings’ houses consumed, Chaldeans broke walls, all hope was doomed.
Captives taken, poorest remained to toil the land, Vineyard keepers and farmers, by Babylon's command.
Bronze pillars, bases, and sea, they took it all, From Yahweh’s house, treasures did fall.
Vessels of gold and silver, every piece they seized, The spoons, bowls, and stands, not a single one appeased.
Pillars tall and strong, pomegranates adorned with care, Eighteen cubits high, bronze capitals rare.
Chief priests and officials, Nebuzaradan took away, To Riblah they were brought, where judgment held sway.
Judah’s people carried off, four thousand six hundred gone, Captivity spread, Jerusalem’s dawn forlorn.
Jehoiachin released, kindness in Babylon’s land, Changed his garments, with honor did stand.
Daily allowance he received, his life restored, Set above kings, by Babylon adored.
All his days he ate, a portion granted till the end, A tale of captivity, but also of a friend.
The city sits alone, once teeming with people wide, Now like a widow, her grandeur, she can't hide. Once a princess, now a slave, she weeps at night, With tears on her cheeks, no lover in sight.
Judah in chains, driven by pain, no place to find rest, Lost among nations, pursued, distressed. Zion's roads mourn, no assembly to see, Desolate gates, priests sighing, bitter she be.
Adversaries rise; enemies take charge, For Yahweh's wrath has come, sins at large. Children captive, majesty gone, like deer they flee, Princes powerless, no pasture to see.
Jerusalem remembers old days of joy, Mocked now by foes, her honor destroyed. Sinned grievously, now unclean and despised, Nakedness revealed, with backward eyes.
"See, Yahweh, my suffering, my vast affliction," The enemy's hand on all, a bitter conviction. Her people sigh, trade treasures for bread, "Look, Yahweh," she cries, "I'm despised and dead."
"To those passing by, see my sorrow's weight, Afflicted by Yahweh's fierce, burning hate. Fire in my bones, a net for my feet, Turned back and faint, no strength to meet."
"The yoke tied tight, my transgressions bound, My strength fails, I'm delivered down. Mighty men crushed, Judah pressed like wine, For these tears, no comfort is mine."
Zion spreads hands, no comfort found, Jacob's foes gather, Jerusalem's unclean ground. "Yahweh is righteous, I've rebelled, see my pain, Virgins and young men, captive again."
"Called for lovers, deceived, left alone, Priests and elders, their spirits have flown. Yahweh, I'm distressed, my heart churns with dread, Sword outside, death at home, my spirit dead."
Enemies hear, they're glad at my plight, But Yahweh, your day will make all right. Bring their wickedness, as you've done to me, Sighs many, heart faint, let justice be.
The Lord's anger's clouding Zion's sky, Beauty of Israel cast down from high.
Dwellings of Jacob swallowed up, no pity, Judah's strongholds thrown down, they're gritty.
Horns of Israel cut off in His rage, Fire consumes Jacob, sets the stage.
Bow bent like a foe, hand as adversary, Zion's tents face wrath, it's scary.
Enemy-like, the Lord swallowed Israel whole, Palaces gone, grief takes its toll.
Like a garden, His tabernacle's torn, Assembly place destroyed, left forlorn.
Altars cast off, His sanctuary despised, Enemies make noise where solemn assembly lies.
Zion's walls doomed by Yahweh's plan, Ramparts weep as He stretches His hand.
Gates sunk low, kings and princes stray, Prophets find no vision, no way.
Elders sit silent, dust on their crown, Virgins hang heads, spirits down.
Eyes weep tears, hearts in trouble deep, Children faint, in the streets they weep.
"Where's the grain and wine?" they cry, Mothers hold them as they die.
What can I say, daughter of Jerusalem? Your breach is vast, who can heal them?
False visions from your prophets' sight, Banishment, no iniquity in light.
Passersby clap in scorn and hiss, "Is this the city's joy and bliss?"
Enemies mock, mouths open wide, "Swallowed her up, with pride."
Yahweh's plan fulfilled, ancient word, Enemies rejoice, His voice heard.
Heart cries out, Zion's wall in tears, Day and night, through all fears.
Arise and cry in night’s quiet, Lift hands for children, soul’s diet.
"Look, Yahweh, see what You've done! Mothers eat children, priests undone."
Youth and old lie slain in streets, Virgins and young men meet defeats.
Days of anger, terrors called in, No escape, consumed by sin.
I've seen affliction, felt the wrath like a rod, Led into darkness where there ain't no God.
Turned his hand against me, day and night, Made my skin old, broke my bones tight.
Surrounded by bitterness, trapped in a wall, Chains so heavy, no way to call.
My prayers blocked, paths turned crooked, A bear lying in wait, my soul shook it.
He pulled me apart, left me desolate, Bent his bow, aimed with deliberate fate.
Arrows hit deep, filled with bitter strife, Became a joke to my people, song of my life.
Fed on wormwood, teeth crushed with gravel, Covered in ashes, my peace unraveled.
"My strength's gone," I cry in despair, "Expectation lost, Yahweh, are you there?"
Still I recall hope, buried in my soul, Yahweh's kindness keeps me whole.
New every morning, faithfulness grand, "My portion," says my soul, "I'll stand."
Yahweh's good to those who wait and seek, Hope and salvation for the humble and meek.
Bear the yoke young, sit in silence and wait, Mouth in the dust, hope for a better fate.
For grief may come, but compassion's near, The Lord's love outweighs the fear.
He doesn't crush or subvert the right, Commands every word, brings dark and light.
So why complain, when sins we bear? Turn to Yahweh, lift hands in prayer.
"We've rebelled," we admit, sins unfold, Yet anger surrounds, our stories told.
Covered with clouds, prayers can't pass, Enemies mock, destruction's amassed.
Tears flow down, won't cease or end, Till Yahweh sees, from heaven descend.
Chased like a bird, thrown in a pit, Waters rise, "I'm cut off," I admit.
Called Yahweh's name from the lowest place, "You heard my cry," and showed your grace.
"Don't be afraid," you said, came near, Redeemed my life, wiped away fear.
Yahweh sees all, the vengeance they plan, He'll judge them rightly, work of their hand.
A heart turned hard, curse at their door, Pursue in anger till they're no more.
Gold's lost its shine, the purest ain't the same, Stones from the sanctuary scattered like a game.
Sons of Zion once like gold, now just clay, Crafted by hands, molded every day.
Even jackals nurse their young with care, But my people turned cold, nothing left to share.
Babies' tongues stick, thirst holds them tight, Kids beg for bread, but there's none in sight.
Once feasted on delicacies, now roam the streets, From royal robes to dunghills, fate repeats.
Zion's sin's heavier than Sodom's fall, No hands touched her, yet wrecked she stood tall.
Nobles once pure, whiter than snow, Now dark as coal, their identity they forgo.
Skin like sticks, to their bones they cling, Hunger's grip a deadly, silent sting.
Sword's death better than starvation's clutch, Fields fruitless, they suffer much.
Mothers in despair, boil their own child, Destruction's feast, horror runs wild.
Yahweh's wrath has burned the ground, Zion's base devoured, no mercy found.
No king believed the enemy'd breach, Jerusalem's gates the foe did reach.
Prophets sinned, priests spilled blood, Blind in streets, in a guilty flood.
“Unclean!” they shout, “Go away, flee!” Exiled, not welcome, homeless to be.
Yahweh's anger scattered them wide, Priests and elders, no respect, denied.
Eyes search in vain for a nation's aid, Hunted steps, dreams fade.
Pursuers faster than eagles in flight, Mountains or wilderness, nowhere's right.
Breath of life, Yahweh's own, ensnared, Thought they'd thrive, but they're impaired.
Edom rejoice now, your turn will come, Drink the cup, reveal what you've done.
Zion's punishment reached its end, No more exile, Edom's sin will rend.
Yahweh, see what's come our way, Strangers walk where we used to stay.
Our homes gone, our lands no more, We’re orphans, mothers feel the widow's score.
Pay for water, wood sold at a cost, Pursued by foes, all hope seems lost.
Sent to Egypt and Assyria's land, Just to fill our mouths, we gave our hand.
Fathers sinned, they're gone, we're left, Bearing burdens, feeling bereft.
Servants rule, we're trapped, you see, No one's here to set us free.
Bread comes with life on the line, Sword in the wild, danger all the time.
Our skin's dark from famine's heat, Zion's women face defeat.
Judah's virgins met with shame, Princes hanged, no honor to claim.
Young men grind, children strain, Elders' wisdom, now in vain.
Joy's gone, dances turned to tears, Our crown has fallen through these years.
Hearts are faint, eyes grow dim, Zion desolate, foxes on a whim.
Yahweh, forever you remain, On an eternal throne, you reign.
"Why forget us, leave us long? Turn us back where we belong."
Bring us back, renew our days, Yet your anger still delays.
In the thirtieth year, fourth month, fifth day, By the river Chebar, visions came my way.
In Jehoiachin’s fifth year of captivity's test, Yahweh's word came; His presence impressed.
A stormy wind from the north, clouds flashed bright, Glowing metal from fire, a powerful sight.
From its center emerged four living things, Human form, with faces and wings.
Four faces each, four wings they displayed, Feet straight and strong, like bronze, finely made.
Hands beneath wings, each face held a plan, Lion, ox, eagle, and the face of a man.
Wings outstretched, two touched, two concealed, They moved straight ahead, their path revealed.
Like burning coals, torches blazing in line, Lightning flashed, creatures moved with a sign.
Beside each face, a wheel on the ground, Wheels within wheels, beryl-like, profound.
High rims, dreadful, eyes all around, With the spirit, they moved, no turning found.
Above their heads, an expanse crystal clear, Wings straightened, like waters they cheer.
A voice above, wings lowered in might, A sapphire throne, a man bathed in light.
Glowing metal, fire's glow bright and wide, Rainbow-like glory encircles his side.
In Yahweh’s presence, I fell to the floor, He spoke, His voice, a thunderous roar.
"Son of man," He said, "stand up, feet firm and true, I'll speak with you now, this message is due."
The Spirit swept in as His voice filled the air, Lifted me upright, His words clear and rare.
"Son of man," He continued, "to Israel you go, To a nation of rebels, they need to know."
"From fathers to sons, they've turned away, Yet today I send you to show them My way."
"Stubborn and hard, these children of mine, Say, 'This is Yahweh's word, straight and divine.'"
"Listen or not, let them choose their stance, But they'll know a prophet took this chance."
"Don't fear their words, nor thorns that sting, Even scorpions can't break the message I bring."
"Speak My words, whether they hear or deny, For they are rebellious, but you must try."
"But you, son of man, heed My decree, Don't be like them, stay true to Me."
"Open your mouth, eat what I give, In this truth, you'll surely live."
A hand reached out, a scroll unrolled, Inside and out, lamentations were told.
"Son of man, take a bite, eat this scroll, Speak to Israel, let my words unfold." Mouth wide open, the scroll tastes sweet, Honey-like flavor, prophecy complete.
He said, "Go to Israel, speak my word, Not to strangers' tongues, but to those who've heard. They won't listen, their hearts are stone, But I've made your face like a hardened bone."
"Diamond forehead, harder than flint, stand strong, Fear not their stares, don't be led wrong. Receive my words, let them fill your heart, Go to your people, play your part."
The Spirit lifted, and I heard a rush, "Bless Yahweh's glory," in a mighty hush. Wings and wheels, the sound so profound, Lifted me up, took me from the ground.
In bitterness, with spirit’s heat inside, Yahweh's hand on me, my guide. To the captives by Chebar, I came, Sat overwhelmed, seven days the same.
After days passed, Yahweh spoke again, "Watchman of Israel, hear my command then. Warn the wicked, 'You will surely die,' If you don't, their blood's on you, oh my."
"Warn the righteous, keep them from sin, If they listen, their life they'll win. Your soul's delivered, your duty fulfilled, Even if warning them gets you killed."
Yahweh's hand spoke, "Meet me on the plain, I'll talk to you there, explain my aim." I rose, I went, His glory stood, Like by Chebar, there I understood.
The Spirit entered, set me on my feet, He spoke with me, words concrete. "Shut in your house, they'll tie you down, Mute your words, but don't you frown."
"When I speak, your mouth I'll free, Say, 'This is Yahweh's decree.' If they hear or refuse, let it be known, To a rebellious house, truth is thrown."
"Son of man, grab a tile, make it real, Draw the city, Jerusalem, make it feel. Lay siege, build forts, raise up a mound, Camps and rams, surround it all around.
Take an iron pan, set it like a wall, Face the city, this siege will stand tall. Lie on your side, for Israel bear the weight, Three hundred ninety days, their sins on your plate.
"When that’s done, switch sides, Judah's turn to bear, Forty days for forty years, their story laid bare. Face the siege, arm out, prophesy strong, With ropes I’ll hold you till the days are long.
"Gather wheat, barley, beans, lentils all in one, Make bread, day by day, till the time is done. Eat by weight, twenty shekels per day, Drink by measure, water rationed all the way.
Make barley cakes, bake them on what man expels, Yahweh declared, 'Unclean bread among the nations dwells.' I cried, 'Lord Yahweh, I’ve kept myself clean, No filthy meat has ever come between!'
Yahweh said, 'Use cow dung instead of man’s, Prepare your bread, as My judgment stands. In Jerusalem, bread will break, fear will rise, Water scarce, they’ll mourn in their own disguise.
In their iniquity, lacking bread and water, Dismay will rule, as they falter and totter.'"

"Son of man, grab a sword, sharp as a blade, Use it like a razor, your head and beard invade. Weigh and divide that hair, piece by piece, A third you'll burn in the city's heart, the fire won't cease.

Another third, strike it with your sword in full force, The last third, scatter it to the wind's course. Bind a few strands in your robe, tight and neat, Then toss them in the fire, let the flames complete.
The Lord Yahweh declares, 'This is Jerusalem's fate, Placed among nations, but rebels at a higher rate. Ignored my laws, more than those nations near, Rejected my statutes, refused to adhere.'
'So I'm against you,' Yahweh firmly says, 'Judgments will rain down, in astonishing ways. What I will do, never done before, Because of your sins, abominations I abhor.
Fathers and sons will eat one another, Judgments scattered, no refuge to recover. Your detestable acts have defiled my place, My eye won't spare; I'll diminish your space.
A third of you will perish by pestilence's claw, Another third by the sword, no mercy, no law. The last third will scatter with the wind as it goes, With a sword chasing after, until my wrath slows.
My anger will rest, my wrath will cease, Then you'll know Yahweh's words bring no peace. I'll make you a desolation, a tale for the lands, A reproach and taunt, seen by all who pass, stands.
My judgments are fierce, like arrows they fly, Famine's the tool to make your strength die. Evil beasts, pestilence, blood through your street, The sword will descend, my words are complete.'"
Yahweh spoke, gave me a task to do, "Son of man, face Israel's mountains, it's true.
Prophesy to them, let my words unfold, To mountains and valleys, my story is told.
'Behold! See the sword that I bring, Your high places fall, your idols will sting.
Altars desolate, incense altars broken, Your slain before idols, that's my token.
Bones scattered round your sacred space, Cities laid waste, a desolate place.
Slain will fall, know my name, Yahweh I am, never in vain.
Yet a remnant left, some escape the sword, Scattered nations, they'll recall my word.
Broken by hearts that strayed, Eyes chasing idols, my love betrayed.
They'll loathe their ways, see the wrongs they've done, They'll know I am Yahweh, the only one.
Lord Yahweh says, 'Clap and stomp, cry "Alas!" Evil abominations, Israel's past.
Fall by sword, famine, pestilence's breath, Accomplishing wrath, amid their death.
Know I'm Yahweh, when slain are laid, Under trees, on hills, where idols are made.
Stretch my hand, desolation's spread, From wilderness to Diblah, where hope is dead.
Then, at last, they'll know my name, Yahweh I am, forever the same.'"
Yahweh spoke, and I heard Him declare, "Son of man, tell Israel, I'm everywhere.
An end has come, on every corner it lands, My anger's unleashed, in judgment it stands.
Your ways come back, your sins on display, No mercy from me, you'll know me this day.
'Evil's unique, behold, it arrives, Your doom is here, it catches your lives.
The time is now, no joy on the hills, My wrath is coming, to judge all your ills.
No pity from me, your ways bring your fall, You'll know it's Yahweh, above it all.
See the day approach, doom's rod has grown, Violence blooms, no wealth to be shown.
Time's here, the day draws near, Buyers and sellers, in fear and tears.
The trumpet sounds, ready or not, My wrath is on you, like a blistering shot.
Sword outside, famine within, Field or city, it's where you’ll begin.
The mountain's refuge, like moaning doves, Hands weak, knees tremble, forsaking loves.
Sackcloth and horror, heads bald, shame, Silver in streets, gold is a stain.
These won't save you, when my wrath descends, Your idol's wealth, iniquity bends.
Foreigners plunder, your treasures defiled, Turn from you, my face exiled.
Chains made ready, the land's full of crime, Nations invade, in your pride's decline.
Destruction comes, peace can't be found, Rumors rise, mischief compounds.
Prophet's vision lost, priest's law is gone, King and prince in mourning, forlorn.
I'll judge by your ways, your own choices revealed, Then you'll know Yahweh, as the truth is unsealed."
In the sixth year, sixth month, fifth day, in the house I sat, Judah's elders with me, then God's hand fell flat.
Behold, fire's likeness, waist down was a blaze, Upward a brightness, like metal ablaze.
A hand reached out, grabbed a lock of my hair, The Spirit lifted me, earth and sky in the air.
Visions took me to Jerusalem's gate, Image of jealousy, provoking God's fate.
God's glory shone, Israel's God in sight, "Son of man," He said, "look north, take flight."
I lifted my eyes, saw the jealousy stand, "Do you see, Son of man, the abominations at hand?
Israel's sins make Me leave My own place, But more abominations you'll soon face."
He led me to the court, a hole in the wall, "Dig through, Son of man, uncover it all."
I dug and found a door, beyond it lay, Wicked abominations, night to day.
Creeping things and idols lined the walls, Seventy elders with censers in the halls.
The incense rose, cloud of a sinful shroud, "In the dark, they say, 'Yahweh's not around.'"
"More abominations yet you will see," To the north gate, where women cried in plea.
"Weeping for Tammuz, have you seen this, my son? Greater abominations are still not done."
Inner court, twenty-five men stood, Back to the temple, sun worship they would.
"Is it light to Judah, these sins they repeat, Filled with violence, their actions indiscreet?
They provoke Me to wrath, the branch to their nose, I will not spare them, My voice won’t close.
Though they cry loud, My ears will not hear, For the acts they've committed, My judgment is near."
A voice shouted loud, echoing near, "Bring the city's leaders, armed, appear!"
Six men came from the gate up north, Each with a weapon, ready to go forth.
In their midst, a man in linen stood, With an inkhorn, in solemn mood.
By the bronze altar, they took their stand, As God's glory moved across the land.
He called to the man with the inkhorn near, Yahweh's voice was strong and clear:
"Go through the city, mark each one, Who cries for the wrongs that have been done."
To the others, the command was stark, "Follow him, strike, but spare the marked."
"Old and young, woman and child, Let none escape, be fierce, be wild."
"Start at my sanctuary, let justice unfold," And so the old men met their fate, bold.
"Defile the house, fill the courts with slain, Go out, let none remain."
While they struck, I fell to the ground, Crying out as chaos abound.
"Ah Lord Yahweh! Will all be lost? In your wrath, what will it cost?"
"The land is full of blood and lies," Came the reply from the skies.
"My eye won't spare, pity won't be seen, Their own ways will come, they'll glean."
The man in linen returned, his task complete, "I've done your bidding, made all meet."
In the sky, above the cherubim high, A throne like sapphire caught the eye.
He spoke to the man, linen-clad and bold, "Go between the wheels, take the coals, be cold.
Scatter them over the city," He said, He moved as I watched, no fear, no dread.
Cherubim stood on the house's right side, The cloud filled the court, nowhere to hide.
Yahweh's glory rose, lighting the scene, Court filled with brightness, pure and clean.
Wings of cherubim roared loud and clear, Like God Almighty's voice, all could hear.
He commanded the man to take fire from the wheels, He stood by a wheel; cherubim hand seals the deals.
The cherub reached out, took fire with care, Hand to linen man, who carried the flare.
Four wheels appeared, next to each face, Wheels like beryl, moved with grace.
Wheels within wheels, no turning in place, Followed where the head looked, steady pace.
Bodies and wings, eyes all around, Even the wheels, eyes did surround.
Called "whirling wheels," they were heard, Faces of cherub, man, lion, and bird.
Cherubim rose, creatures alive, Seen by the river, Chebar's drive.
Wheels beside as cherubim soared, Lifted wings, spirit adored.
Yahweh's glory left the threshold, Stood over them, story retold.
Cherubim lifted, wings spread wide, At the east gate, God's glory their guide.
These were the creatures I'd seen before, Under Israel's God, by the river shore.
Each had four faces, four wings to fly, Hands beneath wings, reaching the sky.
Faces familiar from the river's face, They moved straight ahead, keeping pace.
The Spirit lifted me up, brought me east to the gate, Twenty-five men stand there, princes with their fate.
"Son of man," He said, "these men plot iniquity, Their counsel's wicked, poisoned the city."
"They say, 'No need for homes, we're safe in this heat, This is the cauldron, we are the meat.'"
"Prophesy, son of man, against their deceit." Yahweh's Spirit on me, His words I repeat:
"You've filled the streets with the slain, no one alive, This cauldron's no safe haven, you won't survive."
"You feared the sword, and the sword you shall meet, Judgment awaits, strangers will sweep you off your feet."
"This is not your cauldron, you're not the feast, You'll know I'm Yahweh when your rebellion's ceased."
Pelatiah fell dead, I cried out in dismay, "Will Israel's remnant vanish, Lord, I pray?"
Yahweh spoke again: "Your brothers are cast aside, Jerusalem's claim, 'This land's our pride.'"
"But tell them: 'Though scattered wide, I'll be your place, A sanctuary afar, for a time, in grace.'"
"I'll gather you back, from lands far and near, Return you to Israel, cleanse what's dear."
"A new heart I'll give, flesh where stone once lay, Walk my statutes, be my people, come what may."
"Yet those clinging to abominations and vile ways, Their deeds will judge them, end of days."
The cherubim rose, wings and wheels in sync, The glory of Yahweh, on the city's brink.
The Spirit took me back, across the land wide, To captives in Chaldea, with vision as my guide.
I spoke to them all, what Yahweh had shown, His message of judgment and mercy, they'd own.
In the midst of rebels, the message was clear, "Son of man, listen, and lend me your ear. Eyes they have, yet sight’s out of reach, Ears they own, but they don’t heed my speech.
Pack up your stuff, let them see you leave, In broad daylight, let them watch and perceive. It's a sign to a house that never complies, Carry it out and let them realize.
Dig through the wall, let the rubble fall, In their view, carry it out, take it all. Cover your face, don’t see the land, For you're a sign, as I’ve planned.
I did what He said, moved in the day, Dug through the wall, took my things away. Darkness my cloak, on my shoulder's weight, In their sight, all of this I create.
Morning came, Yahweh spoke anew, "Rebellious Israel questions, ‘What do you do?’ Say to them, ‘This is a burden true, The prince, the people, it concerns you.’
‘Like me, they’ll leave, exiled and gone, Through the wall and into the dawn. The prince will carry, face covered tight, He won’t see the land, but he'll face the night.
I’ll spread my net, caught in my snare, To Babylon bound, yet not seeing there. Scattered in winds, their bands will go, Chased by the sword, they’ll surely know.
Then they’ll know I am Yahweh indeed, Few will escape, from sword, famine freed. They’ll declare their ways in foreign zones, And know I’m Yahweh, on my throne."
"Son of man, eat with trembling hands, Drink your water, fear in the lands. Tell them their bread will be eaten in fear, For violence and waste are drawing near.
Cities once full, desolate and bare, Then they’ll know I’m Yahweh, everywhere."
Yahweh said, "What’s this saying they’ve got, ‘Days prolonged, visions all for naught’? Tell them ‘Yahweh says it’ll cease, Prophecies won’t delay, none for lease.
Visions will come, false words won’t last, In your days, rebellious, the word’s cast. I’ll speak it, perform it, no more wait, What I declare will find its fate.’
Again Yahweh spoke, "They say, ‘It’s far, Visions for days away, like a distant star.’ Tell them, ‘No more delays, it’s time to act, My words fulfilled, that is a fact.’"
Yahweh spoke, a message to share, "Son of man, hear and beware.
Tell those prophets, who claim in vain, They speak from the heart, but it’s all a game.
'Woe to these fools,' Yahweh declares, They’ve seen nothing, but act like they care.
Israel's prophets, like foxes they play, Not building walls, just leading astray.
Claiming visions, false words they say, But Yahweh ain’t sent them anyway.
'You’ve seen false sights,' Yahweh calls it out, 'Spoken lies, sowing doubt.'
'So hear this now,' Yahweh’s decree, 'Because you lie, I’m coming for thee.'
'My hand’s against those who pretend, Not in my council, without a friend.
You won’t enter Israel's land, Then you’ll know it’s Yahweh’s hand.'
'You promise peace where none will dwell, Whitewash walls, they’ll all fell.'
'Rain will pour, hail will fall, Where’s your plaster, when down goes the wall?'
'With storm and wrath, I’ll tear it apart, Expose foundations, revealing the heart.'
'The wall’s no more, nor those who built, False prophets, with peace, stained with guilt.'
Turn to the women, prophesy bold, Speaking lies, for barley and gold.
'Woe to those with pillows, kerchiefs made, Hunting souls, in deception’s trade.'
Yahweh's against your deceitful ways, Ripping away your soul-catching plays.
'Freeing those that you ensnared, My people will know that I’ve cared.'
'No more lies, no more false sights, I’ll save my people, set things right.'
Yahweh's words, through truth they flow, Now you’ll know, He rules the show."
Elders of Israel sat down, solemn and still, Yahweh's word came, His message to fulfill. "Son of man, these folks got idols deep inside, Should I let them ask, let them confide?"
"Tell 'em, every man who clings to stone and wood, Who seeks the prophet, misunderstood. In their hearts, they've wandered, strayed so far, Estranged from me, like a distant star."
"Return, O Israel, from idols turn away, Face me again, don't go astray. Anyone who separates, seeks his own path, I'll answer him with a fierce wrath."
"I'll set my face against him, a tale to tell, A sign among the people, where he fell. Prophets deceived, their words will betray, For I, Yahweh, will lead them astray."
"Iniquity they bear, iniquity shared, That they stray no more, be my people prepared. When a land sins, and my hand I stretch wide, Famine, drought, no place to hide."
"Noah, Daniel, Job, righteous trio, Save only themselves, no sons to show. Wild beasts ravage, desolation reigns, Yet they alone escape the chains."
"If I call the sword, the blade must fall, Men, beasts, all, heed the call. Pestilence strikes, wrath pours out, Only the righteous find the drought."
"Four judgments on Jerusalem, I will send, Sword, famine, beasts, pestilence without end. But a remnant will remain, sons, daughters too, They'll come to you, you'll see what they do."
"They'll comfort you with their ways, Proving I didn't act without cause, in all my days."
Yahweh spoke to me right there, "Son of man, see that vine, thin as air.
What's it more than a tree so grand? Can you make a tool with that in your hand?
Toss it in the fire, watch it burn, Ends devoured, the middle can't return.
When it was whole, it had no use, Now it's burned, what's left to produce?"
So the Lord Yahweh makes it clear, Like that vine, Jerusalem's near.
"I'll turn my face, set against their land, They'll escape the fire, but can't withstand.
Then you'll know I'm Yahweh's might, When my face turns, dark as night.
I'll leave the land barren, empty and sore, Because their trespass, it can't be ignored," Yahweh swore.
Yo, listen up, Yahweh's word's in play, "Son of man, to Jerusalem, let's convey.
Your roots in Canaan, your birth in the land, Amorite dad, Hittite mom, understand.
You were born, no cord was snipped, No water washed you, no blankets gripped.
No eye showed you a hint of love, Cast in the field, no cover above.
I passed by, saw you in blood, Said, 'Live in that crimson flood.'
I made you grow, beauty displayed, But you were bare, no clothes arrayed.
Time for love, I spread my cloak, Covenant made, our bond bespoke.
I washed you clean, anointed with oil, Embroidery and silk, I dressed you in royal.
Jewels and gold adorned your form, You were stunning, took the world by storm.
But you trusted beauty, played the fool, Prostituted fame, broke every rule.
Made shrines with garments, colors bright, Worshipped objects, lost in sight.
Gave bread and oil to idols, oh why? Sacrificed sons and daughters, made Yahweh cry.
Forgot your youth, naked and bare, Wallowing in blood, without a care.
"Woe to you!"—Yahweh's refrain, Built lofty places, but brought only pain.
Egyptians, Assyrians, you entertained, With merchants, ever unsatisfied, remained.
Weak heart, impudent in your way, Not even scorned pay, for shame shall stay.
A wife unfaithful, adultery rife, Giving gifts to lovers, courting strife.
"Therefore, hear Yahweh's decree," Your filthiness exposed for all to see.
Lovers gathered, nakedness shown, Judgment like women with broken vows known.
Stripped and stoned, wrath and fire, No more prostitution, your ways retire.
In your shame, remember the past, When Yahweh's love was meant to last.
Yet, Yahweh's covenant never fades, Promised to restore, though choices made.
Remember your shame, sisters to embrace, Yahweh's forgiveness, his eternal grace.
When all sins are forgiven, and shame's undone, And you know Yahweh, the lasting One."
Yahweh spoke to me, said "Tell a riddle, son, A parable for Israel, let the story run. A great eagle soared, wings long and wide, Colorful feathers, to Lebanon it did glide.
Took the cedar's top, the highest twig, you know, Carried it to merchants, where traffic flows. Planted in the city, in the soil of trade, A new tree grew where the eagle laid.
Seed from the land, in fertile land it flowed, By waters placed, a willow it showed. Grew to be a vine, low and wide, Branches leaned back, roots by its side.
Then came another eagle, wings spread wide, The vine reached for it, roots did hide. Planted in good soil, by waters, it aimed, Hoped to grow branches, fruit it claimed.
Yahweh says, "Will it truly thrive? Won't he pull roots, make it wither, not survive? Strong arms and many can't make it grow, East wind hits, then its fate we know."
Yahweh asked me, "Do you understand? Babylon's king took Jerusalem's land. Took the king, the princes, to his place, Made a covenant with them, to keep them in grace.
Yet rebellion came, ambassadors sent, Horses sought, covenant was bent. Will he escape, this oath despised? In Babylon's heart, it's there he'll reside."
Pharaoh's might can't save him from war, Forts will rise, cut off many more. Despised the oath, broke the deal, In my snare, judgment he'll feel.
Fugitives fall, scattered by the wind, Yahweh's word is what I've pinned. "I'll take a cedar's top, plant it high, On Israel's peak, it will reach the sky.
Branches will grow, fruit will bear, Birds find shade, in its care. High brought low, low exalted, Green dried up, dry tree vaulted.
I, Yahweh, have spoken, see what's done, In the field, my will is the only one."
Got a word from Yahweh, listen close, "What's this proverb y'all boast?
Fathers eat sour grapes, kids' teeth get sore, Not in my land, not anymore.
Every soul is mine, father and son, The one who sins? That's the one who's done.
If a man stays right, lawful in sight, Doesn't feast on mountains, avoids idols' light.
No neighbor's wife did he defile, No robbery, just offers a smile.
Feeds the hungry, clothes those in need, No interest taken, from iniquity freed.
Walks in my ways, keeps my decree, That man will live, surely, you'll see.
But if his son turns ruthless and cold, Sheds blood, robs, and breaks the mold,
Eats at shrines, defiles, lifts his eyes, To idols of stone, he lives in lies.
This son shall perish, blood on his head, Abominations done, he's surely dead.
Now if this wicked man has a son, Sees the father's sins and decides to run,
Avoids the shrines, keeps the law tight, Doesn't follow darkness, walks in the light,
Feeds the hungry, avoids the loan's snare, He won't die for dad's sins, life's fair.
Father may die in his own cruel way, But the son's got life, he's here to stay.
"Why doesn't the son bear the father's sin?" When he's living right, why drag him in?
Sins are personal, soul by soul, Righteous or wicked, each one whole.
But if the wicked man turns and repents, Follows my statutes, to righteousness he consents.
His past's forgotten, nothing to fear, In his new path, he'll find life here.
