"Do I want the wicked dead?" Yahweh asks, "Turn and live, that's the task."
But if the righteous switches to wrong, And starts singing the wicked song,
His past good deeds won't count, he’ll fall, In his iniquity, he'll lose it all.
"Unfair!" you say, "Your ways aren't straight!" Israel, check your paths, yours hold the weight.
A righteous man turns evil, he dies in sin, A wicked man turns good, his life's a win.
House of Israel, hear my call, I'll judge you, every one of y'all.
Turn from sin, make a new start, Get a new spirit, a fresh heart.
I find no joy in death's cold sting, Turn back to me, and live, my offspring."
Yo, listen up, here's a tale to be told, About a lioness bold, with cubs in her hold.
She raised her young strong, among lions she sat, One grew to hunt, a lion in combat.
He roared in the land, devouring men, Till nations caught wind and trapped him in the fen.
Into Egypt he went, in chains and in pain, A prisoner bound, no longer to reign.
But mama lioness wasn't done, she tried once more, Another cub grew fierce, prowling the forest floor.
He roamed with might, cities quaked at his roar, Till the nations attacked, they couldn't ignore.
They caught him in nets, dragged to Babylon's den, Locked in a cage, never to roar again.
"Your mother, a vine, by the waters she lay, Branches reaching high, in the light of the day."
Strong were her branches, rulers' scepters they bore, But fury plucked her up, cast down to the floor.
The east wind blew, and her fruits did dry, Her strong arms broke, under a fiery sky.
Now she's planted in a wilderness, barren and dry, No more scepters, her time passed by.
This lament, hear it loud, hear it clear, A song of loss, of hope turned to fear.
The seventh year, fifth month, day ten, Elders of Israel sat before me again.
Yahweh's word came, a message to send, "Son of man, hear, to the elders, extend:
'Is it Me you inquire, is it Me you seek? As I live,' says Yahweh, 'I won't speak.'
Judge them, son of man, let them understand, The wrongs of their fathers, in this very land.
When I chose Israel, made them my own, In Egypt I swore, they'd not be alone.
'I am Yahweh your God,' I declared, A land rich and glorious, for them I prepared.
'Throw away idols, don't defile your soul, For I am Yahweh,' I made my goal.
But rebellion stirred, they turned away, Idols of Egypt, they chose to display.
I threatened my wrath, to let anger flow, But for my name's sake, I let mercy show.
Out of Egypt, into wilderness wide, My laws I gave, to be their guide.
Sabbaths as signs, between them and me, Yet in the wild, they'd not let it be.
My statutes they scorned, my Sabbaths defiled, Declared my wrath, but again I smiled.
For my own name, among nations, no shame, In their presence, I spared my flame.
To their children I spoke, 'Don't walk their path, Forsake the idols, heed not their wrath.
I am Yahweh, follow my ways, Keep my Sabbaths, through all your days.'
Yet the children rebelled, just like before, Statutes abandoned, idols adored.
I held back my wrath for my name's sake, But swore they'd scatter, their bond to break.
In lands unknown, they'd wander afar, For idols' sake, they'd gone too far.
Son of man, declare to Israel's house, Their fathers' blasphemy, loud as a louse.
In their promised land, high hills they sought, Sacrifices offered, their defilement taught.
"Do you follow their path?" Yahweh asks, "Will idols defile, in deceptive masks?"
"Think not of nations, with wood and stone, I'll reign as king, make my power known.
I'll gather you out, from lands abroad, Face to face, you'll meet your God.
Judgment awaits, as I once swore, Rebels purged, in covenant's core.
House of Israel, go serve your lies, But my name, no more will you despise.
In holy mountains, you'll serve me true, Gifts and offerings, from me to you.
I’ll gather you close, a fragrant delight, In sight of nations, my name in light.
You'll remember your ways, deeds once done, Loathe your evils, under the sun.
Know I am Yahweh, not for your sake, For my own name, my mercy I make."
Yahweh commanded, "Face south, son of man, Prophesy the fire, devour the land.
Green tree, dry tree, all will burn, A flame unquenched, the world will learn.
Everyone will see, Yahweh's hand is true, The fire kindled, forever in view."
I cried, "Ah Lord! They mock my plight, 'He's just a speaker of riddles,' they spite."
Yahweh's word came to me, loud and clear, "Son of man, face Jerusalem, bring it near.
Preach to the sanctuaries, speak to the land, 'Yahweh says, "Against you I stand.
I'll draw my sword from its sheath, no delay, Cutting both righteous and wicked away.
From south to north, my sword will glide, All flesh will know Yahweh's on this ride.
It won’t return, it’s out for good." So sigh, son of man, as you should.
When they ask, 'Why the sigh, why the groan?' Say, 'The news is coming, it’s known.
Every heart will melt, hands will shake, Spirits will faint, knees will quake.
Behold, it comes, it shall be done, Says Yahweh, the only one.'"
Yahweh spoke again, "Prophesy, say aloud, 'A sword! A sword! Sharp and proud.
Polished to flash like lightning bright, Sharpened to slaughter, create fright.
Should we laugh? The rod condemns, Polished for the killer's hands, it sends.
Cry, wail, son of man, for the sword’s on its way, Princes of Israel, it will slay.
Delivered to the sword, my people’s fate, So beat your thigh, for it’s too late.
A trial comes, the rod may fail, But strike your hands, let the tale prevail.
Double the sword, strike three times, The fatally wounded, in their primes.
Threatening all gates, hearts will melt, Lightning sharp, its purpose felt.
Gather, go right, then go left, I’ll strike my hands, leave them bereft."
Yahweh’s word again did speak, "Son of man, two paths to seek.
The sword of Babylon king to come, Mark the place, where roads are from.
One way to Ammon, one to Judah’s door, The king sees signs, arrows soar.
In one hand, the lot for Jerusalem's fate, Battering rams, the city gate.
Though they think it false, oaths are sworn, Iniquity remembered, all forlorn.
Yahweh says, 'Your sins are found, You'll be taken, bound to ground.
Wounded prince, your time is near, Remove the crown, the end is clear.
I’ll overturn, again and again, Till he comes, rightful to reign.'"
"Now for Ammon’s children, hear this call, 'A sword is drawn, sharp for all.
Though lies are seen, false visions dance, The wicked fall, they lose their chance.
Return it to sheath, judge in their place, Indignation burns, no escape.
Brutish men will take you down, Fuel for fire, in the ground.
Your blood there, you won’t remain, For I, Yahweh, have spoken plain.'"
Yahweh spoke, said it clear, "Son of man, hear my plea, Judge this bloody city, expose her infamy. A town shedding blood, idols crafted in hate, Guilty of her actions, her own end she'll create."
"Shamed by the nations, mocked far and near, Infamous city, full of chaos and fear. Princes shed blood, power corrupt and wild, Parents disrespected, orphans and widows reviled."
"You've scorned my holy things, my Sabbaths profaned, Slander and lewdness in mountains, unrestrained. Abominations abound, neighbor's wife defiled, Daughter-in-law shamed, sister made reviled."
"Bribes for blood, interest taken with greed, Oppressed your neighbors, forgot my creed. I've struck my hand at your dishonest gain, Can you endure the judgment, face the pain?"
"Scattered you'll be, across nations wide, Profaned and filthy, no place to hide. Then you'll know, Yahweh's name you'll see, For I've spoken, it's my decree."
"Israel's become dross, like metals in flame, Bronze, tin, iron, in the furnace of shame. Gathered in wrath, melted by fire, You'll feel my anger, my burning desire."
"Prophets conspire, like lions roar, Devouring souls, treasures they store. Priests violate law, desecrate the sacred line, Make no distinction, between holy and unclean sign."
"Princes like wolves, prey they pursue, Shedding blood, dishonest gain their view. Prophets false visions, whitewashed lies they tell, Claiming Yahweh's word, when silence fell."
"Opression runs rampant, robbery is rife, Poor and needy suffer, foreigner faces strife. Sought a man to stand, the gap to bridge, Found none among them, so wrath is my pledge."
"My indignation poured, the fire's fierce track, Their ways on their heads, no turning back."
Two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, named, Played games in Egypt, where their youth was tamed. They were mine, yet they strayed, chasing desire, Lusting for Assyrians, setting hearts on fire.
Oholah, the elder, chased her Assyrian dreams, Men in blue, on horses, a sight that gleams. She gave herself away, defiled by their hands, Never left her past in those foreign lands.
"Thus I gave her to her lovers, those she adored, They stripped her bare, left her with a sword. Her children taken, her life laid to waste, Her story a warning, in haste, they faced."
Yet Oholibah saw, and deeper she fell, After Assyrian lords, she lusted as well. Images on walls, Chaldeans with pride, She sent word, and they came to her side.
In the bed of love, polluted she became, Her soul turned cold, her heart aflame. She uncovered herself, her past she'd revive, Her youthful passions, in Egypt she'd strive.
God said, "Oholibah, your lovers will rise, From Babylon, Assyria, see their eyes. They'll come with weapons, fury in their hand, Judgment passed by their command."
"Jealousy and rage, they'll strip you bare, Your children lost, your jewels rare. Your lewdness will cease, no more Egypt's fame, Forget your past, no more of that game."
Oholibah, you'll drink from your sister's cup, A deep, bitter draught, won't let up. "Desolation and sorrow, you'll tear your own breast, For you've forgotten me, failed my test."
God spoke, "Shall you judge these sisters, man? Adultery and blood, in their own hands ran. Defiled my house, on my Sabbath they tread, Children passed through fire, to idols misled."
"They called for men, from afar they came, Painted eyes, adorned, seeking fame. Drunkards and fools, they entertained in bed, Even on sacred ground, they boldly tread."

"Righteous men will judge, adulteresses condemned, For blood on their hands, to destruction they're penned. A mob will rise, stones and swords will fall, Homes burned to ashes, they'll face their call."
"In this, lewdness will cease, a lesson taught, Women will learn, to sin they ought not. You'll bear your idols' sins, all will see, Then you'll know, I am Yahweh, let it be."
In the ninth year, tenth month, tenth day, Yahweh spoke, here's what He had to say:
"Son of man, write this day, make it known, The king of Babylon's near, Jerusalem's own.
Tell the rebels a story—parables unfold, ‘The Lord Yahweh says, put the cauldron on bold.
Fill it with water, gather choice meat, Thighs, shoulders, bones, make it a feast.
Boil it well, let the fire ignite, Watch the city rust in the heat of the night.
Woe to the city, bloody through and through, Rust in the cauldron, here's what you do:
Piece by piece, take it apart, No dice, no luck, just a broken heart.
Blood on the rock, left uncovered, Vengeance comes, justice discovered.
Heap the wood, make the fire great, Boil the broth; let the bones incinerate.
Empty the cauldron, let the bronze blaze, Filth melts away, consumed in the blaze.
For your filth's deep, lewdness has reigned, Cleansed you before, but no cleansing remained.
My wrath will rest, I won't spare, "I, Yahweh, have spoken," declares the air.
Then Yahweh spoke again, a word so cold, "Son of man, I'll take your heart's hold.
The desire of your eyes, with a single stroke, No mourning, no tears, no weeping cloak.
Sigh in silence, no cries aloud, Wear your headdress, sandals unbowed.
No mourner's bread, keep your lips bare, Mourn not for the dead, let them stare."
I did as commanded, the morning came, That evening, my wife gone, the same.
People asked, "Tell us, what does this show?" I said, "Yahweh's word, you need to know.
He'll profane His sanctuary, pride of your place, Sons, daughters fall by the sword's cruel embrace.
Do as I've done, no mourning, no cries, Turban on head, sandals in ties.
Ezekiel's your sign, a witness to see, When this happens, Yahweh's majesty.
Son of man, when strength they lose, Joy of glory, hearts confused,
Those who escape will hear the word, Your mouth will open, speak undeterred.
You'll be their sign, truth to show, Then they'll know Yahweh in the flow."
Yahweh spoke, a vision, a plan, "Son of man, face Ammon, prophesy, understand. Tell them, hear Yahweh's decree, 'Cause you mocked my sanctuary, you'll see.
When Israel fell, when Judah was chained, You laughed, you cheered, but now you'll be pained. I'll hand you to the east as their prize, They'll camp in your lands, make your home their skies.
Rabbah, a stable, camels will roam, Ammon, a pasture, not your own home. Then you'll know, I am Yahweh, no doubt, For your mocking, you'll be cast out.
You clapped, you stomped, with contempt in your soul, Rejoiced at Israel's fall, but now pay the toll. Stretched my hand, you'll be plundered and gone, Cut from the nations, perish, withdrawn.
Moab and Seir, you said, "Like the rest," Mocked Judah's fall, now face Yahweh's test. I'll open Moab, let the east take hold, Ammon's memory gone, as prophecy told.
Judgment on Moab, justice comes near, Then you'll know Yahweh in every tear. Edom offended, vengeance was claimed, Now Yahweh's wrath, you'll be maimed.
Teman to Dedan, desolate land, Israel's hands will fulfill my command. Vengeance on Edom, with my wrath they'll contend, Then they'll know Yahweh, the beginning and the end.
Philistines sought revenge, with soul's disdain, Eternal hostility, now feel the pain. Cherethites cut off, coasts laid bare, Vengeance will strike, Yahweh's justice everywhere.
Wrathful rebukes, my vengeance will call, Then you'll know Yahweh, once and for all."
In the eleventh year, first day of the scene, God's word came clear, like a dream. "Son of man, hear Tyre's boastful say, 'Aha, Jerusalem's broken, she's ours today!'
But listen up, Tyre, the Lord Yahweh's near, "Behold, I'm against you, feel the fear. Like waves from the sea, nations will rise, They'll crash your walls, tear down your skies.
Scrape off your dust, make you a bare rock, In the sea you'll be, where fishermen flock. For I've spoken," Yahweh said, "Plundered, you'll be, nations will tread.
Nebuchadnezzar's coming, king of kings, From the north, with armies, he brings. Your daughters in fields meet the sword, Against you, he'll build forts, and horde.
Engines will batter, axes will break, Walls will crumble, towers will shake. His horses' dust will cloud your sight, Chariots roar, walls trembling in fright.
Hoofbeats will echo in your streets loud, People fall, pillars hit the ground. Riches plundered, homes torn down, Stones, timber, dust in waters drown.
Songs will cease, harps won't play, Bare rock you'll be, nets where you'll lay. "Never rebuilt," Yahweh's decree, "Mark my words, that's how it'll be."
Islands will tremble at your sound, Princes of the sea will come down. Clothed in trembling, they'll sit, Astonished by Tyre's pitiful split.
They'll lament, "How you've fallen, renowned sea town, Once strong, now laid down. Islands shiver at your departure, Dismayed at Tyre's shattered future."
"When I make you desolate, cities not found, Deep waters cover, no more around. Into the pit, with old you'll go, In desolate places, you'll dwell below.
A terror you'll be, no more seen, Sought but missing, like a faded dream." Thus spoke Yahweh, His word's a bind, Tyre's end, no more will you find.
Yo, listen up, the word came down to me, "Son of man, lament Tyre by the sea.
At the sea's gate, where you trade wide and far, You say, 'I'm perfect, beautiful by far.'
Your borders deep in ocean's heart lie, Crafted by builders, reaching for the sky.
Planks of cypress, masts of Lebanon's best, Oars from Bashan, ivory benches for rest.
Sails of fine linen, banners high you fly, Blue and purple awnings catch the eye.
Sidon and Arvad rowed with might, Your wise men steered you, pilots bright.
Gebal's elders fixed your seams tight and clean, Ships gathered ’round, trading their scene.
Persia, Lud, and Put armed your force, Helmets and shields showing beauty, of course.
Arvad's troops upon your walls stood tall, Shields on towers, perfecting it all.
Tarshish traded silver, iron in your throng, Javan, Tubal, Meshech brought bronze along.
Togarmah's horses came with mules in a line, Dedan's islands brought ivory, ebony fine.
Syria gave purple, emeralds in trade, Judah's wheat and balm, your wealth was made.
Damascus brought you Helbon and wool, Vedan, Javan, yarns made your stores full.
Dedan's cloths rode in splendor and grace, Kedar’s lambs and rams filled up your space.
Sheba, Raamah offered spices and gold, Haran and Eden brought riches untold.
Tarshish ships carried your goods vast and wide, You were glorious, ruling the tide.
But great waters broke you, winds tore you apart, Riches, warriors sunk, deep in the heart.
Pilots’ cries made the coastlands all shake, Sailors and mariners watched your fate break.
On land they stood, weeping, dust on their head, Wailing for Tyre, like the silence of the dead.
Your trades filled peoples, kings with your gold, But the seas broke you, the waters cold.
Islands shook, kings trembled in fear, Merchants hissed, your end was near.
You've become a terror, once mighty, now no more, Tyre, once great, washed up on the shore."
Yahweh's word hit me like a thunderclap, "Son of man, tell the prince of Tyre this rap:
'Your heart's puffed up, you claim you're a god, Sitting in the seas, acting like you’re Lord.
But you're a man, not divine in any way, You think you're wise; Daniel ain't got your sway.
With wisdom and wit, you stacked silver and gold, Trading brought riches, your pride's uncontrolled.
So listen up, here's what Yahweh's gonna do, Bringing strangers, nations terrible and true.
They'll draw their swords, cut through your wisdom's glow, Down to the pit, your brightness will go.
Will you declare to your slayer, 'I'm a god'? You're a man, he'll see through that façade.
Uncircumcised death, by a foreigner’s hand, 'Cause Yahweh's spoken, now do you understand?
Yahweh's voice echoed in my ear once more, "Son of man, let this lamentation soar:
'You were the seal of wisdom, beauty's prime, In Eden's garden, adorned for a time.
Ruby and topaz, emerald and stone, Gold tambourines, pipes in you alone.
Anointed cherub, holy mountain's tread, Perfect till unrighteousness in you spread.
Trading's abundance filled you with might, Sinned, now cast down from the mountain's height.
Your beauty's pride twisted wisdom's path, Before kings laid down, bearing Yahweh's wrath.
Fire from within you, devoured your frame, Now ashes on earth, all witness your shame.
Astonished the people, a terror's your name, Existence snuffed out, no more in the game.'
Yahweh spoke, "Son of man, face Sidon's land, Prophesy against them, as I command:
'Behold, Sidon, Yahweh's against thee, My glory you'll see, then you'll know it's Me.
Pestilence and blood will flood your streets, Swords on all sides, your defeat repeats.
No more thorns for Israel, no briers in their land, They'll know I'm Yahweh, My word will stand.
When Israel's gathered from scattered nations wide, Sanctified in them, in their land they'll abide.
Securely they'll live, vineyards and homes, Judgments executed, no more to roam.
Then they'll know I am Yahweh, their God supreme, In their own land, living the dream."
In the tenth year, tenth month, day twelve came the word, God spoke to me, His voice clearly heard.

"Don't be afraid," the message is clear, Yahweh's might always near.
He’ll rejoice over you, calm in his embrace, Singing love, removing disgrace.
"I'll deal with your foes, gather the lost, Give them praise, no longer at cost.
I'll restore fortunes, bring you honor and fame," Says Yahweh, with power in his name.
In Darius's year two, month six, day one, Came Yahweh's word, a message begun.
Through Haggai the prophet, to leaders it flew, Zerubbabel and Joshua, what they must do.
Yahweh declared, “These people say, 'Not yet time for my house; we'll delay.'”
But Haggai spoke, words sharp and clear, "Is it time for your homes, while mine's left mere?"
“Consider your ways,” said Yahweh with might, “You've sown, yet little comes to sight.
You eat, not satisfied; you drink, still dry, You clothe yourselves, yet warmth's a lie.
Wages drop through holes, nothing you hold, Consider your ways, hear what I’ve told.
Go to the mountains, bring wood, build anew, I'll take pleasure, glorify what's true.”
"You hoped for much, and it came to small, I blew it away, why?" His voice did call.
“Because my house lies waste, while yours you chase, Thus heavens hold dew, earth withholds its grace.
I called drought on land, grain, and oil, On men, beasts, all hands’ toil.”
Zerubbabel, Joshua, and people in fear, Heard Yahweh's voice, obeyed, drew near.
Then Haggai said, "Yahweh's with you," Spirit stirred in hearts, they knew.
Zerubbabel and Joshua, leaders bold, With the people, built as they were told.
On the twenty-fourth day, in month six’s fame, In year of Darius, they honored His name.
Seventh month, twenty-first day, Yahweh spoke, Haggai the prophet, delivering hope's cloak. "Zerubbabel, Joshua, listen to my call, And to all the people, stand strong and tall.
Who remembers this house in former glory? Now it looks like nothing, just a shadow story. Yet be strong, Zerubbabel," Yahweh repeats, "Be strong, Joshua, stand firm on your feet.
All you people, rise, for I am here, Yahweh of Armies speaks, have no fear. I pledged my word when Egypt was left behind, My Spirit lives with you, peace of mind.
Once more I'll shake earth, sea, and sky, Nations will tremble, as glory draws nigh. Silver and gold, all belong to me, This house will shine, greater it shall be.
On the twenty-fourth day, ninth month rolled, Yahweh's new word, by Haggai was told. "Ask the priests about the sacred law, Does holy meat make other food pure?"
"No," said the priests, "it won't transfer the grace." Haggai replied, "This is Israel's case. Unclean they are, in all they present, Their works defiled, they must repent.
Consider the past, when stones were first laid, Shortfall of harvest, in work they stayed. Blight, mildew, hail, struck all that you grew, Yet back to me you never flew.
From this day forth, mark it clear, Blessings will flow, no more fear. Seed in the barn, fruits yet unshown, From today’s end, blessings I’ll loan.”
Again Yahweh spoke, same day’s light, To Zerubbabel, His promise bright. "Heavens and earth, I'll shake once more, Thrones will crumble, kingdoms will pour.
Chariots, riders, all will fall, Each by the sword of his brother’s call. In that day, Zerubbabel, my chosen seal, As a signet ring, my covenant real."
In the eighth month's glow, second year of Darius' show, Yahweh spoke to Zechariah, words began to flow.
"Yahweh's displeased with your fathers, hear me now," "Return to me," He said, "I'll come to you somehow."
"Don't be like them, who ignored my call," They didn't listen, and they faced the fall.
"Fathers are gone, prophets don't last," But my words remain, standing fast.
They repented, realizing their fate, "Yahweh dealt with us, as our ways relate."
Shebat's eleventh month, the vision's clear, A man on a red horse, standing near.
Among myrtle trees in a ravine's fold, Red, brown, white horses, mysteries to be told.
I asked, "What are these, my Lord?" The angel said, "I'll show, heed my word."
The man among trees spoke, "Yahweh's spies," They roam the earth, under the skies.
Reporting back, "The earth's at peace," But the angel asked, "When will mercy release?"
Yahweh answered with comfort and grace, "I burn with jealousy for Zion's place."
"Angry at nations, too much they've done," "My mercy returns, Jerusalem won."
"My house rebuilt, lines drawn with care," "My cities prosper, Yahweh's there."
I lifted my eyes, four horns I saw, "What are these?" I asked in awe.
"Horns scattered Judah, Israel's plight," Four craftsmen come to set things right.
"To cast down nations, terrify, disband," For Judah's sake, they'll take a stand.
Eyes lifted high, saw a man with a line, "Where you headed?" I asked, in the divine.
He said, "To measure Jerusalem, width and length," An angel stepped out, with heavenly strength.
"Run, tell that young man, hear what I say, Jerusalem's vast, no walls in the way."
"Many will gather with livestock and kin, I'll be a fire, my glory within."
"Come on, flee north, leave Babylon's land, I've scattered you wide, like dust from the hand."
"Zion, escape! The call is loud, Let's move from Babylon, join this crowd."
For Yahweh declares, with armies in tow, "Who touches you, feels my wrath, you know."
"Shake my hand, watch them fall and break, Those who served will plunder for your sake."
"Sing, daughter of Zion, rejoice with me, I'm coming to dwell, you'll see who I'll be."
"Many nations will join, they'll all be mine, I'll dwell among you, everything's fine."
"Judah's my choice, my land, my delight, Jerusalem chosen, shining so bright."
Be silent, all flesh, Yahweh awakes, From His holy place, a move He makes.
I saw Joshua stand before the angel's light, With Satan on his right, ready to fight. God spoke to Satan with a rebuke so bold, “Yahweh rebukes you, Satan, behold!
This is a stick plucked from the fire’s heat," Joshua's garments were filthy, at his feet. Angel said, "Remove those filthy clothes, Your sins are gone, and new robes I bestow.”
“Put a clean turban on his head," was my call, They clothed him fresh, standing tall. Yahweh’s angel spoke, words clear and bright, “Walk in my ways, you'll judge with right.
Keep my courts, you'll have a place to stand, Among these here, in this holy land. Joshua, hear, you and your crew, For I’ll bring the Branch, something new.
Before Joshua, a stone with seven eyes, Yahweh's engraving makes the iniquity fly. In one day, sins will vanish away, Then each neighbor, beneath vine and fig stay.”
Neighbors gathered, peace in sight, Under the fig, in Yahweh’s light.
The angel came back, shook me from my sleep, Woke me up like a man from slumber deep.
"What do you see?" he asked me with a gaze, "I see a gold lamp stand with its seven blaze,
A bowl on top, seven lamps alight, Pipes to each lamp, shining bright.
Two olive trees stand, one left, one right," I asked, "What are these?" in the angel's sight.
"Don't you know?" the angel asked, sincere, I replied, "No, my lord, make it clear."
Then he spoke with Yahweh's word to say, "Not by might or power, but my Spirit's way."
"Who are you, mountain, rising in pride? Before Zerubbabel, you'll be flat and wide.
He'll bring the capstone, with shouts of grace, Calling 'Grace, grace!' in this sacred place."
Yahweh's word came straight to me, "Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation, see?
He'll finish the work, his hands will do, Then you'll know Yahweh sent me to you.
Who despises the day of things so small? These seven shall rejoice, watch the plumb line fall.
Yahweh's eyes, they search the earth, Back and forth, seeing every worth."
I asked again, "What are these olive trees, Side by side with the lamp stand, if you please?"
Twice I asked, "What are these branches of gold, Pouring oil from spouts, so bold?"
He replied, "Don't you know?" once more, I said, "No, my lord, I implore."
"These are the anointed ones," he said to me, "Standing by the Lord of earth, faithfully."
I looked up high, what did I see? A scroll flying by, as plain as can be.
He asked, "What do you see there, my friend?" "A flying scroll," I said, "twenty cubits long end to end."
"This is the curse," he declared with power, "For thieves and liars, their final hour."
"It enters the thief's home, no place to hide, Tearing down walls, swallowing pride."
"Lift your eyes," the angel drew near, "See what appears, don't you fear."
"What is it now?" I asked in awe, "An ephah basket, that's what I saw."
A lead weight lifted, a woman inside, "This is Wickedness," he said, open wide.
He tossed her down, sealed her tight, Locked in the basket, out of sight.
Two women flew with wind in their wings, Stork-like they soared, carrying things.
"Where do they take her?" I asked the guide, "To Shinar," he said, "where she will reside."
A house to be built, her own domain, In the land of Shinar, she'll remain.
I lifted my eyes, and what did I see? Four chariots rolling between bronze peaks, wild and free.
The first had red horses, fierce and bold, In the second, black horses, dark as coal.
The third rode in with steeds of white, And the fourth, dappled, a powerful sight.
I asked the angel, "My lord, what’s the deal?" He said, "These are the four winds, heaven's seal."
The black horses charge to the north land, The white behind, as if hand in hand.
The dappled head south, spreading wide, While strong ones roam the earth with pride.
He spoke, "Go, walk the earth, roam and track!" So they moved, forth and back.
Then he called, "Those in the north, They've quieted my spirit from henceforth."
Yahweh’s word came, bold and clear, "Gather from captivity, bring them near.
Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, come today, To Josiah’s house, where they from Babylon stay.
Take silver, take gold, craft a crown, Place it on Joshua, the high priest renowned.
Tell him, 'Yahweh of Armies declares, The Branch will rise, building temple stairs.
Yes, he will build, he’ll bear the glory, He’ll sit on the throne, that's the story.
He'll rule and priest, in peace unite, The counsel of peace shall be their light.
Crowns for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, Hen, A memorial in Yahweh’s temple, amen.
From afar, they’ll come to build Yahweh’s place, You'll know Yahweh sent me in this grace.
It’ll happen if you heed and hear, Yahweh’s voice, loud and clear."
In the fourth year of Darius, the scene was set, Yahweh's word to Zechariah, on the date you won't forget.
From Bethel they came, Sharezer and Regem Melech too, Seeking Yahweh's favor, wondering what to do.
"Should we weep in the fifth month, again this year, As we've done in the past, shedding many a tear?"
Then Yahweh's word came, strong and clear, "Speak to the people, let all the priests hear.
When you fasted and mourned, was it for me? Or was it for yourselves, can't you see?
When you eat and drink, isn't it self-driven? Aren't these the words by prophets once given?
Back when Jerusalem was bustling with life, And around her, cities free from strife."
Then Yahweh spoke again, with a message profound, "True judgment, kindness, let them abound.
Don't oppress the widow, the fatherless, or the poor, Show compassion, keep evil from your core."
But they turned away, refused to hear the call, Hardened their hearts, unyielding as a wall.
Yahweh’s wrath was stirred, from neglect and defiance, He called, they ignored, now they face the consequence.
"Just as they ignored, and turned from my voice, I'll scatter them far, they've left me no choice.
A whirlwind will take them to lands unknown, For the desolate land is what they have sown."
Thus the scene is set, the message is clear, Actions have consequences, heed what you hear.
The word of Yahweh came, strong and true, "Jealous for Zion, with a wrathful hue."
"I’ve returned to Zion, where truth shall reign, In Jerusalem's heart, my presence will remain.
Old men, old women, strolling the street, Boys and girls playing where laughter meets.
If it’s marvelous to you, why not to me?" Yahweh of Armies declares with decree.
"From east and west, my people I'll save, In Jerusalem they'll dwell, as I pave the way.
Be strong, hear this from prophets of old, When no wages were paid, nor peace up for hold.
I won't be as I was in the days gone past, The seed and the vine, their fruit will last.
Once a curse, now a blessing you'll be, So fear not, let your hands work free.
I thought of wrath when your fathers strayed, But now I plan good, so don't be afraid.
Speak truth to your neighbor, let peace preside, Avoid false oaths, let no evil reside.
The word of Yahweh comes once more, Fasts turn to feasts, joy to the core.
Many will come from cities and lands, Seeking Yahweh's favor, in united bands.
In those days, ten will hold fast To the skirt of a Jew, for God is with you, at last."
Yo, listen up, Yahweh's word's gonna fly, Against Hadrach's land and Damascus sky.
The tribes of Israel, their eyes on the Lord, Hamath's next, as they sharpen the sword.
Tyre, she stacked silver like dust in the air, But the Lord's gonna strike, fire everywhere.
Ashkelon sees it, feelin' that fear, Gaza's in pain, Ekron sheds a tear.
Kings will fall, the throne's gonna shake, Ashkelon empty, pride will break.
Foreigners in Ashdod, Philistine pride's gone, "I'll cut it off, no oppressor will go on."
"Blood from his mouth, abominations too, He'll join Judah, be one of you."
"I'll camp 'round my house, armies stay away, No more oppression, I've seen it today."
Zion, daughter, rejoice and shout, Your King is coming, no doubt.
Lowly, yet righteous, salvation he brings, On a donkey's colt, the King of Kings.
Chariots cut off, no more war cries, Peace to nations, from sea to sky.
Prisoners freed, from the pit of despair, "Return with hope, I'm there to care."
Judah's my bow, Ephraim the string, Zion's sons rise, hear the battle ring.
Yahweh's seen, lightning's his arrow, Trumpet sounds, whirlwinds follow.
Yahweh defends, sling stones fly, Drunk with victory, they roar high.
Saved by God, like jewels in a crown, Lifted up, never coming down.
Oh, his goodness, beauty so great, Grain and new wine, it's time to celebrate.
"Ask Yahweh for rain in spring's embrace, He makes storm clouds, showers fall to grace.
Teraphim's lies, diviners deceive, False dreams they spin, but no reprieve.
Sheep wander lost, no shepherd's care, Oppressed they roam, burdened by despair.
"My wrath's for shepherds, goats I’ll scold, Yahweh's flock will be bold.
From Judah comes the stone, the nail, the bow, Mighty rulers, together they grow.
Tread down the streets, mud under their feet, Fight with Yahweh, their victory's sweet.
"I'll strengthen Judah, Joseph I'll save, In mercy's light, they'll leave the grave.
"I am Yahweh, their God who hears, Ephraim rejoices, sheds no tears.
Children see joy like wine's delight, In Yahweh's name, hearts take flight.
"I'll signal, gather, redeem anew, Increase their number, as they once grew.
Scattered afar, they'll remember my name, With children return, they'll never be the same.
"From Egypt's grip, from Assyria's hand, I'll lead them to Gilead, Lebanon's land.
"Through seas of trouble, I'll make a way, Nile's depths dry, pride will sway.
Strength in Yahweh, they'll walk in his fame, Up and down, in his holy name," says Yahweh.
Open up, Lebanon, let the fire consume your trees, Cypress and cedar fall to their knees.
Oaks of Bashan, hear the cries in the wood, The strong have fallen, their pride misunderstood.
Hear the shepherds wail, their glory's gone, Lions roar, the Jordan's pride is withdrawn.
Yahweh declares, "Feed the destined flock, Buyers kill with impunity, stock by stock."
"Shepherds sell and count their gold, No pity shown, just stories told."
"I won't spare the people," declares Yahweh strong, "Men turn on each other, right or wrong."
I fed the destined, the oppressed in their plight, Held two staffs close, called 'Favor' and 'Union' tight.
Three shepherds cut off, in a month, they were done, Weary of them, their loathing for me begun.
I said, "I won't feed, let the dying die, And those left consume, no need to ask why."
Broke Favor's staff, covenant shattered wide, The flock knew Yahweh's word couldn't hide.
"If you deem it right, give me my pay, If not, then keep it," I did say.
They counted out thirty silver coins, my due, Yahweh said, "To the potter, throw them, untrue."
In Yahweh’s house, to the potter, went the price, Union's staff broke, end of brotherhood's ties.
Yahweh spoke, "Take the foolish shepherd's gear, A new shepherd rises, one who won't care."
"Won't mend the broken, nor tend the flock, He'll feast on the fat, tear apart the stock."
"Woe to the shepherd who deserts his post, Sword on his arm, his eye's vision lost."
Yahweh speaks, listen clear, hear His call, He stretched the heavens wide, made earth stand tall. Inside man, His spirit He formed with care, Now His words to Israel, hear them declare:
"Jerusalem a cup all nations will drain, Judah too, feeling the siege's strain. On that day, Jerusalem's weight they'll meet, All who touch it will suffer defeat.
Horses in terror, riders losing their minds, My eyes on Judah, sightless foes left behind. Chieftains whisper, 'Inhabitants strong,' Their strength in Yahweh, where they belong.
On that day, Judah's leaders like flames, Devouring nations, spreading their names. Jerusalem's place, secure and tight, "Yahweh saves," Judah's future bright.
Feeble as David, defense is sure, Like Yahweh’s angel, steadfast and pure. Nations gathered, but destined to fall, Jerusalem's foes, Yahweh will call.
Grace like rain, pouring down, On David's house, grace profound. They'll look to Me, pierced with grief's sting, Mourning deep, a bitter cry they sing.
In that day, mourning fills the air, Like Megiddon's tears, the valley's despair. Each family, separate in their pain, David, Nathan, Levi—mourning's refrain.
Apart they stand, wives and kin, In solitude, their mourning begins. Every family, each their part, Tears and sorrow, heavy on the heart."
In that day, a spring will flow, David's house will know, A cleansing for sin, Jerusalem's glow.
Yahweh of Armies speaks with might, "Idols' names gone, lost from sight."
Prophets and impure spirits, out they'll go, “The land will be pure, just so you know.”
If a prophet dares to rise and lie, Parents will say, "For this, you must die."
No hairy cloaks to deceive and pretend, "I’m no prophet, just a farmer, my friend."
"What are these wounds?" someone will ask, "In my friends' house, they gave me this task."
"Awake, sword, strike my shepherd," Yahweh cries, Sheep will scatter, as confusion flies.
Two parts gone, but one remains, In the fire, I'll purify, break the chains.
Silver refined, gold tested, strong, They'll call Me, I'll listen, where they belong.
"It is my people," Yahweh will declare, "We are His, in His constant care."
A day of Yahweh's wrath, the nations drawn near, Jerusalem's plunder divided, instilling fear.
The city falls, homes rifled, women in tears, Half the folks in chains, but some remain here.
"Yahweh fights," a battle like days of old, Mount Olives splits, a mighty tale to be told.
Flee through the valley, like an earthquake's flight, Yahweh comes with His holy ones, a powerful sight.
No light or frost, uniqueness in the air, Evening brings light, His presence everywhere.
Living waters flow, from Jerusalem they stream, East and west they go, like a vivid dream.
Yahweh reigns as King, earth under His sway, On that day, His name alone we will say.
Land like Arabah, the heights raised high, Jerusalem dwells safe, peace in the sky.
A plague strikes down those who dared to fight, Flesh, eyes, tongue consume, a terrible sight.
Panic spreads, neighbors turn hand on hand, Judah fights bravely, wealth in the land.
Gold, silver, cloth, the nations' riches stored, Animals stricken too, by Yahweh’s word.
Survivors each year will come and kneel, Worship the King, Yahweh, whose power is real.
No rain for those who refuse the feast, Egypt and others, punished like the least.
On horses' bells, "HOLY TO YAHWEH" rings wide, Every pot made holy, Yahweh’s pride.
No Canaanite found in Yahweh’s sacred place, His house purified, full of grace.

Yahweh speaks to Israel, a word through Malachi's pen, "I've loved you," He declares, "How?" you question again. "Esau and Jacob were brothers, remember the tale? I loved Jacob, but Esau's land I made a barren vale."

Edom boasts, "We'll rise, rebuild from the ground," But Yahweh says, "They'll build, yet I'll tear it down. Men will call them 'The Wicked Land,' forever under my frown." Your eyes will see it, and you'll proclaim, "Yahweh is renowned!"

"A son honors his dad, a servant his boss, right? Where's my honor, my respect? You priests, you slight. You ask how you've despised my name, it's plain, Polluted bread you offer on my altar, again and again."

"When you bring the blind for sacrifice, ain't that wrong? The lame and sick you offer, you think that's strong? Would your governor take it, be pleased with such things?" Yahweh asks, "Show me the respect that royalty brings."

"Entreat God's favor, seek His grace," Yahweh suggests, "Would He accept you now, after all this mess?" "If just one would close the doors, stop this hollow flame, I take no joy in you," Yahweh of Armies proclaims.

"From day's first light to its final fall, My name's revered among nations, pure offerings all. But you profane it, call my table a burden to bear, Bring what's beaten, lame, and sick, yet think I'd care?"
"Cursed be the deceiver with a male in his fold, Who vows a good gift, but offers what's cold. For I am a great King," Yahweh's voice rings, "My name is awesome among all earthly things."
Listen up, priests, this command is laid for you, If you won’t listen, hear my truth, it’s due.
"Glorify my name," Yahweh speaks forth, Or curses will rain, blessings lost, henceforth.
Your lineage rebuked, dung on your face, From feasts you uphold, in disgrace.
"You’ll know I sent this word anew, My covenant with Levi, it stands true."
"Life and peace I gave, that reverence be found, He honored my name, with awe profound.
Truth on his lips, no wrong in his stride, Walked in peace, led many to my side."
A priest’s lips hold knowledge, they seek my way, Messenger of Yahweh, in truth they stay.
But you've strayed, caused many to fall, Corrupted Levi’s vow, hear my call.
Contemptible, wicked, the people see, For you’ve twisted my law, shown partiality.
One Father we have, one God made us all, Why betray each other, make the covenant fall?
Judah's betrayal, an unholy affair, With foreign gods, they lay bare.
Yahweh cuts off those who stray, From Jacob’s tents, they’ll fade away.
You cover altars with tears and sighs, But no more is your offering prized.
"Why?" you ask, Yahweh bears witness true, Against your youth’s wife, you've been untrue.
One he made, with Spirit’s breath, For godly offspring, not treacherous death.
"Hate and divorce," Yahweh shouts loud, "Violence you wear, like a shroud.
Pay heed to your spirit, stay faithful, stay right, Unfaithful hearts weary me, in the dead of night."
You weary Yahweh with words you speak, "How weary?" you ask, confused and weak.
Claiming evil is good in Yahweh's sight, Demanding justice, as darkness turns to light.
"Behold, the messenger's on his way, Prepping the road, clearing the fray. The Lord you seek will hit the scene, In His temple, quick and keen.
"Can you stand the day He arrives? Like fire and soap, refining lives. He'll purify Levi's sons with ease, Offerings in righteousness, aiming to please.
Judah, Jerusalem, bringing the past back, Offerings now pleasant, no more slack. A swift witness, I'll come near, Against injustice, let it be clear.
"I, Yahweh, never change, Sons of Jacob, don't rearrange. You've strayed, turned from My call, Return to Me, and I'll restore all."
"How do we return?" you cry, "Robbing God," you deny. Tithes and offerings you've withheld, Cursed the nation, truth be upheld.
Bring tithes, fill My storehouse's space, Test Me, I'll pour blessings, fill the place. Rebuke the devourer, fields shall thrive, Nations call you blessed, see you alive.
"Your words against Me, hard, you say, Serving's vain, you question the way. The proud seem happy, wicked rise, Tempt God, escape, no surprise."
But those who fear, together they stand, Yahweh listens, a book in His hand. "They're My own, they'll be spared, As a son who's loved, deeply cared."
Return, discern, the good and the bad, Who serves God, and who's been had.
A day is coming, hot as a furnace blaze, Proud hearts and wicked ways, they'll go up in flames. "Not a root or a branch will remain," Yahweh declares, Fire will consume them, leaving only air.

But those who fear my name, rise with healing light, "Leaping like the calves, you'll dance out of night." You'll tread down the wicked, ashes under your feet, On the day I act, feel the heat of my beat.
"Remember Moses' law, given in Horeb's sight, Statutes and ordinances, keep them in your life." Elijah's coming, before that great day, Turning hearts around, in a brand new way.
Fathers to children, children to their dads, Or else I'll strike the earth—no time for feeling sad. Yahweh of Armies speaks, His word prevails, From the furnace to the healing, His truth never fails.
From Abraham to Jesus, the line's divine, A heritage of kings, a sacred sign.
Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Judah's crew, Judah and Tamar brought Perez and Zerah too.
Hezron and Ram, lineage maintained, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon named.
By Rahab, Salmon fathered Boaz bold, Boaz and Ruth, their story told.
Obed to Jesse, then David the king, From David to Solomon, history would sing.
Rehoboam, Abijah, Asa's reign, Jehoshaphat, Joram, in the line they remain.
Uzziah and Jotham, Ahaz, the call, Hezekiah, Manasseh, Amon, stand tall.
Josiah, Jechoniah at Babylon's door, Exile came, but the line restored.
From Shealtiel to Zerubbabel's might, Abiud to Azor, the torch passed right.
Zadok, Achim, Eliud stand, Eleazar, Matthan, a destined band.
Jacob and Joseph, to Mary betrothed, From her, Jesus, prophecy clothed.
Fourteen from Abraham to David's throne, Fourteen to exile, then Jesus shown.
Mary, engaged but blessed by the Spirit's power, Joseph, righteous, faced a challenging hour.
"Joseph, son of David," the angel proclaimed, "Fear not, take Mary, don't be ashamed.
She'll bear a son, name him Jesus, the call, He'll save the people, redeem them all."
Prophets spoke of a virgin's child, "Immanuel," God's presence compiled.
Joseph woke, did as told, obeyed the command, Took Mary, awaited the promised land.
He knew her not till the birth was done, And named him Jesus, the awaited one.
Born in Bethlehem, under Herod's reign, Wise men from the east made their claim.
"Where's the King of the Jews?" they said, "We saw his star, it led ahead."
Herod heard and felt the fear, All Jerusalem knew something was near.
Chief priests, scribes, gathered, sought, "In Bethlehem," prophecy taught.
Herod, in secret, called the wise, "Find the child, report back," he devised.
The star led on, guiding bright, Till it stopped, shining its light.
Joy overflowed, the wise men knelt, Mary with the child, the wonder felt.
Gifts of gold, frankincense, myrrh they gave, In worship profound, their hearts did rave.
Warned in a dream, they took a new track, Avoided Herod, never went back.
An angel to Joseph, in dreams did say, "Rise, take the child, to Egypt away."
By night they fled, under the stars, Till Herod's time passed, till all was ours.
Herod's wrath, rage unchecked, Children of Bethlehem faced his wreck.
Prophecy spoke of Rachel's tears, Weeping echoed through those years.
When Herod died, Joseph dreamt again, "Return to Israel, free from pain."
Back they went, but cautious, aware, To Galilee, Nazareth's care.
Fulfillment came as prophets had seen, The child called Nazarene, where he’d been.
In those days, John hit the scene, wild and free, Preaching in Judea, "Repent! The kingdom's near, you see!"
He was the voice Isaiah foretold, In the wilderness, making paths bold.
John rocked camel's hair with a leather belt, Locusts and honey, his meals, heartfelt.
Crowds from all around came to see, Baptized in the Jordan, setting spirits free.
But Pharisees and Sadducees came with a plan, John wasn't impressed, he called out their clan.
"You brood of vipers! Who gave you the tip-off? Produce worthy fruit, or face the cut-off."
"Don't lean on Abraham, thinking you're grand, God could raise children from stones in this land."
"The ax is ready to chop the bad roots, Trees without good fruit get the boot!"
"I baptize with water, but one greater will rise, With the Holy Spirit, fire in his eyes."
"He'll winnow and cleanse, gather the wheat, But burn the chaff with fire oh so neat."
Then Jesus from Galilee stepped into the scene, To be baptized by John in waters so clean.
John hesitated, "I need your touch, Yet you come to me? This is too much!"
Jesus replied, "Let it be so now, To fulfill righteousness, we'll take this vow."
In the water, Jesus rose, heaven's gate swung wide, The Spirit, like a dove, came to abide.
A voice from the heavens thundered strong, "This is my beloved Son, in Him I belong."

Out in the wilderness, the Spirit led him fast, Forty days, forty nights, hunger hit at last. The devil stepped up, said, "Son, make bread from stone," But Jesus replied, “Man ain't fed on bread alone."
Took him to the temple high, said, "Son, take a leap, Angels got your back, your feet won't meet the street." Jesus answered, “It's said, don’t test the Lord, God's in control, heed his holy word."
On a mountain peak, the world spread wide, Devil said, "Bow to me, kingdoms'll be your pride." Jesus shot back, “Get behind me, Satan, Worship only God, his word I’m statin’."
Devil left him be, angels came to serve, Jesus stood firm, never lost his nerve. He heard John's been caught, so he moved on to Galilee, Left Nazareth, Capernaum by the sea.

Fulfilled Isaiah's words, in darkness light was seen, "Repent," he preached, "Heaven's kingdom's keen." Saw brothers by the sea, casting nets with might, "Come after me, fishers of men you'll be tonight."
Left their nets, followed him without delay, Called more brothers, they came, no words to say. Jesus traveled Galilee, preaching Kingdom's news, Healing every sickness, no one did he refuse.
From Galilee to Judea, the crowds they grew, The sick, the possessed, he healed them too. Great multitudes followed, from lands far and wide, His light and love spread, couldn't be denied.
Crowds gathered, mountains climbed, He took a seat, Disciples gathered 'round, ready for the treat.
"Blessed are the poor in spirit, Kingdom of Heaven's theirs, Blessed are the mournful, comfort erases cares.
Blessed are the gentle, they'll inherit the earth, Those hungry for righteousness? They'll find worth.
Blessed are the merciful, mercy they'll obtain, Pure hearts will see God, His presence they'll gain.
Peacemakers are God's kids, known far and wide, Persecuted for righteousness? Kingdom's on their side.
Reproached and persecuted for my name, don't be sad, Rejoice, be glad, rewards in Heaven ain't half bad.
You're the salt of the earth, don't lose your taste, Saltless cast out, trodden, a waste.
You're the light of the world, city on a hill can't hide, Light the lamp on a stand, let it shine with pride.
Let your light shine, show good works to men, Glorify your Father in Heaven, again and again.
Don't think I came to destroy the law, no, I fulfill, Not one letter will pass, 'til all's accomplished, still.
Break the least command? Least in Heaven, I say, Do and teach them all? Great you'll stay.
Unless righteousness surpasses scribes' and Pharisees' call, No entry to the Kingdom, for you at all.
You've heard it said, 'Don't murder, face the law's might,' But anger without cause brings judgment's light.
Say 'Raca' to a brother? Council's near, Call him 'fool'? Fire of Gehenna, fear.
If at the altar, you recall a brother's pain, Make peace first, then offer again.
Agree with adversaries, quickly settle the score, Lest prison holds you, freedom no more.
You've heard it said, 'Adultery, don't commit,' But lust in your heart? Guilty of it.
If your eye offends, pluck it, better to lose a part, Than whole body's plunge into Gehenna's dark.
Hand causing sin? Cut it, throw it away, Better one piece gone than all astray.
Divorce with a decree, it's that you’ve heard, But I say immorality makes the word.
False vows to ancient ones were said, But don't swear at all, keep your head.
Heaven's God's throne, earth His footstool, Jerusalem's the King's city, keep it cool.
Let your 'Yes' be 'Yes,' 'No' be 'No,' Anything else comes from the evil's flow.
'An eye for an eye,' they say, justice tight, But turn the other cheek, don't fight.
Give your cloak if sued for your coat, Go two miles when forced, that's the note.
Give to those who ask, don't turn away, Borrowers receive, come what may.
Love your neighbor, hate your enemy’s the tale, But love, bless, and pray, that's the trail.
Sun rises and rain falls on good and bad, Love those who love you, reward's just a tad.
Tax collectors greet friends, what's your chore? Be perfect as your Father, just that and more."
When you give to the poor, keep it on the down low, Don't blast trumpets, let the good deeds quietly show.
Hypocrites in the streets, seeking glory from men, They got their reward, but it's empty in the end.
When you give, let your left hand be blind, Your Father sees in secret, His rewards you'll find.
When you pray, don’t be like those who seek attention, In the corners, in the synagogues, craving man's mention.
Go to your room, close the door tight, Pray to your Father who sees without sight.
No endless babble, God's got you, He knows, Before you even ask, His wisdom flows.
Pray like this: “Our Father in the sky, Keep Your name holy, Your Kingdom nearby.
Your will be done, here as up there, Give us today what we need to share.
Forgive our debts as we forgive too, Keep us from evil, in everything we do.
For Yours is the Kingdom, power and glory, Forever and ever, that's the story.”
Forgive others' wrongs, then you'll be free, Your Father'll forgive you, that's His decree.
When you fast, don't show it with a gloomy face, Act normal, clean, full of His grace.
Your Father sees the secret, He’ll give reward, Not the men who watch, with their own accord.
Don't store treasures where moth and rust decay, In heaven, they last, they're there to stay.
Where your treasure is, there’s your heart, So choose wisely, play your part.
The body's lamp is the eye, let it shine bright, If it's evil, you'll be lost in the night.
No man can serve two kings on the throne, Loving one, hating the other, you'll be torn.
Don’t stress about life, what you’ll eat or wear, Life's more than these, so don’t despair.
Look at the birds, they don’t worry or sow, Yet your Father feeds them, don’t you know?
Worry can’t add a moment to your day, So trust in faith, let anxiety sway.
Lilies in the fields, they grow without toil, Yet even Solomon can't match their royal.
If God clothes the grass, here today, gone tomorrow, Won't He clothe you, dispel your sorrow?
Seek first His Kingdom, righteousness in sight, Everything you need, He’ll provide in the light.
Don't worry 'bout tomorrow, let it be, Each day has enough for you and me.
"Don't judge others, or you'll be judged the same, With the measure you use, you'll play your own game.
See the speck in your brother's eye? It's plain, But miss the beam in yours—that's insane.
"Remove your own block," He said with a sigh, "Then help your brother, now clear in your eye."
"Don't toss what's holy to dogs, don't be giving, Your pearls to pigs who'll trample and leave you grieving.
Ask, and it's given, seek, and you'll find, Knock, and that door will open in kind.
If your child needs bread, would you hand him a stone? If fish is his wish, would a serpent be thrown?
If you, flawed beings, give gifts that are good, How much more will God, as a Father should.
"Treat others the way you want to be treated, This is the law, the prophets completed.
Enter the narrow gate, it's tight but it's right, The wide path leads to darkness, not light.
Beware of false prophets, in disguise they may be, A wolf in sheep's clothing is not what you see.
By their fruits, you'll know what they yield, Good trees bring life, corrupt trees are killed.
Not everyone crying 'Lord' gets through heaven's gate, Only those who do God's will, their fate is great.
On that day, many will plead, But I'll say, 'I never knew you, leave indeed.'
"Those who hear and act are wise, like rock they stand, The floods, the winds won't move their land.
But those who hear and don’t act, like sand, they fall, The storm takes them down, their ruin was the call."
When Jesus spoke, the crowds were amazed, For He taught with authority, unlike scribes' old ways.
He stepped off the mountain, crowds at his back, A leper knelt, "Lord, please heal the track." Jesus reached out, "I want to make you clean," Touched him, and leprosy was nowhere to be seen.
"Tell no one, show the priest, offer your gift right," As a testimony, let them see the light. In Capernaum, a centurion came in need, "My servant's in pain, can you perform the deed?"
Jesus said, "I'll come and heal him now," The centurion replied, "Just speak, make that vow. I'm under command, I know how it rolls, I say 'go' and they move, just like the scrolls."
Jesus marveled, "Such faith, not found in this land, Many will come, but some will be banned." To the centurion, "Go, your faith made it true," And the servant was healed, all fresh and new.
At Peter's house, his wife’s mother lay still, He touched her hand, and fever had no will. She rose up quickly, served him on the spot, At night, many came, needing healing they sought.
Demons cast out, sickness healed with his word, Fulfilling Isaiah’s prophecy that they heard. Seeing the crowds, he said, "We must depart," A scribe approached, "Teacher, I’ll follow your heart."
"The foxes have holes, birds nests to rest, But the Son of Man roams with no place to nest." Another said, "Let me bury my dead." "Follow me," Jesus said, "Let the dead bury the dead."
They set sail, the sea roared loud and high, But Jesus slept, while the storm passed by. "Save us, Lord," they cried, in fear's embrace, "Why such little faith?" He rebuked the waves' race.
The storm calmed, leaving marveled men in awe, "Even the wind and sea obey his law." In Gergesenes, two fierce souls met, Possessed by demons, a challenge they set.
"What do you want, Son of God, at this hour?" The demons begged, "Send us to that swine tower." "Go!" he commanded, and into pigs they fled, Rushed down the cliff, where the waters spread.
Witnesses ran, told the town all they'd seen, The city came out, begged Jesus to leave the scene.

Stepped in a boat, crossed the sea, hit his city, Paralyzed man brought, friends showed faith gritty. “Son, cheer up! Sins forgiven,” Jesus declared, Scribes whispered "blasphemy," but Jesus wasn't scared.
He read their minds, asked, "Why doubt in your heart? Is it easier to say sins forgiven or make this man start?" Then he turned to the man, “Get up and walk, Take your mat, go home,” no more talk.
Crowds marveled, glorifying God's power, Authority on Earth was the talk of the hour. Jesus saw Matthew, at the tax booth he sat, “Follow me,” he said, Matthew was down with that.

At dinner with sinners, Pharisees complained, "Why eat with these folks?" they disdainfully exclaimed. Jesus replied, “Healthy need no doctor, just the sick, Learn mercy, not sacrifice, that's my pick.”
John’s crew questioned, “Why don’t your guys fast?” “Bridegroom's here now, but this won't last. New cloth on old, new wine in fresh skin, Both are preserved, no bursting within.”
A ruler approached, “My daughter just died, But your touch will revive her,” he cried. On his way with disciples, a woman snuck around, Touched his clothes, her healing was profound.
“Daughter, cheer up! Your faith made you whole,” In that moment, sickness lost control. At the ruler’s house, musicians made a noise, “She's just asleep,” he said, dismissing the ploys.
Crowd laughed, but Jesus took her hand, The girl arose, spread news across the land. Two blind men followed, “Son of David, hear our plea!” “Believe I can do this?” asked He.
“Yes, Lord,” they answered, their faith was true, Touched their eyes, vision renewed. “Don't spread the word,” his command tight, But they shared his fame, couldn't keep it light.
A mute controlled by demons was brought, Jesus cast it out, man spoke, crowd was taut. “Nothing like this in Israel,” they yelled, “By demons’ prince,” Pharisees' accusations swelled.
Jesus traveled, teaching, preaching good news, Healing sickness, mending life's bruise. Seeing crowds, compassion was his view, “Harvest is plenty, laborers are few.
Pray to the Lord, send workers to the field, Gather the harvest, the lost must be healed.”
He called his crew, the twelve in line, Gave them power over spirits, made 'em divine.
Simon called Peter, Andrew his kin, James and John, sons of Zebedee, let the mission begin.
Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas in tow, Matthew the taxman, James with Alphaeus' flow.
Lebbaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Zealot's pride, And Judas Iscariot, who later switched sides.
Jesus sent them out with a command, "Don't hit the Gentiles or Samaritans land.
Go to Israel's lost sheep, bring them the word, The Kingdom's near, let your voice be heard.
Heal the sick, cleanse, and cast out the foe, Freely you've received, so freely let it go.
No gold, no silver, no extra gear, Trust in your journey, you'll be provided here.
In each town, find the worthy, stay while you can, Bless the house entering, that's part of the plan.
If they reject you, shake off their dust, Judgment's gonna come, in God you trust.
"Sheep among wolves, so wise up, see? Be gentle like doves, keep your mind free.
Watch for the councils, they'll put you on trial, But don't stress your words, God's got your style.
Families divided, brother against brother, Yet those who endure will find life like no other.
When they chase you out, move to the next town, Before the Son of Man comes down.
A student ain't above the teacher, that's the truth, If they diss the master, they'll probably diss the youth.
But don't fear the hidden, it'll be revealed, What you hear in whispers, on rooftops, be healed.
Fear not those who harm the flesh alone, Respect the one who holds soul and bone.
Two sparrows for a coin, yet watched by God, Even your hairs are counted, isn't that odd?
Confess me and I'll vouch for you up high, Deny me, and your chance with the Father, goodbye.
"I didn't come for peace, but a sword to divide, Setting kin against kin, breaking family pride.
Love me more than kin, take your cross, be bold, Lose your life for me, find treasures untold.
Receive you, receive me, and Him above, A prophet's reward comes with that kind of love.
Give a cup of water to those in need, Rewards in heaven for the righteous seed."
Jesus sent the twelve, then hit the road, Teaching and preaching, His message flowed.
John in prison heard of Christ's great deeds, Sent two disciples to question His creeds.
"Are you the One, or another's to come?" Jesus replied, "See what's been done:
The blind now see, the lame stride tall, Lepers cleansed, the deaf hear the call,
The dead rise up, the poor hear good news, Blessed is he who doesn’t refuse."
Jesus turned to the crowd, questioning their quest, "In the wilderness, what did you expect?
A reed in the wind, or a man dressed fine, Prophet you sought, and more you'll find.
A messenger foretold, preparing the way, No one greater than John has come to stay.
Yet even the least in Heaven's domain, Is greater than he, let that truth remain.
This kingdom's been taken by force, it’s true, From John's days till now, it's breaking through.
If you can hear and understand, John as Elijah, as was planned."
He compared them to children, hard to please, Playing tunes, but none dance in the breeze.
John abstained, and they claimed a demon, Christ partook, labeled glutton among men.
Wisdom's kids will prove her right, For truth shines through in the darkest night.
Then He denounced the unrepentant lands, For mighty works done by His hands.
"Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to Bethsaida! Tyre and Sidon would've long repented,
In heaven’s heights, you'll find Capernaum fall, Like Sodom, judged beyond recall.
Father, I thank you for hidden truths revealed, To babes, not wise, Your will is sealed.
All that’s Mine, My Father gave, To know the Son, the Father paves.
Come to Me, weary, burdened down, I’ll give you rest, release that frown.
My yoke is easy, my burden light, Learn from Me, end your fight."
Walking through the fields, disciples feeling famished, Plucking grains on Sabbath, Pharisees were astonished.
“Look!” they said, “They break the law today.” Jesus answered, “David did it in his hungry day.
He entered God’s house, ate the sacred bread, Only for priests, but he and his men were fed.
Priests on Sabbath work, yet they’re guilt-free, And one greater than the temple you now see.
Mercy’s what I seek, not mere sacrifice, For the Son of Man rules the Sabbath, precise."
He moved on, to the synagogue he went, A man with a withered hand, their intent was bent.
“Is it lawful to heal today?” they tried to trap, He replied, “Save a sheep on Sabbath, wouldn’t you act?
A man’s worth more, doing good’s the way.” “Stretch your hand,” he said, healed him that day.
Pharisees plotted, sought to take him down, Jesus stepped away, healing in every town.
“Keep it quiet,” he said, fulfilling the prophet’s tone, “My Spirit’s on him, justice will be shown.
He won’t shout loud in the crowded street, Till justice reigns, won’t accept defeat."
A demon-possessed man, blind and mute, Jesus healed him, crowds did dispute.
“Is this David’s son?” they began to talk, Pharisees claimed evil powers were his walk.
Jesus knew their thoughts, made his stand, “A kingdom divided cannot withstand.
If Satan's divided, his reign's at end, But by God’s Spirit, demons I send.
Bind the strong man, take his goods away, With me or against me, where do you stay?”
All sins forgiven, except against the Spirit, Speak against God’s breath, no pardon to inherit.
Tree good or bad, fruit reveals the truth, Hearts overflow, let no one be aloof.
Idle words matter, in judgment they count, Justified or condemned, your words will mount."
“Show us a sign,” scribes and Pharisees plead, “Only Jonah’s sign,” said Jesus, planting seed.
Three days in the whale, three nights too, Son of Man in earth, same will be true.
Nineveh repented, will judge you today, Someone greater here, what more can I say?
Queen of the South, wisdom she sought, Something greater here, don’t get caught.
Unclean spirits wander, seeking a place, Return with more if the house stays in grace.
Talking to the crowds, his family sought his ear, "Who is my family?" Jesus made it clear.
“Who does my Father’s will, they’re kin to me, Brother, sister, mother—family, eternally.”
Jesus hit the seaside, crowds grew wide, He hopped in a boat, left the shore behind.
"Listen up," He said, "here's the farmer's tale, Seeds scattered wide, hear how they prevail.
Some fell by the road, birds swooped down, Others on rocks, scorched and browned.
Thorns choked some, but others found the good ground, Yielding fruit, hundredfold all around."
"Got ears? Then hear," He made it clear, Disciples asked, "Why parables, dear?"
"It's for you to know Kingdom's mystery, They see but don't perceive, it's history.
Isaiah spoke of hearts hard as stone, Eyes shut tight, left alone."
"Blessed are your eyes, they see and hear, Prophets longed for these words, far and near.
The farmer's tale, let me speak, Evil snatches where understanding's weak.
Rocks are those who hear with joy, but face the heat, Persecution trips them, makes them retreat."
"Thorns are life's worries, riches that sneak, Choking the word, making it weak.
Good ground hears and understands, Bearing fruit, as the harvest expands."
"The Kingdom's like good seeds in a field, Enemy's weeds revealed, concealed.
Wait till harvest, let them grow, Reapers separate, the truth to show."
"Kingdom's like mustard seed, small and slight, But grows to a tree, birds take flight.
Like yeast hidden in the meal, Transforms the whole, that's the deal."
Jesus dropped parables, mysteries to unfold, Prophets said it'd happen, stories bold.
Disciples wanted more, weeds explained, Son of Man sows good, devil's seeds profane.
Harvest's end, angels do the deed, Righteous shine, wicked weep indeed.
Kingdom's treasure hidden, a man will sell, The pearl of great price, he knows well.
A dragnet cast, fish gathered tight, Good kept in, bad thrown from sight."
"Understand?" He asked, they replied, "Yes, Lord." Scribes in the Kingdom, treasures to afford.
Jesus taught them, hometown amazed, "Isn't this the carpenter's son?" they crazed.
Offense took hold, prophets scorned near, Mighty works few, unbelief was clear.
Herod heard the news, his mind in fret, "John's back from the dead, that's the power he's met."
He'd jailed John for Herodias, his brother's wife, John spoke out, "This ain't lawful, it's messing with life."
Herod feared the crowd, they saw John as a prophet, But on his birthday, a dance made him forget.
Herodias's girl danced, the king was pleased, Promised her an oath, anything she seized.
Her mom said, "Ask for John's head on a plate." Herod grieved but kept his word, sealed John's fate.
John was beheaded; his head was shown, Disciples took his body, buried him alone.
They told Jesus, and he sought some space, Crowds followed him, seeking his grace.
He healed the sick, his compassion flowed, Disciples worried, "It's late, send them down the road."
Jesus said, "No need to let them go, Give them food, let's start the show."
"Five loaves, two fish," they said in defeat, "Breathe life into these, let them eat."
He blessed, he broke, his hands did share, Five thousand fed from baskets spare.
He sent disciples on a boat to the other side, While he prayed alone, past eventide.
Wind rose up, the sea was wild, Jesus walked on waves, calm and mild.
"It's a ghost!" they cried, fear in their eyes, He said, "Cheer up, it's me, don't disguise."
Peter said, "If it's you, let me walk too," "Come," said Jesus, so Peter stepped true.
Wind made him falter, fear took hold, "Lord, save me!" his courage cold.
Jesus reached out, caught his hand in care, "Why doubt, little faith, I was there."
Back in the boat, the storm laid down, They worshiped him, "Son of God, we crown."
Reached Gennesaret, word spread wide, The sick were brought from far and wide.
Touched his cloak, healing was complete, Faith in his presence made them whole, sweet.
Pharisees and scribes came with questions to raise, "Why don't your disciples follow elder ways?" Jesus replied, "Traditions you hold so tight, But God's commandments, you twist to your delight.
'Honor your parents,' that's God's command, Yet by your rules, that duty's banned. Isaiah spoke of you, called you hypocrite, Lips praise, hearts stray, in vain you submit."
He called to the crowd, "Listen, understand, What goes in the mouth, that's not what's banned. What comes out defiles, from the heart it flows, Words reveal the soul, that's how it goes."
Disciples whispered, "Pharisees took offense." Jesus said, "Every plant not planted will face suspense. Blind leading blind, both will hit the pit, Leave them alone, don't be caught in their writ."
Peter asked, "Explain, we still don't see," Jesus said, "It's not food, but heart's decree. Evil thoughts, false words, that's what defiles, Not eating with hands unwashed with styles."
He traveled to Tyre, a Canaanite cried in pain, "Son of David, my daughter is demon's reign!" He stayed silent, but she begged with hope, "Help me, Lord, in my struggle to cope."
"It's not right to give children's bread to dogs," He said, "Even dogs eat crumbs," was her faithful thread. "Great is your faith," Jesus then declared, Her daughter healed, her heart repaired.
From there, by Galilee, Jesus took His place, Crowds brought the broken, seeking His grace. He healed them all, the multitude amazed, Mute spoke, blind saw, and God was praised.

"Three days they've been here, with nothing to eat," Jesus felt compassion, His love complete. The disciples wondered, "Where to find such bread?" Jesus asked, "How many loaves?" They said, "Seven," instead.
He had them sit, took loaves and fish, Gave thanks, broke them, fulfilled their wish. All ate, were filled, leftovers in baskets, Four thousand men, not counting all the rest.
Sent the crowds away, His work for now done, He sailed to Magdala, under the setting sun.

Pharisees and Sadducees, they came with a test, Asked for a sign from heaven, thinking they're the best. Jesus replied, "You read the sky, know red from blue, But you miss the signs, can't see what's true.
This wicked generation wants a sign, but in vain, Only Jonah's sign you'll get, let me explain." Then He left them standing, no sign to show, Crossed to the other side, where the disciples go.
They forgot the bread, minds in a twist, "Beware the yeast of the Pharisees," Jesus insists. "We forgot the bread," they reasoned, confused, Jesus perceived, "Why's your faith so bruised?

Remember the five loaves, fed five thousand, no lack, And the seven loaves, more baskets to pack. I'm not talking 'bout bread, but beware instead, Of the Pharisees' teachings, the things they've said."
Then they got it, understood the plot, It wasn't about bread, but the teachings they bought. In Caesarea Philippi, the question arose, "Who do people say I am?" Jesus chose.
"John, Elijah, Jeremiah," the guesses flew, "But who do you say I am?" — a question for the few. Peter declared, "You're the Christ, God's Son!" "Blessed are you, Peter, for what's begun.
On this rock, I'll build, Hades won't prevail, Heaven's keys I give, in binding, you'll not fail." But "Tell no one," He said, "keep it discreet, For soon I'll face death, but death I'll defeat."
Peter, in fear, "Lord, never should you die," But Jesus said, "Satan, step aside, don't try. Your mind's not on God's, but on man's way, Take up your cross, follow me, day by day.
Gain the world, lose your soul, what's the gain? For the Son of Man will come to reign. Some here will see the Kingdom unfold, Before death takes its toll, the story told."
After six days, Jesus took the crew, Peter, James, and John's his crew, Up a high mountain, alone in view.
Transformed in light, His face did blaze, Shining bright as the sun's fierce rays.
Moses and Elijah, they appeared that day, Talking with Jesus, in a holy display.
Peter said, “It’s good we're here, let's make three, Tents for You, Moses, and Elijah, let it be.”
While he spoke, a cloud of brightness rolled, A voice declared from its midst and told,
"This is my beloved Son, hear Him speak, In Him I'm pleased, His words you seek.”
Terrified, the disciples fell to the ground, Faces down, in the fear they were found.
Jesus touched them, His voice was kind, “Rise up, don’t fear, peace you’ll find.”
Looking up, all alone was He, No one but Jesus, the vision to see.
Down the mountain, with words profound, "Don’t speak of this till I'm risen from the ground.”
“Why must Elijah come first?” they asked in thought, “Elijah’s come, but respect he got not,”
“They did what they wanted, without delay, The Son of Man will suffer the same way.”
Then they knew He spoke of John’s role, Understanding now filled their soul.
A man approached, in the crowd below, Kneeling, he cried, “Lord, my son's in woe.
Epileptic, he suffers, in fire and in lake, Your disciples tried, their hands did shake.”
“Faithless generation!” Jesus did scold, “How long must I bear this, how long be bold?
Bring him to me,” He commanded with grace, Jesus healed the boy, the demon displaced.
The disciples asked, "Why couldn’t we succeed?" “Your unbelief, the faith you need.
With mustard seed faith, mountains move in sight, But prayer and fasting bring this fight.”
In Galilee, Jesus spoke again, "Son of Man will be taken by men,
They’ll kill Him, but He’ll rise on day three.” Grief filled their hearts, heavy with this decree.
In Capernaum, tax collectors came near, Asked Peter of Jesus, “Does He pay here?”
“Yes, He does,” Peter replied, staying true, Jesus knew and asked, “What do you view?
Kings take tribute from strangers, not their own, Thus, children are exempt, their freedom shown.
But to avoid offense, go cast your line, A fish with a coin, a divine sign.
Take it, pay our due, keep the peace anew.” In every act, wisdom shone through.
Disciples asked, "Who's the greatest, pray?" Jesus called a child to show the way.
"Unless you change, like kids, pure and mild, You won't enter Heaven—be humble like a child.
Receive a child, you receive me, Cause them to stumble? Better sink in the sea.
Woe to the world for stumbling's rise, But woe to the one through whom it flies.
If your hand or foot causes dismay, Cut it off, toss it away.
Better maimed in life to reside, Than whole and cast in the eternal fire wide.
If your eye leads you to err, Pluck it out, better to see with one, than despair.
Don't despise these little ones, I say, Their angels see the Father every day.
The Son of Man's here to save the lost, Seek the stray, no matter the cost.
If a man has a hundred, and one sheep roam, He'll leave the rest to bring that one home.
Rejoice more for the one found astray, Than for the ninety-nine who stayed safe that day.
Father in heaven wants none to be lost, Each soul's precious, regardless the cost.
"If your brother sins, go alone to show, If he hears, you've gained a friend, you know.
If not, take others, have the truth revealed, If he won't listen, let the assembly be appealed.
Treat him as a Gentile, if he won't hear, On earth or in heaven, agreement's clear.
Where two or three gather in my name, There I am, right in the middle of the frame."
Peter asked, "How often to forgive, what's the score?" "Seventy times seven, and then some more."
The Kingdom's like a king who called to account, One servant owed a massive amount.
Couldn't pay, was sold with kin and all, He begged for patience, promised to stand tall.
Moved by compassion, the king set him free, Forgave his debt, a new decree.
But that servant found another who owed few, Grabbed him by the throat, "Pay what's due!"
The fellow servant begged, "Be patient with me," But he was thrown in prison, no mercy to see.
Others saw and told the king the tale, "You wicked servant!" his voice starts to wail.
"I forgave you much, begged for reprieve, Shouldn't you have done the same, believe?"
In anger, he was delivered to the pain, Till he paid the debt that did remain.
Heavenly Father will do the same to you, If you don't forgive your brother, from your heart true.
Jesus wrapped up his words, left Galilee's land, To Judea's borders, where the Jordan sands stand.
Crowds flocked around, healing flowed like a stream, Pharisees tested him with their divorce scheme.
"Is it lawful?" they asked, trying to trip him in speech, He replied, “From the start, male and female, God did teach.
‘Leave mother and father, be one flesh, not two,’ What God joined, let no man undo.”
“But Moses,” they said, “gave divorce command,” “'Cause your hearts were hard, not by God's demand.
From the start, it was never so,” he declared, “Divorce leads to sin, unless infidelity's been shared.”
Disciples, puzzled, questioned his plan, “If marriage is tough, is it better for man?”
“Not all can accept this, only those to whom it’s given, Some choose celibacy for the Kingdom of Heaven.”
Children came near, disciples turned them away, But Jesus said, “Let them come, don't you sway.
The Kingdom belongs to hearts pure as these,” He blessed them, moved on with ease.
A rich man asked, “What must I do for life eternal?” “Keep the commandments, love’s infernal.
Don’t murder, steal, or lie, respect parents true, Love your neighbor—this is your cue.”
“All this I've done, what do I lack?” “Sell all, help the poor, then come back.”
Sad, the man left, for his riches were vast, “It’s hard for the wealthy to reach Heaven’s vast.”
A camel through a needle, a rich man's plight, Disciples wondered, “Who can be saved outright?”
