“With men, impossible, but God makes a way,” Peter asked, “We left all, what’s our pay?”
“In rebirth, you’ll sit on thrones high, Judging tribes in glory’s sky.
Leave all for my name, gain a hundredfold, Eternal life, for the bold.
The first will be last, the last will ascend, In God’s Kingdom, new paths will blend.”
The Kingdom's like a boss, early on the scene, Hiring workers for his vineyard, paying them clean.
A denarius a day, that's the deal they made, Into the vineyard, they went, all ready to get paid.
Around the third hour, he saw some still free, He said, "Go to the vineyard, I'll pay what's right, you'll see."
And again at the sixth, then the ninth hour, he came, Sending more to the vineyard, the deal was the same.
At the eleventh hour, found others standing still, "Why idle all day?" he asked, with a will.
"No one hired us," they replied, standing alone, He said, "To the vineyard, I'll make it right, go on."
Evening came, wages time, the call went out, From last to first, pay the workers all about.
Those hired late got a denarius, paid fair, The first ones thought they'd get more, then came the glare.
"We worked all day in the sun, the heat was great, They worked one hour, yet wages equate?"
He said, "Friend, no wrong did I do, A denarius was the deal, that's what I give you.
Take your pay and go, I choose to bless, Is it wrong if my good causes your distress?"
"The last will be first, the first last," he spoke, "For many are called, few chosen," he awoke.
Jesus heading to Jerusalem, pulled his crew aside, "Soon the Son of Man will be crucified.
Delivered and mocked, scourged cruelly, Raised on the third day, victory fully."
Zebedee's mom came, sons at her side, "Let them sit, your right and left," she cried.
Jesus replied, "You know not what you ask, Can you drink my cup, complete the task?"
"We are able," they said, bold and stout, "My cup you'll drink, but seats? Father sorts that out."
The ten heard, and anger stirred, Jesus called them near, spoke his word.
"Rulers lord over, but not you, Greatness serves, first be a servant true.
Son of Man came to serve, give his life, A ransom for many, ending strife."
Leaving Jericho, crowds did follow, Two blind men by the road, hearts hollow.
"Lord, have mercy, Son of David, please!" The crowd shushed them, but they wouldn't cease.
Jesus paused, asked them clear, "What do you want? Let me hear."
"Open our eyes, Lord, that's our plea," With compassion, he touched, and they did see.
Immediately sight restored, they followed him, The blind now could see, hope no longer dim.
Rolling to Jerusalem, that city so fine, Jesus sent two disciples, with a clear sign:
"Go to the village, find a donkey tied tight, Bring her and her colt, make it right."
"If they ask, say, 'The Lord needs these,' And they'll send them along with ease."
A prophet's words fulfilled, proclaiming the scene, "Your King rides in humble, gentle and clean."
The disciples obeyed, brought the donkey pair, Clothes laid on their backs, Jesus sat there.
Crowds spread garments, branches on the ground, "Hosanna!" they shouted, the joyful sound.
In Jerusalem's heart, the city did shake, "Who is this man?" the people all spake.
"This is Jesus, the prophet," the crowd proclaimed, From Nazareth of Galilee, He came unashamed.
The temple he entered, and chaos he'd unwind, Tables overturned, doves sellers left behind.
"My house is for prayer," He said, in a tone, "But you've turned it to a den, a robber's home."
The blind and the lame, to Him they came, He healed them all, to the priests' disdain.
"Hosanna!" the children cried, pure and bright, Priests questioned, Jesus replied, "They're right."
He left the city, off to Bethany's rest, In the morning, hungry, a fig tree test.
No fruit on the tree, only leaves in sight, "Wither forever!" spoken with might.
The disciples marveled, how quick it died, "Faith can move mountains," Jesus replied.
In the temple again, elders questioned His say, “By what authority do you act this way?”
Jesus countered, "John's baptism, from where did it stem?" The elders pondered, feared the crowd's hem.
Not knowing, they answered, Jesus withheld His own, Parables spoken, truth brightly shown.
A man with two sons, the vineyard's call, One said no, but went after all.
The second agreed, yet did not show, Which did the will? The first, they know.
The tax collectors, they’re coming in first, You saw, you failed to quench your thirst.
Another tale told, a vineyard and its fate, Servants beaten, the son's dire state.
Farmers killed him, seeking greed's allure, "What will the owner do?" they were sure.
"He’ll destroy those men, lease to farmers true," Jesus confirmed, "God's Kingdom is due."
"The stone rejected, now the cornerstone bright, God's work is marvelous, shining in sight."
"The Kingdom's shift, to those bearing fruit, The stone will crush all, none will refute."
The priests and Pharisees felt the parable's sting, Wanted to seize Him, but feared the crowd’s ring.
Jesus spoke in parables, a story to unfold, "The Kingdom's like a king, with a feast to behold.
Sent servants to call, those invited to dine, But nobody came, they ignored the sign.
Sent more with a message, 'Dinner's prepared, Cattle and fatlings, a feast to be shared!'
Some laughed it off, to their farms and trade, Others grabbed his servants, a violent raid.
The king got angry, heard what they’d done, Sent his armies out, judgment begun.
Said to his servants, 'The feast is ready, But those invited, weren't found steady.
Go to the highways, invite all you see, The bad and the good, let them all be free.'
The hall was filled, the guests gathered 'round, But one man stood, in the wrong garb found.
'Friend, how'd you enter, no wedding clothes on?' Speechless he stood, as the king said, 'Be gone!'
'Bind him and cast him, out where it's dark, Weeping and gnashing, where hope is stark.'
Many are called, but few are chosen, The Pharisees plotted, their hearts were frozen.
They sent disciples, with Herodians in tow, "Teacher, you're honest, tell us what you know.
Lawful to pay taxes, to Caesar, or not?" Jesus saw their trap, knew what they sought.
"Show me the coin," he asked with care, "Whose image is this?" They said, "Caesar's, fair."
"Give to Caesar what’s his, to God what’s divine." They marveled at his wisdom, left him, resigned.
Sadducees came, denying the rise, Spoke of seven brothers, a truth in disguise.
"Whose wife in the rise, if each had her hand?" Jesus replied, "You misunderstand.
In resurrection, no marriage ties, Like angels in heaven, no earthly guise.
God spoke of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob's living, He's God of the living, not of the dead, he's giving."
The crowd was amazed at what they'd heard, Pharisees gathered, planning their word.
A lawyer stepped up, testing his might, "Greatest commandment, which one is right?"
"Love the Lord with heart, soul, mind," Jesus said, "Love your neighbor, keep these two in your head.
All the law and prophets hang on these, Love is the greatest, the heart's own keys."
Jesus questioned, "The Christ's lineage, say? David's son or Lord, how do you portray?"
"The Lord said to my Lord, take the throne's seat, Until enemies fall, mere footstools at your feet.”
"If David calls him Lord, how's he his son?" Silence followed, no more questions to run.
Jesus spoke to the crowd, set the scene right, "The scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, uptight.
Do what they say, but not what they do, They lay heavy burdens, but don't help you.
Their works are for show, their garments wide, They love the honor, the best seats provide.
But don't call them 'Rabbi,' for one Teacher's true, One Father in heaven, and you're all crew.
The greatest will serve, the humbled will rise, The exalted brought low, that's no surprise.
"Woe to you, scribes, Pharisees, in disguise! You devour widows' homes, long prayers you devise.
You lock up heaven, won't let others in, Make converts twice the son of sin.
Blind guides swearing by gold, that's not the way, The temple's the greater, hear what I say.
You blind fools, don't you understand? The altar, the gift, don't miss the command.
Tithing mint and cumin, but justice you leave, Strain out the gnat, let the camel deceive.
Clean the cup's outside, but the inside's a mess, Whited tombs, beauty hides distress.
You build tombs for prophets your fathers slew, You claim you'd not join them, but that's not true.
Serpents and vipers, judgment's no game, Righteous blood's on you, from Abel to Zechariah's name.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, killers of the sent, How I longed to gather you, but you never bent.
Your house now desolate, till you proclaim, 'Blessed is He who comes in the Lord's name!'"
Jesus left the temple, the disciples in awe, Showed Him the buildings, He set them to jaw.
"You see these stones? They'll all fall down," Not one will stand, not in this town.
On Olives He sat, the questions came quick, "When's the end, Lord? What's the trick?"
"Be careful," He said, "many will claim, To be the Christ, using My name.
Wars and rumors, they'll come your way, But don't be troubled, it's not the last day.
Nations rise, kingdoms clash, Famines, plagues, the earth will thrash.
These are just the birth pains' start, They'll deliver you up, tear you apart.
Hated for My name, betrayed by friends, False prophets will rise, causing bends.
Iniquity grows, love turns cold, But endurance saves, the brave and bold.
The Kingdom's Good News will be declared, Then the end will come, be prepared.
"When you see the desolation, standing tall, Run to the mountains, don't stall.
Don't fetch your things, don't look back, Woe to the mothers, on this track.
Pray it's not winter, not Sabbath day, For great suffering is on the way.
"If days weren't shortened, none would survive, But for the chosen, hope will revive.
False Christs, prophets, they'll appear, But don't believe, keep your vision clear.
"As lightning flashes, east to west, So comes the Son, in glory dressed.
Sun will darken, moon won't shine, Stars will fall, heavens' decline.
Then the sign, the tribes will mourn, Son of Man, in clouds adorned.
With trumpets sound, angels will fly, Gather the chosen, from sky to sky.
"Learn from the fig, tender leaves show, Summer's near, soon to know.
This generation sees these things, My words stand, though heaven rings.
No one knows the hour, not even the skies, Only the Father, where mystery lies.
"As in Noah's days, unaware they played, Till floodwaters rose, and swept all away.
Two in the field, one will be gone, Grinding at the mill, one's move on.
"Watch, for you know not when, The Lord will come, be vigilant then.
If the master knew the thief's timing, He'd guard his home, no breaking, no climbing.
"Be ready, in an hour not seen, The Son will come, like a dream.
"Who's faithful, wise, serving the rest? Blessed is he, by the Lord, impressed.
Set over all, all possessions in hand, But beware the evil, who misunderstand.
Lord comes when least expected, in stealth, And for the wicked, there's loss of health.
Weeping and gnashing, is where they'll find, The place of hypocrites, left behind."
Ten lamps lit in the night, waiting for the groom, Five girls prepared, the others faced doom. Foolish with no oil, wise with a stash, When the groom was delayed, they all took a nap.
"Behold, he's coming!" the midnight cry rang, Virgins trimmed their lamps as the bridegroom's name sang. "Share your oil," the foolish ones plead, "Not enough for both," wise ones decreed.
Off to the shop, the unready ones fled, The groom arrived, the wise ones led. Locked out, the foolish cried, "Open, please!" But the groom replied, "I don't know you, cease."
Be alert, he warned, for the day you don't know, The Son of Man's coming, be ready to go.
A man gave talents, five, two, and one, To his servants, each by what could be done. The five made ten, the two made four, But the one hid his, fearing a score.
The master returned and praised the wise, "Well done, enter joy, with more to devise." The one who buried? "Wicked and slow, You knew my ways, yet nothing to show."
His talent was taken, given to the most, Thrown to darkness, where regrets engross. For those who have, abundance will grow, To those who lack, even less will they stow.
When the Son returns, his glory displayed, Nations gathered, a verdict conveyed. Sheep to the right, goats to the left, Blessed for kindness, others bereft.
"I was hungry, you gave food, Thirsty, you gave drink, you were good. A stranger welcomed, naked clothed, Sick and in prison, by your love enclosed."
"Lord, when did we see these things?" they ask, "When you served my brethren," he reveals the task. To the left, "You turned away, Now eternal fire, you'll repay."
"Lord, when did we see you and not care?" "When you ignored my brethren, I was there." The righteous enter life, the others, strife, With acts of love, they gain eternal life.
When all the words were said and done, Jesus spoke, "In two days, the Passover's begun. The Son of Man's delivered up, crucified He'll be." The priests and elders plotted secretly.
In Caiaphas' court, they hatched their plan, "Not during the feast, or riots will span." In Bethany, at Simon's humble place, A woman with ointment poured on His face.
Disciples cried, "Why waste what's dear?" "Help the poor," was their collective sneer. Jesus replied, "Why trouble her deed? She prepped my burial, in this she did heed."
"Her act will echo through time and space, A memorial forever, in every place." Judas then schemed, "What will you give me?" Thirty silver pieces, his treachery fee.
"Prepare Passover," the disciples desired, "In the city," Jesus' words inspired. They followed His lead, prepared the feast, In the evening, He reclined with His priests.
"One will betray," Jesus spoke true, Sorrowful, each asked, "Is it I, who?" "The one who dips his hand with mine," Judas asked, "Is it I?" Jesus' words shone like a sign.
Bread was broken, "Take, eat, it's my body," The cup was shared, "For sins, this is my offering." "I'll not drink again till Kingdom comes," He said, A hymn they sang, to Olives, they were led.
"Tonight you'll stumble, the shepherd struck," The flock will scatter, but hope's not stuck. Peter vowed, "I'll never fall," Jesus said, "Three denials before the rooster's call."
In Gethsemane, Jesus prayed alone, "Father, let this cup pass, but let Your will be known." Disciples slept, eyes too weary, "Watch, the spirit's keen, but the flesh is dreary."
Judas arrived with a multitude near, "Betray with a kiss, this is clear." "Friend, why come?" Jesus asked on, Taken by force, His followers gone.
A sword was drawn, an ear struck down, "Put it away, or you'll wear death's crown." "Could call angels, legions of might, But prophecy fulfills on this night."
"Why come with swords as if I'm a thief? I taught in temples, arrests would've been brief." Led to Caiaphas, Peter watched from afar, The council sought lies, but truth was bar.
"Destroy this temple," false words did claim, Asked by the priest, "Are you the same?" Jesus said, "You said it, now you'll see, The Son of Man in power, clouds high and free."
Tears of garments, "Blasphemy!" they cried, "Worthy of death," their anger didn't hide. Spit and fists, He was struck and mocked, "Prophesy, Christ!" their cruel words rocked.
Peter outside, denied with a lie, "Galilean, you're one," he denied with a sigh. Three times, the rooster crowed, Remembered Jesus' words, tears flowed.
Morning light, chief priests plot, taking counsel for the spot Against the man named Jesus, plotting death, so they thought.
Bound him up, took his fate to Pilate, the Roman state, Judas, filled with regret, tried to change his ill-set fate.
Thirty silver coins, he tossed them back, "I’ve sinned," he declared, Chief priests shrugged, "What's that to us?" No sympathy was spared.
Judas left, heart heavy, found a tree to end his strife, Priests, with silver in their hands, bought a field with price of life.
Potter's Field, Field of Blood, Jeremiah's words fulfill, Thirty coins for innocent blood, prophecy stood still.
Jesus stood before Pilate, "King of Jews?" he asked with doubt, "So you say," Jesus replied, silent with no shout.
Accused by many voices, yet not a single word he gave, Pilate marveled at his silence, how Jesus behaved.
Feast time custom, one prisoner released to the crowd, Barabbas or Jesus, Pilate's question was loud.
Priests stirred up the people, "Barabbas!" they all cried, Pilate questioned, "And Jesus?" "Crucify!" they replied.
Pilate washed his hands, "This blood's not on me, you see," "On us and our children," the crowd shouted in glee.
Barabbas freed, Jesus flogged, soldiers led him away, Mocked with thorns, and robe of scarlet, they made him their prey.
"King of the Jews," they taunted, as they knelt with cruel jest, Struck him, spat, and led him on, to crucify with the rest.
On the road, Simon of Cyrene, forced to bear the cross, To Golgotha, place of skulls, where life would meet its loss.
Sour wine and gall, he tasted, but he would not drink, Divided clothes, casting lots, beneath the cross they’d sink.
Accusation hung above, "This is Jesus, King of Jews," Two robbers on each side, shared the same damnable news.
Passersby mocked, priests joined in, "Save yourself, Son of God!" Darkness fell at noon, till ninth hour, creation seemed flawed.
Jesus cried aloud, "My God, why have you left me alone?" Some thought he called Elijah, but the truth was his own.
A sponge of vinegar raised up, "Let's see if help will come," With a loud cry, spirit gone, death's victory won.
Temple veil, from top to bottom, tore with earth's great quake, Tombs were opened, saints arose, as creation seemed to shake.
Centurion and guards looked on, "Truly God's Son," they feared, Women wept from afar, to Jesus their hearts adhered.
Joseph of Arimathea, disciple hidden, now bold, Asked for Jesus' body, in linen, gently rolled.
Placed him in a new tomb, sealed with a stone so round, Mary Magdalene watched on, hearts heavy, thoughts profound.
Next day, priests sought Pilate, "His words could deceive," "Seal the tomb, guard it well, lest disciples make believe."
Pilate granted them a guard, "Make it secure and tight," So they sealed the stone, keeping watch through the night.
Early dawn, the Mary's came to see, The tomb where Jesus was meant to be.
Earth shook, angel from the sky, Rolled the stone and perched up high.
Lightning flash, clothes white as snow, Guards fell like statues, fear on show.
To the women, the angel spoke, “Don’t fear, Jesus' bonds are broke.
He’s risen now, just as he said, Come and see where he once laid dead.
Go tell his friends, he’s up and gone, To Galilee, where he'll move on.”
With joy and fear, they ran fast, To share the news that came at last.
On their path, Jesus appeared, “Rejoice!” he said, as they drew near.
Held his feet in worship's might, “Don’t be afraid, share the light.
Tell my brothers, Galilee’s the place, Where they'll see me, face to face.”
Meanwhile, guards told tales untrue, Chiefs paid silver for their view.
“Say disciples stole him away, While we slept at night, they’ll say.”
The cash in hand, they spread the lie, The story lingers, never to die.
Disciples in Galilee, mountains high, Bow to Jesus, yet some question why.
“All power’s mine,” he declares aloud, “Heaven and earth, before this crowd.
Go, make disciples, nations wide, Baptize them in the Triune tide.
Teach them all I’ve shown and said, I’m with you till the ages spread.”
With that promise, the story ends, Jesus' words, where hope begins. Amen.
The Good News begins with Jesus Christ, the Son of God / Prophets foretold: “My messenger goes ahead, clears your road”
John preached repentance, baptism for forgiveness from sin / They confessed their sins as they were baptized by him
One mightier comes; I’m not worthy to stoop and loosen his shoe / He’ll baptize you with the Holy Spirit; that’s what he’ll do
John baptized Jesus; the Spirit came down like a dove / God’s voice said, “Beloved Son, in you I am pleased,” from above
The Spirit drove him out; Satan tempted him in the wild / Forty days he was tempted; angels served him all the while
After John was taken, Jesus said, “The Kingdom is near” / “Repent and believe the Good News; the time is here”
Galilee’s sea, Jesus called Simon, Andrew: “Come follow me” / “I’ll make you fishers for men”; they left their nets by the sea
James and John mended nets; their father Zebedee was there / They left him in the boat with hired hands, followed elsewhere
On Sabbath, Jesus entered Capernaum’s synagogue to teach / They marveled: his authority surpassed the scribes’ reach
“Nazarene, come to destroy us? I know: God’s Holy One!” he cried / Jesus rebuked him: “Be quiet; come out!”—the demon complied
They marveled: “New teaching! Spirits obey his command” / His report spread through Galilee and the surrounding land
Jesus took Simon’s fevered mother-in-law by the hand / He raised her; the fever left, and her service began
He healed many who were sick; he cast many demons out / Since they all knew him, he would not let them speak or shout
He went to a deserted place alone to pray / Simon and others found him: “Everyone seeks you today”
“Let’s go to the next towns; there I’ll preach the Good News” / “I came out for this reason,” he said to the crew
He preached Good News in synagogues throughout Galilee / And cast out demons through all of the land, so did he
A leper knelt before him, begging on one knee / “If you will, you can make me clean,” was his plea
Jesus touched him: “I want to. Be clean,” he did say / The leprosy left him at once, cleared away
“And tell no one, but go show yourself to the priest,” he said / “Offer Moses’ cleansing rites as witness to them,” he bade
That news spread; Jesus could no more openly enter a town / He stayed in desert places; people came from all around
Jesus came to Capernaum; the house filled up tight / He spoke the word; crowds packed it, no room left in sight
Four bore the paralytic, blocked at the door / They broke up the roof and lowered his mat to the floor
Jesus saw their faith, then spoke to the waiting man / “Son, your sins are forgiven you,” as he began
In their hearts the scribes asked, “Why does this man blaspheme here?” / “Who can forgive sins but God alone?”—their thought was clear
Jesus asked, “Why reason these things in your hearts?” / “Which is easier: ‘Forgiven,’ or ‘Rise, take your mat and walk?’”
The Son of Man has earthly authority to forgive / “Rise, take up your mat, and go home”—his command to him
He rose, took up his mat, and went before them all / They glorified God: “We’ve never seen this!” was their call
At the tax booth, Jesus told Levi, “Follow me,” in the street / Levi then arose and followed, leaving the tax seat
Scribes asked why he ate with tax men and sinners nearby / “The sick need doctors; sinners to repent,” was his reply
John’s disciples and Pharisees asked why they did not fast then / “Guests can’t fast with the bridegroom; when he’s taken, they’ll fast again”
Unshrunk cloth on old clothes makes the tear grow / New wine bursts old skins; in fresh skins they let it flow
The Pharisees asked why the disciples plucked grain then / David ate showbread and shared it with his own men
The Sabbath was made for man, not man for Sabbath’s sway / The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath, as he did say
He entered the synagogue; a man had a withered hand there, / The Pharisees watched his Sabbath healing, seeking to ensnare.
He asked, “On Sabbath, is good or harm lawful? Save a life or kill?” / He told him, “Stand up”; they gave no answer; they stood silent and still.
Grieved at their hard hearts, angry, he said, “Stretch out your hand.” / He stretched it; it matched the other, restored and sound.
Pharisees went out; with Herodians devised a scheme; / At once they plotted how to destroy him, their aim.
Jesus withdrew to the sea; disciples and crowds came near, / He said, “Keep a small boat close, so crowds don’t press here.”
He healed many who had sickness, more than a few; / All sick pressed close upon him, hoping to touch him too.
Unclean spirits fell before him, crying, “You are the Son!” / He sternly warned them, “Tell no one what has been done.”

He appointed twelve to be with him, preach, heal, cast demons away: / Simon Peter; James, John (Boanerges, Sons of Thunder); Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas; James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot; Judas Iscariot, who betrayed.
Again the crowd gathered; they couldn’t eat bread; / His friends went out to seize him: “He’s insane,” they said.
The scribes said, “He has Beelzebul,” and laid the blame; / “By the prince of demons he casts them out,” was their claim.
“Can Satan cast out Satan? A divided kingdom will fall; / A house divided cannot stand; Satan’s end comes with it all.”
“No one can plunder a strong man’s house and seize his prize, / Unless he binds the strong man first, then plunders his supplies.”
“All human sins and blasphemies may be forgiven, it’s true; / But blaspheming the Holy Spirit means eternal judgment too.”
His mother and brothers came and stood outside there; / They sent to him, calling him from where they were.
They said, “Your mother, brothers, sisters are outside, looking for you”; / He asked, “Who are my mother and brothers?” of those nearby.
He looked around: “My mother and brothers are here!” / Whoever does God’s will is my sister, brother, mother to me.
From his boat, Jesus taught the gathered crowd that day / A farmer sowed his seed, and told it in this way
Birds ate the roadside seed; sprouts on rock would wither and be gone / The thorns choked the seed; the good soil bore its harvest, full-grown
Alone, his followers and Twelve came with a question to ask / “How will you understand all?” Jesus questioned them back
God’s Kingdom’s mystery is now to them made known / Those outside hear all things in parables alone
The roadside seed is word that reaches hearers’ ears / Satan comes at once and takes it; it disappears
Rocky-ground hearers take the word with joy, but lack root / Oppression or persecution keeps them from bearing fruit
Life’s cares, riches’ deceit choke the word inside / Other desires can leave no fruit behind
Good soil hears and accepts the word; its fruit is there / Thirty, sixty, hundredfold is what they bear
A lamp is set upon a stand, not out of sight / What’s hidden or made secret will be brought to light
With whatever measure you use, it’s measured to you / More will be given to you who hear; this too is true
God’s Kingdom is like seed; the farmer goes to sleep / He rises; first blade, then ear, then full grain to reap
God’s Kingdom’s like the mustard seed, small as can be / Its great branches shade birds that lodge beneath the tree
Jesus taught the crowd in parables, truths concealed / In private to disciples, all was fully revealed
At evening Jesus said, “Let’s cross to the other side” / They left the crowd and took him; small boats came alongside
Fierce storm waves crashed in; the boat was filling fast / Jesus slept in the stern, upon the cushion, through the blast
They woke him as the storm waves were running high / “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?” their cry
He spoke to the sea, “Peace! Be still!”—the wind obeyed / The wind ceased; a great calm across the water spread
Jesus asked, “How is it you have no faith? Why so afraid?” / They asked, “Who then is this whom the wind and the sea obey?”
Jesus lands in Gadarenes, where tombs are found / A man with an unclean spirit meets him on that ground
Among the tombs, chains and fetters broke; none could restrain / Night and day he cried and cut himself with stones again
He runs and bows, cries, “Jesus, Son of the Most High God!” / “What have I to do with you? Don’t torment me!” he cried
“Come out,” Jesus commands, then asks the spirit its name / “My name is Legion, for we are many,” he explains
Legion begs Jesus, “Don’t send us out of this land” / The demons ask, “Send us to pigs”; he grants their demand
The spirits enter pigs; they rush down the steep incline / About two thousand plunge into the sea and drown in brine
The herders flee and report the tale of what took place that day / They find him clothed and sane, afraid, and beg him to go away
He begs to go; Jesus says, “Go home; tell what the Lord has done” / He tells of mercy, what Jesus did; all marvel, every one
He crosses back; the gathered crowd waits beside the sea / Jairus, synagogue ruler, falls at Jesus’ feet to plead
He begs, “My little daughter is dying; come, lay / Your hands on her, so she may live,” he then prays
She bled twelve years, then touched his robe there in the crowd / “If I just touch his clothes, I’ll be made well,” she vowed
Her flow of blood stops; within her body, healing’s found / Jesus asks who touched his clothes, and turns to look around
She falls before him, trembling, tells the truth of what she endured / “Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace, be cured”
Jairus’s house: “Why trouble him again? Your daughter’s dead” / “Don’t be afraid; only believe,” Jesus then said
He lets Peter, James, John alone follow him near / “The child is not dead, but asleep,” he says; they jeer
He puts them all out; her parents and three disciples stay inside / He enters the room where the girl lies, with them at her side
He takes her hand: “Girl, get up!”; she rises to her feet / He orders them, “Tell no one”; they bring her food to eat
At home on Sabbath, Jesus taught; his mighty works amazed / They asked what wisdom, what great works his hands had raised
“Carpenter, Mary’s son”; James, Joses, Judah, Simon named / “His sisters live among us,” then they took offense, dismayed
A prophet is not without honor, save in his native land / Among his kin and in his house, no honor will he command
He healed a few sick there, and marveled at their doubt / He taught in the villages all along his route
The Twelve went out in pairs, with spirits to obey their call / Take staff and sandals; no bread, purse, coin, or spare clothes at all
Stay in one house till you depart; if none receive, shake dust down / Sodom and Gomorrah fare better when judgment comes round
They preached that people should repent, cast many demons out / They anointed many sick with oil and healed them, no doubt
Herod heard of Jesus: “John the Baptizer’s risen from the dead; / Therefore these powers are at work in him,” Herod said
Some said Elijah, others prophet; rumors quickly spread / “John, I beheaded, has risen from the dead,” Herod declared
Herod jailed John for Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife / John said, “Your brother’s wife is not yours to take by right”
Herodias sought John’s death, but couldn’t get her way / Herod feared John, righteous, holy; kept him safe, heard him gladly say
At Herod’s birthday supper, her dance pleased king and guests / He swore to give whatever she asked, half his kingdom at most
She asked her mother, “What request should I make?” / “John the Baptizer’s head,” her mother told her to take
At once she asked for John’s head, on a platter, to display / Though deeply grieved, for oaths and guests, he would not turn away
A guard beheaded John in prison, brought his head on a tray / He gave it to the girl, who gave her mother without delay
John’s disciples took his body, in a tomb it was laid / Apostles gathered to Jesus, their work and lessons conveyed
He said, “Come apart and rest awhile,” in a deserted place / The people saw them going, knew him, ran ahead to meet his face
He saw them like sheep without a shepherd, moved with care / He began to teach them many things while they gathered there
They urged, “Send them to buy food”; “You feed them,” he replied / Five loaves and two fish were all they could provide
He had them sit in groups, blessed loaves and broke the bread / He gave them to his disciples; they served as Jesus led
All ate and were filled; twelve baskets held what was left / Five thousand men ate loaves, and all were fully fed
He sent them by boat ahead, then sent the crowd away / He climbed the mountain by himself to pray
He saw them all as they fought the wind upon the sea / He walked upon the sea; they thought a ghost was what they’d see
“Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid!” He boarded; the wind ceased / At Gennesaret, sick were brought; all touching his fringe were healed
The scribes and Pharisees saw them eat with unwashed hands / They washed hands and forearms, as tradition commands
Their lips praised God, but their hearts had turned away / Isaiah said their worship was vain; man’s rules were their way
They set God’s commandment firmly to the side / And held to human customs, keeping them as their guide
Moses said, “Honor your parents,” show them care / They called it Corban, and their parents got no share
Nothing from outside defiles the one who takes it in / What comes out of a person makes them unclean
In the house, disciples asked what the parable showed / He then asked if they too lacked the sense to know
Food enters the stomach, not the human heart / Then passes out, making all foods clean as they depart
Sex sins, thefts, murders, and evil thoughts defile / Coveting, deceit, and pride can leave hearts vile
A Greek Syrophoenician woman came and made her plea / Her little girl had an unclean spirit; set her free
He told her, “Let the children first be filled with bread” / “It isn’t right to take their bread and cast it to dogs instead”
She answered, “Yes, Lord,” and the dogs too are fed / Beneath the table, dogs eat crumbs the children shed
He told her, “For what you said, the demon has fled” / She went home and found her child laid upon the bed
They brought a deaf man whose speech was hard to understand / They begged him to lay his hand upon the man
He took him aside, put fingers in his ears, looked to the sky / He spat, touched his tongue, sighed, “Be opened!” he cried
His ears opened, and his speech now came through clear / And he spoke distinctly, his words were clear to hear
He told them, “Tell no one,” and let it be concealed / But they proclaimed it widely, the news was revealed
They marveled, “He has done all things well,” said aloud / “He makes the deaf hear, and the mute speak,” to the crowd
Three days they’d stayed with him, with no food left to share / He felt compassion for the crowd, their hunger laid bare
“Where could we find bread here in this deserted land?” / He asked, “How many loaves?” “Seven,” they had on hand
He gave thanks, broke seven loaves, then shared out the bread / His followers served bread and fish; the crowd was fed
Four thousand were filled; seven baskets were found / Then he sent the multitude away from that ground
Pharisees tested him, seeking a sign from the sky / He sighed, “No sign for this generation,” he replied
One loaf; he warned of yeast from Herod and Pharisees, the gist / They thought he meant no bread; the warning they had missed
Five thousand: twelve baskets; four thousand: seven—that’s the count / “Don’t you understand yet?” he asked, spelling it out
They brought a blind man; he led him out and touched his eyes / He said, “I see men like trees walking,” the blind man replies
Again he laid his hands; the man could see all clear / “Don’t enter the village or tell anyone there”
“Who do people say I am?” Jesus asked on the way / “John the Baptizer, Elijah, or a prophet,” they say
He asked who they said he was; Peter said, “You are the Christ” / He told them, “Tell no one”; keep that secret out of sight
The Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, then die / After three days he would rise and death defy
Peter rebuked him; Jesus turned, saw his disciples too / “Get behind me, Satan! Your thoughts are of men, not God’s view”
Jesus called the crowd and disciples; he gave them the decree / “Deny yourselves, take up your cross, and then follow me”
Whoever saves their life, Jesus said, will lose it instead / Whoever loses it for him and Good News will save it
What profit to gain the whole world, if your life is lost? / What could a man give to exchange for his life? What’s the cost?
He’ll be ashamed of those ashamed of his words and him / When he comes in his Father’s glory, holy angels with him
Some here won’t taste death till God’s Kingdom comes with power / He said some standing there would see it before death’s hour
Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John uphill / They climbed a high mountain, privately, apart and still
Before their eyes, Jesus was changed to another form / His clothes grew glistening white, like snow, beyond earth’s norm
Moses and Elijah spoke with Jesus standing near / They appeared before the three, and talked with Jesus there
Peter said, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here” / “Three tents, one each for you, Moses, Elijah, to appear”
A cloud came over: “This is my beloved Son,” the voice said / “Listen to him”; they looked around and saw Jesus instead
He said, “Tell no one till the Son of Man has risen from the dead” / They wondered what “rising” meant, and kept the saying in their head
They asked why scribes say Elijah must come first, set things right / Son must suffer, despised; Elijah came, they did as they liked
Jesus came; the crowd ran to greet him, amazed to see / Scribes questioned them; the father said, “They could not set him free”
Since childhood, fire and water often tried to take his life / “If you can help, have compassion”; Jesus said, “Bring him to me”
Jesus said, “All things are possible for those who believe” / The father cried, “I believe; help my unbelief!”
He told the deaf and mute spirit, “Leave; never enter him again” / Then took the boy by the hand and raised him from where he’d been
In private, they asked why they could not cast it out / He said, “This kind comes out by prayer and fasting,” without doubt
The Son of Man, handed over, killed, will rise on the third day / They did not understand the saying, and feared to ask him why
They argued who among them was greatest on the way / Jesus said, “First must be last, servant of all,” he said
He held a child: “Whoever receives such a child in my name / Receives me—not me alone, but the One who sent me, the same”
John said, “We stopped one casting demons in your name, not our way” / Jesus said, “Don’t you forbid him; he’s on our side,” he’d say
Who gives a cup in my name, since you’re Christ’s, I say / He will never lose his reward, not in any way
Better a millstone round your neck, then into the sea you tumble / Than make one of these little ones who believe in me stumble
Cut hand, foot, eye that makes you stumble; cast them away / Better enter life maimed than Gehenna; worms don’t die, flames stay
All will be salted with fire, as the teaching said / Each sacrifice is seasoned with salt, as the word read
Salt is good; if salt loses its taste, what will season it then? / Have salt within; be at peace with one another again.
Jesus taught the crowds; Pharisees came testing him aloud / “May a man divorce his wife?” they asked, “Is that allowed?”
He asked what Moses commanded—what rule was applied / “Moses allowed a certificate for divorce,” they replied.
God made them male and female; the two become one / No one should separate what God joined, nor undo what’s done.
He taught: whoever divorces his wife and takes a new mate / Commits adultery against her; that’s what Jesus states.
If a woman divorces her husband and marries once more / She commits adultery, as Jesus taught before.
The Twelve rebuked those bringing children to his side / “Let children come; God’s Kingdom belongs to them,” he replied.
Receive God’s Kingdom like a child; without that, none come in / He took them in his arms, laid hands on them, and blessed them then.
A man knelt: “Good Teacher, how do I gain eternal life?” / “No one is good except God,” Jesus said in reply.
Jesus named the commandments, each one he conveyed / The man said, “From my youth I’ve kept them and obeyed.”
Jesus loved him: “Sell what you own, give to the poor” / “Take up the cross and follow me; leave wealth at the door.”
He went away sorrowful, for possessions made him rich / Jesus said the rich find God’s Kingdom difficult to reach.
A camel through a needle’s eye is easier to get through / Than rich men entering God’s Kingdom; what people can’t, God can do.
Peter said, “We left all”; for his sake and Good News they leave / A hundredfold now, with persecutions, eternal life receive.
Many who are first will be last; the last will be first / To Jerusalem they went; Jesus walked ahead.
The chief priests and scribes condemn the Son of Man to die / They hand him to Gentiles, mock, spit, scourge, kill; third day he’ll rise.
“Grant us seats at your right and left,” the brothers said / “In your glory,” they asked, as their request was made.
“You’ll share my cup and baptism; that fate is sure” / “But seats are prepared; they’re not mine to confer.”
The ten grew indignant; rulers lord it over men / Jesus said, “Not so among you; don’t rule as they’ve been.”
Whoever would be great must serve; whoever is first, servant of all / Son of Man came, served, gave life as ransom for many—that’s the call.
Bartimaeus cried, “Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me!” / They rebuked him; louder he cried, repeating his plea.
Jesus stood still, said, “Call him!” They called him near / “Cheer up! Get up! He’s calling you!”—they made it clear.
He cast his cloak aside, sprang up, and came to Jesus’s side / Jesus asked; “Rabboni, let me see,” he said, healed, followed his guide.
Near Jerusalem, two seek a colt, tied and unridden there / They say, “The Lord needs him”; and he’ll send the colt back here
They find the donkey tied outside; they answer those who ask / They bring the young donkey to Jesus, completing the task
They lay their cloaks upon the colt; Jesus takes his seat / The crowd spreads clothes and branches all along the street
Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the Lord’s name / Blessed is our father David’s kingdom, coming in the Lord’s name
Jesus then enters the temple, looks around / At evening, he and the twelve leave, Bethany-bound
Hungry next day, he sees a leafy fig tree and seeks fruit there / “May no one ever eat fruit from you again!” he declares
He drives out buyers and sellers; money-changers’ tables fall / He topples dove-sellers’ seats, bars vessels through the hall
He says, “My house for all nations shall be called a house of prayer” / “But you have made this house into the robbers’ own lair!”
The chief priests and scribes sought how to destroy him; they feared / The multitude was astonished at his teaching, words they heard
At morning, they see the fig tree withered from its roots down / Peter says, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree you cursed withered now!”
Have faith in God, and let no doubt now in your heart sway / Tell this mountain, ‘Cast to the sea!’—believe it’s underway
“All things you pray and ask for, believe you have received” / “And then you shall have them, as you have believed”
“Whenever you stand and pray, forgive anyone you resent” / “Your Father won’t forgive transgressions if forgiveness you prevent”
The priests, scribes, elders ask, “Who gave you authority then?” / Jesus then asks, “John’s baptism—from heaven or from men?”
They feared all held John for a prophet; answered, “We don’t know” / Jesus says, “Then I won’t tell you by what right I do so”
He planted, fenced it, dug the press, built a tower, rented it there / Then he went abroad; in time he sent a servant for his share
The farmers seized the servant, beat him, sent him away / Empty-handed, they turned him from the vineyard that day
They stoned the next, wounded his head, sent him away / One more they killed; many more were beaten or slain that day
He sent his cherished son, whom he loved, to meet them there / He thought that they would respect the owner's son and heir
They said, “This is the heir; let’s kill him, claim the vineyard land” / They killed him, cast him out, as they had planned
The owner will destroy tenants, give vines to other hands / The Lord made the rejected stone the cornerstone that stands
They knew the parable charged them, tried to seize him in haste / But fearing all the crowd, they turned and left the place
Pharisees and Herodians came to set a snare / “Is paying Caesar’s tax lawful?” they asked with feigned care
He called them hypocrites, asked for the denarius coin / Its image and inscription showed that it was Caesar’s own
Give Caesar what is Caesar’s; give God what belongs to God / They marveled greatly at his words, struck with awe
The Sadducees denied the rise, then asked about a wife / Seven brothers wed her, each died; whose wife when raised to life?
“You err: you know no Scriptures, nor God’s power and might / At rising, none wed, nor are wed; like angels in heaven’s light”
God is God of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, living, not dead / “You are badly mistaken,” Jesus then said to them
A scribe heard how he answered well, then came to say / “Which commandment is greatest?” he asked that day
The Lord is one; with heart, soul, mind, and strength, love God alone / “Love your neighbor as yourself; let equal care be shown”
The scribe said love outweighs burnt offerings and rites / Jesus said, “You’re not far from God’s Kingdom”; that’s right
“How can the Christ be David’s son, when David calls him Lord?” / By the Spirit David said, “Sit at my right hand”; crowd heard his word
He warned: scribes love long robes, greetings, best seats in the place / They devour widows’ homes, make long prayers; greater judgment they face
A poor widow gave two small brass coins into the treasury / Many rich cast in much; they gave abundantly
He said her gift surpassed them all; poor, all she had to live on / They gave from abundance; she gave all she had to live on
A disciple said, “See temple stones and buildings grand” / Jesus said no stone atop another here would stand
Peter, James, John, Andrew asked him, “When will this be? / What sign will show these things fulfilled, what should we see?”
Jesus warned, “Take care no one leads you astray” / Many come in his name, “I am he,” and lead crowds away
Wars and rumors: don’t be troubled; these must happen in their time / Nations clash; quakes, famines, troubles—birth pains, not the end’s sign
They will face councils and synagogue blows for Jesus’ name / Before rulers and kings, they speak; Good News preached to all nations
When they hand you over, don’t plan what you will say / The Holy Spirit, not you, speaks; the words come that day
Brother hands brother to death; children rise against kin / All hate you for my name; endure to the end, be saved then
Desolation stands where it shouldn’t; Judea flee to mountains / Go to the mountains; don’t turn back for goods you might retrieve
Had the Lord not shortened those days, no flesh could survive / For sake of the chosen ones, he shortened that span
Don’t trust these claims, “The Christ is here,” or, “Look, he’s there” / False christs and prophets show signs and wonders to ensnare
After distress, the sun is dark; the moon gives no light / Stars fall; heaven’s powers are shaken from their height
The Son of Man comes in clouds with great power and might / His angels gather chosen from earth’s ends and heaven’s height
A fig tree’s leaves emerge; summer signs appear / When you see these things come to pass, the hour draws near
This generation won’t pass till all these things occur / Heaven and earth will pass; my words will endure
That day and hour are known to the Father alone / Not angels in heaven, nor Son; to them it’s unknown
A man travels abroad, and he grants each servant a chore / And gives them authority, and tells the doorkeeper, “Watch the door”
No one knows: evening, midnight, cockcrow, or dawn when he’ll come / Stay alert, pray, watch, lest asleep he finds you at home
Two days before Passover, priests and scribes plotted to kill / By trickery, not during feast; they feared crowds might riot still
At Simon the leper’s house, she broke the alabaster jar / Pure costly nard she poured on Jesus’ head right there
They cried, “Sell it for the poor!” Christ said, “Leave her alone” / “She anointed me for burial; her memorial will be known”
Judas, one of the Twelve, went to chief priests to betray / They promised him money; he sought a time and way
They asked where to prepare; he sent two into the street / “Follow the man with water; ask the host for our room, where we’ll eat”
They found it as he said, prepared the feast with care / At evening Jesus came with twelve, and sat to share
One sharing bread will betray me; they asked, “Am I the one?” / “One of the Twelve dips with me; better he’d never been born”
He blessed and broke the bread: “Take, eat; this is my body,” he said / He gave the cup: “New covenant blood for many will be shed”
He said, “No fruit of the vine shall I drink until that day” / “In God’s Kingdom I’ll drink it anew,” he did say
After the hymn, on Olives, “You’ll stumble because of me” / “Shepherd struck, sheep scattered; raised, I go ahead to Galilee”
Peter said, “Though all are offended, I will not fall away” / “Before the rooster crows twice, thrice you’ll deny,” Christ did say
At Gethsemane he took Peter, James, John to pray / “My soul is sad to death; stay here and watch,” he said
He fell: “Abba, Father, all things are possible by your power” / “Please remove this cup; not my desire, but yours, in this hour”
He found them sleeping: “Watch and pray; the spirit willing, the flesh weak” / He went away and prayed again, repeating the same words afresh
Found them sleeping again; the third time he returned / “Hour has come; into sinners’ hands the Son of Man is turned”
Judas came with an armed crowd; his sign was a kiss / “He said, ‘Rabbi! Rabbi!’; they seized the one he kissed”
One cut the servant’s ear; Christ asked, “As robber, why this display?” / “I taught daily in temple; Scripture fulfilled”—they fled away
They led him to the high priest; false witnesses made a claim / “I’ll tear this temple down, rebuild in three days”; claims weren’t the same
The high priest asked him to answer; Christ held his tongue / Then asked, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”
He answered, “I am; the Son of Man you’ll see on high, / At Power’s right hand, coming with clouds across the sky.”
The high priest cried blasphemy; they condemned him to die / They spat, struck, and mocked, “Prophesy!” as blows flew by
A maid said, “You were with Jesus, the Nazarene”; Peter denied / “I neither know nor understand”; he went out on porch; rooster cried
The maid said, “He is one of them”; Peter denied again / “You’re Galilean; your speech betrays you,” said the men
He cursed and swore, “I don’t know this man of whom you speak” / Rooster crowed twice; he recalled Christ’s warning, began to weep
At morning, priests, elders, scribes, the council bound him fast / Then carried him to Pilate, delivered him at last
Then Pilate asked, “Are you the King of the Jews?” / Jesus answered, “So you say,” his words were few
Chief priests accused him with charges piled up high / Pilate asked again; Jesus gave no reply
At feast, one prisoner could go free, as custom held / Barabbas, bound with insurgents who in revolt had killed
The crowd called for the custom, their voices raised aloud / Pilate asked, “Shall I release the Jews’ King to this crowd?”
The chief priests stirred the crowd to ask for Barabbas instead / Envy was why they had delivered Jesus, the text said
Pilate asked what to do with the man they called their King / The crowd cried, “Crucify him!” their cries began to ring
Pilate freed Barabbas, flogged Jesus, then complied / He handed Jesus over to be crucified
They clothed him in purple, thorns pressed upon his brow / They hailed him King, struck, spat, and knelt in mock bow
They led him out to crucify, compelled Simon to bear / Cyrene’s Simon carried his cross; no choice was there
At Golgotha they offered myrrh-mixed wine to taste / Jesus refused the drink, left untouched in place
They crucified him; lots divided all his clothes / Above the cross, “THE KING OF THE JEWS” in letters rose
Passersby mocked, “You destroy the temple; come down to the ground!” / “Save yourself from the cross!” their taunts rang out loudly all around
Priests mocked, “He saved others; himself he can’t save. / Let Israel’s King come down, and faith in him we’ll have.”
Darkness covered all the land; it held for hours three / Jesus cried, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
Some who stood by said, “He calls Elijah!” when they heard his sound / A man offered vinegar: “Wait; see if he brings him down.”
Jesus cried aloud, then breathed his last and died / The temple veil tore from top to bottom, split open wide
The centurion saw him cry and breathe his final breath / He said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!” at death
Mary Magdalene and other women watched afar to see / They’d followed him and served him through the days in Galilee
Joseph of Arimathaea boldly asked for Jesus’ remains / Pilate checked with the centurion, then granted his claim
Joseph wrapped Jesus in linen and laid him in the tomb / Mary Magdalene and Mary saw where he was entombed
After Sabbath passed, they bought spices to anoint him / Mary Magdalene, James’s mother, Salome bought them
The stone rolled back; they entered, saw a young man seated there / He said, “The crucified Nazarene has risen; he’s not here.”
“Tell Peter and the disciples: he goes before you there” / “In Galilee you’ll see him, as he said”; they fled in fear
Jesus first appeared to Mary, whom he’d from seven demons freed / She told her mourning friends; her witness they all disbelieved
Two walking in the country saw him in another form / They told the rest; the others disbelieved, as before
At table, Jesus rebuked the eleven for their doubt / Their hard hearts disbelieved the witnesses’ account.
“Go and preach the Good News to all the world, to all creation” / “Baptized believers saved; disbelievers face condemnation.”
After speaking, the Lord was received up on high / He sat down at God’s right hand, enthroned at his side.
They went out, preached everywhere; the Lord worked with them there / He confirmed the word by signs that followed everywhere.
Yo, listen up, I'm setting the scene, A story of truth, things unseen. The days of Herod, king on the throne, A priest named Zacharias, not alone.
His wife Elizabeth, pure and true, Righteous folks, they followed every clue. But no child came, they were old and gray, Yet Zacharias served, come what may.
In the temple, incense he burned, Prayers outside, the people yearned. An angel appeared, the priest's heart raced, "Don't fear," said Gabriel, "your prayers are embraced.
Elizabeth will bear you a son, Call him John, his work's just begun. Many will find joy, he'll be great, In the Spirit's power, he'll create.
He'll prep the way, turn hearts to Him, Make the path straight, no longer dim." Zacharias asked, "How can this be? We're too old, you see?"
Gabriel replied, "I stand with the Divine, You'll be silent, but watch Him shine." The crowd outside waited, time ticked away, He came out mute, had nothing to say.
Elizabeth conceived, she hid in grace, "God's blessed me, removed disgrace." Then Gabriel visited a girl named Mary, "Rejoice, you're blessed, don't be wary.
A son you'll bear, name him Jesus, His reign forever, no one to seize us." Mary asked, "How can this be real?" "The Spirit's power, that's the deal."
Mary visited Elizabeth, joy leaped inside, "Blessed are you," Elizabeth cried. Mary sang praises, her soul magnified, Generations blessed, with God she allied.
Elizabeth gave birth, joy spread around, On the eighth day, a name was found. "Not Zacharias, his name's John!" The people marveled, the silence gone.
Zacharias praised, Spirit-filled he spoke, "Blessed is the Lord," the silence broke. John grew strong, wild and free, Preparing the way for what's to be.
The story unfolds, prophecies told, God's hand in action, witness it unfold.
A decree from Caesar, the empire's call, "Go to your hometown, get enrolled, one and all."
Joseph left Nazareth, to Bethlehem he went, With Mary, soon to be wed, her time was spent.
In the town, no room, just a stable to stay, She gave birth to a son, wrapped him, laid him on hay.
Shepherds in the field, watching flocks by night, An angel appeared, filling them with fright.
"Fear not," he said, "I've news of joy today, A Savior born in David's town, laid in the hay."
Suddenly, a chorus, angels filled the sky, "Praise to God on high, peace to men nearby."
Shepherds hurried to see, and what did they find? Mary, Joseph, and the babe, God's promise unlined.
They spread the word, amazed all who heard, Mary pondered deeply, every spoken word.
Shepherds returned, hearts full of praise, For all they had seen, in those wondrous days.
Baby's eighth day, time for his name, Called Jesus, as angel proclaimed.
To Jerusalem they went, to fulfill the law, Offering turtledoves, in reverent awe.
Simeon in the temple, righteous and devout, "Lord, I've seen salvation!" he began to shout.
A light for the nations, glory for Israel, Joseph and Mary marveled at what he'd tell.
Simeon blessed them, spoke to Mary with care, "This child's a sign, piercing hearts laid bare."

A builder plans, before the tower's raised, A king counts his troops, his strength appraised.
"Renounce what you have, if you follow my call, If salt loses taste, it’s no good at all."
"Listen well, if you have ears," he spoke clear and loud, For those who seek truth, stand out from the crowd.
Tax collectors and sinners drew near, Pharisees shocked, their disapproval clear. "This man welcomes and dines with such folk!" Through a parable, the Teacher spoke:
"If you had a hundred sheep, one lost its way, Would you not leave ninety-nine, come what may? In the wild you'd search, seek until it's found, And when you find it, joy would abound.
You'd hoist it high, shoulders strong, Call your friends, celebrate with song. 'Rejoice with me, my lost sheep's here!' In heaven, one repentant brings more cheer.
Or a woman with ten coins so bright, Loses one, she searches day and night. Lamp in hand, she sweeps, digs around, And when she finds it, joy resounds.
She calls her friends, 'Come, let's rejoice! The lost coin's found, hear my voice!' So too, angels sing from above, When one sinner returns to love."
Then He told of a father, two sons had he, The younger asked for his inheritance free. He left for a distant land, wild and free, Spent it all in reckless spree.
A famine hit, his pockets dry, Fed pigs, while his stomach cried. "I'll return to my father's place, And ask to be a servant in disgrace."
Returning home, father saw him near, Ran with love, wiped away his fear. "Father, I've sinned, let me serve," he said, But his father hugged him, joy widespread.
"Bring the best robe, dress him fine, Put a ring on his hand, sandals aligned. Slay the calf, let's feast and sing, My son was lost, but now he's living."
The elder son heard music, curious sound, Asked the servant what joy he'd found. "Your brother's back, safe and sound," Anger flared, his joy unbound.
"Father, I've served, never gone astray, Yet no feast for me, no special day. But for him, who squandered, you celebrate?" The father spoke clear, no room for hate:
"Son, you're with me, all I have is yours, But joy for the lost who find the doors. Your brother was dead, now alive, see, Lost and found, let love be free."
There was a rich man, had a manager's scheme, Accusations flew, said he wasted the dream.
Rich man called him, "What’s this I hear? Give me your account, your end is near."
Manager thought, "What will I do, Too weak to dig, beggin' ain't my groove."
"I know the plan, I'll make my move, So when I'm out, they’ll give me a room."
Called up debtors, one by one, "How much you owe? Let's get it done."
"A hundred batos," the first one said, "Cut it to fifty, clear your head."
Next owes wheat, "A hundred's your share, Take it to eighty, let's make it fair."
Rich man nodded, "You played it wise, In this world, that's no surprise."
"Use what you got, make friends fast, When wealth is gone, friendships last."
Faithful in little, faithful in all, Dishonest in small, you'll surely fall.
If you can't be trusted with wealth that's wrong, How will you handle true riches long?
Serve two masters? Can't be done, You’ll love one and hate the other one."
Pharisees laughed, lovers of wealth, But God sees hearts, riches don't stealth.
Law and prophets 'til John came through, Now kingdom news breaks like morning dew.
Heaven and earth may fade away, But the law's strokes are here to stay.
Divorce and marriage rules stand tight, Against them, there's no easy flight.
Rich man in fine linen, all dressed to the nines, Lived each day in luxury, sippin' on wines.
Lazarus begged, sores on the ground, Dogs licked his wounds, crumbs not found.
Beggar died, angels carried him high, Rich man buried, down he did lie.
In Hades, he looked, saw Abraham's light, Lazarus comforted, rich in plight.
"Father Abraham, mercy, I plead, Send Lazarus, my tongue in need."
"Son," said Abraham, "remember your life, You had it all, now he's free from strife."
A gulf between us, too wide to span, None cross over, not even one man."
"Send him to my family, five brothers at home, Warn them of torment, before they're alone."
"They have the prophets, Moses to read, Let them listen and take heed."
"If the dead rise, they'll change, I assure," But Abraham said, "They won't be secure."
If they won't hear the words that were said, Not even a risen man will turn their head.
"Stumbles will come, they can't be undone, But woe to the one who makes others run. A millstone around the neck, a deep blue sea, Better than causing little ones to flee."
"Be careful, if your brother sins, call him out, If he repents, forgive, let there be no doubt. Seven times a day, he might fall and rise, But forgive him each time, that's wise."
"Increase our faith!" the apostles plead, The Lord said, "Faith a mustard seed can lead. Tell a tree, 'Move to the sea,' it'd obey, Faith small as this can sway."
"Servants work hard, plow and keep sheep, Do they sit first? No, they duties keep. Prepare the meal, serve first, then dine, They're unworthy servants, doing the line."
On his way to Jerusalem, borders he crossed, Samaria and Galilee, where paths were tossed. Ten lepers cried out, "Master, have grace!" "Show the priests," he said, their illness effaced.
One turned back, praised with loud voice, At Jesus' feet, he made a choice. Jesus asked, "Were ten healed, but where's the nine? Only this foreigner returns, divine."
"Get up, go your way, your faith made you well," The Kingdom within you, no one can tell. Not here, not there, it's inside, In your heart, where faith resides."
"The days will come, you’ll long to see, The Son of Man, but it won't be. Don't chase the signs, when they say, 'Look here!' Like lightning, he'll appear, clear."
"As in Noah’s day, they ate, they wed, Till the flood came down, and all were dead. In Lot's time, fire rained from the sky, Destroyed them all, just by and by."
"When He's revealed, don't look back, Remember Lot’s wife, stay on track. Save your life, you lose it, that's the deal, Lose it, and true life you'll reveal."
"Two in bed, one taken, one left alone, Two grinding grain, one gone, one on their own." "Where, Lord?" they asked, longing to see, "Where the body's found, that's where the vultures will be."

In a city lived a judge, no fear of God, no respect for man, A widow pleaded, "Defend me, do what you can!" For a while he ignored, but she wore him down, "She's bothering me, I'll help her before I drown." The Lord said, "Hear that judge's voice, Won't God avenge His own who cry and rejoice?"

Two men to the temple, a Pharisee and a taxman, Pharisee stood tall, feeling like the righteous man, "Thank God I'm not like others, unrighteous or wild, I fast and give tithes, I'm not defiled." But the taxman, from a distance, beat his chest, "God, have mercy on me, a sinner at best." "This man went home justified," Jesus declared, "Humble yourself, and God will be there."

Babies were brought for a gentle touch, Disciples rebuked, but Jesus didn't mind much, "Let the children come, don't block their way, God's Kingdom's like them," He'd say. "Good Teacher," a ruler asked, looking for the light, "What must I do to inherit eternal life?" "Why call me good?" Jesus replied, "Keep commandments, let them be your guide."

"I've done this since youth," he claimed without shame, "One thing you lack," from Jesus it came. "Sell all you have, give to the poor, Treasure in heaven, that's the core." The ruler was sad, he loved his wealth, Jesus spoke of camels and the needle's stealth. "Who then can be saved?" the crowd began, "With God, all things are possible," was the plan.

Peter said, "We've given all to follow you," Jesus promised blessings, eternal life too. To the twelve, He spoke of Jerusalem's fate, Prophets' words would soon take shape. Delivered, mocked, killed, then rise again, They couldn't grasp it, the hidden plane.

Near Jericho, a blind man by the road, Heard the crowd, in Jesus' name he sowed. "Son of David, have mercy on me!" Though rebuked, he shouted his plea. Jesus asked, "What do you want me to do?" "Lord, let me see, make my world anew." "Receive your sight, your faith's set you free," He followed, glorifying God, for all to see.
He rolled into Jericho, crowd thick as a wall, Zacchaeus was short, but he wanted to see it all.
Chief tax guy, rich, up in a tree he'd race, "Zacchaeus, come down, I'm coming to your place."
He climbed down quick, joy lighting up his face, But folks grumbled, "With a sinner, He gives grace."
Zacchaeus stood up, pledged to make it right, "Half to the poor, I'll restore all I took by night."
Jesus smiled, said, "Salvation's come today, Son of Abraham, the lost I came to save."
Onward He moved, a parable He'd tell, "About a nobleman, hear me well.
He handed coins, told his servants, 'Trade till I return,' But folks didn't want him, their disdain would burn.
He came back king, called servants near, Asked, 'What'd you do while I was not here?'
First servant said, 'Ten more I've gained,' 'Well done, ten cities you shall claim.'
The next said, 'Five more for your purse,' 'Rule five cities, your rewards diverse.'
One hid the coin, fear in his eyes, 'Judge me not, for your ways I despise.'
The nobleman replied, 'Why not invest? Take his coin, give to the best.'
To those who have, more shall be given, For those without, even that's riven."
He moved toward Jerusalem, disciples by his side, Sent for a colt, on it He would ride.
"If asked why you untie, say, 'The Lord's in need,'" Colt came, clothes laid, He'd proceed.
Joyful shouts, cloaks on the road they spread, "Blessed is the King," their praises led.
Pharisees fretted, "Teacher, hush this noise," "If silent, stones would sing," He voiced.
He saw the city, sorrow in His eyes, "If you'd known peace, it wouldn't be disguised.
Enemies will close in, not a stone left alone, For missing the moment, peace overthrown."
He cleared the temple, buyers and sellers scattered, "'House of prayer,' not robbers' den," His voice mattered.
Teaching daily, His words they'd savor, But the leaders sought to end His favor.
Yet the crowd clung tight, to every word He spoke, In the temple, wisdom awoke.
In the temple teachin', preachin' that Good News, Priests and scribes approached, lookin' for clues.
"By what power do you act? Who gave the okay?" Jesus flipped it back, "I got a question today.
John's baptism, was it heaven's design? Or was it just man's, like a grape on the vine?"
They huddled and whispered, caught in a bind, "If we say heaven, he'll ask why we're blind.
But call it man's, and the crowd will stone, For they see John as prophet, a truth well-known."
So they shrugged, "We can't say where it's from," Jesus replied, "Then my answer's none."
He spun a tale, to the crowd he began, "A vineyard owner rented land to some men.
He sent a servant for a share of the grape, But they beat him down, and let him escape.
Another was beaten, treated with shame, The third, tossed out, more of the same.
The lord of the vineyard thought, ‘What's my move? I'll send my son; they'll respect his groove.’
The tenants saw the heir, and plotted with glee, 'Let's kill him now, and the vineyard's free.'
They cast him out and took his life, What will the lord do with this strife?
He'll destroy those tenants, give the land away," The crowd gasped, "May it never be that day!"
Jesus looked, said, "Read the words you reject, ‘The stone rejected, the cornerstone perfect.’
Fall on this stone, you're shattered, not whole, If it falls on you, it'll crush your soul."
The priests and scribes plotted, fear in their eyes, Afraid of the people, they sent out spies.
They asked, “Teacher, we know your righteous way, Should we pay Caesar, or no tax today?”
Jesus saw their trick, asked with flair, "Whose image is this coin? Tell me, be fair."
"Caesar's," they said, trying to stall, Jesus hit back, "Give Caesar his due, give God your all."
They marveled, in silence, their trap undone, Sadducees then came, denying resurrection’s run.
"Teacher, if seven brothers married one bride, In resurrection whose wife does she abide?"
Jesus replied, "In the coming age, no marriage or wed, They're like angels, living, not dead.
Moses showed with the bush aflame, God of the living, Abraham's name."
Some scribes praised, "Teacher, you speak right," Nobody dared to question his might.
Jesus asked, "Why is Christ David's son? Yet David calls him Lord, how is this spun?"
To the crowd, he warned of scribes' pretense, "Long robes, best seats, their prayers immense.
They devour widows, with a show of grace, For them, condemnation has its place."
Rich folks were dropping gifts, making it rain, But a poor widow gave her all, in the smallest of coins' name.
He said, "Hear me now, she gave more than all, They gave from wealth, she gave her all, standing tall."
Talking 'bout the temple, stones shining bright, He warned, "Soon not one stone will be left in sight."
"When’s it gonna happen?" they asked, seeking the sign, "Don't be misled by those claiming 'I’m divine.'"
"Nation against nation, kingdom will rise, Earthquakes, famines, plagues, and signs from the skies."
"They'll grab you, persecute, haul you before kings, But it’s your testimony that your endurance brings."
"Don’t fret what to say, I’ll give you the word, Wisdom they can’t counter, truth to be heard."
"Betrayed by family, for my name you'll stand, But not a hair will perish, you'll be in my hand."
"Jerusalem’s siege—armies closing tight, Flee to the mountains, escape into the night."
"Days of vengeance, prophecy fulfilled, Great distress upon the land, all its peace killed."
"Signs in the heavens, fear in the air, Then see the Son of Man, coming with power beyond compare."
"When you see the fig tree budding, know what's near, God’s Kingdom coming, be ready, have no fear."
"This generation sees it done, heaven and earth may pass, But my words stand eternal, a truth that will last."
"Stay vigilant, avoid life's heavy chain, Be ready for that day, like a snare it will claim."
"Pray to escape, stand strong before the Son," Every day in the temple, teaching till the day was done.
At Olivet each night, he found peace and rest, Crowds gathered in the morning, eager for wisdom’s best.
Feast of the bread, Passover's near, Chief priests plot, filled with fear.
Satan whispers to Judas’ ear, One of the twelve, his path unclear.
He makes a deal, with coins they cheer, Looks for a chance when the crowd ain't near.
Now the day of the bread’s begun, Jesus sends Peter and John, "Get it done."
"Where do we prep?" they ask with care, "In the city, find a man with a jar, follow him there.
Tell the house's master, ‘The Teacher needs a room,’ He'll show a place prepared, free from gloom."
Peter and John found it true, The Passover prep, they perfectly knew.
When the hour came, Jesus sat with his crew, Said, "I’ve wanted this meal before my due.
I won’t eat again till Kingdom’s true, Take this cup, share it anew."
Bread in hand, broke it with grace, “My body for you, keep it in place.”
The cup after supper, the new bond’s sign, “My blood poured for you, covenant divine.
Betrayer's hand with me on the table, Son of Man goes, but woe to the unstable."
They questioned who it might be, And argued who’d be greatest, who’ll see?
Jesus taught the kings’ way versus his, "Serve like the youngest, that’s what it is.
I’m here among you serving all, In my Kingdom, you’ll stand tall."
"Simon, Simon, Satan’s on the prowl, I prayed your faith won’t throw in the towel."
Peter said, "Prison or death, I’m in line," Jesus replied, "Denial before the rooster’s sign."
"Remember when you lacked naught? Now trade cloak for a sword, don’t get caught.
Scripture’s fulfillment must be sought, Counted with transgressors, it’s all been taught."
They went to the Mount, as was his way, Jesus urged, "Pray, avoid temptation today."
Alone he knelt, the night so tight, “Father, your will, not mine tonight.”
Angels came, his strength renewed, Sweat like blood, his prayer pursued.
He found them asleep, grief held them tight, “Wake up, pray, find your fight.”
Judas approached with a betrayer's kiss, "Son of Man betrayed with this?"
The crowd surged with swords and might, A disciple struck, cutting in the night.
"Enough," said Jesus, "let me heal," Touched the ear, made it real.
"Why come like robbers, swords and clubs? In the temple, you showed no grubs."
Seized and led to the priest’s place, Peter followed, hiding his face.
By the fire’s light, the girl did claim, Peter denied, "I don’t know that name."
Another pointed, "You’re one of them," "Man, I’m not," Peter said again.
A third accused, "Galilean sight," "Man, I know not," denial in the night.
The rooster crowed, the Lord’s eyes met, Peter remembered, tears were set.
The guards mocked, with strikes they played, Blindfolded, they called, “Who struck?” they swayed.
Morning assembly, elders drew near, "Are you the Christ?" they asked clear.
“If I tell, you won’t believe, Son of Man at God’s hand, where I'll leave.”
"You the Son of God?" they pressed, "You say it, I am," he confessed.
“No more witness needed,” they cried, “From his own mouth, he supplied.”
The crowd rose up, took him to Pilate's place, Accused him of perverting the nations' face.
"He forbids taxes, claims he's a king," they cried, Pilate asked, "King of the Jews?" Jesus replied.
"You say it," he spoke, calm and clear, Pilate told the priests, "No charges here."
But they pressed on, "He stirs up all the land," From Galilee to here, we understand.
Pilate caught the word "Galilee," asked the case, Sent him to Herod, in Jerusalem's space.
Herod was happy, he'd longed for this day, He wanted miracles, wanted a display.
Questioned with words, but Jesus stood still, While priests and scribes accused with a will.
Herod mocked him, dressed him in fine clothes, Sent him back to Pilate, friends now, not foes.
Pilate called them back, the rulers and the crowd, Examined him, said, "No guilt I've found."
"Herod found nothing, no death-worthy crime, I'll chastise and release him, just give it time."
But the crowd shouted, "Release Barabbas!" A rebel and murderer, causing much fuss.
Pilate tried again, sought Jesus' release, But they shouted, "Crucify him, won't you cease?"
"What has he done?" Pilate asked with a sigh, "I'll chastise him once more, then let him fly."
But their voices rose, louder than before, Demanding crucifixion, their voices soared.
Pilate gave in to their urgent plea, Released Barabbas, but Jesus was to be.
Led him away, Simon bore the cross weight, Following women mourned his fate.
Jesus turned, "Weep not for me," he said, "For your children, save tears instead.
Days will come, barren wombs they'll bless, Mountains and hills they'll wish to address."
Two criminals joined him on this path, At the Skull, they faced the aftermath.
"Father, forgive them," Jesus cried, "They don't know the deed they've tried."
Soldiers gambled for his clothes, looked on, Rulers scoffed, "Save yourself, chosen one!"
A sign read, "King of the Jews," above his head, Mocked by soldiers, vinegar they fed.
One thief mocked, "Save us too, if you're the Christ!" The other rebuked, "We've earned this plight."
"Remember me," he asked with a plea, Jesus replied, "In Paradise, you'll be with me."
Darkness fell from the sixth hour till nine, The temple veil tore, a divine sign.
"Into your hands, I commit my spirit!" he cried, Breathed his last breath, and then he died.
The centurion saw, "Righteous man," he declared, Crowds left, hearts heavy, souls bared.
Joseph from Arimathaea, good and true, Asked Pilate for the body, knew what to do.
Wrapped him in linen, laid him in stone, A tomb untouched, a place of his own.
The Sabbath neared, women watched and wept, Prepared spices, while the commandment they kept.
Early dawn, first day of the week, They came with spices, ready to seek.
Stone rolled back, tomb was bare, Entered in, but He wasn't there.
Two men stood in dazzling light, Terrified, they bowed at the sight.
"Why seek the living here, among the dead? He's risen, remember what He said."
"He'd be delivered, crucified, and then, The third day rise, alive again."
His words came back, they ran to tell, The eleven and others, where they dwell.
Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary too, Told the apostles what they knew.
To them, it seemed a tale, no belief, But Peter ran, seeking relief.
He saw linen, puzzled, and went home, Wondered, "What’s happened? What's gone?"
Two walked to Emmaus, talking the way, When Jesus joined, though hidden that day.
"What are you discussing, looking so sad?" Asked the stranger, making them glad.
Cleopas spoke, "Are you the only one? Don’t know of Jesus, what’s been done?"
"A prophet mighty, condemned to die, We thought He'd redeem, but now He's gone by."
"Women amazed us, said angels they saw, Said He's alive, breaking all law."
"Some checked the tomb, found it just so, But Him they didn't see, where did He go?"
"Foolish and slow, believe what’s been told, Christ had to suffer, as prophets of old."
From Moses to prophets, He showed the plan, Revealed in Scriptures, this Son of Man.
Approaching the village, He seemed to move on, "Stay with us, day's almost gone."
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it there, Eyes opened, then vanished, leaving them aware.
"Weren’t our hearts burning within?" they said, "He opened Scriptures, the living bread."
Back to Jerusalem, that very hour, Found the eleven, shared the power.
"The Lord is risen, appeared to Simon’s eyes!" Shared their story, in breaking bread, surprise.
Jesus Himself stood, "Peace be to you," Terrified, thinking a spirit they knew.
"Why troubled? See, it's truly me, Touch my hands and feet, flesh and bone to see."
"Got food here?" He asked, they offered fish, Ate before them, fulfilling their wish.
"Remember what I told, when we walked before, Moses, prophets, psalms, all Scriptures more."
He opened their minds, Scriptures made plain, "Christ must suffer, rise the third day again."
"Repentance, remission, preached in His name, To all nations, starting at Jerusalem's fame."
"You’re witnesses, power from on high, Wait in the city, don't let it pass by."
Led them to Bethany, hands raised high, Blessed them, then ascended to the sky.
They worshiped, returned with joy to the place, Temple-bound, praising God’s grace.
Amen, they sang, filled with His love, Blessing God always, from below to above.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God / And with God from the beginning, God was the Word
All things were made through him; in him was life and light / The light of men shone through the dark, not overcome by night
