John came to witness to the light, that all might believe / He was not the light himself, but came to testify
The true light came into the world, unknown to them / His own did not receive him; they rejected him
All who received him, believed in his name, gained the right / To be God’s own children, born of God, not human desire
The Word became flesh, lived among us, glory displayed / We saw the Father’s only Son, grace and truth conveyed
From fullness, grace on grace; the Son made God known / The law came through Moses; grace and truth through Christ were shown
The priests and Levites asked John, “Who are you?” / John answered, “I am not the Christ,” that much was true
He said, “Neither Elijah nor the prophet am I” / “I’m the wilderness voice: make the Lord’s way straight,” was his reply
John said, “I baptize in water; one stands unknown to you” / “Comes after, ranks before; his sandal, not worthy to undo”
“He comes after me, yet he was before me,” John would say / “Knew him not; baptized so Israel saw him revealed that day”
John saw the Spirit fall on Jesus, dove-like, then remain / The sender said, “He’ll baptize in the Spirit,” the sign made plain
John said, “I knew him not; the sign identified him” / “I have seen and testified: the Son of God is he”
John called him Lamb of God again the following day / His two disciples heard, and followed Jesus away
Jesus asked, “What seek you?” They said, “Rabbi, where you reside?” / And he said, “Come and see”; they stayed with him, by his side
Andrew told his brother, “We have found Messiah,” he said / And brought him to Jesus, who named him Cephas, Peter by name
Jesus found Philip and called, “Follow; come near” / From Bethsaida, like Andrew and Peter, he’s here
Philip said Moses and prophets wrote of Jesus, Joseph’s son / Can good come from Nazareth? Philip said, “Come and see the one”
Jesus saw Nathanael come, a man whose heart was true / An Israelite indeed, with no deceit in view
Nathanael asked Jesus, “How could you already know me?” / Jesus said, “Before Philip called, I saw you by the fig tree”
Nathanael answered, “Rabbi, you are God’s Son!”—he replied / “You are the King of Israel!”—Nathanael testified
Jesus asked, “You believe because I saw you by the tree?” / “You shall see far greater things than even these,” he said
“You’ll see heaven opened; God’s angels will rise / Then descend on the Son of Man before your eyes”
At Cana’s wedding feast, the wine had all run dry, / His mother told Jesus why: they had no wine.
Jesus said, “My hour has not come; it must wait,” / His mother told the servants, “Do what he says; obey.”
He said, “Fill six stone pots with water to the brim”; they filled, / They drew it, took it; the ruler tasted wine he’d sipped.
This was his first sign, and his glory was shown, / His disciples believed in him, their faith made known.
He made a whip, cast beasts out, poured coins, overturned tables, / Told dove sellers, “Take these out! My Father’s house is no marketplace!”
The Jews asked Jesus, “What sign will you now show, / Since you do these things?”—they challenged him so.
He answered, “Destroy this temple,” for them to hear, / “In three days I will raise it up”—his words were clear.
They said, “Forty-six years to build; raise it in three?” / He spoke of his body, not the building they see.
Raised from the dead, his disciples recalled his own word, / They believed Scripture and the word of Jesus they heard.
Many believed in his name because they saw his signs, / Yet he did not entrust himself; he knew what was in mankind.
Nicodemus, Pharisee, ruler of the Jews, came by night / “Rabbi, we know came from God; no one does signs without God beside”
“Unless born anew, one cannot see God’s Kingdom’s light” / “Can an old man enter his mother’s womb and be born again?”
“Born of water and Spirit, or no one enters God’s reign” / “Flesh gives birth to flesh; Spirit gives birth to spirit again”
“Don’t marvel: you must be born anew,” Jesus makes clear / “The wind’s sound you hear; its source and course are unclear”
Nicodemus asks, “How can these things be?” Jesus makes clear: / “Are you Israel’s teacher, and still these things are not clear?”
“We speak what we know, testify what we’ve seen, yet you don’t receive / Our witness; earthly things you disbelieve—how will you heavenly truth believe?”
“No one ascended but the Son of Man, who came down from above” / “As Moses raised the snake, the Son must be lifted up”
“For God so loved the world, one only Son he gave / Whoever trusts won’t perish, but eternal life they’ll have”
“God sent his Son to save the world, not come to condemn” / “Believers aren’t judged; unbelievers stand judged for not trusting his name”
“The light came into the world; men loved darkness, their works evil” / “Those doing truth come to light; their deeds, done in God, are revealed”
“Jesus and disciples baptized in Judea, where they stayed” / “John baptized near Salim, at Enon, where much water lay”
“A dispute about cleansing; his disciples came to John” / “Jesus baptizes; everyone is coming to him,” they went on
“A person receives nothing unless heaven grants it so” / “I am not the Christ; I was sent before him,” John let them know
“The bridegroom’s friend hears his voice; his joy is fulfilled” / “He must increase; I must decrease,” John says, his heart thrilled
“The one from heaven is above all, yet none receive his word” / “God sends him speaking God’s words; the Spirit without measure poured”
“The Father loves the Son; all things are in his hand” / “The one who believes in the Son has life; God’s wrath remains on the one who disobeys”
The Pharisees heard Jesus made more disciples than John, / He left Judea for Galilee and journeyed on.
At sixth hour, weary, by Jacob’s well he sat that day, / The Samaritan woman came; “Give me a drink,” he’d say.
She asked, “Why would a Jew ask me, a Samaritan, for a drink?” / “If you knew who speaks, and God’s gift, you’d ask him; he’d bring living water.”
She asked, “No bucket; this well is deep—where does that water flow? / Are you greater than Jacob, who gave us this well long ago?”
He said his gift would spring to life; the drinker won’t thirst again, / She asked, “Give me that water, so I needn’t come here then.”
He said, “Call your husband”; she said, “I have none,” / “You’ve had five; the man you have now is not your husband.”
She called him a prophet and asked where worship should be found; / “Our fathers worship on this mountain; Jerusalem is the ground.”
Hour comes: not here or Jerusalem will you worship the Father; / Salvation from Jews; true worship in spirit and truth, not either.
God is spirit; his worshipers must worship in spirit and truth; / The Father seeks such worshipers—these words from Jesus give proof.
She said the Christ would come and make all things clear, / He told her, “I am he, the one speaking to you here.”
She left her water jar and went into the town: / “Come see the man who told my deeds; could Christ be found?”
His disciples urged, “Rabbi, eat”; his food was unknown, / They wondered, “Had someone brought him food of his own?”
“My food is doing the will of the One who sent me, / And accomplishing his work, the task he sent me to do.”
“Lift up your eyes: the fields are white for harvest already, in sight; / The reaper earns wages, gathers fruit, life eternal; both rejoice outright.”
“One sows, while another reaps, as that saying holds true, / You reap what others labored for; their work is before you.”
Her testimony led Samaritans to believe and say, / They begged him to stay; he stayed there with them for two days.
Many more believed because of Jesus’ word, / They told her, “Not your words; we heard Christ, Savior of the world.”
Two days passed; went to Galilee; prophets lack honor at home, / Galileans welcomed him, his Jerusalem works they had known.
In Cana, there was a nobleman’s son who lay near death, / His father begged, “Come down; heal him ere he draws his last breath.”
Jesus said, “Unless you see signs and wonders, you won’t believe,” / The nobleman begged, “Come down before my child dies,” said he.
“Go your way; your son lives,” he said; the man believed, then went. / His servants met him: “Your child lives!”—that was the news they told.
He learned the fever left at seventh hour, as Jesus said; / He and his whole household believed what Jesus conveyed.
Jesus saw him sick thirty-eight years, asked, “Would you be whole?” / By Bethesda’s pool he lay, where sick crowds waited as well.
He had no one to put him in when the waters stirred, / Another stepped in first before his turn occurred.
Jesus said, “Rise, take your mat, and walk,” and he obeyed, / At once he was made well, took up his mat, and walked away.
They said, “It’s Sabbath; carrying your mat is not allowed.” / He answered, “He who healed me said, ‘Take your mat; move along.’”
He didn’t know who healed him; Jesus had withdrawn from view; / Jesus found him in the temple: “Sin no more, or worse may come.”
That man told Jews that Jesus healed him, gave his healer’s name, / They persecuted him, sought his death for Sabbath’s sake.
“My Father still works, and I am working too,” he said that day; / They sought his death: God his own Father, equal, they would say.
The Son does nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father do; / The Father shows him greater works, so you will marvel too.
The Father raises the dead, gives life; the Son does likewise; / The Son gives life to whom he wills; his own desire decides.
The Father gave the Son all judgment, honor him as due, / Who dishonors the Son dishonors the Father who sent him too.
Who hears his word, believes the Sender, gains eternal life, / No judgment; has passed out of death into life, now alive.
The hour comes, now is: the dead hear God’s Son’s voice and live; / All in the tombs hear his voice; good rise, evil judgment receive.
He judges as he hears; his judgment is just and right, / He seeks not his own will, but the Father’s will outright.
His own report would not suffice; John testified aright, / A burning, shining lamp; they rejoiced awhile in his light.
The works his Father gave him testify more than John, / They testify the Father sent him, their witness made known.
The Father testified; his voice they’d never heard, his form unseen; / His word lived not in them; they did not trust the One he’d sent.
The Scriptures testify of him in the words they read, / Yet they would not come to him to find the life they need.
He came in his Father’s name; they turned his call aside, / Another in his own name they’d welcome, without pride.
Moses, where they set their hope, would accuse them with his pen, / If they believed what Moses wrote, they’d believe Jesus then.
A great crowd followed Jesus across Galilee / They saw the signs he did on those who were sick by the sea
Jesus asked Philip where they could buy bread nearby / Two hundred denarii won’t provide each a little supply
Andrew named a boy: five barley loaves, two fish he found / Jesus had five thousand men sit on grass upon the ground
He gave thanks, then passed the bread and fish around / They ate as much as they wished, their hunger quieted down
He said, “Gather broken pieces; let nothing be lost” / Twelve baskets held the fragments; not a piece was tossed
They called him prophet, come into the world, their claim / He withdrew alone when they would force him king by name
Through storm, he walked the sea: “It’s I; don’t be afraid” / They took him in; their boat reached land without delay
They came by boat to Capernaum, seeking his face / They found him: “Rabbi, when did you come to this place?”
“You seek me not for signs, but loaves that left you fed / Seek food that lasts to life; the Son gives it,” Jesus said
They asked what work God asks of them, what deed is meant / “This is God’s work: believe in him whom he has sent”
They asked for signs; their fathers ate the manna from the sky / “Moses didn’t give the bread; my Father gives true bread from on high”
“I am the bread of life; whoever comes is fed” / “Whoever believes in me won’t thirst”—he said
“The Father gives them; I will not cast them away / I do his will: lose none, raise them at the last day”
They murmured, “Joseph’s son—his parents are well known” / “No one comes unless the Father draws, as he has shown”
Only the one from God has seen the Father, Jesus said / Who believes in me has life eternal; I am life’s bread
Their ancestors all ate the manna, yet they died / He is heaven’s living bread; his flesh was for all supplied
They argued with each other, “How can his flesh be food?” / “Who eats my flesh and drinks my blood has life; I’ll raise him, live in me”
As the living Father sent me, by him I am alive / Who feeds on me will also live because of me
They called his teaching hard; he asked, “Does this cause you to stumble?” / “The Spirit gives life; flesh is nothing; my words are spirit and life”
“Some don’t believe; he knew who’d betray, who’d turn away” / “No one can come unless the Father grants the way”
Many disciples turned back, walked with him no more / He asked the twelve, “Do you also want to leave as those before?”
“Lord, to whom would we go? Your words give life eternally” / “We’ve come to believe and know you’re Christ, the living God’s Son”
He chose the twelve; one of them a devil, he declared / He spoke of Judas Iscariot, who’d betray him there
Jesus walked in Galilee; Judea’s Jews sought him to kill / Booths’ feast drew near; his brothers urged, “Go up, reveal”
His brothers said, “Go show your works; no seeker leaves deeds unknown” / Though they believed not in him, they urged his works to be shown
“My time has not yet come; your time is always on / The world can’t hate you; it hates me; I say its works are wrong”
His brothers went up first; he went when they were gone / Not publicly, but secretly, he traveled on
They sought him; some called him good, some said he led them wrong / Fear of the Jews kept all from speaking openly among the throng
Mid-feast, he taught within the temple, speaking clear / They marveled: letters, though no school had taught him here
“My teaching is not mine; the sender is its source / Whoever wills God’s will can know its teaching’s course”
“Who seeks the sender’s glory is true, with no unrighteous deed / Why seek to kill me? None of you the law will heed”
He said, “One work I did; you all marvel at the sight” / They cried, “You have a demon! Who seeks your life?” in reply
You circumcise on Sabbath lest Moses’ law be slighted / I made a man completely well; judge justly, not by sight
“Is this the one they seek to kill? Could rulers know he’s Christ?” / “We know where he comes from; Christ’s source is unknown,” they insist
“You know me, know where I’m from; I came not on my own / The sender is true; you don’t know him, but I know”
They sought to seize him; his hour had not yet come / Many believed: “Will Christ do more signs than this one?”
The Pharisees heard murmurs rising through the press / Chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to arrest
“I’ll stay with you a bit more, then go to him who sent me / You’ll seek me, not find me; where I am, you can’t be”
They wondered, “Will he go and teach the Greeks somewhere? / Will he go to the Dispersion?”—they asked where
On the feast’s last and greatest day, he cried out to the crowd / “If anyone is thirsty, come to me and drink,” he called aloud
“Whoever believes in me, as Scripture has decreed / From within him rivers of living water proceed”
He spoke of Spirit believers were to receive / The Spirit wasn’t given; Jesus wasn’t glorified
Some called him prophet; others said, “The Christ is he” / Some asked, “Christ from Galilee? David’s seed, Bethlehem too?”
Some of them would have arrested him, to seize the man / Yet no one laid a hand on him; none carried out the plan
Pharisees asked, “Have rulers believed? Has one gone astray?” / “The law-ignorant crowd is cursed,” the Pharisees say
Chief priests and Pharisees asked why, with a stern demand / The officers then said, “No man ever spoke like this man!”
Can law judge a man unheard, before it knows what’s done? / “Galilean? Search: no prophet rose there”; each went home, each one.
Jesus taught in the temple; the people gathered there / They brought her, caught in adultery: “What do you say?”
He wrote upon the ground, then looked up at the crowd / “Let one without sin cast the first stone,” he said aloud
One by one they left; Jesus and the woman were alone / “Neither do I condemn you; go your way, sin no more”
“I’m the light of the world,” Jesus said, “my words abide” / “Whoever follows won’t walk in darkness; life’s light will shine bright”
The Pharisees said, “Your witness for yourself has no force” / He said his witness is true; he knows his source and course
He says, “I judge no one; if I judge, my judgment is true” / “The Father who sent me bears witness, confirming what I do”
Asked where his Father was: “You know neither me nor him,” he replied / No one had arrested him; his hour had not yet arrived
“I’m going away; you’ll die in your sins; you cannot come along” / They ask, “Will he kill himself?”—they take his words all wrong
“You’re from beneath, of this world; I’m from above on high” / “Unless you believe ‘I am he,’ in your sins you’ll die”
“Who are you?” He says, “I’ve told you from the beginning clear” / “I say what I heard from him, to all the world, for you to hear”
“When lifted, you’ll know I AM; I do what he taught me to” / “My Father stays with me; I do what pleases him too”
Many believed; remain in my word, be true disciples too / No longer slaves you’ll be, for the truth will make you free
“You say Abraham’s offspring; no one ever held you down” / “Sin makes its doer a slave; the Son can free you now”
“You seek to kill me; my word finds no place within” / “I speak what I have seen with my Father, not from men”
“You call Abraham your father; you’d do the works he did” / “You’d not seek to kill the man who speaks the words God said”
“If God were your Father, you would love me, for I came” / “From God, not of myself; he sent me all the same”
“You’re of your father, the devil; his desires you obey” / “Murderer from the start, a liar; you cast my words away”
“Who can convict me of sin? Why not believe what’s clear?” / “God’s own hear God’s words; you’re not of God, so you don’t hear”
“You call me Samaritan, say a demon is with me” / “I have no demon; I honor my Father, you dishonor me”
Whoever it is who keeps my word will never see death / They say Abraham and prophets died, and question what he saith
They ask, “Are you greater than Abraham?”—the prophets are dead / “Who do you make yourself out to be?”—that’s what they said
“My Father glorifies me; I know his word and keep” / “Abraham saw my day and was glad; his joy ran deep”
They ask, “You’re not yet fifty; how could you see?” / “Before Abraham came to be, ‘I AM,’” said he
They took up stones to throw, but Jesus slipped their view / Hidden, he passed through their midst and from the temple withdrew
Jesus passed and saw a man blind from birth, without light; / His disciples asked, “Who sinned, the man or his parents, that he was born without sight?”
Neither man nor his parents sinned; God’s works through him made plain; / “I must work by day; night comes, none work; I’m the world’s light,” he explained.
He mixed his saliva with the dust and spread the clay; / “Wash in Siloam”; the man went, washed, and saw that day.
Neighbors asked, “Is this the beggar who sat over there?” / Some said yes; others, “He looks like him”; “I am he,” he declared.
Asked how he was healed, he recounted Jesus’ cure; / Asked where Jesus was, he said, “I don’t know,” unsure.
They brought him to the Pharisees to explain; / Sabbath, Jesus made mud, opened eyes again.
He told them how he gained his sight; the Pharisees split; / Some said he wasn’t from God; others asked how sinners did it.
They asked what he said of Jesus, what was his view; / “He is a prophet,” he answered, when asked what he knew.
The Jews doubted he was born blind, so called his parents near; / They asked how their son could see, how his sight could appear.
“Our son was born blind; who opened his eyes? We don’t know; / Ask him; he’s grown,” they said, fearing they’d be disowned.
They said, “Give glory to God; we know he’s a sinner,” they claimed; / “I don’t know if he is; one thing: my sight I’ve regained.”
They asked again what he had done, how he had opened eyes; / “I told you, but you didn’t listen—would you join him?” he replies.
They said, “We follow Moses; God spoke to him long ago”; / “But where he comes from, we don’t know,” they told him.
He said, “God hears his worshipers who do his will, not sinners’ plea; / No born-blind eyes were opened before; without God, no act could be.”
They said, “You were born altogether in sins, and you teach?” / Then they threw him out, refusing to hear his speech.
Jesus heard they’d thrown him out, then found him there that day; / He then asked, “Do you believe in God’s Son?” straightaway.
He asked, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe?” / He worshiped, “Lord, I believe,” having seen him speak.
He came so those who do not see may see, while seers grow blind; / “Are we blind?” “If blind, no sin; now you say ‘We see’; sin remains,” he replied.
The true shepherd comes through the door and leads his sheep away / His sheep hear and know his voice, then follow and obey
The sheep flee from strangers; their voices they don’t know / His hearers failed to grasp the parable’s flow
I’m the sheep’s door; whoever enters will be saved / They go in and out, find pasture, and are fed
The thief only comes to steal, destroy, and to kill / I came so they may have an abundant life
I am the good shepherd; I know each one of my own / They know me, and for them I lay my life down
The hired hand leaves the sheep when the wolf draws near / The wolf snatches and scatters; the hireling doesn’t care
The Father knows me, and I know him; that truth is known / Other sheep I must bring; one flock, one shepherd alone
The Father loves me; I lay my life down, then take it again / No one takes it; I have power, as my Father commands
Some called him demon-possessed, out of his mind, insane / Others said no demon could open blind eyes, they maintained
The Jews asked, “How long will you keep us waiting here? / If you are the Christ, tell us plainly; make it clear”
“I have told you,” said Jesus, “yet you do not believe what I say / The works I do in my Father’s name testify this way”
You do not believe; you’re not my sheep, as I have told / My sheep hear, follow; eternal life is theirs to hold
My Father who gave them is greater than anyone / No one can snatch them from his hand; Father and I are one
The Jews took up stones; he asked, “What work have I done?” / “For which good work from my Father do you stone me, then?”
They said, “Not for good works; blasphemy is the claim / You, being a man, make yourself God,” they proclaimed
“Why do you say I blaspheme for saying, ‘I am God’s Son’?” / “The Father sanctified and sent me; that is what he’s done”
“Believe my works if not me: the Father is in me / And I am in him; they tried to seize me, but I got free”
Though John did no sign, all he said about him was true / Many came and believed in Jesus there too
Lazarus of Bethany fell sick and lay ill, / His sisters sent Jesus word: “The one you love lies still.”
He said, “This sickness won’t end in death; God’s glory will be shown,” / “Through it God’s Son will be glorified; his glory made known.”
Though Jesus loved all three, he stayed two days in one place, / Then told his disciples, “Back to Judea,” led the pace.
He called it sleep and said he’d wake him; they took his words as rest, / Then plainly said, “Lazarus is dead,” correcting what they guessed.
He said, “I’m glad I wasn’t there, so faith may fill your heart,” / Thomas urged, “Let’s go and die with him,” ready to depart.
Four days had passed in the tomb when Jesus arrived, / Martha went to meet him; Mary stayed back inside.
“My brother would not have died if you had been here,” she said, / “Even now, whatever you ask God, he will grant,” she pled.
He told her, “Your own dear brother will rise again,” / She knew he’d rise when the dead are raised at the end.
“I am the resurrection and life; believers live though they die, / Whoever lives and believes in me will never die; believe?”
“Yes, Lord, I’ve come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, / The one who comes into the world,” she said, her confession done.
Martha secretly said, “The Teacher’s here; he calls you today,” / Mary rose quickly and went to him, without delay.
Their weeping troubled Jesus; he asked where his friend might lie, / They said, “Lord, come and see”; Jesus wept before their eyes.
Some of the Jews said, “See how much love he showed that day,” / “Could he who opened blind eyes have kept death away?”
He came and said, “Take away the stone that seals the tomb,” / Martha warned, “Four days he’s dead; the stench will fill the room.”
He asked, “If you believe, God’s glory you will see,” / They moved the stone away, as he decreed.
He thanked the Father for hearing him in prayer, / He spoke so crowds would clearly know God sent him there.
He cried, “Lazarus, come out!” The dead man came outside, / Bound hand and foot, his face wrapped in cloth, his limbs all tied.
He said, “Unbind the wrappings; let him go free,” / Many who saw what Jesus did came to believe.
Some went to the Pharisees and told them the news, / Chief priests and Pharisees met to weigh the signs they knew.
They feared all would believe if they let him stand, / Rome would take their place and nation from their own hand.
Caiaphas said one man should die, to save the people’s lives, / So the whole nation would not perish, but survive.
He prophesied Christ would die, gather God’s scattered children as one, / From that day they planned to kill him; their plot had just begun.
He stayed in Ephraim with disciples; crowds asked, “Will he appear?” / Priests ordered them to report where he was, to seize him there.
At supper Jesus sat with Lazarus near, / Martha served the meal as they gathered there.
Mary poured costly nard and anointed Jesus’ feet, / She wiped them with her hair; the house smelled rich and sweet.
Judas asked, “Why sell for three hundred, give the poor their share?” / Jesus: “Leave her, kept for burial; poor stay, I’m not always here.”
Crowds came to see Jesus and Lazarus, raised from the dead, / Priests plotted Lazarus’ death; through him belief in Jesus spread.
They cried, “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the Lord’s name,” / And they did hail the King of Israel with a loud acclaim.
He rode a young donkey, as Scripture had foretold, / Once glorified, they recalled what they’d done and what was told.
The crowd testified Lazarus had been revived, / The Pharisees said the whole world was on his side.
Some Greeks came to Philip, asking if they could see / Jesus; he and Andrew then carried their plea.
The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, / Like wheat that falls and dies, then bears fruit far and wide.
Love life, lose it; hate your life here, keep it eternally, / Serve me and follow; where I am, the Father honors you.
Troubled, he asked, “Save me from this hour?” For this I came. / Then he prayed, “O my Father, glorify your name!”
A voice from heaven said, “I have glorified it before,” / And promised, “I will glorify it once more.”
He said, “This voice came not for me, but for your sake alone.” / Now judgment comes; the world’s prince will be overthrown.
“When lifted from earth, I will draw all to me,” / He signified the death by which he would die.
The crowd asked, “If Christ remains forever, how can this be? / The Son of Man, they said, must be lifted—who is he?”
“Walk while you have the light; believe, and let it guide, / Become the children of light.” Then he left and went to hide.
Though Jesus showed many signs, they still refused to believe, / Isaiah spoke of blinded eyes and hearts that would not perceive.
Many rulers believed, but would not let it be known, / They feared being put out; human praise outweighed God’s own.
I came as light into the world; believers need not stay, / Whoever believes in me may not remain in night.
I came not to judge the world; to save it I’ve come. / If one hears my words and doesn’t believe, I judge him none.
The word I spoke will judge the one who rejects it on the last day, / The Father gave the words I speak; eternal life they convey.
Before Passover, Jesus knew his hour to leave for the Father / From God he came, loved his own to the end, and would go there
The devil put in Judas Iscariot’s heart a plan to betray / As supper was underway, that plan was already in play
He rose, laid aside his clothes, wrapped a towel round his waist / Poured water in the basin, washed each foot, towel in place
Peter asked, when Jesus came, “Lord, will You wash my feet?” / Jesus said, “You don’t know now; later you will see.”
Peter refused; “If I don’t wash you, no part with me,” said Lord / “Then wash my hands and my head as well,” Peter implored
One who has bathed needs only feet washed clean / “You all are clean, but not all,” He knew the traitor within
After washing, he asked, “Do you know what I’ve done?” / “You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord’; rightly, I am the one.”
As Lord and Teacher, I washed your feet to show you the way / “Wash one another’s feet; do as I have done,” he’d say
No servant's greater than his lord, nor sent one than sender, true / If you know these things and do them, then blessed are you
I know whom I have chosen; Scripture’s word makes it clear / “He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.”
I tell you ahead of time, so when it comes to be / Then you may believe the words I speak: “I am he.”
Whoever welcomes me receives the Sender too / Whoever welcomes one I send receives me—that is true
Troubled in spirit, Jesus testified one would betray / The disciples wondered whom He meant; they could not say
Peter beckoned him to ask, “Lord, who is the one?” / Jesus gave the dipped bread to Judas, Simon’s son
Satan entered Judas after bread; “Do quickly,” Christ said / At once Judas left the supper; into the night he fled
The Son of Man is glorified; God’s glory in Him is shown / Love one another as I loved you; by this you’ll be known
Peter asked, “Where are You going? Why can’t I follow now? I’ll die” / Jesus said, “Not now; later. You’ll deny thrice before rooster’s cry.”
Believe in God, believe in me; I go prepare / A place in my Father’s house; I’ll come and receive you there
Thomas said, “Lord, we don’t know where you are going” / “How can we know the way?” His question he is posing
“I am the way, the truth, and life; no one comes through me” / “And you know him now, and have also seen him too”
Philip asks, “Show us the Father; make his presence known” / Jesus says, “Who sees me sees him; the Father’s works are shown”
“Believe I’m in the Father, and the Father in me” / “Or trust the works; I go to my Father; greater works you’ll see”
“If you love me, keep my commands; don’t set them aside” / “I’ll ask the Father; Truth’s Counselor will stay at your side”
“I will not leave you orphaned; I will come to you” / “The world won’t see me, but you will; since I live, you’ll live too”
“You’ll know I’m in the Father, you in me, and I in you” / “I’ll reveal myself to those who love, keep what I ask you to do”
Judas (not Iscariot) asks, “What has happened here?” / “Why show yourself to us, and not the world appear?”
“Who loves me keeps my word; my Father makes his home” / “Who loves me not keeps not my words; they’re the Father’s own”
“The Father sends the Spirit in my name to teach and guide” / “He’ll remind you of all I said; keep every word in mind”
“My peace I leave with you, not as the world will give” / “Let not your hearts be troubled or afraid; in peace now live”
“I go to my Father, who is greater than I” / “I told you beforehand, so believe when it draws nigh”
“The prince of this world comes; he has nothing in me” / “I do as he commands; rise, let’s go, the world will see”
I am the true vine; my Father, he tends the row / He takes fruitless branches; prunes the fruitful; they grow
Remain in me, and I in you; like branches, stay and cling / Apart from me you can do nothing; no fruit can branches bring
Branches cast out wither, gathered, thrown in fire to burn / If you remain, my words in you, ask; your wish I grant in turn
Much fruit gives my Father glory; it marks disciples true / Father loved me; I loved you; keep commands; stay in my love too
I spoke so joy may stay in you, and your joy be made full / Love one another as I loved; my command to you all
You are my friends if you do whatever I command / No longer servants; all I heard from my Father, I made known
I chose, not you; appointed you to bear fruit that will stay / Ask Father in my name; he may grant what you request, I say
The world will hate you, just as it hated me before / If of the world, it would love you; I chose you out, therefore
If they persecuted me, they’ll persecute you the same / They do this for my name; they don’t know who sent me
Had I not come and spoken, they would not have had sin / He who hates me hates my Father; no excuse for sin
They saw my works no one else had done; still hatred came to show / They hated me and my Father; the law said “without cause,” so
The Spirit of truth, sent by the Father, will testify / You also testify; from the beginning, you’ve been by my side
They'll cast you from synagogues; the hour will strike / Who kills you thinks he serves God as he takes your life
They do this since the Father and I they don't know / I warned you beforehand; remember when it shows
I go to him who sent me; none asks where I depart / You’re filled with sorrow because I said we’d part
You gain by my leaving; I now go away / He won't come unless I go; then I'll send him your way
He convicts the world of sin, because they don't believe in me / I go to my Father; this world's prince is judged; you won't see me
The Spirit of truth will guide you, make all things clear / He speaks what he hears; tells what will soon appear
The Spirit glorifies me, takes mine, makes it known / All that the Father has is mine; it will be shown
You won't see me for a little while; then see me again / They ask what this little while means, unsure of when
You'll weep and mourn; the world rejoices; your sorrow turns to delight / A woman forgets her anguish when her child comes to sight
I'll see you again; no one can steal the joy that stays / Ask in my name; the Father gives, your joy made full that day
I'll speak no more in figures; I'll make the Father clear / He loves you, for you loved me, believed from God I came
I came from the Father, came into the world below / I leave the world and to the Father I go
“Now you speak plainly, no figures stand in the way / You know all things; we need no questions; from God you came,” they say
He asked, “Do you now believe?” You’ll scatter, each depart / Each to his place; leave me alone, yet the Father’s not apart
I told you this so in me your peace may come / Though trouble fills the world, I have overcome
He raised His eyes to heaven; the time had now arrived / “Father, glorify Your Son, that by Him You’re glorified”
Authority over all flesh You gave Me; life to Your own / Eternal life: know You, the true God, and Christ You sent, whom they know
I brought You glory here on earth; Your work through Me is done / Now glorify Me with Your own, with glory ere worlds begun
I made Your name known; they kept Your word, those You gave Me / Received My words, knew I came from You, believed You sent Me
I pray for those You gave to Me, not for the world outside / Holy Father, keep them in Your name; make them one as We are
I kept them; none lost but destruction’s son; Scripture fulfilled / I say these things so My joy in them may be made full
I gave them Your word; the world hates them, they’re not its own / Don’t take them from the world; keep them from the evil one
Your word is truth; set them apart; sanctify them in truth / You sent Me; I send them, for their sake, Myself sanctify in truth
I pray for those who through their word in Me believe / May all be one in Us; the world may perceive You sent Me
The glory You gave Me, I gave them, that their oneness be known / So the world may know You sent Me, and Your love for them be shown
Be with Me where I am, that they may My glory see / You loved Me before the world; Your glory was with Me
The world knew You not, Righteous Father; I knew; they knew You sent Me / I made Your name known, and will; so Your love and I in them may be
Judas knew the garden where Jesus met his band / He brought troops and officers with torches, weapons in hand
He asked whom they sought; “Jesus of Nazareth,” they say / “I am he,” he answered; they fell backward to the ground that day
Again he asked; they said, “Jesus of Nazareth,” again / He said, “I told you that I am he; let these go then”
Peter cut Malchus’s ear; Jesus said, “Sheathe your blade” / “The cup my Father gave me—shall I not drink?” he said
The soldiers seized and bound him, took him first to Annas’ hall / Caiaphas had advised one man should perish for them all
“I spoke in temple and synagogues in public view / Ask those who heard me what I taught; they heard it too”
An officer slapped Jesus: “Do you answer him like that?” / “If I spoke evil, testify; if well, why strike?” he shot back
Annas sent him, still in bonds, to Caiaphas that day / Caiaphas was high priest that year, in office there
At the door they asked if he was one of Jesus’ men / “I am not,” Peter answered, and denied him then
As Peter warmed himself by coals, they asked him once more / He denied that he was Jesus’ disciple, as before
Malchus’s kin asked, “Didn’t I see you with him by your side?” / Peter denied once more; the rooster crowed nearby
Pilate asked, “What charge?” They said, “If not evil, why bring him here?” / “We cannot put a man to death; the law is clear”
Pilate asked, “Are you King of Jews?”—is that your view? / Jesus asked, “Do you say this, or did the others tell you?”
Pilate: “Your nation’s priests delivered you; what have you done?” / “My Kingdom’s not of this world; if it were, they’d fight as one”
“You say I am a king; I was born truth to declare” / “Everyone of truth listens when my voice they hear”
Pilate asked, “What is truth?” then went out to the Jews again / “I find no basis for a charge against him,” he told them then
At Passover, Pilate offered one prisoner to choose / “Do you want me to set him free, the King of the Jews?”
The crowd cried, “Not this man, but Barabbas!”—voices rang aloud / Barabbas, he was a robber, chosen by the crowd.
Pilate had Jesus flogged; thorns were twisted to crown / The soldiers dressed him in purple, a mocking king’s gown
They cried, “Hail, King of the Jews!” as they struck him aloud / They kept on slapping him; their taunts rang through the crowd
Pilate brought Jesus out; no charge against him found / “Behold, the man!” he said, to those gathered round
The priests and officers cried, “Crucify! He must die!” / “Our law says so; he made himself God’s Son,” they replied
Pilate asked where he came from; Jesus gave no reply / “You know I have power to release you or crucify”
“You’d have no power unless it came from above, I say” / “The one who handed me to you bears greater sin and blame”
Pilate sought release; they cried, “Free him, Caesar’s friend you’re not” / “Whoever makes himself a king defies him,” they say
Pilate said, “Behold your King!”; they cried, “Crucify!” / The priests said, “We have no king but Caesar!”—their cry
Pilate delivered Jesus over; they led him away / He went out bearing his cross toward the Skull that day
They crucified Jesus with two on either side / He hung in the middle, with both men crucified
Pilate wrote “Jesus of Nazareth, King of Jews” on display / The priests objected; “What I wrote, I wrote,” he would say
The soldiers divided his garments, each taking a share / They cast lots for his seamless coat, so none would tear
“Woman, behold your son!” he told his mother then / “Behold your mother!”; the disciple took her home again
Jesus said, “I am thirsty,” his throat parched and dry / They raised vinegar on hyssop to his mouth up high
After vinegar, “It’s finished,” he bowed his head / And he gave up his spirit, and then he was dead
They asked to break their legs and take the bodies away / The soldiers broke the first two, and did as they say
They saw Jesus was dead, so his legs they spared / One soldier pierced his side; blood and water appeared
The eyewitness testified that his account was true / Scripture said no bone would break; the pierced one they would view
Joseph took the body; Nicodemus brought spices as well / They bound him in linen, in a new tomb, as the text tells
Mary found the stone rolled back while darkness veiled the sky, / She ran to Peter and the one whom Jesus loved nearby.
They ran; the linen lay, the head cloth rolled apart there, / He saw and believed, though they hadn’t known Scripture’s word clear.
Mary wept beside the tomb; two angels met her eye, / “They took my Lord; I don’t know where they laid him,” she cried.
She thought him the gardener, did not recognize his face, / “Sir, if you carried him, tell where; I’ll take him from that place.”
Jesus called her “Mary”; his voice came to reach her, / “Rabboni!” she answered, meaning “Teacher!”
“Don’t hold me; I have not yet ascended; go and say, / ‘I ascend to my Father and yours, my God and yours’ today.”
Mary told the disciples she had seen the Lord that day, / And shared what he had said to her, passing his words their way.
Behind the locked doors, Jesus stood among them that night, / “Peace be to you”; he showed hands and side; they rejoiced at sight.
“Peace be to you; as Father sent me, I send you,” he explained, / Breathed, “Receive the Spirit”; forgive: sins forgiven; retain: sins retained.
Thomas was away when they had said, “We have seen the Lord!” / “Unless I see nail prints and touch his side, I won’t believe,” he swore.
Eight days later, with Thomas there, Jesus came in view, / “Peace be to you,” he said to them, greeting them anew.
“Reach with your finger; see my hands; put your hand in my side,” / “Don’t be unbelieving, but believing,” Jesus replied.
“My Lord and my God!” Thomas cried, his eyes had finally seen, / He said, “You believe because you saw; blessed who believe unseen.”
Jesus did many other signs that were beyond this page’s frame, / These written so you believe Christ, God’s Son, and have life in his name.
Peter said, “I’ll go fishing”; the others joined the crew / No fish all night; at dawn, the nets were empty too
At dawn, Christ stood upon the shore: “Have you caught a bite?” / “Cast on the right,” he said; they couldn't haul the catch despite their might
Loved disciple cried, “The Lord!”; Peter plunged out of the boat / The others came by boat, net dragging, fish-filled and afloat
Christ said, “Bring fish you just caught”; by coals, bread and fish were laid / Peter hauled 153 great fish; the net held fast, not torn or frayed
After breakfast, Christ asked, “Do you love me more than these?” / Peter: “Yes, Lord, you know my affection”; Christ: “Feed my lambs,” said he
Christ asked a second time, “Do you love me?” again / “Tend my sheep,” Jesus said; he gave him that charge then
Peter grieved: “Do you have affection for me?”—once more / “Lord, you know everything; my affection for you is sure”
Old, hands stretched, another dresses, bears you where you don’t want go / That death would glorify God; “Follow me,” Christ told him so
Peter asked Jesus what the loved disciple’s fate might be / “If I want him to stay till I come, what’s that to you? Follow me.”
The saying spread: the loved disciple would not die, they claimed / But Jesus never said he would; their claim was misplaced
The disciple testified and wrote; his witness is true / The world could not contain books of all Christ’s deeds, were they all here.
I wrote a book to tell the tale, Theophilus, hear me well, Of all the acts and words of Christ, until to heaven he did dwell.
He showed himself alive, they saw, for forty days he taught, Of God's Kingdom and its ways, by many proofs he brought.
Gathered 'round, he gave command, “Don’t leave Jerusalem's gates, Wait for the Father's promised gift, the Holy Spirit awaits.
John baptized with water — true, but Spirit’s coming soon, You'll be soaked in power from above, baptized under the moon.”
"Lord, restore the kingdom now?" the disciples begged to know, “It’s not for you to see the times — the Father runs this show.
But power’s yours when Spirit comes, to witness far and wide, Jerusalem to the ends of Earth, my word you won't hide.”
He spoke, then risen up he went, a cloud took him away, The disciples gazed into the sky, lost in that bright display.
Two men in white stood by and asked, “Why gaze into the blue? This Jesus will return again, the way he left your view.”
From Olivet they traveled back, Jerusalem the place, In the upper room they stayed, prayers filling every space.
Peter stood among them all, a crowd of hundred twenty, “Brothers, the words of David spoke of Judas’ empty plenty.
He led the ones who took our Lord, now fallen, burst apart, His field of blood, in local tongue, a cursed and barren part.
The Psalms declare his place be void, his office someone take, From John’s baptism till now, a witness we must make.”
Two they named, Barsabbas called Justus, and Matthias too, They prayed, “Lord, you know every heart, reveal what we must do.
Pick the one to fill the role from which Judas did fall, They cast their lots, Matthias won, an apostle with them all.
Pentecost hit, they gathered as one, A mighty wind from the sky, like a race begun.
Flames like tongues sat on each of their heads, Filled with the Spirit, speaking languages spread.
In Jerusalem, from nations they came, Hearing their languages, amazed by the same.
"Galileans speaking our native tones, Parthians, Medes, and Elamites' zones.
From Judea, Asia, Egypt's land, Rome, Crete, Arabia, all understand."
Some were amazed, others mocked with disdain, "They're filled with new wine," they claimed in vain.
Peter rose with the eleven, his voice loud and clear, "Men of Judea, let my words ring in your ear.
They're not drunk as you say, it's just morning light, But what the prophet Joel spoke is in sight:
'In the last days, God will pour Spirit on all, Sons and daughters will prophesy, visions will call.
Wonders above, signs down below, Sun darkens, moon's blood will show.
Who calls on the Lord's name will be saved, Through Jesus, mighty wonders God gave.
You crucified Him, but God raised Him high, Death couldn't hold Him, He lives, can't die.
David spoke of Him, foresaw resurrection's might, His flesh didn't decay, now in God's sight.
Exalted on high, Spirit poured from above, This is what you see, proof of His love.
Jesus, whom you crucified, Lord and Christ He stands, Israel, know this, by God's own hands."
The crowd was pierced, hearts deeply moved, "Brothers, what do we do?" they asked, approved.
"Repent, be baptized in Jesus' name, For forgiveness, the Spirit's gift you claim.
This promise for you and your children to hold, For all far off, as the Lord foretold."
Peter preached, "Save from this twisted age," Three thousand baptized, a new chapter's page.
Together they learned, breaking bread in accord, In fellowship, in prayer, praising the Lord.
Fear and wonders spread through their days, Sharing and caring in generous ways.
Daily in the temple, gladness in heart, The Lord added to them, a new life to start.
Peter and John, the temple's hour was near, The ninth hour, to pray, they drew near.
A man lame from birth, placed each day, By the Beautiful Gate, where he'd lay.
He saw them coming, their presence felt, Asked for gifts, longing for help.
Peter fixed his gaze, with John's embrace, "Look at us," he said, face to face.
The man hoped for coins, a generous token, But Peter's words, a miracle was spoken:
"No silver or gold, I've none to give, But in Jesus' name, rise and live!"
He took his hand, lifted him high, Strength filled his feet, he reached for the sky.
Leaping with joy, he walked inside, Praising God loudly, with every stride.
The people saw him, they recognized, The beggar now healed, open-eyed.
Amazed and filled with wonder they stood, At Solomon’s porch, the crowd now good.
Peter spoke, "Why are you amazed? Not by our power, this miracle raised.
The God of our fathers, Abraham's claim, Glorified Jesus, whom you did shame.
You denied the Righteous, chose a thief, Killed the Life Prince, but God brought relief.
Raised Him from death, we stand here today, Faith in His name made him this way.
Brothers, you acted in ignorance, unaware, But God's plan, the prophets did declare.
"Repent and turn, let sins fade away, Times of refreshing will come your way.
God will send Jesus, ordained, to restore, Prophets told of this time before.
Moses said, a prophet will arise, Listen to him, the wise recognize.
Reject him, you'll face destruction's fate, But blessings through Abraham, don't hesitate.
God raised Jesus, sent Him to bless, Turn from wickedness, find righteousness."
The priests and the captain came, feeling the heat, Sadducees were mad 'cause of what they teach on the street.
They grabbed Peter and John, put 'em in a cell, But five thousand heard and believed, that's swell.
Next day in Jerusalem, rulers gathered 'round, Annas, Caiaphas, and kin, ready to throw down.
They stood Peter in the center, asked him with disdain, "By what power or name did you heal and proclaim?"
Filled with Spirit, Peter said, standing tall, "If a cripple is healed, it's by Jesus, y'all.
In the name of Christ, whom you crucified, God raised Him up, and in Him, this man’s revived.
The stone you builders disregarded, now it’s key, No other name can save, take it from me."
They saw the boldness, marveled at the scene, Unlearned men with Jesus, they made the connection clean.
The healed man stood there, silent proof in sight, Council conferred, seeking to dim the light.
"We can't deny the miracle that's been done, But let's stop the spread, keep the people from this one."
They warned them, "No more talk, no Jesus name speak," But Peter and John replied, "We can’t be weak.
Judge for yourselves, is it God or you we should heed? We’ll testify to what we saw, sowing God's seed."
Threats made again, but they let them go, The people praised God for the miracle show.
Back to their people, the apostles relayed, The threats from the leaders, and strong they prayed:
"O Lord, Creator of the earth and the sea, Why do nations rage, plotting against Thee?"
Herod and Pilate, gathered in this plot, Against Jesus, Your anointed, they sought.
"See their threats, Lord, grant us boldness to proclaim, Stretch Your hand, heal, glorify Your Servant’s name."
Place shaking, Spirit filled, they spoke with might, The believers united, hearts and souls held tight.
No one claimed a thing as solely their own, Shared all they had, love and grace were shown.
Apostles testified with power, in the Lord they basked, No one among them lacked, for all needs they asked.
Barnabas sold his field, laid the money down, At the apostles' feet, in the Spirit's renown.
Ananias and Sapphira, sold their land for some cash, Kept a part for themselves, thought they'd make a quick stash.
Laid the rest at the apostles' feet, like it was all they got, But Peter saw through the game, called 'em out on the spot.
"Ananias, why lie to the Spirit, to the Lord? The land was yours, no need for this fraud," he implored.
Ananias heard the truth, fell down, breathed his last, Fear gripped the people, as they buried him fast.
Three hours later, Sapphira came around, Unaware of her husband's fate, or the ground.
Peter asked her, "Was this the price, tell me true?" "Yes," she replied, but the lie caught her too.
"The feet of the men who buried your man stand at the door," She dropped at Peter’s feet, breathed no more.
Fear spread wide, as they laid her in the grave, The assembly learned, and their respect they gave.
Many wonders were performed by the apostles’ hands, In Solomon's porch, they stood strong in faith bands.
Believers grew in number, a mighty crowd, Peter's shadow healed the sick, drew 'em proud.
But the high priest, filled with envy and spite, Seized the apostles, locked them away at night.
An angel freed them, said, "Go and teach in the temple's hall," At daybreak they preached, spreading the word to all.
The council gathered, found the cell empty and bare, Confusion struck, as they wondered who dared.
"Look!" someone cried, "they're teaching in the square," The captain fetched them, careful not to stir the air.
The high priest demanded, "Didn't we command you to cease?" But Peter stood firm, "We obey God, not you, in peace."
"The God of our fathers raised Jesus, who you slew, Made Him a Savior, giving repentance anew."
Their words cut deep, the council's anger burned bright, But Gamaliel stood, spoke wisdom in their sight.
"Be wary," he warned, "leave these men be, If they're of God, you can't fight and won't see victory."
The council agreed, beat them, and let them go, The apostles rejoiced, honored to bear such a blow.
Daily in the temple, in homes, their voices rang, Preaching of Jesus, their Savior, as they sang.
In those days, the disciples grew, complaints began to rise, The Hellenists said the Hebrews left their widows to compromise.
The twelve gathered all and made their voices loud, "It's not right to leave God's word for serving the crowd.
Choose seven men, filled with spirit and wisdom's might, To handle this task, and make sure it's done right.
We'll stay in prayer, keep preaching the word, That's our mission, in service to the Lord."
The crowd agreed, pleased with the plan, They chose Stephen, a faithful, Spirit-filled man.
Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, and Timon too, Parmenas and Nicolaus, proselyte anew.
The apostles prayed, laid hands on their heads, The word of God spread, with new paths it treads.
In Jerusalem, disciples multiplied, Even priests joined, faith amplified.
Stephen, with power, showed wonders and signs, But some from synagogues crossed the lines.
They debated but couldn't overcome his wisdom or spirit's flame, So they whispered lies, trying to ruin his name.
"We heard him speak against Moses and God," they swore, Riling up the elders, they seized him at the door.
Before the council, false witnesses stood, Accusing him of plans to destroy the understood.
Claiming Jesus would change the law's face, But Stephen, like an angel, met their gaze.
The high priest asked, "Is this the truth you know?" Stephen stood up, "Brothers, let me show.
God spoke to Abraham in a distant land, Said, 'Leave your kin, follow my command.'
He left the Chaldaeans, settled in Haran, Till God moved him to this promised land.
No inheritance given, not even a place, Promised it for his seed by God's grace.
God said his offspring would face tribulation, Enslaved and mistreated for generations.
'I’ll judge that nation,' declared the Lord, 'Then they'll serve me, by my word.'
The covenant of circumcision, Abraham received, Isaac, then Jacob, through whom we believed.
The patriarchs, in jealousy, sold Joseph away, But God stayed with him every day.
Joseph rose high in Pharaoh’s land, Then famine struck, as God had planned.
Jacob heard of grain, sent his sons to seek, Joseph revealed himself, not weak.
Brought his family, seventy-five strong, In Egypt, they settled, it didn’t take long.
But soon a king rose who knew not the past, Oppressed our fathers, made life hard and fast.
Moses was born, a child of great light, Raised by Pharaoh’s daughter, trained for the fight.
At forty, he sought his kin, saw their pain, Struck an Egyptian, justice sought to claim.
His people pushed him, 'Who made you the judge?' Moses fled to Midian, where he'd find God's nudge.
Forty years passed, in Sinai’s wild land, God's flame in the bush, His voice took a stand.
'I am the God of your fathers,' He declared, 'Releasing my people, to Egypt you’ll be spared.'
This Moses, once refused and scorned, God sent back, His power adorned.
He led them out, with signs and wonders so grand, Through sea and desert, by divine hand.
Yet they turned back, hearts to Egypt’s ways, Made a calf, rejoiced in their own praise.
God turned them over, idols they would choose, A warning, His presence they might lose.
The tabernacle Moses built by God’s design, Carried through Joshua's time, a sign divine.
Solomon built a house, but God’s not contained, “Heaven’s my throne, earth’s where I’ve reigned.
You stiff-necked people, resist till the end, As your fathers did, so again you offend.
The prophets they killed, and now Him you betray, The Righteous One you slew, you turned away.”
When they heard these words, their hearts were torn, They gnashed their teeth, full of scorn.
Stephen, full of Spirit, gazed up high, Saw God’s glory, Jesus by His side.
“I see the heavens open wide,” he cried, The Son of Man at God’s right side.
They rushed at him, stopped their ears from the sound, Dragged him out, stoned him to the ground.
At Saul’s feet, their garments were laid, As Stephen prayed, his peace displayed.
“Lord Jesus, my spirit receive,” He knelt, forgiving those who didn’t believe.
He cried, “Lord, this sin don’t hold against them!” Then fell asleep, his soul to God did commend.
Saul gave the nod to Stephen's demise, Persecution hit hard, scattered 'neath the skies.
Devout men grieved, buried Stephen with tears, But Saul stormed the houses, spreading more fears.
The scattered ones preached, the Word they shared, Philip hit Samaria, bold and prepared.
Crowds listened close, saw signs he displayed, Demons fled loud, the lame were remade.
Joy filled the city, the air was bright, But Simon the sorcerer stepped in the light.
He amazed them long, they called him great, But Philip's message would change their fate.
Believing in Christ, they were baptized anew, Even Simon joined in, amazed by what's true.
Jerusalem's apostles heard Samaria's news, Sent Peter and John, Spirit to infuse.
Hands were laid, the Spirit came, Simon offered cash, seeking power, not fame.
Peter rebuked him, "Your heart's not right, Repent and pray, escape this plight."
Simon replied, "Pray none of this be," Peter’s words shook him, set Simon free.
They preached in villages, on their way back, An angel spoke to Philip, a new path to track.
He met an Ethiopian, reading on his ride, Philip joined him, heard the scriptures inside.
"Do you understand?" Philip asked with care, The eunuch needed guidance, a truth to share.
From Isaiah's scroll, Philip spoke of the Lamb, Jesus' story unfolded, the eternal plan.
Water appeared, the eunuch cried, "Why wait? Baptize me now, before it's too late!"
Both went down, water held the scene, Spirit caught Philip, gone, like a dream.
The eunuch rejoiced, his heart set free, Philip preached on, from town to sea.
Saul's breathing threats, with hate in his chest, Seeks the high priest, on a mission, no rest.
With letters in hand for Damascus' gate, To bind up the followers, seal their fate.
But on that road, a flash from the sky, Saul hit the ground, heard a voice up high:
"Saul, why persecute me?" came the call, "Who are you, Lord?" Saul asked in thrall.
"I'm Jesus, whom you chase and fight, Get up, go to the city, wait for your light."
His men stood speechless, heard but unseen, Saul opened his eyes, found the world had turned mean.
Blind for three days, no food, no sip, Led to Damascus, feeling the grip.
Ananias in vision heard the Lord's call, "Go to Straight Street, seek Saul of Tarsus, tall.
He's praying, he's seen you lay hands to restore, He'll regain his sight, walk through a new door."
"Lord," said Ananias, fear in his tone, "This Saul is known for breaking bones."
But the Lord replied, "He’s my chosen name, To speak before nations, in suffering gain."
Ananias went, found the house, Laid hands, brought light back to Saul's darkened house.
"Sight’s yours, Holy Spirit's gift," he declared, Scales fell away, Saul was prepared.
He ate, found strength, stayed with the crew, Preached Christ in synagogues, a gospel new.
People amazed, "Isn't this the foe? He bound the believers, now he's aglow?"
Strength in Saul grew, proving Christ’s the key, Jews planned to kill him, but Saul would flee.
Disciples by night, lowered him with care, In a basket through the wall, escaping the snare.
In Jerusalem, he faced fear and doubt, Till Barnabas vouched, "He's changed, no doubt."
Bold in Jesus' name, Saul spoke true, Hellenists plotted, but escape he knew.
The church found peace in Judea’s land, Walking in fear, comfort at hand.
Peter traveled, met Aeneas in bed, "Jesus heals you," and Aeneas rose, instead.
Lydda and Sharon saw, turned to the Lord, Miracles unfolding, through Jesus' word.
In Joppa, Tabitha, kind with her skill, Fell sick and died, but hope lived still.
Peter arrived, widows wept and showed, The garments she made, acts of love bestowed.
Peter prayed, "Tabitha, rise!" She opened her eyes, life in disguise.
Raised her up, called the saints, they saw, News spread wide, faith and awe.
Peter stayed with Simon, a tanner by trade, Miracles of life, the gospel conveyed.
In Caesarea lived a man named Cornelius, bold, A centurion of the Italian Regiment, devout and controlled. Feared God with his family, gave gifts as planned, He prayed to God, a generous hand.
At the ninth hour, an angel appeared in a vision, "Cornelius!" called out with precision. Startled, he asked, "What is it, Lord?" "Your prayers and gifts, they've reached God adored.
"Send men to Joppa, fetch Simon called Peter, He's with a tanner, by the seaside, a caretaker." When the angel left, Cornelius called his crew, Explained it all, sent them off to pursue.
Next day, nearing the city, Peter went to pray, Hungry and waiting, he fell into a trance, they say. Heaven opened, a sheet came descending, Animals and birds, a vision unending.

"Rise, Peter, kill and eat!" said the voice from above, But Peter refused, "Not so, Lord, I keep kosher love." "What God cleansed, don't call unclean," came the reply, Three times it happened, the sheet rose to the sky.
While Peter puzzled over what it all meant, Cornelius' men arrived, their inquiry they sent. The Spirit spoke, "Three men seek, arise, Go with them now, no doubt or surprise."
Peter met them and asked their intent, "Cornelius, a righteous man, you were sent." He invited them in, showed them hospitality, Next day, they traveled with Peter's locality.
In Caesarea, Cornelius gathered his kin, When Peter arrived, Cornelius welcomed him in. Fell to his feet, but Peter said, "Stand tall, I'm just a man, after all."
Peter spoke, "As a Jew, I shouldn't be here, But God showed me, no man should I fear. I ask you now, why did you send?" Cornelius shared the vision, how it did extend.
"Four days ago, as I fasted and prayed, An angel spoke, and this is what he relayed: Send for Peter in Joppa, by the sea, He'll talk, and God's will you'll see."
Peter spoke, "In every nation, God sees the right, No favoritism, just those living in light. Jesus of Nazareth, filled with Spirit and power, Healing and doing good, even at the darkest hour.
"We witnessed his works, in Judea and Jerusalem's land, Killed on a tree, by God's command. Raised on the third day, revealed to a few, Ate and drank with us, as we knew.
"He’s the Judge of living and dead, Prophets spoke, through him, sins are shed." As Peter spoke, the Spirit fell on each, Amazement stirred, all began to preach.
"Can anyone stop their baptismal flight? They have the Spirit, just like us, in sight." Baptized in Christ’s name, they were, Peter stayed there, the message to confer.

Yo, the word was spreading, reaching far and wide, Gentiles heard it too, no longer pushed aside. Peter rolled into Jerusalem, folks were on his case, "You chilled with the uncircumcised? You shared their space?"
He said, "Listen up, in Joppa, I was in a trance, Saw a massive sheet descend, it made me glance. Four-footed beasts, creatures creeping on the ground, Birds from the sky, they were all around.
I heard a voice say, 'Peter, rise and eat!' I shouted back, 'Lord, I’ve kept it clean, no unholy meat!' But the voice hit back, from heaven it came, 'What God cleansed, don’t you call it shame.'
Three times it happened, then the vision flew, Suddenly three men, in front of me, they stood true. The Spirit spoke, 'Go with them, no doubt!' So we entered a man's house, his story poured out.

He saw an angel, said, 'Bring Peter from Joppa's shore, He’ll speak words that save your house forevermore.' As I spoke, the Holy Spirit fell like at the start, Remembered the Lord's words, they hit my heart.
'John baptized with water, but the Spirit's for you,' If God gives this gift, who am I to refuse? They heard, they were silent, then glorified, "God's granted the Gentiles life," they testified.

But persecution spread, sent believers far and wide, Phoenicia, Cyprus, Antioch, the word they did confide. Some hit the Hellenists with the Lord Jesus' story, The hand of God was with them, many turned for glory.

News hit Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas with speed, He saw grace, was glad, and urged them to proceed. Full of Spirit, faith in grace, many turned to the Lord, Barnabas fetched Saul, together they restored.
In Antioch, for a year, they taught with zeal, Disciples named Christians, their faith was real. Prophets from Jerusalem, one named Agabus spoke, A famine was incoming, the Spirit's words woke.
Disciples gave plenty, relief was on the way, To Judea's brothers, through Barnabas and Saul's sway. So the story unfolds, God's work never done, In unity and grace, salvation's won.
Herod was oppressing, James was slain, The Jews were pleased, so he seized Peter, again.
