God wipes away their tears, renews their sight, In His presence, all is pure delight.
The seventh seal opened, silence took the stage, Heaven held its breath, for half an hour's age.
Seven angels stood tall, trumpets in their hand, Ready to sound off, by divine command.
An angel with a censer, golden and bright, Stood by the altar, in heavenly light.
Incense was given, prayers of saints rose high, Smoke curled to God, from the angel's hand to sky.
He took the censer, filled it with fire, Cast it to earth, now things were dire.
Thunder crashed, lightning flashed, the ground shook, The seven angels prepared, no second look.
First trumpet sounded, hail and fire mixed with blood, One third of the earth scorched by this flood.
Trees burned, grass gone, devastation spread, As the first trumpet's call left the planet red.
The second angel blew, a mountain ablaze, Hurled into the sea, causing a haze.
Waters turned to blood, creatures in the sea died, Ships were destroyed, waves of chaos wide.
The third angel's blast brought a star from the sky, Wormwood fell, rivers and springs ran dry.
Water turned bitter, many lives were claimed, By the poison they drank, the star's curse named.
Fourth trumpet's echo struck sun, moon, and stars, One third darkened, cosmic lights marred.
Day lost its shine, and night shared its fate, Darkness covered all, sealing their state.
An eagle soared high, cried out loud and clear, "Woe to those on earth, the end draws near!"
Three trumpets left, disaster yet to sound, Greater woes await, with each trumpet's pound.
The fifth angel blew his horn, a star fell from the sky, Key to the abyss pit was given, down below it did lie.
He opened up the pit, smoke rose like a furnace burn, Sun and air darkened, thick smoke made the world churn.
Out came locusts in the smoke, scorpions with power, Not to harm the grass or trees, but man in this dark hour.
"Don’t touch the sealed," they were told, "torment those instead, For five months bring the pain, but leave them not dead."
Folks sought death, but it ran, elusive like a ghost, Life's a prison, they cried, death denied, the ultimate host.
Locusts looked like war horses, crowns of gold on heads, Faces human, hair flowing, teeth like lions, dread.
Iron breastplates on their chests, wings loud as chariots race, Tails with power to sting, five months they left their trace.
Their king, the abyss angel, Abaddon his name, Apollyon in Greek, but the mission’s the same.
First woe had passed, but look, two more woes on their way, The sixth angel sounded, a new voice came to play.
From the golden altar, the command loudly spoke, “Release the Euphrates-bound angels, now let them invoke!”
Four angels set free for this moment in time, To slay a third of mankind, in a judgment so prime.
Two hundred million horsemen, I heard them declare, Breastplates fiery red, blue, yellow in the air.
Horse heads like lions, from mouths fire, smoke, and sulfur blast, One third of mankind fell, these plagues struck fast.
Power in their mouths and tails, serpents with a bite, As devastation reigned, many lost the fight.
Yet mankind did not repent, held tight to their hand-made ways, Worshipped idols dead and mute, in a haze they stayed.
No turning from violence, magic, lust, or greed, Blind to the warnings, on these sins they still feed.
Out of the sky, an angel came flying, clothed with a cloud, no denying. Rainbow on his head, sun for a face, feet fired up, pillars in place.
In his hand, a little book he held tight, right foot on the sea, left on land, standing might. He roared loud like a lion, bold and grand, the seven thunders echoed, shaking the land.

I moved to write what the thunders had said, but a voice said, “Seal that truth, keep it in your head.” The angel on sea and land raised his hand high, swore by the Everlasting, who fashioned sky and land nearby.
“No more delays,” the angel cried, "when the seventh speaks, mystery untied." The voice from heaven spoke to me once more, “Take the open book, here’s what’s in store.”
I approached the angel, asked for the book, “Eat it,” he said, “bitter and sweet, take a look.” In my mouth, honey, sweetness it brought, but my stomach twisted, bitterness it wrought.
They said, “You’ll prophesy far and wide, over nations, kings, in languages worldwide.”
A reed like a rod was placed in my hand, "Rise, measure the temple, altar, and stand.
Leave out the court that's outside the gate, For the nations will tread it, that's their fate.
Forty-two months they'll trample in scorn, But I'll empower my witnesses, forlorn.
Two olive trees, two lamps stand bold, Prophesying in sackcloth, stories told.
If harm's what they seek, fire will devour, Their words bring plagues, sky won't shower.
When their testimony's done, the beast will rise, From the abyss, make war, claim their lives.
In the great city's street, they'll lie cold, Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord was sold.
For three and a half days, all will stare, Refusing a tomb, leaving them bare.
The earth's dwellers rejoice, exchange gifts wide, Celebrating torment that these two supplied.
But God's breath of life will enter anew, They'll stand on their feet, fear grips the view.
A voice from heaven loud and clear, "Come up here!" and in clouds they appear.
A great quake shakes, a tenth city falls, Seven thousand lost, terror enthralls.
The second woe is gone, the third comes fast, The seventh angel sounds, heaven's voices cast.
"The world's kingdom now the Lord's domain, Forever and ever, He shall reign!"
The elders bow, faces to the ground, "Praise to You, Almighty, power profound.
Nations raged, Your wrath unfurled, Time for judgment now in this world.
Reward Your servants, prophets of light, The great and small, those in Your sight.
Heaven's temple opened, the covenant's ark, Lightning and thunder, the earth goes dark."
In heaven, a vision, grand and bright, A woman clothed with the sun's pure light. Moon underfoot, twelve stars on her crown, With child in pain, her cries resound.
Next, a red dragon, fierce and wild, Seven heads, ten horns, evil compiled. His tail swept stars, casting them down, He waits to devour the newborn crown.
She births a son, destined to reign, With iron rod, he'll break the chain. But up to God, the child ascends, While she retreats where God defends.
War in the sky, Michael takes stand, Against the dragon and his band. But they're defeated, cast from heaven, No place left for them, peace given.
The dragon thrown, the old serpent's fall, Devil and Satan, deceiver to all. In heaven a voice, loud and clear, "Salvation has come, God's Kingdom is here.
Overcome by the Lamb's own blood, Their testimony stood strong in the flood. Rejoice, O heavens, but earth beware, The devil's wrath is near, so take care."
Dragon on earth, he hunts the queen, But wings of eagles intervene. She flies to safety, away from harm, Protected, sheltered, from his alarm.
Serpent spews water, a river wide, But the earth opens, the wave subsides. Dragon enraged, he turns to fight, Against her offspring, holding truth's light.
I stood on the sand by the sea's wide expanse, Saw a beast rise up, as if in a trance. Ten horns, seven heads, each crown shining bright, With names that blaspheme, a fearsome sight.
Looks like a leopard, feet like a bear, Mouth of a lion, a beast beyond compare. The dragon gave power, throne, and authority, A ruler of chaos, a sight of ferocity.
One head was wounded, seemed fatally scarred, But healed it rose, the world caught off guard. They worshiped the dragon, power he bestowed, Said, "Who can compare? Who can break his code?"
A mouth filled with blasphemy, speaking grand things, Forty-two months of war, the chaos it brings. Against God he spoke, defying the divine, Blaspheming heaven, crossing the line.
Given power over nations, tribes, and speech, To conquer the saints, their faith he would breach. The earth in awe, their names not in the book, Worshiped the beast, at the world they shook.
"If you hear, then listen, let truth draw near. Destined for captivity, let that be clear." Endurance and faith, the saints' steady way, Through trials and fire, they stand, they stay.
Another beast rose, from the earth it came, Two horns like a lamb, a voice of dragon flame. With the first beast's power, it made them bow down, To the healed beast, holding its crown.
Signs and wonders, fire from the sky, Deception and awe, the people comply. “Make an image,” it said, “to the one who survived, The sword-struck beast, now revived.”
It gave breath to the image, made it speak loud, And those who refused, laid under a shroud. Marks on their hands, or on their heads, Without it no trade, on this path they tread.
Wisdom calls out, hear the number well, Six hundred sixty-six, a tale to tell. The number of man, a mystery deep, In this prophecy, truths and warnings seep.
Behold the Lamb on Zion's rise, 144,000 stand with eyes on the prize. Their foreheads marked, His name there displayed, Sound from heaven like thunder, a symphony played.
A new song echoes, only their ears know, Redeemed from earth, in purity they glow. Virgins they are, following the Lamb's stride, In truth they walk, never once lied.
An angel flies high, with Good News to share, "Fear the Lord, give glory, for judgment's over there. Worship the Creator, of sea, sky, and land!" Another angel cries, "Babylon's fall at hand."
A third voice warns, "Beware the beast’s dark claim, Receive his mark, and suffer eternal flame. God's wrath is pure, in His cup of anger, Torment awaits, no rest, a constant clangor."

Saints persevere, with faith in their hands, Keeping God's commandments, across all lands. A voice declares, "Blessed those who die in the Lord, They rest from their labors, their works their reward."
A white cloud appears, a man with a crown, A sickle in hand, the harvest’s renown. An angel cries, "Reap, the earth is ripe!" The sickle swings, and humanity's stripe.
Another angel, with a sickle sharp as ice, Calls from the altar, "Gather grapes of vice!" The vintage collected, wrath like a flood, Wine press outside the city, rivers of blood.
I saw a vision, great and high, Seven angels, plagues, God's wrath up in the sky.
A sea of glass, mixed with fire's glow, Victors over the beast, their harps in tow.
They sang a song, Moses and the Lamb's refrain, "Praise the Lord Almighty, forever reign.
Righteous and true, King of all nations, All will come to worship, in adoration."
The temple gates swung open wide, In heaven's court, the truth can't hide.
Seven angels, linen pure and bright, Golden sashes gleaming in the holy light.
A creature gave them bowls of gold, Full of God's wrath, so mighty and bold.
Smoke filled the temple, God's glory in power, No one entered in that solemn hour.
Until the seven plagues would end their run, The mighty work of God would be done.
From the temple, a voice boomed loud and clear, "Pour the seven bowls; let the wrath appear!"
The first angel stepped up, pouring his bowl to the ground, Sores erupted on those with the beast's mark, profound.
The second hit the sea, turned it red like blood, Every creature in the ocean felt the flood.
The third bowl poured where rivers flow, Waters turned crimson, nothing could grow.
An angel declared, "You're righteous and just, For they spilled the blood, now drink it they must."
The altar agreed, "True are your ways, Almighty God, in all your displays."
The fourth bowl unleashed the sun's burning might, Scorching men, yet they cursed the light.
Blazing heat, but no hearts turned, No repentance, though they burned.
The fifth brought darkness over the beast's domain, Tongues gnawed in agony, cursing in vain.
Still, no change, no remorse shown, They clung to their ways, to the bone.
The sixth dried up the Euphrates wide, Clearing paths for kings, with armies at their side.
Out came spirits like frogs, sneaky and sly, Deceiving the leaders under the sky.
"Behold, I come like a thief in the night, Blessed is he who's ready, clothed in the light."
To Megiddo, he gathered them all, For the great day, when kingdoms would fall.
The seventh poured his bowl into the air, "It is done!" echoed from the heavenly chair.
Lightning flashed, thunder roared so fierce, An earthquake split the ground, humanity pierced.
Cities crumbled, Babylon's fate was sealed, Every island vanished, mountains no longer revealed.
Hailstones fell, heavy as a talent's weight, Men cursed God's name under the crushing slate.
An angel approached, with a bowl in his hand, "Come see the judgment, the scene I have planned.
The great prostitute on many waters she sits, The kings of the earth in her web, they commit.
Drunk on her wine, the earthlings all roam, He carried me off, to the wild we were flown.
There sat a woman on a beast blazing red, Covered in blasphemy, many heads it spread.
Dressed in fine purple, with gold she was bright, Holding a cup of earth’s sins in her sight.
"MYSTERY," it read on her brow with pride, Babylon the Great, in her horror I spied.
Drunk on saints' blood, martyrs of the Lamb, I gazed in wonder, she didn’t give a damn.
The angel asked, "Why do you stare? I'll reveal the mystery, if you dare.
The beast you saw, was, is not, will rise, From the abyss to its own demise.
Earth's dwellers marvel, their names not found, In the book of life, from time's very ground.
Seven heads are seven hills she rides, Seven kings fallen, one still bides.
The beast’s the eighth, yet part of the seven, Headed for destruction, far from heaven.
Ten horns are kings, no kingdoms yet, With the beast they rise, a bond they set.
Warring the Lamb, but the Lamb prevails, Lord of lords, King of kings, He never fails.
The waters are nations, peoples and tongues, Where she sits, where her dirge is sung.
The horns and beast, they'll turn with hate, Strip her bare, burn her fate.
For God's will beats in their hearts as one, To give the kingdom till His words are done.
The woman you saw, that great city's might, Ruling kings, in her darkened light."
Out the sky, an angel came down with power so great, Lit up the earth, left no room for debate.
With a mighty voice, he called out the fate, "Babylon has fallen, now demons congregate.
Nations drunk on her sin, kings in her embrace, Merchants rich from her luxury, a disgrace."
Another voice from heaven, a warning to state, "Come out, my people, avoid her cursed fate.
Her sins reach the sky, God won't forget, Repay her double, she'll get what she set.
She boasted strong, said mourning ain't her game, But in one day, fire will claim her name.
Kings will wail as they see her smoke rise, Standing afar, fear in their eyes.
'Woe, woe, Babylon, your judgment's come fast,' In one single hour, your riches couldn't last."
Merchants will cry over their unsold wares, Gold, silver, and silks, lost in despair.
Spices and goods, all vanished from view, What you lusted after, now lost to you.
They'll stand afar, mourning in pain, "Great city, your riches have gone down the drain.
In an hour, all wealth turns to dust, The sea folk watch, their fortunes combust."
Dust on their heads, they cry with a roar, "Woe, the great city, now rich no more."
Heaven rejoice, for justice is delivered, Babylon's fall, the saints' hearts are quivered.
A mighty angel flings a stone to the sea, "With violence, Babylon's history will be.
No more music, no craftsman's hand, The city's light extinguished, barren the land.
Bride and groom's voices silenced in gloom, For merchants deceived, cast spells of doom.
In her found the blood of the pure and the brave, Prophets and saints resting in their grave."
A loud voice in heaven, a shout so grand, “Hallelujah! Salvation and power are in God's hand.
His judgments are true, righteous as they stand, Judged the great prostitute, avenged the blood on this land.”
A second voice echoed, “Hallelujah, forever her smoke will burn,” Elders and creatures fell, God's praise their eternal concern.
From the throne came a call, “Praise Him, both small and great!” A multitude roared, like waters and thunder, proclaiming His fate.
“Hallelujah! The Lord Almighty reigns, Rejoice, give glory, for the Lamb's wedding remains.”
The bride in fine linen, pure and bright, Saints’ righteous deeds, shining in the light.
“Write this,” he said, “Blessed are those at the Lamb's feast,” “These are God's words, true,” he ceased.
I bowed to worship, but he lifted me, “Don't! I'm a servant too, worship God alone, that's the point.”
Heaven opened, a white horse in view, Faithful and True, He judges, makes war anew.
Eyes of flame, crowns galore, Names unknown, mystery at the core.
Clothed in blood, the Word of God is His name, Heavenly armies followed, white horses, no shame.
From His mouth, a sword sharp and bright, Strikes nations, rules with iron, wrath's might.
On His garment, thigh, a name clear and bold, “KING OF KINGS, LORD OF LORDS,” the story told.
An angel in the sun, called birds to a feast, “Come, eat the flesh of kings, captains, and beast.”
The beast and kings, armies amassed, Made war on the Rider, the final clash.
The beast and prophet, deceived the marked, Thrown alive in fire, sulfur sparked.
The rest fell by the sword, from the Rider's mouth it came, Birds filled with flesh, the end of their game.
An angel came down from heaven's gate, With a key to the abyss, a chain to seal fate.
The dragon, old serpent, devil in disguise, Captured and bound, couldn't spread his lies.
Into the abyss, cast and sealed tight, For a thousand years, he'd be out of sight.
Saw thrones set high, judgment was given, Souls of the martyred, for Christ they'd risen.
They reigned with Him a thousand years strong, A mark they refused, they stood all along.
Rest of the dead, they waited their turn, First resurrection, the blessed concern.
"Blessed and holy," in this they delight, Priests of God, reigning in the light.
After a thousand years, Satan breaks free, Deceiving the nations, a war decree.
Gathering forces, like sand by the sea, Surrounding the saints, thinking they'd flee.
But fire from heaven came raining down, Devoured them all, took the devil's crown.
The devil was tossed in the fiery lake, With the beast and prophet, forever to ache.
A throne stood great, white as snow, Heaven and earth fled, nowhere to go.
The dead stood tall, both great and small, Books of deeds opened, the judgment call.
The sea gave its dead, Hades and Death, Judged by their works, each took a breath.
Thrown into fire, death met its end, That lake of fire, where souls descend.
If not in the book of life, they'd retire, To the endless torment of the lake of fire.
I saw a new heaven, a fresh earth too, The old and the sea vanished, out of view.
A city descended, New Jerusalem's grace, Like a bride in beauty, took her place.
A voice from the sky declared so clear, “God’s with His people, He’s dwelling here.
Tears wiped away, death shall cease, No more sorrow, only peace.
'Behold,' said the throne, 'I make things new, Write it down, these words are true.'”
“I'm Alpha, Omega, Start and End, To the thirsty, living water I send.
He who conquers will be my son, I’ll be his God, my will be done.
But the cowards, liars, and all who deceive, In the burning lake they'll grieve.”
An angel arrived, with plagues in bowls, “Come see the Lamb's bride,” was his goal.
He took me high, to the mountain's view, Showed me the city with a light so true.
Glory like jasper, crystal clear, Walls and gates, twelve angels near.
East, north, south, and west, three gates each, On foundations, apostles' names did preach.
Golden reed for measure in hand, City's a square, a perfect land.
Walls of jasper, city gold like glass, Gem foundations, precious stones amassed.
Gates of pearl, streets of gold so bright, No temple needed, God’s glory is light.
No sun or moon, the Lamb is the lamp, Nations walk by light, no night’s stamp.
Gates open wide, no night to fear, Only the pure and true enter here.
No evil or lies in this place of life, Only those in the Lamb’s book, free from strife.
A river flows, clear as crystal, from the throne, Life's water runs, giving life unknown.
In the middle, streets and trees align, Twelve fruits they bear, month by month in line.
Leaves heal nations, no curse remains, God's throne is here, His servants reign.
They'll see His face, His name's on their heads, No need for night, by God's light they're led.
"These words are true," the angel said to me, "Sent by God's spirit, prophecy to see."
"Behold, I'm coming quick," said the Lord, "Blessed are those who keep this holy word."
I, John, saw it all and fell in awe, But the angel stopped me, "Worship God alone," he saw.
"Don't seal these words, the time is near, Let the unjust and holy keep their sphere."
"Behold, I'm coming quick, with rewards in hand, Alpha, Omega, First and Last, I stand."
Blessed are those who keep His command, Enter the city, by His tree stand.
Outside are dogs, sorcerers in their lies, But in this city, truth never dies.
"I, Jesus, sent my angel to proclaim, Root of David, Morning Star, in my name."
The Spirit and bride shout, "Come!" Let the thirsty take life’s water some.
"Don't add or take from this prophecy," Or face the plagues and lose the holy tree.
He says, "Yes, I come quickly," and we say, Amen! Come, Lord Jesus, without delay.
Grace be with all who read this scroll, The Lord Jesus Christ saves every soul. Amen.
